description: Use dCas9 to recruit AP-1 or a pioneer-like FOS/JUN domain to a neutral reporter locus with a transient pulse. Then test whether the locus keeps a more accessible state and responds faster after the recruitment is gone, which would show AP-1 is sufficient for memory.

question: ap1
title: Degron depletion after priming
description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) before re-stimulation. If enhanced response and accessibility persist without AP-1, memory is held elsewhere. If they collapse, AP-1 is required for maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse-and-probe
description: Use light-controlled AP-1 activation with defined pulse number, amplitude, and interval, then re-stimulate after variable delays. Measure the response and decay half-life to test sufficiency, dose-dependence, and hysteresis of memory without other signaling inputs.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome with lineage barcodes
description: Do paired RNA+ATAC on primed and naive cells with heritable barcodes to track clones across divisions. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are clonally inherited and whether they predict individual cells' re-stimulation response.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and residence-time measurements
description: Combine live-cell single-molecule tracking and CUT&RUN on mitotic-arrested cells to measure whether FOS/JUN stay bound at primed enhancers through mitosis. Compare residence times in primed vs naive cells to show stable, heritable binding.

question: ap1
title: Motif-specific enhancer editing and forced recruitment
description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs at persistently accessible enhancers to test necessity, and use dCas9-FOS/JUN to recruit AP-1 to naive loci to test sufficiency. Read out the kinetics of re-stimulation, accessibility, and H3K27ac, separating AP-1 from other chromatin-based memory.

question: ap1
title: Prime–washout–restimulate with acute degron
description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wash out, then acutely degrade (dTAG/AID) c-Jun/Fos or express A-Fos either before or after the rest period, and measure the faster/stronger secondary response. If memory persists after AP-1 removal, AP-1 is only the initiator. If it requires AP-1 during the rest period or at recall, AP-1 is the maintainer.

question: ap1
title: Time-resolved chromatin accessibility and histone marks at AP-1 sites
description: Run ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, AP-1 factors) at several time points after priming and withdrawal. Test whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers stay open or marked, and whether their persistence predicts the magnitude of the recall response.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage-resolved memory with live AP-1 reporters
description: Tag endogenous Fos/Jun and a target gene with fluorescent reporters, and track primed cells and their descendants by live imaging across divisions. Compare sister-cell correlations and decay kinetics with those of unprimed controls to quantify heritability and test whether memory is cell-autonomous and AP-1 dependent.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis and bistability test with a feedback model
description: Expose cells to increasing and then decreasing stimulus doses and measure single-cell AP-1 activity and target output, looking for bimodal distributions and path-dependent thresholds. Fit a model of c-Jun autoregulation, and test its predictions by breaking the feedback loop, for example by mutating the AP-1 site in the JUN promoter.

question: ap1
title: Locus-specific causal test by motif editing and dCas9 perturbation
description: At a memory-associated enhancer, base-edit the AP-1 motif or use dCas9-KRAB to close it, either before priming or after priming and washout. Then test recall of the target gene to show whether the local AP-1 site is necessary for establishing the memory, for maintaining it, or for both.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved binding and perturbation map
description: Use CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq with antibodies or epitope tags for individual FOS, JUN, ATF and MAF members before, during and after stimulus. Combine this with paralog-specific degron depletion to find which dimers mark and maintain remembered loci, so that results are not blurred across the whole family.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron removal after the stimulus ends
description: Prime cells, wash out the stimulus, then rapidly degrade AP-1 factors (dTAG or AID) at different delays before restimulation. If the enhanced response and accessibility persist without AP-1, the memory is downstream of it. If they collapse, AP-1 is needed for maintenance and not only for establishment.

question: ap1
title: Separating memory from ongoing signaling input
description: Block upstream kinases (JNK, ERK) after priming and measure AP-1 phosphorylation, protein abundance, and binding over days. Pair this with a nuclear-localization or synthetic-input reporter, so you can tell self-sustaining AP-1 states (such as positive feedback via FOS/JUN promoters) from continued signaling.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage-tracked memory readout
description: Combine live-cell AP-1 reporters or endogenous FOS/JUN tagging with time-lapse imaging and lineage tracking through divisions, then restimulate and record each cell's response. Compare sister cells to test whether memory is heritable, digital or graded, and how much heterogeneity the population average hides.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 recruitment to test sufficiency
description: Use dCas9 or a tethered AP-1 DNA-binding domain to impose transient AP-1 binding at a naive enhancer or reporter, and track chromatin accessibility, histone marks and later inducibility after release. This tests whether AP-1 occupancy alone can write a heritable state. Repeat it across cell types and stimulus histories, such as repeated versus single pulses, to test context-dependence.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-specific degron and ChIP/CUT&RUN time course
description: Use endogenous degron tags on individual Fos, Jun and ATF family members, together with paralog-specific CUT&RUN, to find which AP-1 dimers bind during stimulation and which stay bound after the signal ends. Memory-bearing dimers would be those whose acute loss erases the response, which separates them from family members that are only transiently active.

question: ap1
title: Stimulus-then-degrade AP-1 separation of AP-1 from its chromatin legacy
description: Stimulate cells, wash out the stimulus, then deplete AP-1 (dTAG or a dominant-negative such as A-Fos) after the transcriptional response has returned to baseline. Compare ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and re-stimulation responses with and without depletion, to test whether AP-1-opened chromatin keeps the memory after AP-1 has gone.

question: ap1
title: Necessity-and-sufficiency with timed optogenetic or chemogenetic AP-1 control
description: Drive c-Fos/c-Jun with a light- or drug-inducible system without the natural stimulus, then test whether a pulse is enough to leave a lasting state. Block AP-1 during the original stimulus and see whether later memory is lost. This replaces correlation with causal manipulation.

question: ap1
title: Enhancer-level perturbation of AP-1 motifs and pioneer context
description: Run a massively parallel reporter assay in the native chromatin context, using CRISPR base editing of AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers. Pair it with measures of nucleosome occupancy and the binding of other pioneer factors, to see which motifs are needed to set and keep the primed state.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell live imaging and multiomics lineage tracing of memory
description: Image AP-1 reporters, such as endogenous Fos-tagged knock-ins, in single cells through stimulation, washout and re-stimulation. Combine this with single-cell multiome (RNA and ATAC) and barcode lineage tracing to see whether memory is bistable, inherited through division, and heterogeneous across clones. Also test priming by comparing re-stimulation response size against a first-exposure control.

question: ap1
title: Paralog-resolved CUT&RUN and degron panel
description: Profile individual Fos/Jun/ATF/Maf family members before, during and long after stimulus, and use paralog-specific degrons to determine which dimer composition marks and maintains memory sites. This tests the assumption that AP-1 is one uniform factor.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin-state persistence after AP-1 removal
description: After a priming stimulus, measure accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac and H3K4me1 at AP-1 sites in cells where AP-1 is depleted or washed out, comparing them to cells where it remains. Persistence of the marks without AP-1 would place memory in chromatin instead of in the factor.

question: ap1
title: Timed acute degradation to separate establishment from maintenance
description: Use dTAG/auxin or a dominant-negative A-Fos to remove AP-1 function at defined windows (during priming, after priming, or during restimulation), then measure the restimulation response. This separates a hit-and-run establishment role from continuous maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Genome-wide re-induction kinetics and priming
description: Compare naive and previously stimulated cells after a rest period using nascent RNA assays (PRO-seq, TT-seq) at restimulation, quantifying faster or stronger induction genome-wide. This captures memory as primed responsiveness, not only persistent expression of canonical targets.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing through divisions
description: Run single-cell ATAC plus RNA with barcoded lineage tracing or live AP-1 reporters, and follow clonal sister cells across divisions and rest periods to see whether memory is a heritable all-or-none state. Compare AP-1 motif accessibility with response in sister cells to test heterogeneity and inheritance.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-specific degron and mutant panel
description: Use acute degradation (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative lines (A-Fos, specific bZIP mutants) for individual Fos/Jun/ATF family members, and test which ones are needed for priming versus recall. This tests whether memory belongs to a particular AP-1 dimer rather than to AP-1 as a whole.

question: ap1
title: Priming-then-depletion order-of-events experiment
description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wash it out, then degrade AP-1 during the rest period. Re-stimulate and measure whether the enhanced transcriptional response (nascent RNA, PRO-seq) persists without AP-1. If it does, AP-1 initiates memory but chromatin maintains it. If it doesn't, AP-1 maintains memory itself.

question: ap1
title: Time-resolved occupancy and accessibility tracking
description: Run CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag for AP-1 members, together with ATAC-seq and H3K27ac, at several points: during the stimulus, at hours and days after washout, and after re-stimulation. This shows whether AP-1 stays bound at primed enhancers or leaves behind accessibility that persists without it.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and response
description: Image endogenously tagged Fos/Jun, or use an AP-1 reporter, in single cells through repeated stimulations, and link each cell's earlier AP-1 history to its later response. This tests whether memory is a heterogeneous, cell-autonomous state, and whether it is inherited through division by lineage tracing.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 site editing and rewiring
description: Use CRISPR to mutate or insert AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers, or to recruit dCas9 AP-1 activators or repressors. Then test whether the primed response, accessibility and re-induction speed change at those loci. This gives causal evidence at specific sites and tests whether AP-1 sites are sufficient to create memory in naive loci. Pair it with perturbation of partners such as pioneer factors or SWI/SNF to find out what else is required.

question: ap1
title: Paralog- and dimer-resolved memory mapping
description: Run CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq for individual FOS, JUN, and ATF family members, and for their dimers (for example by re-ChIP or proximity-based methods). Do this before, during, and after stimulus withdrawal. This shows which specific AP-1 complexes persist at sites that give a memory response, and which do not.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron depletion after the memory is set
description: Make a degron (dTAG or AID) knock-in of a key AP-1 subunit, or express a dominant-negative such as A-FOS. Remove AP-1 only after stimulation has ended and test whether the primed accessibility and the faster re-induction on second challenge are lost. If AP-1 is needed to maintain memory, depletion should erase it. If it is needed only to set it, the memory should persist.

question: ap1
title: Test for a hand-off to other factors and chromatin marks
description: Follow AP-1, histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1), DNA methylation, and co-factors (for example BAF/SWI-SNF and lineage factors) at memory loci over time after stimulus withdrawal. Combine this with chromatin-modifier inhibitors or catalytic-dead editing at those loci. The aim is to find out whether AP-1 holds the memory itself or only sets the chromatin state that does.

question: ap1
title: Restimulation-challenge time course with a primed-state readout
description: Give a first stimulus, wait for varying gaps (hours to weeks), then give a second stimulus of the same or a different type. Measure the speed and size of AP-1-dependent gene induction by nascent RNA (PRO-seq or TT-seq) and AP-1 binding. This tests for latent memory that shows up only on restimulation, and for how long it lasts and how specific it is.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing and live reporters
description: Use single-cell multiome (ATAC plus RNA) with clonal barcodes, plus live-cell AP-1 activity reporters, to follow whether memory is inherited through cell division in sister cells. Link each cell's past AP-1 activity to its later response. This separates real heritable memory from population averaging, and shows whether memory is all-or-none or graded.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-specific degron and CUT&RUN panel
description: Endogenously tag individual Fos, Jun, ATF and Maf family members with degrons and map each one's occupancy and role in primed enhancers after a stimulus/rest/restimulus protocol. This tests which specific AP-1 composition, if any, carries memory rather than treating AP-1 as one factor.

question: ap1
title: Acute depletion after establishment (establishment vs maintenance)
description: Prime cells with stimulus, wash out, then rapidly degrade AP-1 (e.g., dTAG/auxin or dominant-negative A-Fos) during the rest phase only, and compare restimulation response with depletion applied during priming only. If memory persists after AP-1 loss, AP-1 is an initiator and not the maintainer; if it is lost, AP-1 is required for maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin-versus-AP-1 uncoupling with epigenome editing
description: Use dCas9-based tools to erase or install H3K27ac/accessibility at AP-1 motif enhancers, or mutate AP-1 motifs by base editing, and test whether memory follows the AP-1 site or the chromatin state. This separates AP-1 as the memory carrier from downstream chromatin marks that could be self-sustaining.

question: ap1
title: Live-cell single-cell AP-1 reporters with lineage tracking
description: Image endogenously tagged Fos/Jun and a transcriptional reporter in single cells through priming, rest, and restimulation, tracking lineages through divisions. Quantify whether the memory is bimodal, how it correlates with AP-1 dynamics, and whether it is inherited by daughter cells, going beyond bulk averages.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome across stimuli, contexts and delays
description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC (with AP-1 motif deviation analysis) in several cell types, such as fibroblasts, macrophages and T cells, with different priming stimuli, rest durations, and passage numbers. Test if memory is graded, locus-specific, stimulus-specific and durable through divisions, and whether AP-1 motif activity predicts the secondary response across contexts.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-specific degron and CRISPR screen
description: Use acute degron tagging of individual Fos/Jun/ATF family members at different phases (during priming, after washout, before restimulation) with CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq to define which dimers establish versus maintain the memory state. This resolves the family heterogeneity and separates initiation from maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 depletion after priming to test chromatin-state-as-memory
description: After priming and washout, when AP-1 levels have returned to baseline, rapidly deplete or block AP-1 DNA binding (dominant-negative A-Fos, degron) and then restimulate. If memory persists and the sites keep H3K27ac/accessibility, the chromatin state rather than continuing AP-1 activity carries it; if memory is lost, AP-1 must be continually required.

question: ap1
title: Targeted editing of AP-1 motifs and enhancers
description: Mutate AP-1 motifs or use dCas9 epigenetic modifiers at memory-associated enhancers and measure the effect on re-induction of nearby genes. This tests whether persistent accessibility is functionally required rather than just correlated.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing
description: Combine scATAC/scRNA multiome with barcoded lineage tracing or live reporters of memory genes to ask whether memory is inherited by sister cells in a heterogeneous, all-or-none or graded manner. Compare AP-1 motif accessibility and expression noise between memory-positive and memory-negative clones.

question: ap1
title: Stimulus-history time course and in vivo validation
description: Vary dose, duration, number of pulses and rest interval to build a memory decay curve, tracking kinetics, amplitude and Micro-C enhancer-promoter contacts at AP-1 loci. Repeat in an in vivo model such as skin wound or inflammatory memory in stem cells, with AP-1 perturbation, to test graded, decaying memory and physiological relevance.

question: ap1
title: Paralog-resolved ChIP/CUT&RUN time course
description: Profile individual FOS, FOSL, JUN, JUND and ATF family members by CUT&RUN before, during, and days after the stimulus to see which dimers remain at memory loci. This tests the single-entity assumption by showing whether memory is carried by specific complexes.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron removal after the stimulus
description: Prime cells, then deplete AP-1 with a dTAG or auxin degron (for example, c-JUN or a dominant-negative A-FOS) only after the stimulus has cleared, and measure whether the faster secondary response and the open chromatin persist. If memory survives AP-1 loss, it lives in chromatin rather than in AP-1, which separates AP-1 as the memory carrier from AP-1 as the writer.

question: ap1
title: Long-term washout with matched ATAC, histone marks and AP-1 occupancy
description: Measure accessibility, H3K27ac/H3K4me1 and AP-1 binding at several time points over many days and cell divisions after the stimulus ends. Comparing their decay kinetics shows whether AP-1 stays bound (a true memory mechanism) or only leaves behind marks, and avoids single-time-point snapshots.

question: ap1
title: Site-specific causal perturbation of AP-1 motifs
description: Use CRISPR base editing or dCas9-based tethering to mutate or recruit AP-1 at individual enhancers, then test the primed response of the linked genes after a rest period. This tests causality at individual loci rather than motif enrichment, and tests whether AP-1 binding alone is sufficient to create memory.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome with live AP-1 reporters and lineage tracking
description: Combine live-cell imaging of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN with single-cell RNA and ATAC, and track daughter cells after division, to test whether memory is digital, heritable and tied to AP-1 state in each cell. Memory should appear as a bimodal, clonally inherited state that bulk averages would miss.

question: ap1
title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN reanalysis of AP-1 motif accessibility after transient stimuli
description: Reanalyze public time-course chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) ChIP/CUT&RUN datasets from injury, inflammation, or stress models (e.g., epidermal wound, macrophage training, neuronal activity) to find loci that stay open long after stimulus withdrawal. Test whether this persistent accessibility is enriched for AP-1 motifs (chromVAR/HOMER) and for occupancy by AP-1 or its pioneer-like partners such as BAF/ARID1A.

question: ap1
title: Cross-dataset test of 'memory' enhancers: AP-1 binding vs. faster secondary response
description: Use public primed/trained-immunity, epithelial inflammatory-memory, and repeated-stimulus datasets (ATAC, H3K27ac, RNA-seq) to identify enhancers that gain accessibility or H3K27ac after the first stimulus and persist. Then test whether these predict faster or stronger transcription at re-stimulation, and whether AP-1 motif strength or ChIP occupancy at them predicts this effect beyond other TF motifs (regression/model comparison).

question: ap1
title: Integrative modeling of AP-1 dynamics vs. epigenetic persistence using public single-cell multiome and perturbation data
description: Use public scRNA/scATAC or multiome time courses to estimate, per cell, AP-1 activity (FOS/JUN expression and regulon scores) and chromatin state over time. Use trajectory/lag analysis to ask whether transient AP-1 activity precedes durable accessibility changes, and whether AP-1 expression itself decays (signaling-driven) or is self-sustained.

question: ap1
title: Meta-analysis of AP-1 loss-of-function datasets to test necessity for maintenance versus establishment
description: Collect public datasets with AP-1 perturbation (JUN/FOS knockouts, dominant-negative A-FOS, degron or inhibitor treatments such as T-5224) paired with chromatin profiling. Compare the loss of accessibility and expression at memory loci when AP-1 is removed before, during, or after stimulus (where timing exists), to separate establishment from maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Cross-species and cross-tissue comparison of AP-1-dependent memory loci using human genetic and epigenomic resources
description: Overlay memory loci with public resources (ENCODE/Roadmap, GTEx, caQTL/eQTL, and AP-1 motif-altering variants) to test whether variants that disrupt AP-1 motifs change chromatin accessibility or response. Check conservation of AP-1-linked memory loci across species and tissues, and test whether they are enriched in chronic-disease GWAS loci such as psoriasis, IBD, or cancer.

question: ap1
title: Primed-versus-naive re-stimulation time course with ATAC/CUT&RUN
description: Stimulate cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) with a transient signal such as TNF, EGF or PMA, rest them for days to weeks, then restimulate and compare to naive cells. Measure chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding by CUT&RUN, H3K27ac, and nascent transcription (PRO-seq/4sU-seq) to see whether AP-1-bound sites stay open and give faster or stronger responses (cost roughly $8–12k).

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the rest phase
description: Use dTAG/auxin-degron or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus or only during the rest period, then restimulate. If memory needs continuous AP-1 occupancy, depletion during rest will erase the primed response. If AP-1 is only needed to establish memory, depletion during rest will not erase it, which separates initiation from maintenance (about $10–15k with existing degron lines or CRISPR knock-in).

question: ap1
title: Site-specific AP-1 motif perturbation and reporter test
description: Use CRISPR to mutate or delete AP-1 motifs, or use dCas9-KRAB/dCas9 blocking, at a few primed enhancers. Test whether memory of accessibility and of gene induction is lost. In parallel, run a lentiviral MPRA or reporter library with wild-type and mutated AP-1 motifs, integrated and chromatinized, to test sufficiency and motif-grammar rules (about $6–10k).

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell imaging of heritability
description: Run 10x multiome (RNA + ATAC) on stimulated, rested and restimulated cells to link AP-1 motif activity (chromVAR) to single-cell memory states. Add a live-cell AP-1 reporter (e.g., a FOS-promoter or AP-1 response element driving destabilized fluorescent protein) and track lineages by time-lapse across divisions to measure how long the state lasts and whether sister cells inherit it, which would indicate bistable or self-sustaining memory (about $12–18k).

question: ap1
title: Reanalysis of public datasets for AP-1 memory signatures
description: Mine existing ATAC, ChIP and RNA-seq data from trained immunity, wound-healing, neuronal activity, and epithelial inflammatory-memory studies. Test whether sites that stay open after stimulus withdrawal are enriched for AP-1 motifs and binding, and whether this predicts faster re-induction. Check for co-occurrence with pioneer factors (e.g., CEBP, ETS) and for histone mark persistence, which gives cheap, cross-system evidence of generality (under $2k compute).

question: ap1
title: Endogenous AP-1 reporter tracking across stimulus-washout-restimulus
description: Knock in fluorescent tags (e.g., c-Fos/JunB-mNeonGreen) or a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter (TRE-driven destabilized fluorescent protein) and image single cells over days through a first stimulus (e.g., EGF, TPA, or TNF), washout, and a second stimulus. Test whether single-cell response amplitude, kinetics and fraction of responders in the second round depend on the first, and how long that history effect lasts (memory decay time).

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 state inheritance through divisions
description: Time-lapse imaging of AP-1 reporter levels in lineages after transient stimulation, quantifying correlation of reporter state between mother, daughter and sister cells over multiple generations. Compare with the correlation expected from shared noise or cell-cycle effects to determine if the AP-1 state is heritable (mitotically stable) and how many divisions it persists.

question: ap1
title: Bistability and hysteresis from dose-ramp imaging
description: Expose cells to ascending and then descending stimulus dose ramps while tracking AP-1 reporter per cell, and plot single-cell dose-response curves for each direction. Bimodal distributions and a hysteresis loop (different thresholds on the up and down ramps) would indicate a self-sustaining, positive-feedback memory state rather than a simple graded response.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse-encoding with live readout of persistence
description: Use optogenetic control of AP-1 activity (e.g., light-inducible c-Jun/c-Fos dimerization or upstream ERK/JNK activation via optoSOS) with varying pulse number, duration and frequency, while imaging a separate AP-1 target reporter and the AP-1 factor itself. Determine whether defined input histories produce persistent output after light off, identifying the input dynamics needed to 'write' memory and whether it requires AP-1 positive autoregulation (c-Jun/FOS promoter feedback).

question: ap1
title: Live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and chromatin accessibility/target locus at single loci
description: Co-image fluorescently tagged AP-1 (e.g., Halo-JunD/c-Fos) with single-molecule tracking for residence time and with live MS2/PP7 nascent transcript reporters on AP-1 target genes, or a chromatin-state live sensor, during primary and secondary stimulation. Test whether prior stimulation lengthens AP-1 binding dwell times, increases burst frequency, or primes loci to respond faster, and whether acute AP-1 degradation (degron tag, imaged) after the first stimulus abolishes the primed response, establishing necessity for memory maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Priming-and-rechallenge time course with chromatin accessibility readout
description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or keratinocytes) to a transient AP-1-activating stimulus such as TPA, EGF, or wounding cues, wash it out, and rechallenge after days to weeks. Compare transcription and ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) in primed versus naive cells to ask whether response magnitude and kinetics persist after AP-1 activity itself has returned to baseline.

question: ap1
title: Longitudinal single-cell multiome tracking of AP-1 motif accessibility and gene expression
description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC-seq (or lineage-barcoded sampling) at multiple times before, during, and long after transient stimulation, and quantify whether FOS/JUN family motif-accessible regions (e.g., ChromVAR scores) stay open in the subset of cells that previously had high AP-1 activity. Linking prior AP-1 dose to later accessibility and responsiveness at single-cell level distinguishes true heritable memory from population heterogeneity.

question: ap1
title: Live-cell reporter imaging of AP-1 dynamics and inheritance across divisions
description: Use cells carrying a knock-in-free, transient or lentiviral-free approach is not needed: instead, apply a non-integrating AP-1 transcriptional reporter or live-cell dyes/antibody-fragment imaging in endogenous cells and track single-cell AP-1 activity through repeated stimulations and cell divisions with lineage reconstruction. Correlating mother and daughter responses and past history with present response tests whether memory is cell-autonomous and mitotically heritable, and whether it depends on pulse frequency or duration.

question: ap1
title: Pharmacological dissection of maintenance mechanisms
description: After priming, apply small-molecule inhibitors at distinct windows, such as JNK/MAPK inhibitors, BAF/SWI-SNF ATPase inhibitors, HDAC/HAT (p300/CBP) inhibitors, or DNA/histone methylation inhibitors, either during priming or only during the memory interval, and then rechallenge. Whether memory is lost when each is applied during establishment versus maintenance reveals if AP-1 binding, continuous signaling, or chromatin changes carry the memory.

question: ap1
title: Genomic footprinting and pioneer-activity profiling in natural in vivo injury/inflammation models
description: Profile cells from tissues after resolved natural perturbations (e.g., skin wounding, inflammation, or aged vs. young tissue) using ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS, and Hi-C or HiChIP, and compare with matched naive tissue. Persistent AP-1 motif footprints, retained enhancer-promoter loops, and faster re-induction of target genes on a second injury, correlated with the motif-containing regions that were opened by the first event, would support AP-1-dependent memory under physiological conditions without genetic manipulation.

question: ap1
title: Drosophila wing disc regeneration: JNK/AP-1 (Fos/Jun) chromatin memory
description: After transient ablation (e.g., eiger or rpr pulse) in Drosophila wing imaginal discs, profile Fos/Jun (Kayak/Jra) binding and chromatin accessibility (CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq) in regenerated tissue versus never-damaged tissue at multiple time points after healing. Then re-injure and test whether the primed enhancers give faster or stronger transcriptional and regenerative responses, and whether acute Fos/Jun knockdown (TARGET/Gal80ts) during the initial injury alone abolishes this priming.

question: ap1
title: Yeast Gcn4/Yap1 (AP-1 homologs) transcriptional memory single-cell lineage tracking
description: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, expose cells to a transient stress (oxidative stress for Yap1, amino-acid starvation for Gcn4), then track reinduction kinetics of fluorescent reporter genes in microfluidic mother-machine lineages over several generations. Compare wild type with AP-1 binding-site mutants, nuclear-retention mutants and chromatin-modifier deletions (e.g., Set1, histone variant H2A.Z) to determine memory duration, heritability and whether the AP-1 factor itself or a chromatin mark carries the memory.

question: ap1
title: Zebrafish fin/heart regeneration enhancer memory with AP-1 motif perturbation
description: Use ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for H3K27ac and Fos/Jun, and single-cell multiome in zebrafish fin or heart across injury, regeneration and repeat injury. Test necessity of AP-1 motifs by CRISPR deletion of injury-responsive enhancers, or by dominant-negative AP-1 (A-Fos) expressed transiently, to see whether lasting accessibility and faster re-response depend on AP-1 at the first injury.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic AP-1 dynamics in Drosophila S2 or zebrafish cells with epigenetic readout
description: Use optogenetic control of Fos/Jun activity or nuclear translocation (e.g., light-inducible Jun) to deliver pulses of defined duration, frequency and amplitude, then wash out and measure persistence of accessibility (single-cell ATAC), enhancer-reporter activity and nascent transcription (live MS2 imaging). Varying input dynamics reveals thresholds for memory formation and whether memory encodes history (dose/frequency) or just prior activation.

question: ap1
title: C. elegans FOS-1/JUN-1 (AP-1) in stress-induced and transgenerational memory
description: Expose C. elegans to transient stress such as wounding, pathogen or heat, and test whether fos-1/jun-1/fos-1 targets show faster or stronger induction upon rechallenge, using auxin-inducible degradation of AP-1 factors only during the first exposure. Combine with tissue-specific ChIP/ATAC-seq and fluorescent reporters over later life stages and subsequent generations, to distinguish somatic from heritable memory and to separate AP-1 requirements for establishment versus maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Transient stimulus then washout: AP-1 binding and accessibility persistence
description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a defined stimulus such as TPA, serum, or LPS, then wash out and run CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN and ATAC-seq at multiple time points (1 h to 14 days). Sites where AP-1 occupancy and accessibility persist after the stimulus and AP-1 protein levels have returned to baseline are candidate memory loci.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 degradation to test maintenance versus initiation
description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degron knock-ins for FOS, JUN or the pioneer-like subunit, and degrade the protein either during stimulation or after memory is established. Compare ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP and RNA-seq to determine whether AP-1 is required only to establish the accessible state or also to maintain it, which is the central criterion that separates a memory mechanism from a one-time trigger.

question: ap1
title: Memory functional assay: primed re-stimulation response
description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, rest them for days to weeks, then re-stimulate and measure the speed and magnitude of transcription (nascent RNA, PRO-seq or 4sU-seq) compared with naive cells. Repeat with AP-1 degron or dominant-negative (A-FOS) perturbation at priming only, to test whether AP-1 is needed to encode the enhanced response.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing across divisions
description: Perform single-cell RNA and ATAC (multiome) on primed and naive cells, with barcode lineage tracing or sister-cell pairing after division, and infer AP-1 motif activity (e.g., chromVAR). Test whether sister cells share accessibility and AP-1 activity states more than random cells do, and whether memory is heritable through mitosis and bimodal versus graded.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and locus-specific causal editing
description: Use live-cell imaging or single-molecule tracking of tagged JUN and FOS, plus CUT&RUN on mitotically arrested cells, to test whether AP-1 stays on chromatin during mitosis. Then use dCas9 or motif mutation (CRISPR editing) at selected memory enhancers to test whether the AP-1 site is necessary for the persistent accessibility and primed response, and use dCas9-KRAB to test sufficiency.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome in previously stimulated vs naive cells
description: Do joint scRNA/scATAC-seq at one time point long after stimulus withdrawal on primed and naive populations. Test whether AP-1 (FOS/JUN) motif accessibility, footprints and target-gene expression stay elevated in primed cells, and whether the primed cells carry a distinct, stable AP-1-linked chromatin state.

question: ap1
title: AP-1 binding and chromatin state profiling (CUT&Tag/ChIP) at memory loci
description: At a single post-stimulus time point, profile JUN/FOS occupancy with H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and accessibility in primed vs naive cells. Test whether AP-1 stays bound at, or leaves behind, latent/primed enhancers, and whether the sites retained correlate with enhanced re-induction of nearby genes.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming, then readout
description: Prime cells, let the stimulus decay, then rapidly deplete AP-1 (dTAG/AID degron of JUN/FOS, or dominant-negative A-FOS) and measure chromatin accessibility and transcription at one later time point versus controls. If the primed state is lost, AP-1 is needed to maintain memory. If it persists, AP-1 only initiates it.

question: ap1
title: Re-stimulation response test with AP-1 perturbation (single endpoint)
description: Give primed and naive cells, with or without AP-1 perturbation during priming only, an identical second stimulus. Measure RNA-seq or a reporter at one fixed time point after it, and compare the magnitude and speed of the response. This separates AP-1's role in establishing memory from its role in executing the response.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell AP-1 protein level/state snapshot with lineage-tracked heritability
description: Use imaging or flow cytometry of endogenous tagged FOS/JUN with an AP-1 reporter in one fixed snapshot of a clonal population, such as sister cells or barcoded clones. Test whether the high and low AP-1 states are shared among related cells beyond chance, which indicates heritable memory. Correlate the states with the history of the stimulus (e.g. a prior pulse) and the downstream targets.

question: ap1
title: Paired longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag of AP-1 occupancy before, during and after stimulus
description: Using serial biopsies or blood-derived cells (e.g., inflamed vs. resolved psoriatic skin, or fibroblasts/keratinocytes from patients), map accessibility, AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and H3K27ac at baseline, during inflammation and after resolution. Persistence of AP-1-motif-containing open sites after the signal is gone, relative to healthy donor controls, would show an AP-1-dependent epigenetic memory.

question: ap1
title: Ex vivo re-challenge of patient primary cells with AP-1 inhibition
description: Isolate cells from patients with prior inflammatory exposure (e.g., synovial fibroblasts from RA patients, or airway basal cells from asthma patients) and from matched healthy donors, rest them in culture, then re-stimulate. Test whether faster or stronger transcriptional recall depends on AP-1 using a small-molecule inhibitor (e.g., T-5224) or dominant-negative FOS (A-FOS), measured by RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) with AP-1 motif activity inference across patient states
description: Perform scRNA/scATAC on patient tissue or blood across disease stages, and compute chromVAR/SCENIC AP-1 activity and footprinting per cell. Test whether a stable AP-1-high subpopulation persists across time points or after treatment, and whether its accessible regions predict relapse or recall gene expression.

question: ap1
title: Pioneer-like AP-1 'bookmarking' during mitosis and across cell divisions in patient-derived cells
description: In patient-derived primary cells or organoids, use CUT&RUN/ChIP-seq on mitotically enriched versus interphase cells and live imaging of endogenous FOS/JUN tagged alleles to determine whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through division. Combining this with lineage-tracing barcodes or clonal expansion would test whether daughter cells inherit the AP-1 state, a core requirement of cellular memory.

question: ap1
title: Linking AP-1 chromatin memory to genetic variants and clinical outcomes in patient cohorts
description: Use patient-derived cells from genotyped cohorts to map chromatin accessibility QTLs and allele-specific AP-1 binding at disease-risk variants lying in AP-1 motifs. Test whether AP-1-dependent memory signatures at these loci (including after therapy withdrawal) correlate with disease relapse, treatment response or sustained gene expression, with CRISPR editing in patient iPSC-derived cells for validation.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking live-imaging and Mitotic ChIP
description: Image endogenously tagged (HaloTag) FOS/JUN with single-molecule tracking in mitotic versus interphase cells, and perform CUT&RUN on FACS-sorted mitotic cells. This tests whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through division, and whether its mitotic retention at specific enhancers predicts which sites reactivate fastest after mitosis.

question: ap1
title: Dwell-time and cooperativity analysis by single-molecule footprinting
description: Use single-molecule footprinting (SMF/Fiber-seq) in primed and naive cells to resolve, on individual DNA molecules, AP-1 motif occupancy together with nucleosome positions and co-bound TFs. This tests whether memory is stored as a stable AP-1-nucleosome-remodeler configuration, or as heterogeneous cell-to-cell occupancy that is quickly lost.

question: ap1
title: Motif-mutant enhancer knock-in with recall reporter
description: Use base or prime editing to mutate AP-1 sites at a few endogenous memory-associated enhancers. Then measure whether priming-induced accessibility and the stronger second transcriptional response are lost at those loci specifically. This gives a cis-acting, locus-level causal test that is independent of global AP-1 knockdown, and it separates the memory role from AP-1's role in normal gene activation.

question: ap1
title: Dosage and dynamics encoding with optogenetic pulse patterns
description: Drive endogenous AP-1 or its upstream kinases (e.g. optogenetic ERK/JNK) with pulses of different duration, frequency and amplitude. Then quantify how each pulse pattern maps to lasting accessibility and to the response to rechallenge. This tests whether memory is a thresholded or integrating function of AP-1 history, which a simple on/off priming design cannot reveal.

question: ap1
title: Competition between AP-1 family members and pioneer-factor swap
description: Perform paired, time-resolved CUT&Tag for different FOS/JUN paralogs (e.g. FOSL1, JUNB, ATF3) and for pioneer or lineage factors during priming and during memory. Combine this with paralog-specific degradation to ask whether memory is carried by a specific AP-1 composition, or is handed off to a lineage TF that maintains the sites after AP-1 is gone. This would distinguish AP-1 as an initiator from AP-1 as a maintainer.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse-frequency encoding of memory
description: Use optogenetically controlled FOS/JUN (or light-gated dimerization) to deliver identical total AP-1 dose with different pulse durations and frequencies, then measure persistent accessibility and recall after washout. This tests whether memory is encoded by AP-1 dynamics (transient vs sustained) rather than mere presence, and defines a threshold for memory writing.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 memory without the native stimulus
description: Express a drug-inducible, AP-1-only synthetic activator (e.g., constitutively active JUN/FOS fusion, pulsed and then removed) in naive cells and ask whether it alone reproduces the primed accessibility and recall response of the natural stimulus. A sufficiency test like this separates AP-1 as a memory writer from other signaling arms such as NF-κB, MAPK or STAT that normally co-activate.

question: ap1
title: Nucleosome-resolved single-molecule footprinting at memory loci
description: Use Fiber-seq or SMF/NOMe-seq on primed versus naive cells to read nucleosome positions and TF occupancy on single DNA molecules at AP-1 sites after washout. This shows whether memory is a stable open state in a subpopulation of alleles (bimodal, heritable) or a graded shift, and whether AP-1 is still bound or has left behind a remodeled nucleosome.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific memory in hybrid cells with a single mutated AP-1 site
description: In F1 hybrid or heterozygous cells, mutate the AP-1 motif on one allele and track allele-specific accessibility, H3K27ac and nascent RNA through priming, washout, and restimulation. Two alleles in the same nucleus share trans factors, so any difference in memory is cis-encoded at the AP-1 site rather than due to a global cell state.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and replication-coupled retention assay
description: Combine CUT&Tag or live imaging of FOS/JUN on mitotic chromosomes with synchronization, EdU-based replication-timing and cell-cycle arrest experiments to test whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through mitosis. Comparing memory persistence in cells forced through division with that in arrested non-dividing cells shows whether memory depends on propagation across divisions or on persistent chromatin state.

question: ap1
title: Pioneer-like occupancy vs. motif-independent persistence via nucleosome phasing footprinting
description: Use single-molecule footprinting (e.g., Fiber-seq or SMF/NOMe-seq) before, after, and long after stimulus to resolve whether AP-1-dependent loci retain remodeled nucleosome arrays and co-occupancy on the same DNA molecules after AP-1 leaves. Molecule-level bimodality of retained remodeled fibers, without AP-1 binding, would distinguish a chromatin-encoded memory from continued AP-1 occupancy.

question: ap1
title: Memory carried by AP-1 protein/mRNA levels vs. chromatin: nuclear transplant or cell-fusion test
description: Fuse primed cells with naive cells (heterokaryons, with species-polymorphic SNPs to assign alleles) or transfer primed nuclei into naive cytoplasm, then ask whether primed enhancers stay open in cis while naive-derived ones remain closed. Cis-restricted persistence argues for a chromatin-based memory, while trans-spreading implicates diffusible factors such as AP-1 levels or feed-forward loops.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific memory with a single-allele AP-1 site switch
description: In F1 hybrid cells (or heterozygous knock-in lines) with a motif mutation on only one allele, track allele-specific ATAC, H3K27ac, and nascent RNA after stimulus and rest to test if priming is cis-encoded. A retained primed state only on the intact allele within a shared nuclear environment shows that memory is locally written rather than set by global signaling state.

question: ap1
title: Quantitative AP-1 dynamics decoding via live-cell reporters and optogenetic pulse-train design
description: Use endogenously tagged FOS/JUN with a live-cell reporter and an optogenetic upstream kinase or AP-1 activator to deliver pulses with varied amplitude, duration, and frequency, then measure the later response of a memory reporter at the same cells. Identifying a threshold, frequency dependence, or hysteresis (path-dependent response to the same input) would test for bistable memory and distinguish it from simple lingering signaling.

question: ap1
title: Competition with the memory: mapping AP-1 paralog switching and BAF/ATF/CEBP handoff in a CRISPR-barcoded cofactor screen
description: Run a pooled CRISPR screen (with a memory-reporter readout like a sorted primed-enhancer-driven fluorescent reporter) after the washout period, targeting AP-1 family members, chromatin remodelers, histone modifiers, and partner TFs. Genes whose loss specifically erases maintenance (not initial response) and the paralog composition of AP-1 dimers identified by re-ChIP or Co-IP at late time points would reveal what mechanism actually holds the memory.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule footprinting of AP-1 site occupancy vs. accessibility
description: Use SMF/Fiber-seq (or NOMe-seq) on primed and naive cells after washout to determine whether memory sites retain nucleosome-depleted, TF-bound molecules, or whether they are accessible but unoccupied (a 'scar'). Coupling this with motif-mutated alleles tests whether residual accessibility is maintained by AP-1 itself or by successor factors.

question: ap1
title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking (ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN)
description: Expose cells to a brief pulse of a stimulus (e.g., serum, TNF, or injury) that activates AP-1 (FOS/JUN), then wash it out and profile accessibility and AP-1 binding by ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN at days to weeks. Persistence of AP-1-motif-containing open regions, like a 'spookology' of ghost marks left after the stimulus is gone, would show a lasting memory footprint. Naive and pulsed cells give the baseline comparison.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 degradation at defined times (degron, dominant-negative A-FOS)
description: Use a degron-tagged JUN/FOS or inducible A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during the stimulus, or after the stimulus has ended. If accessibility and faster re-induction persist after post-stimulus AP-1 loss, the memory is self-sustained by chromatin. If they decay, AP-1 is continuously required to maintain it. Comparing the two timings separates initiation from maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Priming and re-stimulation transcriptional response assay
description: Give two stimulus pulses separated by a rest interval of varying length, and measure nascent transcription (PRO-seq or EU-seq) and target-gene RNA after the second pulse. Faster or stronger induction in primed cells than in naive cells, at AP-1 target genes only, would indicate memory. The decay time of this enhanced response quantifies memory duration. AP-1 knockdown before priming tests necessity.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome and live reporter lineage tracing
description: Combine single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing with live-cell imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter (or endogenous tagged FOS) across cell divisions. Track whether daughter cells inherit the primed state, which would show mitotic heritability. Use the data to ask whether memory is a bistable, all-or-none state or a graded one, and to find cell-to-cell variability in it.

question: ap1
title: Sufficiency test by targeted AP-1 recruitment plus histone/DNA-methylation readouts
description: Recruit JUN or FOS to a synthetic reporter or a chosen enhancer with dCas9 or a Gal4 system for a limited time, then release it and watch the reporter over many cell divisions. Pair this with ChIP or CUT&Tag for H3K27ac and H3K4me1 and with methylation profiling, and test cooperation with the SWI/SNF (BAF) complex using a BRG1 inhibitor. Persistent activity and marks after release would show that AP-1 alone is sufficient to set a memory state. A lack of persistence would show that it is not.

question: ap1
title: Heritability of AP-1 state across clonal lineages
description: Use live-cell reporters of AP-1 activity (e.g., TRE-driven fluorescent protein) with long-term imaging and cell tracking to quantify mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations in reporter level, fitting the decay of correlation with generation number to estimate a memory half-life. Pair this with single-cell RNA/ATAC profiling of sorted high- and low-reporter cells to confirm that the imaging readout reflects a broader transcriptional state.

question: ap1
title: Transient stimulation plus timed AP-1 removal
description: Deliver a brief stimulus that activates AP-1 (cytokine, drug pulse, matrix stiffening, or scratch wound), then use degron-tagged FOS/JUN family proteins to eliminate AP-1 either during the stimulus or only after it has subsided, and ask which window is required for the persistent downstream phenotype. If AP-1 is needed only transiently to establish a state that then persists in its absence, that favors an initiator role; if continued presence is required, it acts as a self-sustaining maintenance circuit.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin footprint persistence after signal withdrawal
description: Run time-course ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors, and histone modification profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) across stimulation and a long washout, testing whether AP-1-motif-containing enhancers opened during stimulation remain accessible and primed long after AP-1 occupancy and target transcription have returned to baseline. Latent, still-open enhancers that reactivate faster upon restimulation would be direct evidence of a stored chromatin trace.

question: ap1
title: Restimulation kinetics as a memory assay
description: Compare naive cells with cells that experienced a prior stimulus days or weeks earlier, measuring the speed, amplitude, and dose threshold of AP-1 target induction on a second exposure using nascent transcription readouts. Faster or stronger secondary responses that scale with the chromatin changes above would operationalize memory as an altered input-output relationship rather than a static expression difference.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic perturbation of the AP-1 feedback loop
description: Use CRISPRa/CRISPRi or inducible expression to force AP-1 activity on or off for a defined window in otherwise unstimulated cells, then follow whether the induced state persists after the perturbation ends and whether mutating AP-1 binding sites at key self-reinforcing loci (including FOS/JUN autoregulatory enhancers) abolishes persistence. This tests sufficiency and identifies the specific cis-elements that store the state.

question: ap1
title: Stimulus washout time course of AP-1 occupancy versus chromatin state
description: Deliver a defined transient stimulus (growth factor, cytokine, or drug pulse), then profile AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN family members), chromatin accessibility, and target gene expression at densely sampled time points after washout. Memory is supported if enhancer accessibility and transcriptional output outlast both the stimulus and the AP-1 protein burst itself.

question: ap1
title: Heritability of AP-1 state measured through clonal lineage tracing
description: Use expressed DNA barcodes combined with single-cell RNA and ATAC profiling to ask whether cells sharing a recent ancestor also share high or low AP-1 target activity. Quantifying how barcode identity predicts AP-1 state as a function of generations elapsed gives a direct estimate of the memory half-life in divisions rather than hours.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron removal of AP-1 subunits after a state is established
description: Knock degron tags into endogenous FOS, FOSL1, and JUN loci so the proteins can be eliminated within minutes at chosen times. Comparing degradation during stimulation versus long after it reveals whether AP-1 is required only to write the state or must be continuously present to maintain it, which distinguishes a true memory element from a persistent signaling readout.

question: ap1
title: Second-stimulus challenge to test for priming and faster reactivation
description: Expose cells to one pulse, allow a long recovery, then re-stimulate and measure response speed, amplitude, and fraction of responding cells relative to naive controls. A faster or larger response in previously exposed cells, tracked alongside AP-1 motif accessibility at the responsive enhancers, is the functional behavioral assay for memory.

question: ap1
title: Live single-cell reporters linking AP-1 dynamics to downstream fate
description: Build knock-in fluorescent reporters for an AP-1 subunit and for a downstream target gene, then image individual cells continuously through and beyond a stimulus while tracking lineage relationships. This directly tests whether transient differences in AP-1 activity at the moment of stimulation predict divergent long-term states in daughter cells, and whether that prediction decays over time.

question: ap1
title: Clonal heritability of AP-1 activity
description: Expand single-cell-derived clones carrying an AP-1 transcriptional reporter and heritable barcodes, then compare between-clone versus within-clone variance in reporter level and AP-1 motif accessibility. Fit decay of clonal correlation versus division number to estimate a memory half-life and test it against protein-dilution expectations.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase perturbation with washout
description: Transiently induce AP-1 with a degron-tagged or optogenetic FOS/JUN construct (or suppress it with A-FOS), then withdraw the perturbation and track accessibility, expression, and phenotype for weeks. A state that outlives the pulse argues AP-1 writes memory; collapse on washout argues it only maintains an ongoing state.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 removal in cells that already remember
description: Apply rapid degradation of AP-1 subunits in cells already in a primed state, such as drug-tolerant persisters or previously stimulated cells. Ask whether memory-associated enhancer accessibility, H3K27ac, and the enhanced recall response are lost, separating continuous occupancy from a self-sustaining chromatin mark.

question: ap1
title: Re-stimulation kinetics as the functional readout
description: Prime cells, allow the primary response to resolve, then re-stimulate and measure response latency, amplitude, and responding-cell fraction by live imaging or time-resolved sequencing. Memory predicts faster or larger secondary induction specifically at AP-1-bound loci, which should vanish when AP-1 sites are mutated.

question: ap1
title: Motif-resolution causal mapping at candidate memory enhancers
description: Use base or prime editing to disrupt individual AP-1 motifs at enhancers that remain open after the signal ends, with scrambled and neighboring-motif controls. If these motifs store the memory, editing should abolish retained accessibility and the primed response while leaving the acute primary response intact.

question: ap1
title: Barcoded lineage tracing across a state transition
description: Use clonal DNA barcodes to split sister cells, measuring AP-1 motif accessibility or FOS/JUN levels in one half and challenging the other half with a stimulus such as a drug or differentiation cue. Ask whether the pre-measured AP-1 state predicts the clone's eventual fate, the core test of a heritable, predictive memory.

question: ap1
title: Degron-based timed removal separating establishment from maintenance
description: Tag c-JUN/c-FOS with an auxin or dTAG degron (or express dominant-negative A-FOS) and deplete AP-1 either during a priming stimulus or only after it ends. Memory requires that post-stimulus depletion erases the primed response even though the initiating signal is already gone.

question: ap1
title: Direct measurement of persistence and heritability timescales
description: Track an endogenous AP-1 reporter such as a knock-in FOS-HaloTag or AP-1 motif-driven fluorophore by live imaging across many divisions. Extract state autocorrelation times, mother-daughter correlations, and switching rates to distinguish true multigenerational memory from slow protein turnover.

question: ap1
title: Decoupling AP-1 binding from chromatin accessibility
description: Perform paired ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS before, during, and long after stimulation to test whether stimulus-opened enhancers remain accessible after AP-1 unbinds. This asks whether AP-1 acts as a pioneer factor that writes a latent chromatin memory read out upon restimulation.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic write/erase perturbation of specific AP-1 enhancers
description: Use dCas9-VPR or targeted recruitment of JUN to a defined set of AP-1-bound enhancers, plus CRISPRi or deletion to remove them. Test whether transiently imposing the AP-1 state suffices to install a long-lived primed phenotype and whether erasing those elements abolishes memory of prior exposure.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron depletion staged across a pulse-chase
description: Tag FOS/JUN family members with an auxin or dTAG degron and deplete AP-1 either during a transient stimulus or only after it has been withdrawn, then assay whether the stimulus-induced state persists. This separates a role for AP-1 in establishing a state from a requirement for continuous AP-1 activity to maintain it, which is the core claim of a memory mechanism.

question: ap1
title: Heritability of AP-1 activity across cell divisions by live imaging
description: Build a fluorescent AP-1 (TRE) transcriptional reporter plus an endogenous JUN/FOS protein tag, and track individual cells through several divisions to compute mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations and the autocorrelation half-life of AP-1 activity. Memory predicts correlations that persist well beyond the protein and mRNA turnover timescale and are transmitted through mitosis.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin priming and re-stimulation kinetics at AP-1 motifs
description: Perform time-resolved ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and footprinting after stimulus withdrawal to identify regions that stay accessible without ongoing signaling, then re-challenge cells and ask whether those primed, AP-1-motif-containing enhancers are the ones that reactivate faster or more strongly. Causality can be tested by CRISPRi or base-editing the AP-1 motifs in the retained peaks.

question: ap1
title: Lineage barcoding to link prior AP-1 state to later cell fate
description: Barcode cells, sort or record high- versus low-AP-1 cells using a reporter at an early timepoint, and then assay the fate of their barcode-matched descendants (e.g., drug survival, differentiation, invasion) days to weeks later. A memory mechanism predicts that early AP-1 state predicts clonally concordant later outcomes, and that perturbing AP-1 in the interim erases that predictive power.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis and feedback test with a tunable synthetic AP-1 circuit
description: Drive AP-1 activity with a dose-tunable inducible FOS/JUN construct and measure the output while ramping the input up and then back down, looking for bistability and hysteresis rather than a single dose-response curve. Pair this with mapping AP-1 binding at its own and its partners' loci to test whether an autoregulatory positive-feedback loop, the simplest molecular basis for such memory, is actually wired in the cell type of interest.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase perturbation: does the state outlive the trigger?
description: Deliver a transient AP-1 stimulus (drug or cytokine pulse, or optogenetic/degron-controlled FOS/JUN induction), withdraw it, and then track AP-1 target accessibility (ATAC-seq) and transcription (RNA FISH, scRNA-seq) over days to weeks. A genuine memory mechanism should show target-state persistence long after AP-1 protein returns to baseline, and the gap between chromatin and transcript decay reveals which layer stores the information.

question: ap1
title: Lineage barcoding to measure heritability across divisions
description: Barcode cells, let clones expand, then split sister cells and profile them with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or MemorySeq-style enrichment for slow-fluctuating genes). Quantifying how much more similar AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target expression are within clones than between them yields a direct estimate of how many generations the state is inherited.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 removal at defined times after state establishment
description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on c-Jun/c-Fos (or a dominant-negative A-Fos) to strip AP-1 either during state establishment or only after the state is already set, and compare outcomes. If AP-1 is required to write but not to read the memory, late degradation should leave the accessible/primed state and its phenotype largely intact.

question: ap1
title: Re-stimulation kinetics as a functional memory assay
description: Give cells a first stimulus, allow full recovery, then re-stimulate after varying intervals and measure the speed and amplitude of AP-1 target induction and of the downstream phenotype (e.g., drug tolerance, migration, differentiation competence). Faster or stronger secondary responses that decay with rest interval, and that are abolished by AP-1 loss during the first exposure, are the hallmark of a trained/primed memory.

question: ap1
title: Mapping what physically holds the mark at AP-1 sites
description: At AP-1-bound enhancers that stay open after the stimulus, profile the candidate storage layers in parallel: histone modifications (H3K4me1/H3K27ac CUT&RUN), nucleosome positioning, DNA methylation, pioneer-factor and BRD4/cohesin occupancy, and enhancer-promoter contacts (Micro-C). Then test causality by targeting erasers or writers (dCas9-LSD1, dCas9-p300) to those specific sites to see which perturbation wipes or installs the memory.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase of AP-1 activity with clonal lineage tracing
description: Transiently induce AP-1 (e.g., optogenetic or degron-controlled FOS/JUN, or a brief TPA pulse), then follow barcoded clones by single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq across many divisions. This directly measures how long an AP-1-opened chromatin and expression state persists after the inducing signal is gone, and whether persistence is heritable within clones.

question: ap1
title: Priming assay: does a prior AP-1 pulse change the response to a later stimulus?
description: Give cells a first AP-1-activating stimulus, wash out and rest for days to weeks, then rechallenge and compare response magnitude, speed, and gene set to naive cells. A memory mechanism predicts faster/stronger reactivation at previously bound loci, which can be mapped by comparing ATAC/CUT&RUN peaks before, between, and after the two stimuli.

question: ap1
title: Loss-of-function during the memory window versus during encoding
description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron to deplete FOS/JUN either only during the initial stimulus (encoding) or only during the rest period (maintenance), then test whether the primed state survives. This separates AP-1's role as an initiator of a state from a continuously required maintainer, which is the crux of calling it a memory mechanism.

question: ap1
title: Quantify mitotic transmission: AP-1 bookmarking and post-division state recovery
description: Combine live imaging of tagged JUN/FOS through mitosis with mitotic chromatin profiling (e.g., CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic cells) and sister-cell comparisons of expression after division. Concordance between sister cells beyond what noise predicts, plus retention of AP-1 at mitotic chromatin, would support heritable rather than merely slow-decaying memory.

question: ap1
title: Perturb AP-1 motif content at specific enhancers and test state stability
description: Use base editing or prime editing to delete or add TRE/CRE motifs at candidate memory enhancers, then measure whether the primed/persistent transcriptional state is lost or gained at those loci. Pair with a synthetic reporter carrying a tunable number of AP-1 sites to ask how motif density maps onto duration of state retention.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase stimulation with time-resolved AP-1 and chromatin readouts
description: Deliver a transient stimulus (e.g., a brief cytokine, growth-factor, or drug pulse), wash it out, and then track AP-1 protein levels, AP-1 motif accessibility (ATAC-seq), and target-gene expression over many days. Memory is supported if accessibility at AP-1-bound enhancers and the primed transcriptional response persist long after the AP-1 proteins themselves and the original signal have decayed.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 state heritability
description: Use expressed DNA barcodes (e.g., Rewind/Watermelon-style clone tracking) combined with single-cell RNA-seq or a live AP-1 reporter to ask whether sister cells and clonal descendants share AP-1 activity levels. Quantifying how the correlation of AP-1 state between relatives decays with generations gives a direct measurement of the memory timescale and whether it is heritable versus transient.

question: ap1
title: Degron-based acute removal to separate maintenance from establishment
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with an auxin or dTAG degron so AP-1 can be eliminated acutely at chosen times: before, during, or long after a priming stimulus. If removal after priming erases the retained accessibility and the faster/stronger secondary response, AP-1 is actively maintaining the memory rather than merely establishing it.

question: ap1
title: Restimulation challenge assays quantifying the memory benefit
description: Compare naive versus previously primed cells in a second challenge (same stimulus, a different stimulus, or a drug-resistance assay) and measure response latency, amplitude, fraction of responding cells, and cell-fate outcome. A genuine memory mechanism should produce a quantitatively faster or larger response that scales with prior AP-1 activation and is abolished by AP-1 perturbation.

question: ap1
title: Targeted AP-1 writing and erasing at specific enhancers
description: Use dCas9-fused AP-1 activation domains or dominant-negative A-FOS/engineered motif deletions at candidate enhancers to install or remove AP-1 occupancy in the absence of any stimulus. Sufficiency (synthetic AP-1 recruitment alone creates a long-lived primed state) plus necessity (motif deletion blocks memory at that locus but not globally) is the strongest causal test, and pairing it with CUT&RUN for cofactors and histone marks reveals the molecular carrier of the memory.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis loops (from magnetism)
description: Slowly ramp a stimulus such as TGF-β, a drug, or serum up to a peak and back down. At each step, measure AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN), AP-1 motif accessibility (ATAC) and target expression in single cells. If AP-1 holds a memory, the up and down paths will differ, and AP-1 knockdown should shrink the area between them (loop area) more than it changes the response at steady state.

question: ap1
title: Volatile vs. non-volatile storage test (from computer RAM)
description: Prime cells, then acutely degrade AP-1 subunits with degron-tagged FOS/JUN/FOSL (dTAG or AID) during the post-stimulus 'storage' window and restore them before re-challenge. If the memory survives removal during storage, AP-1 only reads the memory out. If it is lost, AP-1 is needed to keep the memory going, like RAM that needs constant refreshing.

question: ap1
title: Kinship-correlation decay (from twin and pedigree studies)
description: Use lineage barcoding (e.g., Rewind or clonal scRNA/ATAC) to measure how strongly sisters, cousins and second cousins agree on AP-1 target accessibility after a transient stimulus. Fit the drop in correlation per generation to get a memory half-life in cell divisions, and compare it with lines where the AP-1 motifs are mutated or AP-1 is inhibited.

question: ap1
title: Bits of memory (from information theory)
description: Expose cells to random combinations of past stimulus histories, then use single-cell multiome to estimate the mutual information between each cell's history and its current state. Divide that information into the part carried by AP-1 motif accessibility and the part that is not, and test how much is lost with AP-1 perturbation.

question: ap1
title: Annealing schedules and locus-level bit-flips (from metallurgy and hard drives)
description: After priming, apply defined 'annealing' treatments (passage time, forced divisions, HDAC or BAF inhibitors) to find what erases faster re-induction on a second challenge. Then use base editing on single AP-1 sites at the remembered enhancers to test whether destroying one site removes the memory only at that locus.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis loop mapping (ferromagnetism)
description: Ramp a stimulus (serum, TGF-beta, or a MAPK inhibitor) up in fine dose steps and then back down, measuring AP-1 factor levels, AP-1 motif accessibility, and target gene output at each step by single-cell ATAC/RNA. A reproducible open loop between the ascending and descending branches, which collapses when AP-1 is acutely degraded with dTAG-FOS/JUN at a matched point on each branch, is the signature of AP-1-maintained bistable memory rather than slow relaxation.

question: ap1
title: Heritability partitioning across lineage trees (quantitative genetics)
description: Combine live imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter with expressed lineage barcodes so that each cell's state can be placed on a family tree, then compute intraclass correlation of AP-1 activity and of AP-1-dependent target expression between sisters, cousins, and increasingly distant relatives. Fitting the decay of kinship correlation with generation number gives a quantitative memory half-life in cell divisions, and the analysis can be repeated under AP-1 degradation to ask whether AP-1 is the carrier or merely a correlate of the inherited state.

question: ap1
title: Mutual information between stimulus history and present state (information theory)
description: Expose cells to randomized sequences of stimulus pulses, then at a later readout time estimate the mutual information, in bits, between the past pulse sequence and current single-cell AP-1 occupancy, chromatin accessibility, and transcriptome. Memory is quantified as information about the past that survives after the stimulus is gone, and the causal claim is tested by showing that this bit count drops sharply when AP-1 is degraded during the silent interval but not when an unrelated abundant factor is degraded.

question: ap1
title: Frequency-response and step-response profiling with optogenetic AP-1 (control engineering)
description: Use a light-controlled AP-1 (optogenetic FOS/JUN dimer or LOV-caged degron) to deliver pulse trains spanning a wide range of frequencies and duty cycles while holding total AP-1 dose constant, and record downstream enhancer accessibility and gene output. Building an effective Bode plot, with a low-pass characteristic plus persistence of output long after input ceases, distinguishes a true integrator-with-memory from a system that simply tracks its input, and the measured time constants predict responses to novel input waveforms.

question: ap1
title: Molecular stratigraphy with a DNA recorder (archaeology)
description: Place a CRISPR base-editing or recombinase-based recorder under an AP-1-responsive promoter so that each episode of AP-1 activity leaves a dated, cumulative edit layer in the genome, then read the recorded history and the current chromatin and expression state from the very same single cell. This directly tests whether cells carrying a deeper record of past AP-1 activity retain a distinguishable present-day state, converting a correlational claim about memory into a within-cell comparison of past and present.

question: ap1
title: Memory-kernel system identification (borrowed from control engineering)
description: Drive the pathway with optogenetically delivered, precisely patterned input sequences (varying pulse amplitude, duration, interval, and frequency, including pseudo-random m-sequences) while live-imaging a FOS/JUN translocation reporter and an AP-1-driven transcriptional reporter, then fit a Volterra/linear-nonlinear model to extract the system's memory kernel. A genuine memory element shows a kernel with a long tail and history-dependent gain that disappears when AP-1 dimerization is blocked, whereas a pure relay shows a short, stimulus-locked kernel.

question: ap1
title: Channel-capacity accounting of stored stimulus history (borrowed from information theory)
description: Expose cells to a defined library of past stimulus histories, then after a long washout quantify, cell by cell, the mutual information between which history a cell experienced and its current AP-1 occupancy, AP-1 motif accessibility, and target transcript counts. This yields an explicit number of bits of past experience retained, a decay-rate curve for those bits over time and divisions, and a direct test of how much of the retained information is lost when AP-1 components are degraded during the washout.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell divergence clocks (borrowed from plasmid segregation genetics)
description: Use live lineage-tracking microscopy plus endpoint single-cell multiome on microdissected sibling pairs to measure how the similarity in AP-1 state between sisters, cousins, and second cousins decays with generational distance after a transient stimulus. Comparing the measured decay constant against a null model of random molecular partitioning at mitosis distinguishes actively maintained, heritable AP-1 states from passive dilution of leftover protein.

question: ap1
title: Event-recorder timestamping of past AP-1 activity (borrowed from flight data recorders)
description: Place a base-editing or recombinase-based DNA writer under an AP-1-responsive promoter so that every episode of AP-1 activity is permanently inscribed into a genomic barcode, with recording windows gated by an inducible component. Sequencing the barcode alongside the cell's current phenotype directly tests whether a cell's documented AP-1 history, as opposed to its present AP-1 level, predicts later behavior such as drug tolerance or differentiation bias.

question: ap1
title: Write/erase/overwrite addressing test (borrowed from read-write storage devices)
description: Treat AP-1 as a memory register and test each storage operation separately: write by pulsing exogenous FOS/JUN alone with no upstream stimulus, read by assaying target output after full decay of the pulse, erase by targeted degron-mediated removal or dCas9-based site-specific displacement of AP-1 at defined enhancers, and overwrite by writing a competing dimer such as a different bZIP partner. Memory is supported only if writing is sufficient without the original stimulus and erasing at specific loci selectively deletes the corresponding stored response.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis loop mapping (ferromagnetism / materials science)
description: Ramp a stimulus such as TGF-beta, serum, or a drug up in graded steps and then back down, measuring AP-1 target accessibility and reporter output in single cells at each step. A split between the ascending and descending branches is the signature of history dependence; test AP-1 dependence by attempting to collapse the loop with A-Fos or a FOS/JUN degron.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded pedigree tracking (population genetics / heritability estimation)
description: Use clonal barcoding plus single-cell ATAC and RNA to compute the heritability of AP-1 site accessibility across cell divisions and sister-cell pairs, partitioning variance into clone-of-origin versus noise. Formal heritability and decay-half-life-across-generations statistics convert a vague memory claim into an estimated persistence timescale.

question: ap1
title: Write/erase/read latency benchmarking (computer memory engineering)
description: Treat the AP-1 site as a storage device by delivering pulsed optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization of defined amplitude and duration, then assaying retention time, minimum write duration, and the recall advantage on a second stimulus. Plotting retention versus write parameters distinguishes a bistable latch from a leaky capacitor or a pure relay.

question: ap1
title: Savings paradigm at the moment of recall (Ebbinghaus memory psychology)
