description: Psychological memory is measured by faster relearning rather than spontaneous recall, so prime cells, wait until the transcriptional response fully returns to baseline, then re-stimulate and measure response latency and amplitude. Degrading AP-1 selectively during the silent interval versus during recall separates AP-1 as the stored trace from AP-1 as the readout machinery.

question: ap1
title: Serial passaging as an epidemiological cohort (survival analysis)
description: Follow single-cell-derived clones with differing initial AP-1 activity as a longitudinal cohort, using Cox proportional-hazards models in which the event is loss of the primed phenotype such as drug tolerance or accessibility state. Covariates like AP-1 motif occupancy, partner TF identity, and CpG methylation reveal which features predict durable versus transient memory.

question: ap1
title: Measure how much information AP-1 carries about past stimuli (from information theory)
description: Expose cells to several defined stimulus histories, then use single-cell multiome to estimate the mutual information between each history and the cell's present state, with and without conditioning on AP-1 footprint and activity. If AP-1 is the memory, it should account for nearly all of the history information, so conditioning on it should leave almost none.

question: ap1
title: Compare memory half-life with AP-1 half-lives (from radioactive decay)
description: Using pulse-chase designs, measure how fast the primed response fades after a single stimulus. Compare that rate with the half-lives of FOS/JUN proteins (e.g., HaloTag pulse-chase) and of AP-1 chromatin occupancy (CUT&Tag time courses). If the memory lasts much longer than both, AP-1 is more likely to start the memory than to store it.

question: ap1
title: Test whether AP-1 is enough to create memory (from epidemiology's Bradford Hill criteria)
description: Address sufficiency, a test that observational correlation can't answer. Use a dCas9 fusion, or a chemically induced AP-1 recruitment system, to tether AP-1 at chosen enhancers for a short time without any stimulus, then release it. Afterwards, check whether those loci stay accessible and respond more strongly to a later challenge.

question: ap1
title: Check whether memory moves between cells or stays on the chromatin (from organ transplantation)
description: Fuse primed cells with naive cells to form heterokaryons, or move nuclei into enucleated cytoplasts, and use species- or allele-specific readouts. If the memory moves to the naive nucleus, it is carried by a diffusible factor such as AP-1 protein. If it stays with the primed chromatin, it is stored in the chromatin itself (cis).

question: ap1
title: Test whether stimulus order matters (from path dependence in economics)
description: Give cells stimulus A then B, or B then A, with matched total exposure, and measure end states and how they later respond to a drug. Then test whether the effect of order disappears when AP-1 is inhibited, or can be predicted from AP-1 footprints left by the first stimulus.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis loops, borrowed from ferromagnetism
description: Slowly ramp a stimulus (e.g., TPA, EGF, or drug dose) up and then back down. At each step, measure single-cell AP-1 activity with a live reporter, plus AP-1 motif accessibility with scATAC. If the downward path does not retrace the upward path (an open hysteresis loop, with a width that persists over time), the system has memory; if AP-1 motifs are knocked out, that memory should disappear.

question: ap1
title: Write vs. refresh test, modeled on DRAM
description: In computer DRAM, stored data fades unless it is periodically refreshed. By analogy, use an inducible degron (dTAG-FOS/JUN or a dominant-negative A-FOS) to remove AP-1 at different times after a transient stimulus. Then measure whether chromatin accessibility and the faster re-response persist. This tells you whether AP-1 only writes the memory (it survives removal) or must keep refreshing it (it decays with a measurable time constant).

question: ap1
title: Twin-study heritability with lineage barcodes
description: Borrowing heritability estimation from quantitative genetics, use lineage barcoding (e.g., Rewind or ClonMapper) to track sister and cousin cells across several divisions after a stimulus. Then calculate how strongly AP-1 target accessibility and expression correlate within each lineage. If the correlation within clones decays slowly across generations, and does so more slowly than for non-AP-1 programs, that is evidence AP-1 carries a state that cells inherit.

question: ap1
title: Measuring the system's response to pulses, as in signal processing
description: Use optogenetic ERK/RAS control or microfluidics to deliver pulse trains that vary in frequency, duration, and spacing. Then fit linear and nonlinear transfer-function models to AP-1 reporter dynamics and downstream enhancer opening. If the fitted decay time constant is much longer than the turnover of AP-1 protein and mRNA, the memory sits downstream of AP-1 (e.g., in chromatin), not in AP-1 levels themselves.

question: ap1
title: Prime-boost recall test with edited AP-1 motifs, borrowed from vaccination
description: Prime cells, let them rest until AP-1 levels return to baseline, then challenge them again and measure how fast and how strongly AP-1 target genes respond, including in contexts such as drug-resistance priming. Repeat this in lines where base editing has destroyed the AP-1 motifs at specific memory enhancers. Losing the faster, stronger second response without changing the first response would show that the memory is carried at those AP-1 sites.

question: ap1
title: Twin-study heritability (behavioral genetics) via lineage barcoding
description: Use barcode lineage tracing to find sister and cousin cells, then measure how similar related cells are in AP-1 activity (FOS/JUN RNA FISH and AP-1 motif accessibility) and in their later response to a stimulus, across several generations. If AP-1 carries memory, its similarity between relatives should decay at the same rate as the similarity in response, and this shared heritability should disappear when AP-1 is knocked down.

question: ap1
title: Channel capacity (information theory): how much past information is retained
description: Expose cells to defined stimulus histories, remove the stimulus, and wait varying times. Then calculate the mutual information between the past history and the present single-cell state (scATAC/scRNA) at AP-1 targets versus non-AP-1 loci. Test whether AP-1 inhibition lowers the number of bits retained or makes the information fade faster.

question: ap1
title: Radiocarbon dating: an AP-1 chromatin clock for elapsed time
description: Collect a time series after the stimulus is removed and train a model that predicts the time since stimulation from AP-1-bound enhancer accessibility and histone marks, much as decaying isotopes are used to date objects. If AP-1 chromatin features predict elapsed time much better than transcripts do, AP-1 is a persistent record of the past.

question: ap1
title: Non-commutativity (algebra): does stimulus order matter?
description: Treat cells with two signals in the order A-then-B and B-then-A, using equal doses and equal total exposure. Measure the final transcriptional and phenotypic state. A memory mechanism predicts the order will matter, so test whether the order effect lines up with AP-1 dimer composition and goes away when the AP-1 family is blocked.

question: ap1
title: Metal fatigue (Miner's rule): accumulating weak signals
description: Give cells repeated stimulus pulses that are each too weak to trigger a response, at different spacings. Test whether AP-1 occupancy and accessibility build up step by step until the cells reach a persistent state, and whether the summed AP-1 signal predicts when the switch happens. This would show AP-1 integrating and storing past exposure.

question: ap1
title: Forgetting curves and the spacing effect (borrowed from learning psychology)
description: Adapt Ebbinghaus-style protocols: give cells one stimulus pulse, wait a variable retention interval, then give an identical test pulse and quantify 'savings' (faster or larger AP-1 target induction by scRNA-seq or live reporters) as a function of interval length and of massed versus spaced training pulses. A genuine memory system should show a quantifiable retention decay constant and an advantage for spaced over massed stimulation, and knocking down specific Fos/Jun family members should selectively flatten that curve.

question: ap1
title: Read-write-erase head assay (borrowed from magnetic tape storage)
description: Treat a single AP-1-bound enhancer as a storage bit: use dCas9-Fos/Jun fusions to 'write' the state transiently at a naive locus, remove the writer, then assay persistence of accessibility and transcription over many days, and finally 'erase' with targeted motif disruption or a repressive domain and rewrite. Demonstrating independent, locus-specific write/erase/rewrite cycles separates true storage from continuous instructive signaling.

question: ap1
title: Counting bits of stimulus history (borrowed from information theory)
description: Expose cells to many randomized stimulus histories (sequences of cytokine, growth factor or drug pulses), then compute the mutual information between the past input sequence and the present single-cell AP-1 chromatin or expression state to estimate how many bits of history the network retains and for how long. Comparing channel capacity in wild-type versus AP-1 motif-mutant or Fos-degron cells quantifies AP-1's specific contribution to memory capacity rather than to instantaneous response.

question: ap1
title: Tree-ring autocorrelation across lineages (borrowed from dendrochronology)
description: Combine an evolving CRISPR lineage recorder with single-cell multiome readout so that each cell's AP-1 accessibility state can be placed on a reconstructed division tree, then measure how the correlation in AP-1 state decays with lineage distance and number of intervening mitoses. Heritable memory predicts correlation that persists over several generations and decays with division number rather than with elapsed wall-clock time.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase dating of the memory carrier (borrowed from isotope geochronology)
description: Use heavy amino acid labeling of Fos/Jun proteins together with labeled-histone nucleosome turnover measurements at the same loci, chasing both after stimulus withdrawal, to date which molecular layer actually carries the persisting signal. If target-gene memory outlives the labeled AP-1 protein pool but tracks the age of nucleosomes or DNA methylation at AP-1 sites, memory is stored in chromatin that AP-1 merely deposited, a distinction that sustained-expression experiments alone cannot make.

question: ap1
title: Write-pulse, remove-stimulus, subthreshold-read retention assay
description: Deliver a calibrated stimulus pulse of defined amplitude and duration (e.g., TPA, TNF, or growth factor for 15-120 min), wash it out completely, then at intervals from hours to weeks probe cells with a deliberately subthreshold challenge dose that is too weak to re-write the state, scoring AP-1 target induction, AP-1 motif accessibility, and FOS/JUN occupancy. The memory signature is a larger response in pulsed than naive cells long after FOS/JUN protein has returned to baseline.

question: ap1
title: Accelerated decay testing with extrapolated retention lifetime
description: Because the memory may outlast a practical experiment, accelerate its loss along defined axes (raising proliferation rate, forcing and counting divisions by dye dilution, or shifting temperature) and fit the decay rates to extrapolate a retention half-life under normal conditions. This yields a quantitative claim, such as the number of divisions over which the AP-1-encoded state persists, rather than a binary answer.

question: ap1
title: Rate-dependent hysteresis loops of stimulus versus AP-1 output
description: Sweep stimulus dose slowly up and then back down at several sweep rates, measuring AP-1 activity and target output in single cells, to test whether the dose-response traces a pinched hysteresis loop whose area grows with sweep speed and collapses at very slow sweeps. Identical doses giving different outputs on ascending versus descending arms is direct evidence that state depends on history, not just instantaneous input.

question: ap1
title: Imaging the physical substrate forming and dissolving with the stored state
description: Pair functional readouts with in-situ structural measurements of the proposed storage medium: live-cell imaging of tagged FOS/JUN, single-cell ATAC or CUT-and-Tag time courses, and DNA or nascent RNA FISH at specific AP-1-bound enhancers, to show a defined chromatin feature (nucleosome eviction, enhancer-promoter contact) appears on writing and disappears on loss. Memory is supported only if the feature's lifetime matches functional retention in the same cells.

question: ap1
title: Erase, rewrite, and endurance cycling with targeted perturbations
description: Selectively erase the stored state with AP-1-directed interventions (auxin degron on FOS/JUN, dominant-negative A-FOS, or dCas9-KRAB/HDAC recruitment to the specific AP-1 enhancers), re-apply the stimulus to confirm rewriting, and repeat write/erase cycles to detect degradation or drift. Clean erasure by an AP-1-specific perturbation with intact rewriting establishes AP-1 as the causal storage element rather than a correlate of some other persistent change.

question: ap1
title: Decoding probes for stimulus history from AP-1 state, with a decay curve
description: Expose cells to a panel of distinct transient stimuli, wash out, and at a log-spaced series of delays profile AP-1 family occupancy and AP-1 motif accessibility (CUT&RUN plus ATAC-seq); train a classifier to predict which stimulus a cell/sample previously saw from AP-1-associated features alone. Plot classification accuracy versus delay and compare it to probes built on non-AP-1 features, so that memory is quantified as a decodability half-life rather than a binary claim.

question: ap1
title: Ablation/knockdown timed after the stimulus has ended
description: Degrade AP-1 subunits (dTAG or auxin-degron on FOS/JUN family members) only during the post-stimulus interval, after the acute response has resolved, and ask whether the history-dependent behavior disappears while the acute response remains intact. This is the biological analogue of activation patching: removing the candidate component should erase the downstream history effect without touching the original input processing.

question: ap1
title: Transfer test by installing a foreign AP-1 state
description: Use synthetic reprogramming of the AP-1 state (inducible expression of a defined FOS/JUN dimer combination, or dCas9-based recruitment of AP-1 to the enhancer set marked by stimulus A) in naive cells, then challenge with a common second stimulus. If AP-1 carries the memory, these cells should produce the stimulus-A-specific downstream response even though they never saw stimulus A.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage tracing to measure how long the AP-1 trace survives division
description: Combine heritable clonal barcoding with paired single-cell ATAC/RNA at multiple timepoints after a transient stimulus to ask whether AP-1 site accessibility and AP-1 target expression are concordant within clones and discordant between them. Clone-level autocorrelation decay gives a direct memory timescale and separates heritable epigenetic storage from slowly decaying protein-level carryover.

question: ap1
title: Dose/sequence experiments that distinguish a true integrator from a correlated readout
description: Vary stimulus amplitude, duration, number of pulses, and inter-pulse interval, then test whether AP-1 occupancy predicts the later response better than the stimulus parameters themselves do — i.e., whether AP-1 is a sufficient statistic that screens off the input history. Pairing this with mediation analysis and with partial AP-1 ablation at graded degrader doses tests whether response magnitude scales with the amount of the putative memory component that remains.

question: ap1
title: Kaiser-effect assay: graded re-stimulation after a known peak
description: Prime cells with a calibrated stimulus amplitude (e.g., serum, TGF-β, or stiffness), let signaling fully relax, then re-challenge parallel wells across a dose ladder spanning below and above the prime, reading out de novo AP-1 target transcription with live-cell FOS/JUN-family reporters and nascent-RNA (SLAM-seq) so that 'emission onset' is timed precisely. Memory is demonstrated if transcriptional response stays suppressed until the dose exceeds the prior peak and then rises sharply, with the breakpoint tracking the prime amplitude.

question: ap1
title: Decay-of-memory kinetics: delay, division number, and 'annealing' conditions
description: Repeat the prime/probe protocol while systematically varying the inter-stimulus interval, number of cell divisions (tracked by dye dilution or FUCCI sorting), and stressors analogous to temperature/saturation (HDAC or BRD4 inhibition, replication stress, osmotic chromatin decompaction), fitting the shift in re-activation threshold to an exponential or stretched-exponential decay. This yields a quantitative memory half-life and identifies which perturbations erase, accelerate, or protect the AP-1 record, distinguishing true storage from slow signal clearance.

question: ap1
title: Microstructural readout: latent AP-1 enhancers as the memory-bearing feature
description: Pair each mechanical-memory time point with ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and H3K4me1/H3K27ac profiling to identify sites that open during the first exposure and remain open (or newly nucleosome-depleted) after signaling returns to baseline, exactly as microCT links preconsolidation memory to retained microcracks. Correlate the number and residual accessibility of these retained sites, site by site, with the measured re-activation threshold across priming doses.

question: ap1
title: Causal site-closure and site-opening test
description: Use dCas9-KRAB/DNMT3A to selectively re-close the retained AP-1 enhancers identified above, and dCas9-p300 or synthetic AP-1 tethering to pre-open them in naive cells, then re-run the graded re-stimulation assay. If these elements carry the record, closing them should abolish the threshold shift and opening them should install a false memory of an exposure that never occurred.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell preconsolidation inference and load-path discrimination
description: Treat each cell as a specimen: from single-cell multiome (ATAC+RNA) of cells with hidden exposure histories, fit the breakpoint in AP-1 target output versus log(stimulus dose) to infer a per-cell 'preconsolidation amplitude', then validate against the known true peak and test cell-to-cell spread. Contrast one large exposure against many sub-threshold cycles delivering equal cumulative dose to determine whether AP-1 records only the historical maximum or ratchets with cumulative loading.

question: ap1
title: Persistence test on post-pulse chromatin time series
description: Give cells a brief stimulus that induces AP-1 (e.g., a TPA or cytokine pulse, then washout). Profile accessibility (ATAC-seq) and AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN) at many time points over days to weeks, then fit a decay model to each locus, much as economists run persistence or unit-root tests on unemployment. AP-1-bound sites that stay open after AP-1 protein returns to baseline, while matched non-AP-1 sites return to normal, would be candidate memory loci.

question: ap1
title: Impulse responses to a clean, AP-1-only pulse
description: Use an inducible or degron-tagged Fos/Jun construct to deliver a pulse that activates only AP-1, which plays the role of an identified transitory shock. Estimate local-projection-style responses at each later time point: chromatin state, and gene induction after a standard rechallenge. This tests whether AP-1 alone is enough to leave a lasting mark, separate from the other pathways a natural stimulus turns on.

question: ap1
title: Removing AP-1 at different phases to find what carries the memory
description: Use acute degradation (dTAG/auxin) of AP-1 subunits at three points: during the priming pulse, during the quiet interval, or only at rechallenge. In parallel, inhibit candidate carriers such as SWI/SNF recruitment, H3K4me1 writers, or cooperating lineage transcription factors. This mirrors separating skill loss, capital scrapping and insider bargaining as hysteresis mechanisms. If memory survives removing AP-1 during the interval but depends on a co-factor, AP-1 starts the memory but does not maintain it.

question: ap1
title: Barcoded lineage difference-in-differences across cell divisions
description: Barcode clones, split sister lineages into primed and unprimed arms, and compare their rechallenge responses at increasing numbers of divisions after priming. This is a difference-in-differences design, like displaced-worker scarring studies. Pairing it with mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN shows whether AP-1-dependent memory is passed through mitosis (bookmarking) or fades with dilution.

question: ap1
title: Natural variation in AP-1 motifs as a cross-context comparison
description: In F1 hybrid cells or donor panels, find enhancers where a SNP disrupts the AP-1 motif on one allele. Compare allele-specific accessibility and expression memory after priming. This is like cross-country designs where the proposed carrier, such as union coverage, differs: if AP-1 drives the memory, it should persist only on the allele with an intact motif, within the same nucleus.

question: ap1
title: Ramp-up/ramp-down dose hysteresis loops for AP-1
description: Mirror CO2 ramp experiments: step a stimulus (TPA, TNF, growth factor, or a targeted inhibitor) slowly up through a dose series and then back down through the identical doses, reading AP-1 activity at each step with live FOS/JUN reporters plus smFISH for AP-1 target genes. A down-ramp trajectory displaced from the up-ramp trajectory traces a hysteresis loop and defines the dose window in which AP-1 state depends on history rather than current input.

question: ap1
title: Bistable-window mapping with history-matched cells
description: Prepare two populations under identical current conditions but opposite histories (previously high-AP-1 versus naive), then place both at a ladder of intermediate stimulus levels for many divisions. The range of inputs over which the two populations stably maintain different AP-1 activity and target-gene output is the empirical bistable range, the cell-biological analog of the AMOC bistability window.

question: ap1
title: Early-warning statistics in single-cell AP-1 traces
description: Apply critical-slowing-down diagnostics to long-term live imaging of an AP-1 transcriptional reporter: lag-1 autocorrelation, variance, and recovery time after brief optogenetic or drug pulses as cells approach a transition point in stimulus dose. Rising autocorrelation, variance, and recovery time near the inferred threshold would support a genuine bistable attractor rather than a graded dose response.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin proxies as a paleo-record of past forcing
description: Treat AP-1-bound enhancers as proxy archives: after stimulus removal, profile ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and H3K4me1/K27ac at AP-1 motifs in cells that are transcriptionally indistinguishable from naive cells, to see whether the chromatin still encodes prior exposure. Pairing this with lineage barcoding tests whether the chromatin proxy predicts which cells reactivate fastest on re-stimulation, i.e. whether the record is functional memory rather than an inert scar.

question: ap1
title: Transient AP-1 'hosing' to test state switching and reversibility
description: Analogous to freshwater hosing, deliver a short defined pulse of AP-1 activity alone (optogenetic JUN/FOS dimer or auxin-degron release) without the upstream stimulus, then remove it and follow cells for weeks. If supra-threshold pulses drive a self-sustaining high state while sub-threshold pulses relax back, AP-1 is sufficient to set the memory; running it in reverse (acute AP-1 degradation in memory-bearing cells) tests whether the state can be pushed back across the threshold.

question: ap1
title: Stimulus cycling with a transient AP-1 dip
description: Prime cells with stimulus A, then transiently remove AP-1 function for a defined window (degron-tagged cJun/FOSL1 or inducible A-FOS), then restore AP-1 and re-challenge with A. If the primed response returns intact, memory survives independently of AP-1; if the dip erases the faster/larger secondary response, AP-1 itself is the storage element, and varying dip duration and depth gives a dose-response for erasure.

question: ap1
title: Waiting-time scaling of memory decay
description: Vary priming duration (t_w) across a wide range and then measure, at many rest times (t) after withdrawal, both AP-1 motif accessibility (ATAC/CUT&Tag) and the magnitude of the secondary response. Test whether decay curves from different t_w collapse onto a single function of t/t_w, the aging signature; such scaling would show AP-1 enhancer states integrate exposure history rather than acting as a simple on/off switch.

question: ap1
title: Remanent chromatin state after stimulus removal
description: Analogous to thermoremanent magnetization, remove the stimulus and map what remains: AP-1 occupancy, enhancer accessibility, H3K4me1/K27ac, and cohesin-dependent contacts at AP-1 sites, at matched transcriptional baselines. Loci that keep AP-1 footprints after the transcriptional response has fully decayed are the candidate carriers of the imprint, and their overlap with the sites reactivated fastest on re-challenge quantifies how much of the memory they explain.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell overlap order parameter between priming and recall
description: Use lineage barcoding plus paired scATAC/scRNA to compute a configuration overlap between each clone's primed state and its state after rest and re-challenge, mirroring overlap distributions in spin-glass simulations. A broad, bimodal overlap distribution restricted to AP-1-bound regions would indicate that a subset of cells and a specific set of AP-1 loci carry the memory, rather than a uniform population-level shift.

question: ap1
title: Frequency-resolved response to oscillating stimulation
description: Deliver the stimulus as square-wave pulse trains across several decades of period (minutes to days) using microfluidics or optogenetic AP-1 pathway control, and measure response amplitude and phase lag of AP-1 target output, the biological analog of AC susceptibility. Slow components whose characteristic relaxation time grows with prior priming duration would demonstrate aging-like, history-dependent AP-1 dynamics, and comparing with and without AP-1 degradation localizes those slow modes.

question: ap1
title: Priming learning curve with an explicit depreciation term
description: Stimulate cells a controlled number of times with systematically varied rest intervals and fit the re-challenge response to a Wright-type learning curve in which cumulative exposures are discounted by a decay factor, yielding a per-gene and per-enhancer AP-1 memory half-life. Adding an unrelated second stimulus measures 'transfer of learning,' separating stimulus-specific memory from a general increase in responsiveness.

question: ap1
title: Timed degron turnover shocks at encoding, storage, and recall
description: Use dTAG/auxin degron alleles of FOS, JUN, JUNB, and ATF3 to deplete AP-1 only during the first stimulus, only during the quiescent storage interval, or only just before re-challenge, with washout and re-expression controls. If AP-1 is the memory store rather than the writer or reader, only storage-window depletion should erase the primed response.

question: ap1
title: Partition the memory between protein, chromatin, and network feedback
description: In the same primed cells, measure AP-1 protein residence time (pulse-chase SILAC, FRAP), the chromatin record (ATAC-seq, FOS/JUN CUT&RUN, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, DNA methylation at AP-1 motifs), and the AP-1 autoregulatory feedback dynamics, then test whether primed accessibility outlives AP-1 protein by many half-lives. Persistence after the protein is gone localizes the engram to AP-1-written chromatin; decay tracking protein turnover localizes it to AP-1 itself.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell split design with clonal barcodes
description: Barcode cells, let clones divide, then challenge one sister branch and use its response to predict the untouched sister's response after the same priming history, as a function of intervening divisions, giving a mitotic retention rate that separates heritable memory from noise. Transplanting primed cells into a naive microenvironment tests whether the memory travels with the cell or with its context.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon fusion and nuclear/cytoplasmic swap
description: Fuse primed to naive cells (and primed nuclei to naive cytoplasts via enucleation or nuclear transfer) with allele-distinguishable reporters, then score allele-specific AP-1 target induction in the hybrid. Dominance of the primed state and whether it is nucleus- or cytoplasm-borne pins down the physical substrate, and recruitment of the naive genome would indicate a diffusible trans-acting AP-1 memory rather than a cis-chromatin one.

question: ap1
title: Persistence regression with lineage tracing and formal mediation
description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus, withdraw it, and track barcoded clones over many divisions with longitudinal scATAC/scRNA, regressing later response amplitude on past exposure dose. Then run mediation analysis to ask how much of the persistence coefficient is carried by retained AP-1 motif accessibility/FOS-JUN occupancy versus competing carriers such as DNA methylation, H3K4me1, BAF retention, or residual protein.

question: ap1
title: Abolish the institution: degron removal during the memory window
description: Apply an auxin/dTAG degron to FOS/JUN family members only after stimulus withdrawal and before restimulation, mimicking the political-science test of whether persistence survives abolition of the carrier. If AP-1 maintains memory, degradation confined to the latent period should erase enhanced recall despite an intact exposure history.

question: ap1
title: Placebo loci: matched AP-1 motifs that were never occupied
description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs that gained stable accessibility after the transient stimulus (the treated border) alongside sequence- and expression-matched motifs that were never occupied (the placebo border with no institutional consequence). Memory should be lost only for the first set, excluding generic AP-1 dependence or motif-adjacent genomic context.

question: ap1
title: Allele-level natural experiment in F1 hybrid cells
description: In F1 hybrid cells, use heterozygous SNPs that disrupt AP-1 motifs as a within-nucleus discontinuity: both alleles share an identical trans environment and exposure history, so allele-specific differences in retained priming and recall isolate cis AP-1 motif function. Motif-neutral heterozygous sites serve as the placebo comparison.

question: ap1
title: Dose-threshold discontinuity plus an orthogonal instrument
description: Finely titrate stimulus to locate the sharp threshold where AP-1 enhancer priming switches on, then compare cells just below versus just above the cutoff (sorted on a live AP-1 reporter) for long-term recall. Complement with instrumental-variable logic by inducing FOS/JUN optogenetically without the original stimulus, shifting AP-1 activity through a route that bypasses other stimulus-induced changes.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis ladder: measure memory as a bistable loop, not a decay curve
description: Titrate an AP-1-driving input (serum, TGF-beta, substrate stiffness, or inducible MEK) up a dose ladder and then back down the identical ladder, reading an AP-1 target reporter in single cells at each step. A genuine memory mechanism yields a hysteresis loop whose width quantifies stored information, while slow signal decay does not; single-cell readout separates true per-cell bistability from graded responses with heterogeneous thresholds.

question: ap1
title: Is the memory clocked in hours or in cell divisions?
description: After a transient AP-1 pulse, split cells into cycling versus arrested conditions (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, thymidine block) matched for elapsed time and measure decay of the primed state per hour versus per division. Replication-coupled dilution of a chromatin mark predicts division-clocked decay, whereas protein- or feedback-based persistence predicts time-clocked decay.

question: ap1
title: Erase-and-restore with a pan-AP-1 family degron
description: Tag all expressed bZIP partners (FOS/FOSB/FOSL1/JUN/JUNB/JUND) with degrons so the entire family can be cleared for defined windows after priming and then restored. Recovery of the primed state would show AP-1 is a reader/writer of memory stored elsewhere, while permanent erasure would show AP-1 occupancy is itself the storage medium, a distinction single-factor knockdowns cannot make because of redundancy.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic TRE-array locus library for minimal sufficient encoding of memory
description: Integrate at one fixed safe-harbor site a library of synthetic loci varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, and core promoter, then deliver a standardized AP-1 pulse and assay which configurations stay active days later. This tests whether AP-1 sites alone suffice to build a memory element and reveals the sequence grammar that converts transient binding into a persistent state.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific cis test using heterozygous TRE motif disruption
description: Destroy the AP-1 motif on only one allele of candidate memory enhancers (or use F1 hybrid/heterozygous lines with natural motif-disrupting variants) and measure allele-resolved accessibility and nascent transcription before, during, and long after a pulse. Because both alleles share nucleus, trans environment, and stimulus history, persistent loss of priming only in cis is strong evidence that AP-1 binding at that element carries the memory.

question: ap1
title: Division-coupled dilution clock: is memory stored in protein or in chromatin?
description: Pulse-chase label AP-1 subunits (SNAP/HaloTag or photoconvertible Dendra-FOS/JUN/JUNB) and measure each subunit's protein half-life and nuclear residence time alongside the decay of functional memory, in parallel in cycling versus pharmacologically arrested (or contact-inhibited) cells. If memory half-life scales with cell-division-driven dilution of a long-lived AP-1 pool rather than with elapsed time in arrested cells, the 'memory' is a protein reservoir, not a chromatin template; the two regimes make opposite, quantitative predictions.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic minimal AP-1 memory circuit with tunable hysteresis
description: In a cell type with little endogenous AP-1 activity, build an orthogonal bZIP (AP-1 leucine zipper fused to a non-native DNA-binding domain) driving a synthetic enhancer array in which motif number, spacing, and feedback strength are systematically varied, and drive it transiently with a small-molecule or light input. Measure the hysteresis width and bistability boundary of the resulting input-output curves to determine whether AP-1's autoregulatory architecture is by itself sufficient to store a stable state, and which design parameters set memory duration.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic memory capacity across combinatorial stimulus histories
description: Expose cells to all sequences of a small set of distinct stimuli (e.g., 3 inputs in 2-3 step orders, including order permutations and repeats), then after a long washout read out single-cell chromatin and transcription plus AP-1 dimer composition (multiplexed proximity ligation or dimer-specific CUT&Tag). Compute the mutual information between past history and present state to quantify how many bits are stored and whether the stored code is non-commutative (order-dependent), which would distinguish a genuine combinatorial AP-1 memory from a single scalar 'how recently were you stimulated' variable.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific cis test of AP-1 motifs in F1 hybrid cells
description: Use F1 hybrid cells (e.g., mouse F1 fibroblasts/ESCs or human trio-derived lines) where the two haplotypes differ at thousands of AP-1 motifs, and measure allele-specific accessibility and transcription at the primed enhancers long after a transient stimulus. Because both alleles share the same nucleus, trans-environment, and AP-1 protein pool, persistent allelic imbalance that tracks AP-1 motif strength is a clean natural-variation test that the motif itself — not correlated chromatin features — carries the memory, and can be extended by prime-editing single motif variants in the weaker haplotype.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic writing rules: dose, duration, and sufficiency of AP-1 for installing memory
description: Use a light-controlled AP-1 (optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization or LOV-caged bZIP) to deliver precisely shaped AP-1 activity pulses — varying amplitude, duration, and pulse number at fixed integrated dose — in the complete absence of the upstream stimulus, then assay memory depth weeks later. Mapping whether memory depends on integrated dose, peak amplitude, or number of pulses defines the encoding rule, and successful 'writing' without the physiological signal (or 'erasing' by a counter-pulse of a repressive bZIP) establishes sufficiency with a quantitative transfer function rather than a binary knockout result.

question: ap1
title: Division-coupled versus time-coupled forgetting
description: Measure decay of the primed state as a function of number of cell divisions rather than elapsed time, comparing cycling cells, slowly cycling cells (CDK4/6 inhibition or contact inhibition), and reversibly arrested cells, with division number tracked by dye dilution or live imaging. A replication-coupled chromatin memory should lose a fixed fraction per S phase, whereas a protein-level or autoregulatory-feedback memory should decay on a wall-clock timescale independent of division number.

question: ap1
title: Allele-resolved test of whether the memory acts in cis
description: In F1 hybrid or SNP-rich cells, or in clones with the AP-1 motif deleted from only one allele of a target enhancer, prime the cells and then measure allele-specific accessibility, nascent transcription (allele-resolved Pro-seq or intronic smFISH with SNP probes), and reactivation kinetics on rechallenge. If memory is carried by the chromatin at the site, the two alleles should remember independently and discordantly; if it is carried by a diffusible AP-1 pool or feedback loop, both alleles should behave identically.

question: ap1
title: Transient recruitment to a naive synthetic locus
description: Integrate a motif-free synthetic reporter locus at a defined genomic position and recruit FOS/JUN bZIP domains to it for a controlled pulse using dox-inducible dCas9 or zinc-finger fusions, then withdraw the recruiter and ask whether accessibility and expression self-sustain for days and through divisions. Repeating with dimerization-dead, DNA-binding-dead, and transactivation-dead variants, and with recruited partners removed, isolates exactly which AP-1 activity is sufficient to install heritable state at a locus with no prior history.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-composition code and memory interference
description: Ask whether the identity of the remembered stimulus is stored in which FOS/JUN family dimer occupies a site, by measuring dimer composition over time with pairwise proximity ligation, split-fluorophore dimer reporters, or crosslinking mass spectrometry, combined with a cross-stimulus interference design (prime with stimulus A, challenge with an unrelated AP-1-activating stimulus B, then test for A). Overwriting, saturation, or retroactive interference between stimuli would show the memory has limited capacity and is written in dimer composition, not merely in generic enhancer opening.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase of AP-1 protein molecules to test protein-as-carrier
description: HaloTag-knock-in FOS and JUN, pulse-label the existing protein pool with a bright dye, chase with a blocking ligand, and use single-molecule tracking plus chromatin fractionation to ask whether the same old molecules remain bound at primed sites, are re-deposited after mitosis, or are replaced by newly synthesized protein while the memory persists. Residence times and the fraction of old protein retained set an upper bound on how much of the memory the protein itself can carry versus what must be handed off to chromatin.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon fusion to separate cis-chromatin memory from trans-acting AP-1 protein
description: Fuse a 'primed' cell (prior transient stimulus) with a genetically distinguishable naive cell and use allele-specific ATAC-seq/RNA-seq to ask whether the primed chromatin state is maintained only on the experienced genome or is imposed in trans on the naive genome by the shared AP-1 protein pool. Cis-restricted persistence argues for a chromatin-encoded memory, whereas dominant trans conversion argues that AP-1 is simply a long-lived diffusible signal rather than a memory element.

question: ap1
title: Quantitative accounting of AP-1 protein lifetime versus memory lifetime
description: Use HaloTag pulse-chase labeling (plus SILAC turnover measurement) of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN to directly measure degradation and mitotic dilution rates of the AP-1 protein molecules present at the time of stimulation, and compare those decay kinetics quantitatively to the decay of the primed phenotype in the same cells. Memory that substantially outlives the original protein pool, with no sustained new synthesis, cannot be explained by slow TF decay and requires a self-propagating mechanism.

question: ap1
title: Decoupling the AP-1 autoregulatory circuit without removing the protein
description: Place JUN/FOS expression under exogenous doxycycline control at the endogenous locus while deleting the endogenous AP-1-bound autoregulatory enhancers, so that AP-1 protein levels can be clamped independently of feedback. If transient stimulation no longer produces a persistent state despite identical AP-1 protein levels, memory is a property of the self-reinforcing circuit rather than of AP-1 occupancy per se.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic minimal AP-1 memory element
description: Integrate synthetic arrays of TRE/AP-1 motifs (varying motif number, spacing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequences, and partner motifs such as TEAD or ETS) upstream of an inert reporter at a defined safe-harbor locus, then deliver a transient AP-1 pulse and measure how long accessibility and reporter expression persist. This reconstitution asks whether AP-1 binding sites alone are sufficient to convert a transient input into a stable state, and defines the minimal sequence grammar required.

question: ap1
title: Multi-stimulus history decoding to test what information AP-1 actually stores
description: Expose cells to ordered combinations of distinct AP-1-activating inputs (e.g., growth factor, mechanical stretch, cytokine) in different sequences and intervals, then train a classifier on single-cell AP-1 binding/accessibility profiles to decode which history a cell experienced, quantifying mutual information between past input and present state as a function of elapsed time and divisions. A genuine memory mechanism should preserve stimulus identity and order rather than collapsing all histories onto a single magnitude axis.

question: ap1
title: Separate time-decay from division-dilution of the memory
description: Measure decay of the AP-1-associated state as a function of completed divisions rather than elapsed time, comparing cycling cells (dye-dilution or FUCCI-sorted generations) against cells arrested for the same duration (contact inhibition, CDK4/6 inhibition), then use repli-ATAC or nascent-chromatin capture to time how fast accessibility is re-established behind the replication fork at AP-1 sites. A true heritable memory should decay per generation with active post-replicative re-establishment, whereas a long-lived protein or RNA pool should decay per unit time and simply be diluted.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic TRE grammar array to measure memory capacity
description: Integrate a library of synthetic reporter loci at a fixed safe-harbor site that systematically vary TRE/CRE motif number, affinity, spacing, and co-occurring partner motifs, then deliver a single calibrated stimulus pulse and measure how long each configuration holds its expression state. This converts 'does AP-1 store memory' into a quantitative dose-response between binding-site grammar and memory half-life, and identifies whether storage requires cooperative multi-site occupancy or a partner factor.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic readout of stimulus history
description: Deliver defined sequences of stimuli differing in order, dose, and spacing (A-then-B versus B-then-A, pulsed versus sustained), then compute the mutual information between stimulus history and single-cell AP-1 occupancy/accessibility versus the rest of the transcriptome. This asks not merely whether AP-1 persists but how many bits of past experience it actually carries and whether it encodes order and magnitude or only the binary fact of prior exposure.

question: ap1
title: Old-versus-new protein pulse-chase to localize the memory substrate
description: Use HaloTag pulse-chase labeling of endogenous FOS, JUN, JUND, and FRA1 combined with single-molecule tracking and FRAP to measure dimer composition, residence time, and turnover of the specific protein molecules present during the memory window. If memory resides in a slowly exchanging long-lived dimer pool (e.g., JUND/FRA1) rather than in chromatin, old labeled protein should remain locus-bound across the memory period; if chromatin is the substrate, newly synthesized protein should be recruited to the same sites.

question: ap1
title: Two-phase maintenance CRISPR screen applied only after the stimulus ends
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPRi/ORF screen in which perturbations are induced only after the stimulus is withdrawn, scoring loss of a stable AP-1-driven reporter or loss of primed restimulation, so that maintenance factors are cleanly separated from factors required for the acute response. Hits that are dispensable for induction but required for persistence would define the machinery that actually stores the AP-1 state and provide the causal handle for selectively erasing memory without blocking signaling.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon cis/trans test of where the memory lives
description: Fuse a stimulus-primed cell with a naive cell (distinguishable nuclei via labeled histones or species-specific SNPs) and use per-nucleus nascent intron FISH plus single-nucleus ATAC to ask whether the naive nucleus acquires the primed program. If AP-1 memory is carried by diffusible trans factors both nuclei should converge; if it is stored in cis at chromatin, the two nuclei should retain distinct AP-1 target states within the shared cytoplasm.

question: ap1
title: Division clock versus wall clock decay of the memory
description: Measure memory decay (reporter output, target-gene expression, AP-1-site accessibility) in parallel populations held non-dividing (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, serum starvation) versus freely cycling, and fit decay as a function of elapsed time versus number of completed divisions. A memory that decays per-division implicates replication-coupled dilution of a chromatin-templated state, whereas decay per unit time implicates protein turnover or a self-sustaining feedback loop.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic enhancer library defining the architecture that converts a pulse into a persistent state
description: Integrate at a single safe-harbor landing pad a barcoded library of synthetic enhancers that systematically vary AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, NF-kB), and nucleosome-positioning sequences, then measure reporter output and barcode-level accessibility days after a single stimulus pulse. This maps the design rules by which AP-1 binding sites are sufficient to store a past input, separating sequence-encoded memory capacity from endogenous locus context.

question: ap1
title: Decoding stimulus history from single cells as an information-theoretic measurement
description: Expose cells to a panel of distinct transient inputs (different cytokines, doses, durations, pulse orders), then at long delay perform joint scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq and train a classifier to recover which input each cell experienced, quantifying the mutual information (bits) between past stimulus and present state. Repeating this under AP-1 perturbation tests whether AP-1 is the actual storage channel by measuring how much recoverable information about the past is lost, rather than merely whether some genes change.

question: ap1
title: In vitro replication of AP-1-bound chromatin to test self-propagation capability
description: Assemble nucleosomal arrays containing AP-1 sites, load purified Fos/Jun dimers (and candidate cofactors), and replicate the templates in Xenopus egg extract or a reconstituted replisome system, then assay occupancy and accessibility on the two daughter templates with and without free AP-1 in solution. This asks directly whether AP-1 can survive or be re-templated through fork passage, distinguishing an intrinsically self-propagating mark from a state that must be rebuilt by the soluble pool each cycle.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic minimal memory elements in a landing-pad library
description: Integrate a barcoded library of synthetic enhancers at a single neutral genomic landing pad, systematically varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and co-occurring partner motifs, then deliver one defined stimulus pulse and track reporter expression and accessibility for days. This turns the question into a quantitative sufficiency map of which cis-architectures convert a transient input into a persistent output, free of endogenous locus history.

question: ap1
title: Memory duration versus AP-1 protein lifetime arithmetic
description: Use HaloTag pulse-chase or SILAC on endogenously tagged FOS/JUN to measure actual protein half-lives and dilution-by-division rates in the same cells whose memory duration is being assayed. If the phenotypic memory substantially outlasts the integrated lifetime of all AP-1 protein present at the end of the stimulus, the information cannot reside in AP-1 protein levels and must be relayed to a chromatin or feedback-based store, a decisive and rarely performed accounting test.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and single-molecule residence time as the heritability mechanism
description: Combine single-molecule tracking of Halo-FOS/JUN through mitosis with mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN in synchronized cells to ask whether AP-1 remains bound to memory enhancers when the rest of the genome is evicted. Then test separation-of-function mutants (e.g., bZIP phospho-site or DNA-binding-surface variants) that selectively abolish mitotic retention without altering interphase binding, and ask whether memory survives division.

question: ap1
title: Dimer identity, not AP-1 amount, as the stored variable
description: Quantify the full bZIP dimer repertoire (FOS/FOSB/FRA1/FRA2 x JUN/JUNB/JUND, plus ATF partners) in single cells over the memory window using dimer-specific proximity ligation or split-reporter/BiFC panels, paired with per-cell response magnitude on restimulation. The test is whether the memory-predictive variable is which dimer species persists rather than total AP-1 activity, which would reframe AP-1 memory as a combinatorial code.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic capacity of AP-1 for stimulus history
description: Deliver programmed pulse trains that vary amplitude, duration, number, and inter-pulse interval (microfluidics or optogenetic input), and compute the mutual information between past input sequence and present AP-1 state or chromatin readout at single-cell resolution. This quantifies in bits how much history AP-1 actually stores and distinguishes genuine multi-state memory from a single slowly relaxing variable, since true memory should preserve information about pulse order and spacing, not just cumulative dose.

question: ap1
title: Separate time-based from division-based forgetting, and test mitotic bookmarking
description: Measure decay of the primed state (accessibility and re-response amplitude) in matched populations that are cycling versus reversibly arrested (CDK4/6 inhibitor or G0, with FUCCI staging), to ask whether memory half-life is set in hours or in cell divisions. Pair this with Halo-tagged Fos/Jun live imaging and mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN to test whether AP-1 is retained on condensed chromatin, which is the mechanism a division-counting memory would require.

question: ap1
title: Kinetic signature of memory: single-molecule tracking rather than occupancy
description: Use HaloTag single-molecule tracking (plus FRAP and AP-1 hub imaging) to compare residence time, bound fraction, and target-search time of JunB/Fos in naive versus primed cells held at matched AP-1 protein levels by a titratable degron. This tests the hypothesis that memory is stored as a faster or more stable rebinding kinetics at primed sites (a search advantage) rather than as higher steady-state occupancy, and predicts how fast memory should recover after transient AP-1 removal.

question: ap1
title: Memory interference between two AP-1-dependent programs
description: Prime cells with stimulus A, then deliver an unrelated AP-1-inducing stimulus B, and ask whether B erases, overwrites, or leaves intact the A-specific primed response (and vice versa), including a titration of B's strength. A shared, limiting trans-acting AP-1 pool predicts dose-dependent retroactive interference between memories, whereas locus-local chromatin storage predicts independence; adding an AP-1 decoy-site sponge array that can be excised provides an orthogonal limiting-pool test.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic sufficiency test using stimulus-history microfluidics
description: Deliver defined sequences of stimulus histories in a microfluidic device to cells carrying a live AP-1 activity reporter plus a downstream response reporter, then compute I(history; AP-1 state) and the conditional information I(history; response | AP-1 state). If AP-1 is the memory substrate, the conditional term should collapse to near zero, which is a quantitative, model-free test that AP-1 lies on the causal path rather than merely correlating with history.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific memory in F1 hybrid or heterozygous-donor cells
description: In F1 hybrid mouse cells or human donor cells heterozygous at thousands of AP-1 motifs, use allele-resolved ATAC and nascent RNA before and long after a transient stimulus to ask whether the persistent (memory) state tracks the motif-disrupting allele in cis. Thousands of natural motif variants give a genome-scale, internally controlled causal test, and the subset showing memory loss without acute-induction loss identifies motifs needed for maintenance specifically.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase decoupling of AP-1 establishment from maintenance
description: Use an optogenetic or chemically inducible AP-1 construct (plus a degron on endogenous Jun/Fos family members) to deliver a defined transient pulse, then chase for many days and track target-gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Depleting AP-1 at staggered times after the pulse distinguishes whether AP-1 is only needed to write the state or is continuously required to hold it — the key discriminator between a memory mechanism and a simple persistent signal.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded sister-cell concordance of AP-1 target states
description: Barcode single cells and profile single-cell RNA plus ATAC after several divisions, quantifying how much more similar AP-1 target expression and AP-1 motif accessibility are between clonal relatives than between unrelated cells, as a function of generations since the common ancestor. The decay of this concordance gives a direct, quantitative memory half-life in cell divisions rather than in hours.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping of AP-1 dose-response
description: Expose cells to graded stimulus levels on both an ascending and a descending ramp and read out AP-1 activity with a live reporter at single-cell resolution. A reproducible gap between the up and down curves is the classic signature of a bistable, self-reinforcing circuit, and its absence would argue AP-1 is relaying rather than storing information.

question: ap1
title: Sort-and-regrow stability assay on an endogenous AP-1 reporter
description: Knock a fluorescent reporter into an endogenous AP-1 target locus, sort the top and bottom expression deciles, regrow each population, and measure how quickly the full distribution is regenerated. The relaxation timescale, compared with cell-cycle time and mRNA/protein half-lives, reveals whether the state is heritably locked or merely slow-fluctuating noise.

question: ap1
title: Prime-and-challenge transcriptional priming with enhancer dissection
description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wait until AP-1 protein and target transcripts return to baseline, then rechallenge and measure the speed and amplitude of the nascent transcriptional response. CRISPR deletion of individual AP-1-bound enhancers, and a heterologous second stimulus, then test whether the stored memory is localized to specific elements and whether it is stimulus-specific or general.

question: ap1
title: Epoch-resolved degron mapping of when AP-1 is actually needed
description: Tag FOS and JUN with auxin- or dTAG-inducible degrons and deplete them in narrow windows — during the priming stimulus, during the washout/storage interval, or only at the moment of restimulation — then score the primed response. This dissociates AP-1's role in writing the memory, holding it, and reading it out, which a simple knockout cannot do and which is the single most diagnostic experiment for calling AP-1 a memory mechanism rather than just a signal transducer.

question: ap1
title: Heritability half-life from sister- and cousin-cell correlations
description: Combine heritable clonal barcoding with single-cell multiome (or live imaging of an AP-1 reporter) to measure how the correlation in AP-1 target expression and AP-1-site accessibility decays as a function of the number of divisions separating two related cells. The resulting correlation decay constant gives a quantitative memory half-life in generations, and comparing it to the AP-1 protein half-life tests whether the memory outlives its putative carrier.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic history-writing with a cross-stimulus generalization matrix
description: Use optogenetic control of ERK or JNK to deliver precisely defined pulse histories (amplitude, duration, number, spacing) that are otherwise impossible to control, then read out the response to a later challenge. Extending this to a prime-A/challenge-B matrix across different stimuli tests whether AP-1 stores a stimulus-specific trace or a generic one — specificity is the property that separates real memory from general hypersensitivity.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic TRE arrays as a minimal sufficient memory element
description: Build a library of integrated reporters that vary the number, affinity, and spacing of AP-1 motifs plus the presence of nearby cofactor motifs, stimulate once, and measure how long each architecture sustains a primed state. This moves from correlation at endogenous loci to a sufficiency claim and yields a design rule for how much memory a given enhancer architecture can hold.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic retention and single-molecule residence time in primed cells
description: Ask how AP-1 physically persists by imaging Halo-tagged JUN/FOS retention on mitotic chromosomes (with mitotic CUT&RUN as the genomic counterpart) and by single-molecule tracking of bound fraction and residence time in naive versus primed cells. Longer residence or bookmarking in primed cells would supply the mechanistic carrier for heritability, whereas unchanged kinetics would point the memory to chromatin or cofactors instead.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-washout-rechallenge with a tunable memory decay curve
description: Deliver a defined pulse of AP-1 activation (optogenetic FOS/JUN or a short growth-factor/stress pulse), wash out, then rechallenge cohorts at systematically increasing gaps to measure how long the primed response amplitude persists. The resulting decay curve gives a quantitative memory half-life that can be compared directly against AP-1 protein and mRNA turnover rates, distinguishing true memory from slow relaxation.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis test for bistable AP-1 feedback
description: Titrate an AP-1-activating input up from zero and down from saturation, measuring steady-state AP-1 reporter output at matched doses along each arm. Non-overlapping up and down curves at the same dose would demonstrate hysteresis, the hallmark of a self-sustaining feedback memory rather than a passive stimulus-tracking response.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell and lineage-tree partitioning of AP-1 state heritability
description: Combine live imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter with tracked lineage trees (or expressed lineage barcodes with single-cell multiome) to compute how correlated AP-1 state is between sisters, cousins, and unrelated cells. This partitions AP-1 variation into heritable versus transient components and directly estimates how many generations the state survives.

question: ap1
title: Degron separation of AP-1 protein from its chromatin footprint
description: After priming, acutely degrade FOS/JUN family members with dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons during the memory window, then restore them and rechallenge. If the primed response survives transient AP-1 loss, memory is stored in chromatin or another substrate rather than in persisting AP-1 protein itself.

question: ap1
title: Chromatin-perturbation screen during the memory window
description: Apply inhibitors or targeted knockdowns of candidate storage machinery (SWI/SNF, EP300, BRD4, HDACs, specific histone modifiers) only in the interval between priming and rechallenge, with no perturbation during either event. Hits that selectively erase the primed response identify the physical substrate holding the AP-1 memory, and distinguish it from effects on AP-1 signaling itself.

question: ap1
title: Decoupling writing from maintenance with acute AP-1 degradation
description: Establish a primed state with a defined stimulus, then use dTAG or auxin degrons to acutely deplete JUN/FOS family proteins only after the stimulus is withdrawn, and ask whether the accessible enhancers, enhancer-promoter contacts, and faster re-induction survive. If memory persists without AP-1 protein, AP-1 writes a chromatin mark rather than being the memory itself; if memory collapses, AP-1 is the continuously required carrier.

question: ap1
title: Division-counted memory half-life from lineage-resolved live imaging
description: Image a destabilized AP-1 activity reporter in a tracked lineage tree after a stimulus pulse and compute mother-daughter, sister, and cousin correlations to extract a memory half-life measured in cell divisions rather than hours. Repeating this in cycling versus arrested cells separates replication-coupled dilution of the state from simple time-dependent decay, which is the key discriminator between chromatin-based inheritance and slow protein turnover.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis scan for bistability in the AP-1 feedback loop
description: Titrate a tunable AP-1 input (optogenetic FOS/JUN or a graded growth factor dose) upward in one population and downward in a pre-activated population, then read AP-1 target expression per cell at matched doses. A reproducible gap between the ascending and descending branches is direct evidence that AP-1 autoregulation supports two stable states, which is the mechanistic signature a memory module should have.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 motif reporter series testing sufficiency
description: Integrate at a single safe-harbor locus a library of reporters that systematically vary AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and neighboring pioneer-factor motifs, then measure both acute induction and persistence after the stimulus ends. This asks whether AP-1 sites alone are sufficient to encode memory or only do so in specific sequence contexts, cleanly separating AP-1's inducer role from its memory role.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific maintenance in hybrid cells
description: In F1 hybrid or heterozygously motif-edited cells, perform allele-resolved ATAC and nascent transcription after stimulus withdrawal to test whether the primed state is maintained in cis at individual alleles. Persistent allelic asymmetry would show the memory is written into the chromatin of the locus, while symmetric behavior would indicate memory lives in trans in the cellular AP-1 pool.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-resolved heritability of AP-1 activity
description: Barcode single cells (LARRY/Watermelon-style) and profile sister and cousin cells by scRNA-seq or live AP-1 reporter imaging to compute how AP-1 activity autocorrelates across divisions. Comparing the decay constant for AP-1 target output against other signaling-responsive programs gives a quantitative, assumption-light test of whether AP-1 state is actually heritable rather than just stimulus-driven.

question: ap1
title: Degron separation of establishment from maintenance
description: Tag FOS/JUN with a degron and deplete AP-1 either before stimulation or hours after the state has formed, then read out accessibility (ATAC) and restimulation response. True memory predicts that the primed state persists after AP-1 protein is removed, whereas a purely sustained-signal model predicts collapse.

question: ap1
title: Prime-rest-rechallenge transcriptional priming assay
description: Deliver a defined transient stimulus, wash out and rest cells for varying intervals and division numbers, then rechallenge and measure the amplitude and latency of AP-1 target induction by nascent RNA (TT-seq or single-molecule FISH). Faster or larger secondary responses that decay with time and divisions directly quantify the strength and lifetime of the memory.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 site array for sufficiency
description: Integrate arrays of AP-1 motifs (and motif-scrambled controls) at a neutral genomic locus adjacent to a reporter, then drive AP-1 binding transiently with an optogenetic or chemically inducible Fos/Jun module. Persistent reporter expression and accessibility after induction ends would show AP-1 binding is sufficient to write a heritable state, independent of pre-existing locus context.

question: ap1
title: Does the memory survive replication and mitosis?
description: Compare persistence of AP-1-primed accessibility in cycling cells versus cells arrested pharmacologically or in post-mitotic states, and perform mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN to test for AP-1 bookmarking. This distinguishes a slowly-decaying protein/chromatin state from a genuinely replication-heritable epigenetic mechanism and identifies the step where memory is copied or lost.

question: ap1
title: Sister-clone splitting to quantify heritability of AP-1 state
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into sister subclones after a defined number of divisions, and compare AP-1 reporter activity and AP-1 target-gene expression between sisters versus random pairs. The intraclass correlation as a function of elapsed divisions directly yields the memory half-life of the AP-1 state and separates true heredity from transient, stimulus-driven fluctuation.

question: ap1
title: Washout-and-rechallenge priming assay
description: Transiently induce AP-1 (growth factor, optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization, or an inducible construct), wash out, wait for AP-1 protein and transcript levels to return to baseline, then re-stimulate and measure response amplitude and kinetics. A faster or larger secondary response in previously stimulated cells—when current AP-1 levels are indistinguishable—is the cleanest functional signature of stored memory rather than persistent signaling.

question: ap1
title: Decoupling stored chromatin state from ongoing AP-1 activity by acute degron depletion
description: Use a dTAG/auxin degron on FOS and JUN family members to acutely remove AP-1 protein for hours to days, then restore it, measuring enhancer accessibility (ATAC) and target expression before, during, and after. If the pre-depletion enhancer landscape is re-established in the same cells, the memory is carried by something other than AP-1 occupancy itself; if it resets to a naive state, AP-1 occupancy is the memory.

question: ap1
title: Prospective sorting plus retrospective lineage tracing of AP-1-high cells
description: Sort AP-1-reporter-high and -low cells from a barcoded population, let each grow out for several weeks, then measure both the reporter distribution and a functional fate (e.g., drug survival or invasion) in the progeny. Combining this with barcode recovery lets you ask whether a given clone's AP-1 state at time zero predicts its fate at time T, which is the operational definition of a memory mechanism.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis and bistability mapping of the AP-1 dose response
description: Expose cells to a graded series of stimulus doses from below and from above (stepping up from zero versus stepping down from saturating stimulus) and measure single-cell AP-1 activity at matched steady-state doses. Overlapping curves indicate a passive relay; a hysteresis loop with a bistable regime would show AP-1 is wired as a self-sustaining memory switch, and mutating AP-1 motifs in FOS/JUN's own regulatory elements should collapse the loop.

question: ap1
title: Twin-cell split assay with lineage barcodes to measure the memory half-life
description: Barcode cells, deliver a brief AP-1-activating stimulus, then let clones divide and physically split sister/cousin cells so one is profiled (scRNA-seq or reporter level) while the relative is challenged later. The concordance between relatives as a function of elapsed generations gives a quantitative memory half-life in divisions, and distinguishes true heritable memory from slowly decaying protein that is diluted equally in all cells.

question: ap1
title: Degron time-window dissection of writing, maintaining, and reading
description: Use dTAG or auxin degrons on endogenously tagged FOS and JUN to remove AP-1 protein only during the stimulus, only during the quiescent interval, or only at the time of the second challenge. If memory survives depletion during the interval but not during the stimulus, the information is stored in something AP-1 deposits rather than in AP-1 itself.

question: ap1
title: Post-replication single-molecule footprinting of AP-1 enhancers
description: Combine nascent-strand labeling with single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) to ask whether AP-1 motifs on newly replicated daughter chromatin are re-opened and co-occupied in cis, and how fast. This tests the central requirement for epigenetic memory, that the state is re-established on both daughter molecules after each round of replication.

question: ap1
title: Two-pulse potentiation kinetics and information-theoretic memory capacity
description: Deliver pairs of stimulus pulses with systematically varied inter-pulse intervals and read out single-cell AP-1 target induction, fitting the decay of potentiation to get a memory time constant. Computing the mutual information between past stimulus history and the current single-cell state quantifies how many bits of history AP-1 actually stores, and whether memory is graded or bistable.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic enhancer library screen for memory-competent AP-1 grammar
description: Build a reporter library systematically varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and flanking partner motifs, integrate it at a fixed locus, and sort for reporters that stay on long after the stimulus ends. This converts a correlative question into a sufficiency test and reveals which cis-architectures are necessary to convert a transient AP-1 input into a persistent state.

question: ap1
title: Storage-window degron: is AP-1 the memory, or just the writer?
description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on endogenous FOS, JUN, JUNB and FOSL1 so that AP-1 can be eliminated selectively during the interval between a priming stimulus and a rechallenge, leaving induction and readout phases intact. If priming survives AP-1 loss during storage, AP-1 writes the memory into chromatin; if it collapses, AP-1 protein persistence is itself the memory trace, and the two cases are cleanly distinguished by a single timing variable.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule footprinting of primed enhancers
description: Apply long-read methylation footprinting (Fiber-seq or SAMOSA) to naive, stimulated, and rested cells to ask whether primed AP-1 enhancers show a bimodal population in which a subset of molecules remain fully open and bound, versus a uniform intermediate state across all molecules. Population-average ATAC cannot tell these apart, yet they imply completely different memory mechanisms (a stable per-allele latch versus a graded relaxation).

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping in stimulus dose space
description: Measure AP-1 target output across an ascending and then descending ladder of stimulus doses with matched equilibration times, testing for a hysteresis loop in which cells approaching from the high-dose side stay active at doses that cannot activate naive cells. An open loop is a direct, model-free signature of bistable memory, and the loop width quantifies memory depth; its absence argues for slow relaxation instead.

question: ap1
title: Mitosis-and-replication tracking of the primed state
description: Combine clonal barcoding with division counting (dye dilution or FUCCI-gated sorting) and single-cell multiome to measure how many cell divisions a primed AP-1 chromatin state survives, and whether sister cells inherit priming concordantly. Heritability across mitosis plus concordance between sisters is the operational definition of cellular memory and separates it from a long-lived but non-heritable cytoplasmic state.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 site arrays as a tunable memory element
description: Integrate at a fixed safe-harbor locus a panel of reporters whose enhancers differ in AP-1 site number, affinity, spacing and neighboring cofactor motifs, then run identical prime–wait–rechallenge protocols on each. This converts a correlational question into a design rule: it identifies the minimal cis architecture sufficient to store a transient AP-1 input and shows which features set memory duration.

question: ap1
title: Phase-resolved degron dissection of write, hold, and read
description: Tag endogenous c-Jun/c-Fos (and a second redundant family member) with dTAG or auxin degrons and deplete AP-1 acutely in non-overlapping windows: only during the priming stimulus, only during the memory interval with no stimulus present, and only at the moment of restimulation. If memory survives depletion during the interval but not during priming, AP-1 writes but does not store the trace, which directly separates causality from maintenance and avoids the confounds of constitutive knockouts.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell split assay with heritable barcodes
description: Lineage-barcode cells (ClonMapper/Watermelon), prime the population, then physically split sister cells after one division and challenge one sister while profiling the other, repeating across increasing numbers of divisions. This distinguishes true per-cell heritable memory from selection of a pre-existing responsive subpopulation, and quantifies memory as a probability of concordance between relatives rather than a bulk average.

question: ap1
title: Transfer-function mapping to expose latent (invisible) memory
description: Instead of asking whether a resting AP-1 state persists, measure the full dose-response and kinetic transfer function to a second stimulus across a matrix of priming doses and rest intervals, using a live AP-1 (TRE) reporter plus a target-gene reporter. Memory then appears as a shift in threshold, amplitude, or latency even when baseline chromatin and transcriptome have returned to naive, capturing primed states that steady-state assays declare erased.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-composition barcoding of the AP-1 state
description: Use subunit-resolved CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag for Fos, FosB, Fra-1, Fra-2, JunB, JunD, c-Jun and ATF3 at matched timepoints, combined with split-reporter or proximity-ligation dimer sensors and rapid-exchange (FRAP / SNAP-tag pulse-chase) measurements at the same loci. The test is whether the memory is encoded as a stable swap in dimer identity and residence time at shared sites rather than as a change in total AP-1 output.

question: ap1
title: Cell-versus-matrix swap to localize where the memory is stored
description: Prime cells on a deformable or decellularizable substrate, then cross-transplant: primed cells onto naive-cell-derived matrix, naive cells onto primed-cell-derived matrix, plus conditioned-medium swaps and serial replating onto fresh stiffness-matched surfaces. If recall follows the matrix rather than the cell, AP-1 is a mechanochemical relay re-reading an extracellular trace, and the intracellular 'memory' is reconstructed each time rather than stored.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping instead of decay curves
description: Using a live AP-1 activity reporter, drive cells up and then back down a graded stimulus dose (e.g. serum, TGF-beta, stiffness, or an optogenetic FOS/JUN input) and ask whether the up- and down-going dose-response curves separate into a hysteresis loop with a bistable region, rather than retracing one another. This distinguishes a true self-sustaining memory state from slow first-order relaxation, which no 'state persists for N days' experiment can do.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved pulse-chase of who actually stores the information
description: Endogenously HaloTag every major AP-1 subunit, then use pulse-chase labeling plus CUT&RUN and sequential (re-)ChIP to measure, for each specific dimer, protein lifetime and residence at candidate memory enhancers across the memory window. If memory duration tracks one long-lived species (e.g. a FosB/deltaFosB- or JUND-containing dimer) and not aggregate motif accessibility, the storage element is a particular dimer, not 'AP-1'.

question: ap1
title: Swap the matrix, not the cell
