description: Test whether memory is extrinsic by moving 'remembering' cells onto decellularized naive ECM (and naive cells onto ECM deposited by remembering cells), and by replating at clonal density in fresh matrix with autocrine signaling blocked. If memory transfers with the matrix or evaporates when self-deposited ECM and autocrine loops are removed, AP-1 is a continuously re-driven reporter of an environmental store rather than the memory itself.

question: ap1
title: Locus-targeted write/erase to test sufficiency and necessity of the footprint
description: Use dCas9-recruited synthetic AP-1 activation domains to transiently write AP-1 occupancy at a handful of candidate memory enhancers with no upstream stimulus, remove the recruiter, and ask whether the downstream state persists; conversely, use an acute AP-1 degron applied only after the state is established to test whether AP-1 is required to maintain, not just to establish, the state. Pairing this with inhibition of candidate chromatin writers separates AP-1 as the cause from AP-1 accessibility as a readout.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded single-cell tracking across controlled division rates
description: Combine heritable barcoding (Rewind/ClonMapper-style) with longitudinal live imaging of an AP-1 reporter to measure sister-sister and mother-daughter correlation decay, giving a memory half-life in generations versus in hours; then repeat with division rate manipulated (contact inhibition, serum starvation, CDK inhibition, or post-mitotic cells). If memory decays per unit time rather than per division, and if barcodes show the persistent state is re-entered by naive cells rather than only inherited by a pre-existing clone, the mechanism is neither replication-coupled nor selection.

question: ap1
title: Forgetting curves from a two-hit stimulus grid
description: Breaks the 'stable switch / no second stimulus' assumption: deliver stimulus 1, then stimulus 2 after a logarithmically spaced interval series (1 h to 6 weeks), and read out the full dose-response of the second response rather than a single dose. Fitting the decay of the memory index gives a timescale that can be compared directly against measured FOS/JUN protein half-lives and chromatin mark turnover, distinguishing a bistable latch from a slowly leaking analog trace.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic sufficiency: writing memory with a stimulus-free AP-1 pulse
description: Breaks the 'necessity equals mechanism' assumption: use an optogenetic or chemically dimerizable FOS-JUN (or dCas9-fused AP-1 activation domain targeted to specific motif sets) to deliver a defined-amplitude, defined-duration AP-1 pulse in otherwise unstimulated cells, then test whether the later response to a real stimulus is shifted exactly as it is in genuinely pre-stimulated cells. Pair with an acute degron that removes AP-1 only during the quiescent interval to separate writing from maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved accounting of writer versus keeper
description: Breaks the 'AP-1 is one entity' assumption: endogenously tag each FOS- and JUN-family paralog with distinct degrons and fluorophores, track absolute per-cell protein abundance and dimer composition over the memory interval by live imaging plus proximity ligation or dimer-specific CUT&RUN, and degrade each paralog individually in narrow time windows. This identifies which dimer occupies memory loci during the interval, which is merely transient during induction, and whether composition switching (e.g., FOS to FRA1) is the actual carrier.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded single-cell tracing of memory through division
description: Breaks the 'population average equals per-cell heritable memory' assumption: heritably barcode cells before stimulus 1, let them divide a controlled number of times, then apply stimulus 2 and read out scRNA/scATAC with barcodes so that sibling cells can be compared. This separates true heritable per-cell memory (siblings concordant, memory present in all cells) from selection of a pre-existing responsive subpopulation (memory confined to specific clones) and quantifies how many divisions the trace survives.

question: ap1
title: Medium-swap and nuclear-transplant tests of where the trace actually lives
description: Breaks the 'AP-1 is the storage medium' assumption: cross-transfer conditioned medium, decellularized ECM, and cells between naive and pre-stimulated conditions, and separately move nuclei or chromatin from pre-stimulated cells into naive cytoplasm (heterokaryon or nuclear transfer, or permeabilized-cell reconstitution). If the memory travels with the medium or matrix rather than the nucleus, AP-1 is a readout of an extracellular loop; CRISPRi or scarless motif deletion at candidate memory enhancers then tests whether the AP-1 sites themselves are causally load-bearing.

question: ap1
title: Switch AP-1 off after the first signal
description: Use a degron to remove the relevant AP-1 subunits (for example FOSL2 or JUN) only after the first stimulus has ended, then check whether the faster response to a second stimulus disappears. If AP-1 is only needed during the first exposure, it is starting the memory, not holding it (tests assumption 1).

question: ap1
title: Separate open chromatin from ongoing binding
description: Over the period between stimuli, measure open chromatin (ATAC-seq) and AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN) at the same sites over time. Then use dCas9-KRAB or dCas9-p300 to close or open individual AP-1 sites and see if that removes or creates memory at nearby genes (tests assumption 2).

question: ap1
title: Track memory in single cells with barcodes
description: Label cells with heritable barcodes and do single-cell RNA plus chromatin profiling before the first stimulus, after it, and after the second. This shows whether the cells with a stronger second response came from the AP-1-high cells that responded first, or from cells that were already primed before any stimulus (tests assumptions 3 and 6).

question: ap1
title: Check whether memory survives cell division
description: Use a live-cell AP-1 activity reporter with time-lapse imaging to compare related cells (sisters and cousins) across several divisions after the stimulus. Measure how quickly the reporter level and the faster second response fade per division, and compare normal cells with cells whose division has been stopped (tests assumption 4).

question: ap1
title: Map which dimer pairs do what
description: Use a CRISPRi screen across AP-1 family members, or tethered dimers that force specific pairs, to test which ones are needed to set up the memory and which are needed to keep it. Back this up with mass spectrometry of AP-1 complexes, run on chromatin during the period between stimuli (tests assumption 5).

question: ap1
title: Naive-niche transplantation with ECM and secretome swaps
description: After stimulation and washout, serially transfer barcoded cells into decellularized naive ECM, defined hydrogels, or fresh media with blocking antibodies/receptor inhibitors against candidate autocrine ligands, and ask whether AP-1 activity and second-response priming travel with the cell or stay with the dish. The reciprocal transfer of naive cells onto conditioned matrix tests whether the 'memory' can be transplanted without any cell that experienced the stimulus.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved accounting of which AP-1 species carries memory
description: Combine endogenous tagging of multiple Fos/Jun/ATF members with pulse-chase proteomics, per-member CUT&RUN, and dimer-specific readouts (BiFC or proximity ligation) to measure which dimer composition persists after washout and at which loci, then use dimer-selective dominant negatives (A-Fos vs A-Jun) and member-specific degrons to ask which single species is required. The prediction to test is that a long-half-life member such as Fra-1/JunB, not the canonical c-Fos pulse, is the actual carrier.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron separation of storage from maintenance
description: Establish memory, then acutely deplete AP-1 protein with a dTAG/auxin degron for a defined window and restore it, measuring whether accessibility, histone marks and the primed second response survive the absence of the factor. Persistence through AP-1 removal means chromatin stores the memory; collapse means AP-1 occupancy itself is the store and the 'epigenetic' interpretation of the ATAC peak is wrong.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-resolved live imaging of memory half-life across divisions
description: Use a live-cell AP-1 transcriptional reporter plus clonal barcoding and continuous tracking through several divisions to compute mother-daughter and sister-sister correlation decay, and to score whether memory is re-established after each mitosis or passively diluted. This distinguishes a uniform population half-life from a rare subpopulation of long-memory cells, and yields the heritability coefficient that any memory claim requires.

question: ap1
title: Clamp-and-write test of sufficiency with AP-1 held constant
description: Use optogenetic or dox-tunable synthetic AP-1 to hold AP-1 activity at a fixed level in cells with different stimulus histories: if history still predicts future behavior at matched AP-1 activity, AP-1 is not the store but a relay. Conversely, deliver a defined synthetic AP-1 pulse to naive cells and challenge them with a panel of orthogonal stimuli to test whether AP-1 alone is sufficient to write a memory, and whether that memory is stimulus-specific or generic.

question: ap1
title: Clamp the upstream signal, not the factor
description: Targets the cell-autonomy assumption: after stimulus withdrawal, hold candidate upstream maintainers at defined levels during the memory window using optogenetic ERK/JNK clamps, MEK or FAK/ROCK inhibition, substrate-stiffness switching, and conditioned-medium swaps, then assay whether primed AP-1 accessibility and the enhanced second response survive. If memory only collapses when the upstream input is extinguished, AP-1 is a readout of a sustained signal rather than the storage device itself.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved encode-versus-maintain swap
description: Targets the 'AP-1 is one thing' assumption: build a panel of subunit-specific degrons (cFos, FosB/dFosB, JunB, JunD, ATF3, JDP2) combined with per-subunit CUT&RUN and dimer-specific proximity ligation or split-fluorophore reporters, and degrade each subunit selectively during encoding versus during maintenance. Rescue with a different subunit during the maintenance window to test whether the identity of the dimer that writes the state differs from the one that keeps it.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell and barcoded-clone priming assay
description: Targets the bulk-equals-single-cell assumption: lineage-barcode cells, live-image an AP-1 transcriptional reporter through a prime-rest-restimulate cycle, and compare second-response concordance between sister cells, clonal relatives, and unrelated cells, with split-clone scATAC at both time points. True per-cell memory predicts within-cell and sister concordance that exceeds what clone-level selection of pre-existing responders can explain.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron windows with footprint-resolution readout
description: Targets the continuous-occupancy assumption: deplete all AP-1 activity only after encoding is complete, using an auxin or dTAG degron plus a dominant-negative A-Fos, and ask whether the primed accessibility, nucleosome positioning, and accelerated second-response kinetics persist in the factor's absence. Pair with single-molecule footprinting, SLAM-seq, and histone-turnover measurement to identify what holds the state open if AP-1 is dispensable for maintenance.

question: ap1
title: Per-division versus per-hour decay accounting
description: Targets the persistence-equals-heritability assumption: measure the state's decay as a function of division number rather than elapsed time by varying proliferation rate (serum, CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, mitotic arrest), and simultaneously pulse-chase-label AP-1 protein with HaloTag or SNAP ligands to compare protein half-life to state half-life. Add live imaging of AP-1 during mitosis to test for bookmarking; memory that decays per division but outlives the protein implicates an actively re-established chromatin state rather than residual factor.

question: ap1
title: Environment clamp: strip the cell of every persistent input and ask if AP-1 state survives
description: Take cells that 'remember' a stimulus and systematically remove candidate continuous inputs, by serial single-cell isolation into fresh microwells, decellularization and replating onto naive matrix, and acute inhibition of MAPK/integrin/autocrine receptor signaling, then measure AP-1 occupancy and target expression. The reciprocal arm plates naive cells onto matrix deposited by remembering cells, which would show that the 'memory' is stored outside the cell entirely.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved occupancy time course rather than bulk AP-1 motif accessibility
description: Use subunit-specific CUT&RUN or sequential re-ChIP, plus split-fluorophore or proximity-ligation dimer reporters, to determine which specific FOS/JUN dimer occupies which enhancer at induction versus weeks later, and pair this with single-subunit degron panels to find which dimer is dispensable for writing but required for keeping the state.

question: ap1
title: Erase-and-watch: acute total AP-1 degradation followed by washout
description: Degrade all FOS/JUN family members with a multiplexed dTAG/auxin degron for a defined window in the remembering state, then restore them and ask whether the enhancer landscape and phenotype return. Spontaneous recovery means AP-1 is a readout of an upstream store; failure to recover means AP-1 itself, or chromatin it maintains, is the store.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic write-then-release test of sufficiency at defined loci
description: Recruit a FOS/JUN activation domain to specific candidate memory enhancers with dCas9 or a chemically induced dimerizer for a controlled pulse, remove the recruiter, and track whether the locus and the associated phenotype self-sustain. Titrating pulse amplitude and duration maps the threshold and dose-dependence of memory installation, which a knockout can never reveal.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-resolved decay constants and division-counting
description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with heritable barcoding and long-term imaging to extract per-lineage autocorrelation times, sister-cell correlation decay across divisions, and the fraction of lineages that remember. Comparing decay in cycling versus pharmacologically arrested or slowed cells distinguishes dilution-per-division from turnover-per-unit-time, converting 'is it memory?' into a measured timescale and heritability number.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-resolved memory map (breaks the 'AP-1 is one thing' assumption)
description: Endogenously tag each major Fos/Jun/ATF subunit and use sequential ChIP/CUT&RUN and dimerization-dependent split-fluorophore reporters to determine which specific dimer compositions occupy memory loci during induction versus maintenance versus recall. Pair with subunit-specific degrons to ask whether the dimer that establishes a site is the same one that maintains it.

question: ap1
title: Erase-and-restore kinetics with acute degron plus single-molecule tracking (breaks 'persistence = storage')
description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron to fully remove AP-1 protein for a defined window during the maintenance phase, then restore it and test recall; simultaneously measure AP-1 residence times and turnover by live single-molecule tracking and SNAP-tag pulse-chase. If memory survives transient total loss of AP-1, the information is stored elsewhere and AP-1 is a reader/relay; if it does not, AP-1 occupancy is itself the store.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic sufficiency test by targeted AP-1 writing (breaks the correlation-is-causation assumption)
description: Recruit a Fos/Jun bZIP effector to defined candidate memory enhancers with dCas9 in the absence of any stimulus, then withdraw recruitment and assay whether primed behavior appears days later; complement with base-edited destruction of individual endogenous AP-1 motifs to test necessity for maintenance separately from necessity for the acute response.

question: ap1
title: Memory transplantation across cells and matrix (breaks the cell-intrinsic assumption)
description: Test whether the primed state travels with the cell or with its environment by swapping decellularized ECM and conditioned medium between primed and naive cultures, co-culturing primed with naive cells, and transplanting primed cells into naive hosts (and vice versa). Readout is AP-1 site accessibility and recall competence in the recipient population.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic dose/duration/order encoding with clonal lineage recall (breaks the binary, population-average assumptions)
description: Deliver quantitatively defined ERK or Fos input patterns with optogenetics while live-imaging an endogenous AP-1 activity reporter, then barcode and track single lineages through division to a second, independent recall stimulus. This measures how much information (amplitude, duration, pulse order) the AP-1 state stores, its decay half-life, and how fast sister-cell correlations are lost.

question: ap1
title: Check whether genes in MemorySeq data that stay on or off for many cell divisions have nearby AP-1 sites
description: Use published MemorySeq data (Shaffer et al. 2020, Cell) that identify genes whose expression stays on or off across several generations of a clone. Test whether these 'memory genes' have more AP-1 motifs, and more AP-1 binding in public ENCODE ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq data, than non-memory genes with the same expression level, variability and baseline accessibility.

question: ap1
title: Measure how similar AP-1 activity is within barcoded clones
description: Reanalyze public lineage-barcoded single-cell RNA, ATAC or multiome datasets (e.g., FateMap, Rewind, LARRY, ClonMapper, CellTag-multi). Score each cell's TF motif accessibility with chromVAR, then compare how much more alike sister cells are than unrelated cells for AP-1 versus other TF families. Also test whether a cell's AP-1 activity at an early time point predicts the fate of its clone later on.

question: ap1
title: Compare how long AP-1 sites stay open with how long AP-1 itself is present after a stimulus is removed
description: Collect public time courses that include a withdrawal phase, such as inflammatory memory in epithelial stem cells (Larsen et al. 2021), trained immunity in macrophages, serum/TPA pulses and BRAF-inhibitor drug holidays in melanoma. Estimate how fast AP-1 FOS/JUN mRNA and protein disappear versus how fast chromatin at AP-1 motif sites closes. Use TOBIAS footprinting to tell whether AP-1 is still bound or has left an open 'scar' behind it. If sites stay open long after the factor is gone, that suggests AP-1 lays down a lasting mark.

question: ap1
title: Meta-analysis across systems: are AP-1 motifs specifically enriched at sites that stay open?
description: Gather public before/during/after chromatin datasets from many memory paradigms (inflammatory memory, trained immunity, wound healing, senescence, drug-tolerant persisters, T-cell exhaustion, activity-dependent neuronal enhancers). Classify the induced chromatin sites as persistent or transient. Then test whether AP-1 motifs are enriched at persistent sites compared with transient sites matched for GC content, induction strength and baseline accessibility. The matching controls for AP-1 being common at enhancers in general.

question: ap1
title: Test AP-1 knockout/inhibition data and mitotic binding data for whether AP-1 maintains memory
description: Reanalyze public datasets where AP-1 was knocked out or blocked with dominant-negative FOS or JUN, either before or after a priming stimulus (e.g., Vierbuchen et al. 2017; Fosl2/Jun knockouts in inflammatory-memory and T-cell studies). This tests whether AP-1 is needed only to set up lasting accessibility or also to keep it. Separately, check public mitotic ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq data to see whether AP-1 sites stay bound or open during mitosis, which would show whether AP-1 itself can carry the memory through cell division.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase decay kinetics of AP-1 binding versus chromatin accessibility
description: Deliver a transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA or a brief MEK-inhibitor pulse), wash out, and collect a time course out to 2-3 weeks for low-input ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for FOSL1/JUN, asking whether accessibility at AP-1 sites persists after AP-1 protein has returned to baseline. Roughly 30-40 libraries with in-house Tn5 and a shared NovaSeq lane fits comfortably under $20k and directly distinguishes a self-erasing signal from a durable chromatin mark.

question: ap1
title: Degron washout test of whether AP-1 is required to maintain versus establish a state
description: Knock a dTAG or auxin degron into an endogenous AP-1 subunit, then compare acute depletion during state establishment versus after a state has been stably held, reading out accessibility at a few hundred AP-1 loci by targeted ATAC or a small qPCR/amplicon panel. The informative result is whether an established state survives AP-1 removal and whether it re-establishes after degrader washout, which is the operational definition of a memory-maintaining factor.

question: ap1
title: Clonal barcoding to ask whether AP-1 state is heritable through cell divisions
description: Combine a lentiviral barcode library with FACS sorting of an AP-1 activity reporter, split each sorted population, and sequence barcodes plus re-measure reporter distributions over ~20 divisions to test whether high- and low-AP-1 clones regenerate the parental distribution or stay fixed. Barcode amplicon sequencing is cheap (a few thousand dollars), and the division-number at which memory decays gives a quantitative half-life of the state.

question: ap1
title: Second-stimulus priming assay for faster or stronger reactivation
description: Prime cells with a stimulus, let AP-1 activity fully return to baseline, then restimulate and compare induction kinetics and amplitude of AP-1 target genes against naive cells using a modest qPCR or 3'-end RNA-seq panel. Faster or larger secondary responses are the classic signature of transcriptional memory, and the assay costs only reagents and a few sequencing lanes.

question: ap1
title: Live single-cell imaging of AP-1 reporter dynamics across lineages
description: Use a stable AP-1-responsive fluorescent reporter plus a nuclear marker, image dividing cells for several days on an existing widefield or confocal system, and build lineage trees to quantify mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations in reporter level. Mother-daughter correlation that decays slowly relative to sister correlation would show heritable, cell-intrinsic memory rather than shared microenvironment, and the main cost is reporter construction plus imaging time.

question: ap1
title: Prime–rest–rechallenge imaging of single cells with lineage tracking
description: Using cells with endogenously tagged AP-1 subunits (e.g., c-Fos, c-Jun, FosL1) plus a short-lived AP-1-responsive transcriptional reporter, image continuously through a stimulus pulse, a long washout, and a second identical pulse, tracking each lineage. Memory is supported if a cell's second-response amplitude or latency is predicted by its first response beyond what current AP-1 levels explain.

question: ap1
title: Decay-versus-persistence kinetics after signal withdrawal
description: Measure, in single cells, the time constants of nuclear AP-1 protein, AP-1 reporter output, and a downstream phenotype after acute removal of the stimulus (including with inducible-degron removal of specific AP-1 subunits). A memory mechanism should show reporter/phenotype persistence substantially outlasting the inducing signal, and that persistence should collapse when AP-1 is degraded during the rest period.

question: ap1
title: Mother–daughter and sister-cell correlation of AP-1 state across divisions
description: Track AP-1 reporter intensity through mitosis in long movies to quantify how strongly daughters inherit the mother's AP-1 level and how long sister-cell correlations decay relative to unrelated cells. Heritable, slowly decaying correlations that exceed the lifetime of the AP-1 proteins themselves argue for a self-propagating memory rather than passive protein dilution.

question: ap1
title: Optogenetic writing of defined AP-1 histories to test sufficiency
description: Use a light-controlled AP-1 dimer (e.g., photo-dimerizable Fos/Jun or LOV-caged activation domain) to impose precisely timed amplitude/duration/pulse-number histories in single cells while imaging the reporter and a phenotypic marker. If AP-1 stores memory, the retained downstream state should depend on the integrated history (total dose, pulse number) rather than only on the instantaneous light level.

question: ap1
title: Live readout of AP-1 chromatin residence and target-locus accessibility over time
description: Combine single-molecule tracking / FRAP of tagged AP-1 to measure bound-fraction and residence times with a live chromatin-accessibility or locus-visualization readout (e.g., ANCHOR/ParB-labeled enhancer, or nucleosome-sensor reporter) at a key target enhancer before, during, and long after stimulation. A memory role predicts that AP-1-dependent increases in enhancer accessibility and rapid-rebinding behavior persist after signal removal and are lost upon acute AP-1 degradation.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-washout-rechallenge chromatin time course
description: Expose cells to a brief, defined stimulus pulse (e.g. TNF, serum, or a MEK inhibitor), wash it out, and then profile ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun family members at a dense series of timepoints spanning hours to weeks after washout. Memory is supported if a subset of AP-1-bound accessible regions remains open long after AP-1 protein levels and upstream signaling have returned to baseline, and if rechallenge produces a faster or larger response specifically at those retained sites.

question: ap1
title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter lineage tracing through division
description: Use a non-integrating or pre-existing AP-1 activity reporter line and long-term live imaging to track individual cells and their progeny through many divisions, quantifying how reporter intensity correlates between mother and daughter and between sisters as a function of elapsed time. The decay constant of this correlation gives a direct, model-free measurement of how long AP-1 state information persists and whether it survives mitosis, which is the defining test of heritable memory versus transient signaling.

question: ap1
title: Pharmacological clamp-and-release to separate maintenance from establishment
description: Use small-molecule AP-1 inhibitors (e.g. T-5224 or a JNK inhibitor) applied either only during the initial stimulus or only during the post-stimulus memory window, then assay the response to a later rechallenge. If blocking AP-1 during establishment abolishes memory but blocking it afterward does not, AP-1 writes the memory; if blocking it during the window also erases memory, AP-1 is required continuously to maintain it, which distinguishes a writer from a self-sustaining latch.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell multiome correlation of AP-1 motif accessibility with response history
description: Perform joint single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling on a population carrying heterogeneous stimulus histories (created by staggered pulse timing or by sorting cells on an early response reporter), and ask whether per-cell AP-1 motif accessibility scores predict that cell's transcriptional response to a subsequent challenge. A strong single-cell predictive relationship, stronger than that for other motif families, would show AP-1 chromatin state is the physical carrier of the remembered information rather than a correlate of it.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and post-mitotic reestablishment kinetics
description: Synchronize cells pharmacologically (e.g. thymidine block and release, or nocodazole arrest), then measure AP-1 factor retention on mitotic chromosomes by imaging and by CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic and early-G1 cells, tracking how quickly accessibility and transcription are restored at previously induced loci. Retention of a subset of AP-1 on condensed chromatin plus accelerated reactivation of exactly those loci in G1 would provide a concrete molecular mechanism for how the memory crosses cell division.

question: ap1
title: Serial-amputation priming of AP-1 regeneration enhancers in zebrafish fins
description: Amputate caudal fins, allow complete regeneration and a long rest period, then re-amputate and ask whether previously injured tissue responds faster or more strongly, while profiling ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN (Fosl1a, Junba, H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at AP-1-bound tissue-regeneration enhancer elements at matched timepoints. A memory model predicts residual primed chromatin (retained accessibility or H3K4me1 without H3K27ac) at these enhancers long after the first regenerate is complete, and that fosl1a/junb mutants or enhancer-motif deletions erase the accelerated second response.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase degron separation of AP-1 initiation from maintenance in Drosophila imaginal discs
description: Use auxin-inducible or GFP-nanobody degrons to deplete Jra/Kayak protein at defined times after genetic ablation of a wing disc, distinguishing whether AP-1 is needed only to establish the damage-responsive state or continuously to maintain it, with G-TRACE lineage labeling of AP-1-reporter-positive cells to track how long descendants retain the state. Measuring the decay of target accessibility and expression after acute AP-1 removal gives a direct half-life for AP-1-independent memory versus AP-1-dependent persistence.

question: ap1
title: Inheritance of AP-1 occupancy and state through mitosis in zebrafish melanoma cells
description: In ZMEL1 zebrafish melanoma cells, perform single-molecule tracking of HaloTag-Fosl1a/Junb to measure residence times and mitotic chromosome retention, combined with mitotic CUT&RUN to test for bookmarking of AP-1 target enhancers. Pair this with clonal barcoding and sister-cell split assays (scRNA-seq of separated daughters) to quantify how many divisions an AP-1-high transcriptional state persists and whether that heritability predicts drug-tolerant behavior.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 pulses to map the dose-duration requirements for memory formation
description: In Drosophila S2 cells (or zebrafish embryos), deliver calibrated optogenetic or dCas9-recruited AP-1 activation pulses at an endogenous or integrated reporter locus, varying amplitude and duration, then withdraw the stimulus and measure how long accessibility, histone marks, and expression persist. This sufficiency test defines whether there is a threshold pulse that converts a transient input into a self-sustaining state, and whether memory decays by dilution at division or by time-dependent chromatin reversion (distinguished with cell-cycle arrest).

question: ap1
title: Does AP-1 write or read positional memory in axolotl limb regeneration?
description: Profile AP-1 motif accessibility and Fos/Jun binding in connective-tissue cells from proximal versus distal limb levels before injury, during the AP-1 injury pulse, and in blastemas, including classic proximal-to-distal grafts and retinoic-acid proximalization that experimentally rewrite positional memory. If AP-1 is a memory mechanism rather than a generic injury switch, position-specific chromatin differences should be stored at AP-1-bound elements before injury and be reset by treatments that reprogram positional identity; AP-1 inhibition (dominant-negative A-Fos) should then disrupt memory recall without blocking wound healing.

question: ap1
title: Pulse–chase hysteresis assay: does AP-1 activity persist after the signal is gone?
description: Deliver graded, defined-duration pulses of an AP-1-activating stimulus (TPA, serum/growth factor, or substrate stiffness) and then withdraw it, sampling RNA-seq plus a TRE-driven destabilized-fluorophore reporter at 0, 6, 24, 48, 96 h and 1 week to measure the decay timescale of AP-1 target output relative to FOS/JUN protein half-life. The key memory signature is hysteresis: cells approaching the same final stimulus level from above versus below should settle into different stable AP-1 output states, which is a 6–8 week experiment with a dose×history matrix read out by flow cytometry.

question: ap1
title: Degron separation of establishment versus maintenance
description: Knock dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons into endogenous FOSL1/JUN (or express a dominant-negative A-FOS under a Tet promoter) so AP-1 can be removed acutely either during a priming stimulus or only after the primed state is established, then compare ATAC-seq and RNA-seq outcomes. A true memory mechanism requires continuous AP-1 occupancy for maintenance, so the informative result is whether late depletion collapses the primed state (AP-1 is the memory carrier) or leaves it intact (AP-1 only writes a state stored elsewhere, e.g., in chromatin or DNA methylation).

question: ap1
title: Latent-enhancer priming and second-stimulus amplification
description: Run matched ATAC-seq and FOS/JUN CUT&RUN time courses across stimulus, washout, and re-stimulation, asking whether AP-1 motif-containing peaks opened during the first exposure remain accessible days after AP-1 binding has decayed, and whether those specific loci show faster/larger induction on a second exposure. Quantifying the fraction of primed peaks and the magnitude of the re-stimulation boost (with nascent transcription by SLAM-seq or EU-seq) directly tests the 'latent enhancer' model of AP-1 memory within roughly two months.

question: ap1
title: Clone-splitting heritability test with barcode lineage tracing
description: Sort cells on an AP-1 activity reporter into high and low bins, let each bin expand for 5–10 divisions, then re-measure the distribution and compute the memory half-life in generations; in parallel, use a lentiviral barcode library so sister cells from the same clone can be split across plates and compared. Strong within-clone concordance of AP-1 state relative to between-clone variance (an intraclass correlation estimate) distinguishes mitotically heritable memory from fast stochastic fluctuation, and can be run in ~10 weeks in a fast-cycling line.

question: ap1
title: Targeted AP-1 recruitment as a sufficiency test
description: Use dCas9 fused to a JUN or FOS activation domain (or a chemically induced dimerization recruitment system) to pulse AP-1 onto a handful of endogenous primed enhancers for 24–48 h, then release and track locus accessibility, target gene expression, and reporter output for two weeks. If a transient synthetic AP-1 pulse alone installs a self-sustaining accessible state at those loci in the absence of any upstream signal, that is causal evidence that AP-1 writes rather than merely reports cellular memory.

question: ap1
title: Split-clone twin assay for heritable AP-1 state
description: Lineage-barcode a population, let it expand, then split each clone's descendants into two dishes: harvest one immediately for scATAC/scRNA (AP-1 motif accessibility, FOS/JUN/FRA-1 levels) and challenge the other with a stimulus and harvest once for recall magnitude. Clone-level correlation between the baseline AP-1 state in one twin and the recall response in the other demonstrates a heritable, cell-intrinsic AP-1 memory rather than transient signaling noise.

question: ap1
title: Degron cohorts that separate storage from readout
description: Use dTAG/auxin-degron FOS, JUN, and FRA-1 lines with a pulse stimulus, then degrade AP-1 in different cohorts during distinct windows (during the pulse, during the stimulus-free interval, or only at re-challenge), with each dish measured exactly once at a fixed endpoint. If degradation only during the stimulus-free interval erases enhanced recall, AP-1 protein is actively maintaining the memory, not merely reading it out.

question: ap1
title: Division-resolved memory via dye dilution at a single endpoint
description: Label cells with CellTrace/CFSE before a priming pulse and, at one harvest, use dye intensity to read out each cell's division history while simultaneously measuring AP-1 target transcripts and AP-1 motif accessibility by flow-sorted scATAC or single-cell imaging. This converts a time course into one snapshot and tests the defining property of epigenetic memory: whether the AP-1-associated state survives a quantifiable number of mitoses.

question: ap1
title: Decoupling latent enhancer accessibility from AP-1 occupancy
description: In a cohort series of primed-and-rested versus naive cells, each profiled once, combine CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN/FRA-1, ATAC footprinting, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, and CpG methylation at the same loci. Memory encoded by persistent AP-1 occupancy predicts footprints without ongoing stimulus, whereas accessible AP-1 motifs that are unoccupied would instead implicate a handoff to chromatin marks, distinguishing AP-1-as-storage from AP-1-as-writer.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic locus writing and release with dCas9-tethered Jun
description: Tether a dox-inducible dCas9-JUN (and a DNA-binding-dead AP-1 control) to a naive reporter locus, withdraw dox, and assay independent dishes at a single fixed endpoint for reporter accessibility, expression, and inducibility. Persistence of an acquired permissive state after the tether is gone is a sufficiency test that AP-1 binding alone can install a self-maintaining memory at a defined site.

question: ap1
title: Serial-biopsy persistence test across a drug holiday
description: In patients with planned intermittent dosing (e.g., BRAF/MEK or EGFR inhibitor holidays), collect matched pre-treatment, on-treatment, and off-drug biopsies and profile them by single-nucleus ATAC/RNA multiome to ask whether AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target expression induced on-treatment persist after the stimulus is withdrawn. Persistence that is uncoupled from ongoing MAPK/JNK signaling (measured by phospho-ERK/JNK staining on the same specimens) is the core signature of memory rather than sustained signaling.

question: ap1
title: Recall kinetics in patient-derived organoids after wash-out and re-challenge
description: Expose patient-derived organoids to drug or cytokine, wash out and expand for a defined number of divisions, then re-challenge and compare the speed and amplitude of the AP-1-dependent transcriptional response to naive sibling cultures. A faster or larger second response that scales with retained AP-1-primed accessibility distinguishes true memory from simple re-induction.

question: ap1
title: Clonal barcoding to test heritability of the AP-1 state through division
description: Lentivirally barcode low-passage patient-derived cells or PDX-derived lines, split each barcoded population into twin arms, and test whether AP-1-high clones in one arm predict AP-1-high or resistant fate in the sister arm. Concordance across sibling clones demonstrates a heritable, clonally transmitted AP-1 state rather than stochastic fluctuation.

question: ap1
title: Relaxation dynamics after sorting on a live AP-1 reporter
description: Introduce a TRE-driven fluorescent reporter (or sort on a validated AP-1 surface-marker proxy) into patient-derived organoids or lines, FACS-isolate the top and bottom tails, and track how quickly each fraction re-establishes the parental distribution. Slow, multi-generation relaxation implies a long-lived memory state, whereas rapid re-equilibration implies fast stochastic switching.

question: ap1
title: Causal necessity and sufficiency via degron and CRISPRa in patient-derived organoids
description: In patient-derived organoids carrying an auxin-inducible FOS/JUN degron or dCas9-based activation targeted to AP-1-bound enhancers, degrade AP-1 only during the maintenance window after stimulus removal to test whether the stored state is erased, and separately force AP-1 in naive cells to test whether it alone installs the primed state. ATAC and CUT&RUN readouts reveal whether the enhancer landscape is lost, retained, or newly created.

question: ap1
title: Dilution clock: decay per division versus decay per hour
description: Establish the AP-1-dependent state, then compare matched arms with identical elapsed time but different numbers of divisions (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, serum titration, mitomycin-C arrest) and fit whether the memory half-life is better expressed in generations or in hours, distinguishing replication-coupled chromatin storage from a slowly decaying protein/RNA reservoir. Complement with EdU-based nascent-chromatin capture to measure how rapidly AP-1 sites regain accessibility and factor occupancy behind the replication fork.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon and allele-resolved cis/trans discrimination
description: Fuse a memory-bearing cell to a naive cell of a distinguishable genotype (F1 hybrid or SNP-divergent lines) and read out AP-1 target expression and accessibility allele-specifically in the shared nucleus. Conversion of the naive genome implies a diffusible trans carrier, whereas persistent discordance between the two genomes implies the state is stored in cis chromatin, a distinction no washout time course can make.

question: ap1
title: Mitosis-restricted degron plus mitotic bookmarking measurement
description: Quantify whether AP-1 factors are retained on condensed mitotic chromosomes using single-molecule tracking/FRAP residence times and CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic cells, then deplete AP-1 only during the mitotic window with a timed degron so it is present in interphase both before and after division. Failure to transmit the state under this narrow perturbation would localize storage to the mitotic bookmark rather than to steady-state interphase occupancy.

question: ap1
title: Frequency-domain stimulation to measure the memory time constant
description: Deliver stimulus as square waves across roughly two orders of magnitude of frequency at matched total dose using microfluidics or automated media exchange, and fit the amplitude and phase of AP-1 target output as a transfer function. A genuine memory element acts as a low-pass integrator whose corner frequency sets the retention time, giving a dynamical memory estimate that can be cross-validated against the per-division estimate.

question: ap1
title: Screening-off test: is AP-1 state statistically sufficient for history?
description: Using expressed clonal barcodes, measure stimulus history, intermediate AP-1 activity, and later fate within the same lineages, then test whether conditioning on AP-1 state renders past history and future outcome conditionally independent. Residual history-dependence quantifies the fraction of stored information AP-1 does not carry, directly testing the sufficiency claim that most memory experiments assume.

question: ap1
title: Allele-resolved memory as a cis/trans discriminator
description: In F1 hybrid or densely heterozygous cells, phase ATAC/CUT&RUN/nascent-RNA reads to the two alleles of the same AP-1 target enhancer after a transient pulse and ask whether the alleles retain or lose the state independently. Persistent trans-acting AP-1 protein predicts tightly correlated alleles within a nucleus, whereas cis-encoded chromatin memory predicts allelic independence and stable monoallelic 'memorized' states.

question: ap1
title: Replication-coupled dilution and re-establishment kinetics
description: Pulse-label nascent chromatin (EdU/BrdU capture or nascent-chromatin ATAC) at defined times after a stimulus to measure how much AP-1 occupancy and accessibility survive passage of the replication fork, how fast it is restored on daughter strands, and whether sister chromatids inherit it symmetrically. Genuinely self-propagating memory must show rapid template-directed restoration rather than slow re-equilibration from bulk AP-1 levels.

question: ap1
title: Non-commutativity: does the enhancer landscape store stimulus order?
description: Deliver matched pairs of pulses in opposite orders (A then B versus B then A) with identical total dose and spacing, then compare final AP-1 binding, accessibility, and transcriptome. Reproducibly different end states show the system stores more than a single decaying scalar, and counting distinguishable history-to-state mappings estimates memory capacity in bits.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic writing and motif-grammar decoding of persistence
description: Integrate a barcoded library of synthetic enhancers at a single landing pad that systematically varies AP-1 motif affinity, copy number, spacing, and partner motifs (pioneer factor, NF-kB, TEAD), and separately deliver a timed pulse of AP-1 recruitment via chemically induced dimerization of a bZIP domain to dCas9 at naive loci. Together these test sufficiency: which sequence configurations convert a transient AP-1 pulse into a persistent state, and whether an AP-1 pulse alone can install memory where none existed.

question: ap1
title: The dimer-composition code on chromatin
description: Apply quantitative targeted mass spectrometry of the chromatin-bound AP-1 interactome, plus dimer-specific sequential CUT&RUN and proximity ligation, across the decay phase, and test whether forced expression of individual dimers reproduces the maintained state. Memory may reside not in how much AP-1 is bound but in a switch to long-lived, slowly exchanging dimers such as FRA1-JUND, which pan-AP-1 occupancy measurements cannot see.

question: ap1
title: Cis/trans variance decomposition with allele-resolved reporters
description: Place two spectrally distinct but otherwise identical AP-1-driven reporters at the two homologous alleles of one locus, and read endogenous memory loci allele-specifically in F1 hybrid cells using SNPs. Correlated allelic states implicate a diffusible trans carrier (the AP-1 protein pool), while independent allelic memory implicates a cis chromatin mark, a distinction bulk degron or washout experiments cannot make.

question: ap1
title: Replication-coupled restoration kinetics of AP-1 sites
description: Use nascent chromatin capture (ChOR-seq or EdU-pulldown ATAC) to time re-establishment of AP-1 occupancy, accessibility, and H3K27ac behind the replication fork at memory loci versus acutely induced loci, and compare memory decay in time-matched cycling versus replication-arrested (CDK4/6-inhibited or quiescent) cells. Erasure that scales per division rather than per hour, with slow locus-selective restoration, identifies replication as the rate-limiting step for AP-1 rewriting.

question: ap1
title: Mitosis-restricted AP-1 removal to test bookmarking
description: Fuse AP-1 subunits to a cell-cycle-gated degron (APC/C-dependent, or chemically timed in synchronized cells) so the protein is absent only during mitosis and early G1, then restored. Loss of heritable accessibility under this narrow window but not under equal-duration interphase depletion would show AP-1 transmits memory by mitotic bookmarking rather than continuous interphase occupancy.

question: ap1
title: Open-loop clamp of AP-1 expression
description: Delete or mutate the AP-1 binding sites in the FOS/JUN promoters themselves and re-supply the subunits from a tunable exogenous promoter titrated to match wild-type mean protein level. Collapse of heritable state despite identical average AP-1 activity would localize memory to the trans autoregulatory feedback loop rather than to the chromatin AP-1 binds.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule residence time and fiber co-occupancy at matched AP-1 levels
description: In primed versus naive cells with equal AP-1 protein concentration, measure FOS/JUN residence-time distributions and bound fraction by single-molecule tracking, and measure combinatorial multi-site co-occupancy on individual DNA molecules by methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA). Memory stored as kinetic stabilization or cooperative multi-motif occupancy predicts longer-lived binding and non-independent site occupancy, which bulk ChIP and ATAC averages cannot resolve.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon fusion test of cis- versus trans-encoded memory
description: Fuse stimulus-primed cells with naive cells (distinguished by nuclear-localized fluorophores or species-specific reads) and assay, nucleus-by-nucleus, whether primed AP-1 target expression and accessibility spread to the naive nucleus or stay confined to the primed one. Trans-dominant transfer implicates a diffusible AP-1 protein/dimer pool as the store, whereas strictly nucleus-autonomous persistence implicates chromatin-encoded memory at AP-1 sites, a distinction that bulk time courses cannot make.

question: ap1
title: Allele-specific memory at heterozygous AP-1 motifs
description: In F1 hybrid cells (or CRISPR-generated heterozygotes in which the TRE/CRE motif is destroyed on one allele only), use allele-resolved ATAC, CUT&RUN, and nascent RNA to ask whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist exclusively on the motif-bearing allele within the same nucleus. Because both alleles share one cytoplasm and one trans environment, allele discordance is a near-airtight demonstration that the memory is written in cis at AP-1 elements rather than inherited as a cellular signaling state.

question: ap1
title: Open-loop feedback clamp on AP-1 autoregulation
description: Replace the endogenous AP-1 binding sites in the JUN/FOS/FOSL1 regulatory regions with an orthogonal doxycycline- or rapamycin-controlled input, titrating dose so that mean and cell-to-cell variance of AP-1 protein match wild type under acute stimulation. If memory collapses in these open-loop cells despite matched acute responses, the memory resides in transcriptional positive feedback; if it survives, feedback is dispensable and a chromatin or cofactor mechanism must carry it.

question: ap1
title: Binding kinetics and single-fiber co-occupancy as the remembered variable
description: Compare naive and long-after-stimulus primed cells by single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN (residence times, bound fraction, search time, cluster/condensate formation) and by single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) that reports actual protein occupancy and combinatorial co-accessibility of linked enhancers on the same DNA fiber. This tests whether memory is stored as altered AP-1 binding kinetics or as coordinated multi-enhancer configurations, rather than as changes in AP-1 abundance or bulk accessibility.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic bottleneck test with designed stimulus histories
description: Expose single cells to a library of distinguishable stimulus histories (varying order, spacing, amplitude), then jointly measure AP-1 state and downstream phenotype in the same cells and compute mutual information between history and AP-1 state, history and phenotype, and the conditional information remaining once AP-1 state is known. If AP-1 is the memory channel, the data-processing inequality should hold with little history information bypassing it; substantial residual information identifies a parallel, non-AP-1 memory store and bounds how much of the memory AP-1 can possibly explain.

question: ap1
title: Cis vs. trans memory via twin identical reporters
description: Integrate two spectrally distinct but sequence-identical AP-1-responsive reporters at different genomic loci in the same cell and track both after a stimulus pulse. Locus-autonomous chromatin memory predicts the two reporters decorrelate and decay independently, while cell-wide protein/feedback memory predicts they remain tightly correlated, separating the two leading mechanistic classes with one measurement.

question: ap1
title: Clock vs. counter: does the state decay per hour or per division?
description: Compare decay of the stimulus-induced state in cell-cycle-arrested versus cycling cells (CDK4/6 inhibition, serum starvation, contact inhibition) over matched wall-clock time, and use EdU- or sister-chromatid-resolved readouts to test whether loss occurs specifically at replication. Template-copied chromatin memory should decay per division, whereas protein-level or metabolic memory decays per hour.

question: ap1
title: Kinetic and dimer-composition signature of the memory state
description: Apply single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN/FOS in live nuclei together with two-color single-molecule pull-down or FRET to ask whether post-stimulus cells differ from naive cells in residence time, bound fraction, and dimer identity (e.g., long-lived FRA1-JUND replacing transient FOS-JUN) at matched total activity. This tests whether memory is stored in binding kinetics and partner choice rather than in AP-1 abundance.

question: ap1
title: Motif-matched surrogate bZIP swap
description: In an AP-1-null or degron-depleted background, re-express a chimera carrying the AP-1 bZIP DNA-binding domain fused to a minimal heterologous activation domain, so the same motifs are bound and activated by a protein lacking AP-1's native cofactor and pioneer interactions. If the surrogate restores acute induction but not persistence, memory resides in AP-1 protein surfaces rather than in motif occupancy per se.

question: ap1
title: Write AP-1 activity history into DNA with a molecular recorder
description: Drive a prime-editing or recombinase-based recorder (ENGRAM/DNA-Typewriter-style) from an AP-1-responsive promoter so each cell accumulates an ordered, cumulative record of its past AP-1 activity, then read the record and the current transcriptome from the same single cell. This decouples integrated past AP-1 dose from present state without sorting or fixing cells at an arbitrarily chosen early timepoint.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping: bistability versus slow relaxation
description: Titrate a tunable AP-1 input (e.g., degron-stabilized FOS/JUN or a graded cytokine dose) up and then back down along the same concentration ladder, reading a single-cell AP-1 target reporter at steady state at each step, so that the up-ramp and down-ramp branches can be compared directly. A true memory element should show a hysteresis loop with two stable states at the same input level — a signature that a merely slow-decaying state cannot produce — and the loop should collapse if AP-1 self-reinforcement is broken with a TRE-motif decoy sponge or a feedback-dead promoter allele.

question: ap1
title: Decouple the clock from the cell-division counter
description: Hold cells at matched post-stimulus times in cycling versus arrested conditions (CDK4/6 inhibitor, contact inhibition, reversible serum withdrawal) and compare decay of AP-1 target accessibility and expression per unit time versus per division, then release arrest to test whether decay resumes on the division schedule. Combine with EdU-pulse sorting and nascent-chromatin readout to measure how accessibility at AP-1 sites is re-established behind the replication fork — whether memory is replication-diluted, replication-refreshed, or indifferent to S phase determines which class of mechanism is even possible.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-identity relay as the storage variable
description: Test whether the memory is carried not by AP-1 occupancy but by which family member occupies the site, using ChIP-reChIP or proximity ligation to track the composition shift from labile FOS/JUN to long-lived FRA1/FOSB/JUNB at the same motifs over time, with pulse-SILAC to measure the half-lives of the proteins actually resident at persistent sites. Then swap degrons between family members (chimeras with identical DNA-binding domains but exchanged stability determinants) to ask whether protein lifetime alone, rather than chromatin, sets the duration of the state.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic sufficiency array: design rules for a memory-competent site
description: Integrate a combinatorial library of synthetic AP-1 elements at a single genomic landing pad — varying motif number, affinity, spacing/helical phasing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, and co-occurring partner motifs — each linked to a reporter, then pulse the cells and sequence/sort for which configurations retain the on-state after the stimulus is gone. This converts correlative enhancer surveys into a quantitative rule for what makes an AP-1 site remember, and predicts which endogenous sites should be memory-competent.

question: ap1
title: How many bits, and of what, does the state store?
description: Stimulate cells with a panel of distinct AP-1-activating inputs at several doses and durations, then at later time points measure single-cell AP-1 target states and compute the mutual information between past stimulus identity/dose and present state. This asks whether AP-1 is a high-capacity memory that preserves stimulus identity or a degenerate one-bit latch, and tracking how capacity decays over time separates loss of amplitude from loss of specificity.

question: ap1
title: Heterokaryon cis/trans test for where the memory is stored
description: Fuse a primed cell with a naive cell of distinguishable genotype (SNP- or species-distinct) and measure allele-specific transcription and accessibility in the shared cytoplasm. Retention of each genome's own state implicates cis chromatin storage, whereas conversion of the naive genome implicates diffusible AP-1 protein or autoregulatory feedback.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis and bistability mapping of the AP-1 input-output curve
description: Titrate an AP-1-activating input upward from zero and downward from saturation, measuring steady-state single-cell output at each dose with a quantitative reporter. A true memory system should show a hysteretic loop, bimodal populations within the loop, and measurable spontaneous switching rates, which slow passive decay cannot generate.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule footprinting of primed enhancers
description: Apply dual-enzyme methyltransferase single-molecule footprinting with long reads at candidate memory enhancers to determine whether priming increases the fraction of cells with an open element or alters per-molecule occupancy and dwell structure. Co-occupancy correlations among multiple AP-1 sites on the same molecule reveal cis-coordination invisible to population ATAC-seq.

question: ap1
title: AP-1 dimer composition as the stored variable
description: Track dimer identity at primed loci over the memory window using sequential/co-IP CUT&RUN and crosslinked-dimer mass spectrometry, testing whether short-lived FOS is replaced by long-lived FRA1/FRA2/JUND. Isoform-specific degrons applied only during the maintenance phase test whether the long-lived subunit, rather than chromatin, carries the memory.

question: ap1
title: Decoding stimulus history and measuring memory capacity
description: Deliver combinatorial stimulus histories that differ in identity, order, and spacing, then quantify how much of the history is decodable from current chromatin and transcriptome, and whether decoding collapses when AP-1 motifs are disrupted. Running matched arms in proliferating versus arrested cells separates replication-driven dilution from time-dependent decay.

question: ap1
title: Primed–naive cell fusion to separate nuclear-intrinsic from diffusible memory
description: Fuse differentially labeled primed and naive cells (PEG or virus-mediated heterokaryons, scored by imaging; or fuse cells with distinguishable SNP/barcode genomes and read out allele-specific ATAC/RNA in the fused population) and ask whether each nucleus keeps its own AP-1 accessibility and response state in a shared cytoplasm. Nucleus-autonomous persistence argues for a chromatin-encoded record, whereas rapid equalization of both nuclei indicates the 'memory' is really a diffusible/autoregulatory AP-1 network state.

question: ap1
title: Is the memory clocked by divisions or by wall-clock time?
description: Hold primed cells in matched conditions that decouple time from proliferation — cycling versus arrested (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, or serum deprivation) and fast versus slow cycling (thymidine or low-dose aphidicolin) — and fit the decay of AP-1 motif accessibility and restimulation advantage to a per-division versus per-hour model; complement with nascent-chromatin ATAC (repli-ATAC/early-late BrdU-sorted fractions) to see how quickly AP-1 footprints are rebuilt behind the fork. Replication-coupled dilution versus continuous turnover implies completely different molecular carriers and makes different predictions about heritability.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping of AP-1 dose versus enhancer state
description: Using a tunable AP-1 input (doxycycline-titratable JUN/FOS, or graded degron depletion), drive cells up a dose ladder and then back down along the same ladder, measuring accessibility and target output at each matched dose. A true memory element should show hysteresis — the same AP-1 concentration yields different chromatin/transcriptional states depending on history — and the width of the loop quantifies memory strength, whereas a perfectly retraced curve means AP-1 is a graded relay, not a latch.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule fiber footprinting to test whether memory is digital and locally coordinated
description: Apply long-read single-molecule chromatin footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA/nanoNOMe) to primed and naive cells so that occupancy of many AP-1 motifs across an enhancer cluster is read on the same DNA molecule. This distinguishes an all-or-none heritable unit (molecules are fully primed or fully naive, with correlated multi-site occupancy) from a graded probabilistic shift, and reveals whether memory requires cooperative engagement of several motifs or a single bookmark site.

question: ap1
title: Information-theoretic accounting: how many bits of the past does the AP-1 state actually store?
description: Deliver a graded ladder of first-stimulus doses (and distinct stimulus identities), then compute at single-cell resolution the mutual information between the prior exposure and the later AP-1 reporter/response distribution, repeating at several delays to obtain a bit-decay curve. This converts 'memory' from a yes/no claim into a measured capacity and tests the sharper question of whether cells remember only that something happened or also how much and which stimulus — with AP-1 perturbation expected to collapse capacity toward zero bits.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded decay curves for AP-1 chromatin states
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes plus joint single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling to measure how similar related cells remain at AP-1 motif-containing enhancers across 1 to 10+ divisions, yielding an explicit memory half-life in generations. Compare that half-life against non-AP-1 enhancers and against cells where AP-1 factors are acutely degraded, to see whether AP-1 sets the timescale or merely marks it.

question: ap1
title: Separating the writing of memory from its maintenance with timed degron pulses
description: Tag FOS, JUN, and FOSL1 with auxin or dTAG degrons and remove them either during a stimulus (blocking establishment) or days afterward (testing maintenance), then re-challenge the cells and measure the magnitude of the primed response. If memory survives late depletion, AP-1 is a writer handing off to another substrate; if it collapses, AP-1 itself is the stored state.

question: ap1
title: Reconstituting memory by synthetic AP-1 tethering alone
description: Use dCas9 or a chemically inducible recruitment system to deposit AP-1 family members at defined endogenous enhancers for a controlled duration, release them, and then ask whether the locus shows faster and larger reactivation to a later real stimulus. This converts a correlation into a sufficiency test, and dose/duration titration maps the minimum AP-1 exposure needed to install a persistent state.

question: ap1
title: Quantitative replication-coupled tracking of AP-1 site reassembly
description: Combine nascent-chromatin capture (such as labeling newly replicated DNA and profiling the proteins and accessibility on it) with live imaging of tagged AP-1 factors to measure how quickly AP-1 reoccupies its sites behind the replication fork. Memory that survives mitosis should show rapid, site-specific reassembly with preserved relative occupancy, and the recovery kinetics distinguish true bookmarking from de novo re-establishment driven by upstream signaling.

question: ap1
title: Perturbation-response mapping that tests memory as a prediction, not a description
description: Expose isogenic cells to combinations of stimuli separated by defined intervals and fit a model where the AP-1 state measured after the first exposure predicts the quantitative response to the second, at single-cell resolution. A genuine memory mechanism should make AP-1 state a better predictor of future behavior than current signaling activity or overall cell state, and the model's failures identify the additional components memory requires.

question: ap1
title: Timed degron removal of AP-1 after priming
description: Tag endogenous FOS, FOSL1, and JUN family members with dTAG or auxin degrons and deplete them at defined intervals after a priming stimulus, then re-challenge the cells. Comparing loss of the remembered response when AP-1 is removed during writing versus long after it separates AP-1's establishment role from a continuous maintenance requirement.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded measurement of memory half-life
description: Combine clonal barcoding with sister-cell transcriptomics and ATAC profiling to quantify how many divisions AP-1 target programs and AP-1-bound accessible sites stay correlated within a clone. Running the same assay in AP-1-inhibited cells (A-FOS or compound knockouts) converts the qualitative memory claim into a measured decay timescale.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis mapping with live AP-1 reporters
description: Image endogenous AP-1 activity together with upstream kinase reporters while slowly ramping a stimulus up and then back down over days. A memory mechanism should show a gap between the rising and falling dose-response curves, and the width of that gap gives the quantitative signature to compare across cell types and stimuli.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 tethering as a sufficiency test
description: Use inducible dCas9 or optogenetic recruitment to deposit AP-1 subunits at defined loci for a brief window, then release them and track accessibility, histone marks, and re-inducibility for weeks. This asks whether AP-1 occupancy alone, with no upstream signaling, is sufficient to write a persistent state.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and daughter-cell inheritance
description: Profile AP-1 binding and chromatin accessibility in synchronized mitotic cells and in freshly divided daughter pairs to see whether AP-1-marked sites are retained through chromosome condensation. Pairing this with live imaging of reporter reactivation timing in daughters tests whether physical inheritance, rather than re-establishment from signaling, carries the memory.

question: ap1
title: Pulse-chase AP-1 degron timing experiment
description: Fuse FOS/JUN family members to auxin- or dTAG-degrons, deliver a defined stimulus pulse, then degrade AP-1 at staggered delays and measure how long the degradation window must be to erase the altered response to a second stimulus days later. This separates AP-1 as a transient signal transducer from AP-1 as the physical carrier of the memory.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-resolved memory tracing with heritable barcodes
description: Combine expressed clonal barcodes with longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC across a stimulus/rest/restimulus protocol, testing whether sibling cells share AP-1 site accessibility and reactivation behavior more than expected by chance. Memory is then quantified directly as heritability of the AP-1 regulatory state through cell divisions.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking of AP-1 target enhancers
description: Use live imaging of tagged FOS/JUN plus CUT&RUN at synchronized cell-cycle stages to ask whether AP-1 remains bound to its target enhancers on mitotic chromatin. Separation-of-function mutants that lose mitotic retention but keep interphase binding would test whether bookmarking is what transmits memory across division.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 circuits to test sufficiency
description: Build a minimal synthetic locus with tunable numbers and affinities of TRE/AP-1 motifs alongside inducible synthetic AP-1 factors, and map the parameter regime in which a transient input yields a self-sustaining chromatin state. This establishes sufficiency rather than mere necessity for bistable cellular memory.

question: ap1
title: Joint single-molecule and single-cell measurement of the feedback loop
description: In the same cells, measure AP-1 protein abundance, chromatin residence time by single-molecule tracking, target enhancer accessibility, and transcriptional bursting before, during, and after stimulus. Fitting dynamical models to these data tests whether AP-1 autoregulatory feedback is quantitatively strong enough to sustain memory or whether a slower chromatin/DNA-methylation layer is required.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-resolved decay rates of AP-1 chromatin state versus transcription
description: Use clonal barcoding with paired single-cell ATAC and RNA readouts to track sister cells for many divisions after a transient stimulus, measuring separately how fast AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target transcription relax toward baseline. Memory is demonstrated if accessibility half-lives substantially exceed those of both AP-1 protein levels and target mRNA.

question: ap1
title: Degron erasure test: is AP-1 protein required to maintain its own footprint?
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with inducible degrons and deplete them at defined times after stimulation, then assay whether previously opened AP-1 sites stay open and whether the cell still responds faster to a second stimulus. Distinguishing a self-sustaining chromatin mark from continuous AP-1 occupancy is the crux of any memory claim.

question: ap1
title: Re-stimulation dose-response mapping of the primed state
description: Quantify, at single-cell resolution, the stimulus dose and latency needed to re-trigger a response in previously stimulated versus naive cells across a long range of rest intervals. A genuine memory predicts a measurable leftward shift in threshold and shortened latency that decays with a characteristic timescale, giving memory an operational, quantitative definition rather than a correlative one.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and dilution accounting across the cell cycle
description: Combine live imaging of tagged AP-1 with cell-cycle sensors and post-mitotic chromatin profiling of daughter pairs to ask whether AP-1 sites are re-established after mitosis, and whether the two daughters inherit matched or divergent states. Measuring inheritance fidelity per division turns 'memory' into a per-generation transmission probability.

question: ap1
title: Synthetic AP-1 site insertion to test sufficiency at a naive locus
description: Insert defined arrays of AP-1 motifs, with varied spacing and partner motifs, at neutral genomic locations alongside a reporter, then stimulate and measure whether the site autonomously acquires and retains accessibility and a faster second response. This converts the question from observational association to a sufficiency experiment with tunable sequence grammar.

question: ap1
title: Decay-per-division vs. decay-per-hour: decoupling time from mitosis
description: Deliver a defined pulse of AP-1 activity (optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization or a degron-stabilized bZIP), then measure the decay of primed enhancer accessibility and of the amplified secondary response while independently varying proliferation rate (contact inhibition, serum, CDK4/6 inhibitors, or cell-cycle-arrested cells). Memory that dilutes as a function of cell divisions implicates a chromatin-templated carrier, whereas decay that tracks wall-clock time regardless of division implicates protein/RNA half-life, and the two models are quantitatively distinguishable from the decay curves alone.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell splitting plus clonal barcoding to measure the heritability of AP-1 state
description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with lineage barcoding, then physically split sister cells (or clonal subpopulations) and challenge one half while profiling the other, quantifying how much of a cell's future stimulus response is predicted by its own mother's prior AP-1 state versus population average. This converts 'memory' into an explicit heritability statistic (mother-daughter and sister-sister correlation as a function of generations elapsed), which can be compared head-to-head against DNA methylation or H3K27me3 as alternative carriers.

question: ap1
title: Tether-and-release: sufficiency of AP-1 at a single enhancer
description: Recruit the FOS/JUN bZIP or transactivation domain to one chosen naive enhancer with dCas9, then wash out or degrade the tether and ask whether that single element remains accessible, nucleosome-depleted, and hyper-responsive to later stimulation relative to unmanipulated alleles in the same nucleus. Allele-specific readouts (targeting one haplotype) give an internally controlled test of whether transient AP-1 occupancy is sufficient to install a persistent local state.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking and daughter-cell inheritance of AP-1 sites
description: Use live single-molecule imaging of FOS/JUN residence times through mitosis plus mitotic CUT&RUN/ATAC and daughter-cell-resolved accessibility profiling to determine whether AP-1 retains, rapidly re-occupies, or entirely loses its binding sites across division. The decisive measurement is the timing of re-establishment in early G1 relative to global chromatin reopening: true bookmarking predicts AP-1 sites reopen first and in a parent-matched, allele-correlated pattern.

question: ap1
title: Acute post-encoding degradation: is AP-1 the memory or merely its reader?
description: Separate the encoding window from the maintenance window with an auxin/dTAG degron that removes AP-1 subunits only after a primed state has been established, then test whether the potentiated response survives the AP-1-free interval and returns when AP-1 is restored. Persistence without AP-1 would show that the factor writes and later interprets a memory stored elsewhere (nucleosome positioning, histone marks, or a cofactor), reframing AP-1 as a reader rather than the storage medium itself.

question: ap1
title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming separates writing from maintaining memory
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with degron systems and deplete them only after a priming stimulus has resolved, then re-stimulate. If primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist without AP-1 present during the interval, AP-1 writes the memory but does not store it.

question: ap1
title: Lineage-barcoded clonal tracking of AP-1 state heritability
description: Combine clonal barcoding with paired single-cell ATAC and RNA readouts to quantify how strongly AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are shared among sibling cells across many divisions. The decay of within-clone similarity over generations gives a direct half-life for the putative memory.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking imaging of AP-1 through division
description: Live-image endogenously tagged AP-1 subunits with single-molecule residence-time measurement through mitosis, paired with mitotic-chromosome ATAC. Determine whether a subset of sites retains bound factor or open chromatin through condensation, which is the physical requirement for passing the state to daughters.

question: ap1
title: Motif-resolution epigenome editing at primed AP-1 sites
description: Use targeted editing or CRISPRi tiling to disrupt individual AP-1 motifs within primed enhancers without touching the factor itself, then test the second-stimulus response. This distinguishes site-specific memory elements from a global AP-1 dosage effect.

question: ap1
title: Dose-and-interval mapping of memory decay in single cells
description: Systematically vary stimulus strength, duration, and the gap before re-stimulation, reading out per-cell response amplitude and AP-1 site accessibility. Fitting the resulting surface tests whether the system behaves like a bistable switch, a slowly decaying analog trace, or simple residual protein.

question: ap1
title: Degron timing: is AP-1 the ledger or the pen?
description: Tag FOS/JUN with auxin degrons, establish an AP-1-dependent cell state (e.g., drug-tolerant melanoma, activated fibroblasts), then degrade AP-1 after establishment while tracking accessibility, nascent transcription, and state markers hourly, with washout re-induction. A state that survives acute AP-1 loss but cannot be re-established shows AP-1 writes the memory without storing it.

question: ap1
title: Hysteresis curves instead of on/off experiments
description: Drive AP-1 with a dose- and duration-tunable synthetic input (inducible FOS-JUN dimer or optogenetic dimerizer) and map the full up-and-down dose-response of enhancer accessibility and target gene output. Memory becomes a measured quantity: the area of the hysteresis loop and the width of the bistable range, comparable across cell types.

question: ap1
title: Memory half-life measured per cell division, not per hour
description: Combine a live AP-1 activity reporter with lineage barcoding and continuous imaging so stimulus-induced state is followed through known numbers of mitoses in single lineages. Fitting decay of mother-daughter and cousin-cousin correlations separates dilution-by-division from time-dependent decay, distinguishing heritable chromatin memory from a merely slow protein.

question: ap1
title: Watching memory get rebuilt behind the replication fork
description: Use EdU-capture-coupled ATAC and CUT&RUN to ask, minute-by-minute after fork passage, whether AP-1 reoccupies its sites before accessibility returns or vice versa, and image AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes. The temporal ordering identifies the physical carrier of the memory rather than just its correlates.

question: ap1
title: Motif knock-ins that break recall but not response
description: CRISPR-mutate individual AP-1 motifs in candidate memory enhancers, in cells and in a mouse epithelium with wound or inflammatory memory, then assay the second stimulus rather than the first. A mutation leaving the naive response intact while abolishing faster/stronger recall is direct evidence that those sites are the memory element itself.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell concordance of AP-1 state after division
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes plus single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) to compare AP-1 motif accessibility and target-gene output between sister and cousin cells across increasing numbers of divisions.
