Heritability shows up as concordance that decays with lineage distance, and live imaging of tagged FOS/JUN through mitosis tests whether the factor itself is retained on chromatin as the physical carrier.

question: ap1
title: Acute degron removal of AP-1 after the signal is gone
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with an auxin or dTAG degron, let cells establish a primed state, then deplete AP-1 only after the inducing stimulus has been washed out. If accessibility and re-inducibility collapse during depletion and fail to return after restoring the protein, AP-1 is actively maintaining the state rather than having merely initiated it.

question: ap1
title: Decay curves and the second-challenge test
description: Deliver a transient stimulus, then measure AP-1 enhancer accessibility, binding, and transcriptional output at a dense timecourse out to weeks, and at each timepoint re-challenge a subpopulation. Genuine memory predicts a measurable storage half-life plus a faster, larger, or lower-threshold second response in exactly the cells that retained the AP-1 state.

question: ap1
title: Writing a state with synthetic AP-1 recruitment
description: Use chemically controlled dCas9 or LID-tag recruitment of FOS/JUN activation domains to specific endogenous enhancers, hold it briefly, then release. Persistence of accessibility and expression after release, in cells that never saw the original stimulus, would establish that AP-1 occupancy alone is sufficient to install the memory.

question: ap1
title: Saturation mutagenesis of endogenous TRE sites
description: Base-edit or prime-edit individual AP-1 motifs across a panel of primed enhancers, varying motif affinity, number, and spacing, and score both initial induction and long-term retention separately. Finding sites required for retention but not for induction would separate the memory function from the response function at single-basepair resolution.

question: ap1
title: "Perches in the soul" — residence-time vs. heritability mapping
description: Measure single-molecule chromatin residence times of FOS/JUN/JUNB by live-cell single-particle tracking and compare them to the persistence of the accessible sites those factors create (ATAC-seq time-chase over multiple divisions). Cellular memory requires the site to outlive the factor by orders of magnitude; matched timescales would instead indicate continuous driving rather than a stored mark.

question: ap1
title: "Sings the tune without the words" — accessibility decoupled from transcription
description: Run matched ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and nascent transcription (PRO-seq/TT-seq) time courses far past stimulus withdrawal to find loci that stay open and AP-1-bound with no ongoing nascent output. A long silent-but-primed window that converts to faster, larger induction on restimulation is the signature of a latent memory element.

question: ap1
title: "Sweetest in the Gale" — second-hit amplification as the functional readout
description: Prime cells, wait, then re-challenge and quantify gains in response rate, amplitude, and the fraction of responding cells at candidate AP-1 memory loci. Show specificity by deleting the TRE motif or CRISPRi-silencing the individual primed enhancer, so that amplification is lost locus-specifically rather than only upon global AP-1 depletion.

question: ap1
title: "Sore must be the storm that could abash" — erasure threshold titration
description: Systematically titrate candidate memory erasers (cell-cycle arrest versus forced divisions, replication inhibition, p300/HDAC inhibition, BAF/SMARCA4 degron, H3.3 and histone-chaperone knockdown, AP-1 subunit degrons) to build a dose-by-duration map of what collapses primed accessibility. The identity and magnitude of the required insult discriminates replication-coupled, remodeler-dependent, and histone-variant-based memory mechanisms.

question: ap1
title: "Never asked a crumb of me" — maintenance without ongoing input
description: Use auxin/dTAG degrons to remove AP-1 protein completely after priming and test whether the primed, open state is maintained and still re-inducible without its founder factor. Combine with lineage-barcoded single-cell multiome (scATAC + scRNA) to test clonal heritability of the primed state across divisions, distinguishing a self-sustaining mark from one requiring continuous feeding.

question: ap1
title: "The hand that mocked them": decoupling AP-1 occupancy from its chromatin trace
description: After a transient stimulus, run parallel time courses of AP-1 protein levels (FOS/JUN immunofluorescence, degron-tagged reporters) and of chromatin state at AP-1 motifs (ATAC-seq, FOS/JUN CUT&RUN, H3K27ac). Memory is supported only if accessibility and enhancer marks persist long after AP-1 occupancy has decayed, just as the inscription outlasts the sculptor's hand.

question: ap1
title: "Look on my Works": restimulation latency as a readout of a stored trace
description: Stimulate, let the response fully subside, then restimulate at a range of intervals while imaging an AP-1 target reporter in single living cells to quantify response latency, amplitude, and responder fraction. Faster or larger second responses that decay as a function of the inter-stimulus interval give a quantitative memory half-life, read out by the second 'traveller'.

question: ap1
title: "Nothing beside remains": acute AP-1 erasure separating establishment from maintenance
description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degradation of FOS/JUN applied either during the initial stimulus or only afterward, during the putative memory window. Persistence of the trace despite post-hoc depletion would localize memory to chromatin, whereas its collapse would show memory is merely sustained AP-1 presence.

question: ap1
title: The pedestal that outlasts the king: a genomic recorder of past AP-1 activity
description: Engineer an AP-1-responsive enhancer driving a recombinase or base editor that writes a permanent DNA barcode when AP-1 fires, then read the written mark jointly with scRNA-seq or ATAC days later. This tests cell by cell whether a past AP-1 episode predicts present transcriptional and chromatin state independently of current AP-1 levels.

question: ap1
title: "Round the decay of that colossal Wreck": dilution versus erosion of the trace
description: Compare memory persistence in proliferating versus cell-cycle-arrested cells and assay AP-1 mitotic bookmarking by CUT&RUN on mitotic chromosomes, distinguishing stepwise loss per division from continuous chromatin turnover. Analyzing which sites survive versus crumble (motif strength, cooperating factors, CpG content, enhancer-promoter contacts) identifies the determinants of a durable memory trace.

question: ap1
title: Stipple test: clonal barcoding of first and second responses
description: Inspired by the poem's 'rose-moles all in stipple' — a mottled pattern that is stable rather than random — use heritable lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/FateMap-style) to stimulate cells, let them divide through a rest period, then re-stimulate, and ask whether high- and low-responding cells fall into the same clones both times. True AP-1 memory predicts clonally heritable second-response amplitude that correlates with first-response AP-1 target output, whereas a non-memory model predicts clone-independent, resampled variability.

question: ap1
title: Couple-colour: which Fos/Jun dimer holds the mark
description: AP-1 is a family of heterodimers, not one protein, so apply subunit-specific degron tags (FOS, FOSL1, JUN, JUNB, ATF3) and deplete each only during the quiescent interval between stimulations, leaving induction itself intact. Pair this with CUT&RUN time courses of each subunit at memory enhancers to distinguish a continuously occupied 'maintenance dimer' from a hit-and-run initiating dimer whose mark is kept by something else.

question: ap1
title: Swift, slow: decay-constant mismatch between occupancy, accessibility, and output
description: Memory requires that some layer outlive its input, so measure, in the same time course after a pulsed stimulus, the decay kinetics of AP-1 protein, AP-1 ChIP/CUT&RUN occupancy, ATAC accessibility, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, and nascent transcription at the same loci. The memory signature is a quantitatively slower accessibility half-life than occupancy half-life at a specific enhancer subset; loci where all layers decay together serve as internal negative controls.

question: ap1
title: Landscape plotted and pieced: synthetic enhancer grammar for persistence
description: Build an MPRA/synthetic-locus library varying TRE/AP-1 motif number, spacing, affinity, partner-motif identity, and flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, integrated at a fixed landing pad, then score which designs convert a transient stimulus into weeks-long accessibility and faster re-induction. Validate the top rules by prime-editing the corresponding motifs at endogenous memory enhancers to show that the predicted design features are causally required.

question: ap1
title: Past change: does the memory survive replication, and who re-writes it?
description: Test whether the mark is 'past change' through DNA replication by comparing memory retention in cycling versus pharmacologically or contact-arrested cells, and by nascent-chromatin capture (NCC/repli-ATAC) to see whether AP-1 and accessibility are re-established on daughter strands within one cell cycle. Combine with acute MLL3/4, BRD4, or BAF (SMARCA4) inhibition applied only during the rest interval to identify which cofactor actually maintains or re-writes the mark once AP-1 levels have returned to baseline.

question: ap1
title: Does the anchor hold? Stimulus pulse-chase with AP-1 degradation
description: Deliver a transient stimulus (serum, TGF-beta, or a targeted inhibitor), wash out, then track AP-1 factor levels, chromatin accessibility at AP-1 motifs (ATAC-seq), and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 over days to weeks. True memory requires that the open, primed state persist after AP-1 protein itself has decayed; acute degradation (dTAG/auxin) of FOS/JUN at defined times after the pulse distinguishes whether AP-1 is the stored memory or only the writer that sets the anchor.

question: ap1
title: Filament, filament, filament: lineage barcoding plus AP-1 reporter across cell divisions
description: Combine heritable lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/CellTag-style) with a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter and single-cell RNA/ATAC readout, so that an individual cell's AP-1 state before a perturbation can be linked to the behavior of its descendants many divisions later. Memory predicts intra-clone concordance of AP-1 activity and downstream fate that exceeds what is expected from shared transient signaling, and that concordance should decay with a measurable half-life in generations.

question: ap1
title: Throwing the thread twice: dose-response to repeated stimulation
description: Stimulate cells, allow full return to baseline, then restimulate at varying intervals and doses, measuring transcriptional output amplitude, latency, and the fraction of responding cells. A memory mechanism predicts potentiated or faster secondary responses (or a leftward-shifted dose-response) specifically at AP-1-dependent loci, and this priming should be abolished by degrading AP-1 during the rest interval if AP-1 maintains it, or preserved if AP-1 merely wrote it.

question: ap1
title: Measureless oceans of space: 3D genome anchoring of AP-1-primed enhancers
description: Use Micro-C or region-capture Hi-C together with AP-1 CUT&RUN before, during, and long after a transient stimulus to ask whether AP-1 establishes persistent enhancer-promoter contacts that outlast the signal. Stable loops anchored at AP-1 sites that remain after factor loss would be a structural substrate for memory, testable by degron removal of AP-1 or by CRISPRi silencing of individual anchors.

question: ap1
title: Isolated on a promontory: single-cell perturbation of AP-1 in otherwise identical cells
description: In a clonal, unstimulated population, use dCas9-based activation or optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization to transiently drive AP-1 only in sparse, trackable cells, then follow those cells and their progeny by live imaging and matched single-cell multiome. If a brief, cell-autonomous AP-1 pulse alone is sufficient to shift long-term state and drug response relative to neighbors in the same dish, AP-1 is causally sufficient for memory rather than a correlate of upstream signaling.

question: ap1
title: "Nothing gold can stay": decoupling factor decay from state persistence
description: Pulse-stimulate cells, wash out, and run matched time courses of FOS/JUN protein levels (quantitative immunoblot, Halo-tag pulse-chase) against chromatin accessibility and nucleosome positioning at AP-1 motifs (ATAC-seq plus AP-1 CUT&RUN). Memory is supported only if the accessible state at AP-1-bound enhancers outlives the protein by many half-lives; co-decay would instead indicate ongoing signaling rather than memory.

question: ap1
title: "So dawn goes down to day": testing the handoff to a durable successor
description: Perform time-resolved CUT&RUN for FOS, FOSB, FRA1/FRA2, JUN, JUNB, and JUND together with co-IP of dimer composition at matched timepoints, asking whether labile FOS-containing dimers at a given site are replaced by longer-lived FRA1/JUND dimers or by resident lineage factors. A site-preserving compositional handoff is the concrete mechanistic form that AP-1 memory would need to take.

question: ap1
title: "Her hardest hue to hold": mitotic dilution as the decay clock
description: Pair a stimulus pulse with FUCCI/live imaging and with cell-cycle arrest (CDK4/6 inhibition or contact arrest), then measure how many divisions the primed state survives using re-stimulation reporters and ATAC-seq on cells sorted by division number via dye dilution. Decay scaling with divisions implies a replication-coupled chromatin carrier, whereas decay on wall-clock time regardless of division implicates slow protein or RNA turnover.

question: ap1
title: "But only so an hour": degron separation of establishment versus maintenance
description: Tag endogenous FOS and JUN with dTAG or AID degrons and deplete them either before stimulation, during the first hour of response, or only after the state is established. A memory function requires that post-establishment depletion preserves primed accessibility and accelerated secondary responses, while early depletion abolishes both.

question: ap1
title: "Then leaf subsides to leaf": clone-resolved second-hit restimulation
description: Lineage-barcode cells, stimulate, allow a long rest period, then restimulate and use single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq to ask whether enhanced re-induction is heritable within clones rather than merely a population average. Shared priming among sister cells of the same clone distinguishes a genuinely inherited chromatin state from averaging over transient responders.

question: ap1
title: Fearful symmetry: sister-cell concordance as a memory clock
description: Live-image an endogenous FOS/JUN reporter through cell division, then measure the correlation in restimulation response between sister cells versus randomly paired cells. The decay of this 'symmetry' as a function of time since division yields a direct half-life for the heritable AP-1 state, with cousin and second-cousin comparisons separating true heritable memory from shared microenvironment.

question: ap1
title: The immortal hand that framed, then left: AP-1 degron washout
description: Tag FOS/JUNB with dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons and acutely destroy the protein during defined windows after a priming stimulus, then restimulate. If the primed response survives AP-1 protein loss, AP-1 is the writer of a memory stored elsewhere (chromatin); if memory collapses with the protein, AP-1 is itself the storage medium.

question: ap1
title: Dare seize the fire: latent enhancers across prime-rest-restimulate
description: Collect matched ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and nascent transcription (PRO-seq or intronic scRNA-seq) across a prime to long-rest to restimulate time course, identifying sites that retain accessibility during rest even after AP-1 occupancy decays. Testing whether these retained, AP-1-motif-enriched sites are precisely the loci that fire faster or higher on the second stimulus is the central mechanistic test.

question: ap1
title: What distant deeps: lineage barcodes tracing the fire to its origin
description: Combine heritable lineage barcoding (CRISPR recorders or static barcodes as in Watermelon/FateMap) with single-cell ATAC and RNA to ask whether drug-tolerant or hyper-responsive cells descend preferentially from AP-1-high ancestors. This quantifies how many generations the AP-1 state persists and how much of final-state variance it explains.

question: ap1
title: The returning refrain: a memory transfer function from spaced stimuli
description: Deliver two identical stimulus pulses separated by systematically varied intervals (minutes to many days, spanning several divisions) and fit response amplitude versus inter-pulse interval to extract a memory decay constant, then test whether it matches decay of AP-1-site accessibility rather than AP-1 protein. As a sufficiency arm, insert synthetic AP-1 motif arrays at ectopic naive loci and ask whether they can be framed into acquiring the same memory behavior.

question: ap1
title: The "Pavements Grey" Washout–Recall Assay
description: Mirroring the poem's speaker who still hears the absent lake while standing on grey pavements, stimulate cells (serum, TGF-beta, MAPK activation, or drug), wash out, wait a defined interval, then re-challenge, while separately tracking endogenously tagged AP-1 proteins (FOS/FOSL1/JUN), AP-1-motif chromatin accessibility, and transcriptional output. The memory signature is a faster or larger second response measured at a time when AP-1 protein has already decayed to baseline, which distinguishes a persistent AP-1 occupancy model from a latent primed-chromatin model.

question: ap1
title: "Nine Bean-Rows": Clonal Heritability of AP-1 State
description: Because memory implies transmission to daughters, barcode cells (CellTag/Watermelon-style) and sort on a live AP-1 activity reporter, then use scRNA-seq plus time-lapse lineage tracing to measure how strongly AP-1 state and the primed response correlate between sister, cousin, and more distant relatives as a function of generations since division. This partitions observed variance into heritable memory versus cell-intrinsic noise and yields a quantitative memory half-life in cell divisions.

question: ap1
title: "Peace Comes Dropping Slow": Timed Degron and Optogenetic Windows
description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons on AP-1 subunits, or optogenetic AP-1 constructs, to remove or supply AP-1 activity selectively during the encoding phase, the storage interval, or the recall challenge. Comparing these three windows separates whether AP-1 writes the memory, is required to maintain it, or is only needed to read it out, which is the central mechanistic distinction the question asks about.

question: ap1
title: "Veils of the Morning": Single-Molecule Footprinting of the Stored Trace
description: Apply long-read single-molecule footprinting (nanopore methyltransferase footprinting, or CUT&RUN with long-read sequencing) at primed enhancers during the memory interval to ask whether AP-1 is literally still bound or has lifted its veil and handed the trace off to nucleosome positioning, DNA methylation, cohesin, or mitotic bookmarking. Including mitotic timepoints tests whether AP-1 bookmarks its target enhancers through chromosome condensation.

question: ap1
title: "Lake Water Lapping": Frequency Encoding of Input History
description: Deliver the upstream stimulus as pulse trains of systematically varied frequency, amplitude, and duration using microfluidics or optogenetics, then compute the mutual information between past input history and current AP-1-dependent chromatin and transcriptional state. This tests whether AP-1 behaves as a leaky integrator that stores a running record of stimulation history rather than an instantaneous reporter of present signaling.

question: ap1
title: Prime–rest–rechallenge with windowed AP-1 degradation (the "inward eye" recall test)
description: Stimulate cells (serum, TGF-β, wounding, or drug), allow full return to baseline transcriptome, then restimulate days later and quantify whether the secondary response is faster, larger, or qualitatively different — the signature of recall. Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on FOS/JUN to delete AP-1 selectively during the priming window, the quiescent storage window, or the recall window, which dissociates AP-1's role as the writer, the maintainer, or merely the reader of the memory.

question: ap1
title: Single-cell lineage tracing of primed state through quiescence
description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with expressed lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/CellTag-style) so that individual primed cells and their descendants can be re-identified at rechallenge and profiled by scRNA-seq. This distinguishes true per-cell memory from a population-level artifact in which a pre-existing responsive subpopulation is simply selected or expanded, and it measures what fraction of cells actually retain the state.

question: ap1
title: Division-coupled decay and mitotic bookmarking assay
description: Prime cells, then use CFSE dilution or a FUCCI/division-counting reporter to sort descendants by number of divisions completed, and measure memory half-life in units of cell divisions rather than hours. In parallel, perform mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN and live imaging of tagged FOS/JUN in mitosis to test whether AP-1 remains bound to memory enhancers during mitosis, the physical mechanism that would allow the state to be copied to daughters.

question: ap1
title: Dimer-composition code at memory enhancers
description: Apply sequential/dual CUT&RUN (or CUT&Tag with antibodies against FOS, FOSB, FRA1, FRA2, JUN, JUNB, JUND) plus quantitative IP–mass spectrometry across the priming, resting, and recall phases to determine whether the persistent feature is a specific long-lived dimer, such as a FOSB/ΔFOSB-containing complex, rather than total AP-1 occupancy. Then swap dimer identity by targeted knock-in or degron and test whether memory duration tracks the dimer's protein half-life.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule binding kinetics and optogenetic pulse decoding
description: Use HaloTag single-molecule tracking and FRAP on endogenous JUN/FOS to measure residence time, bound fraction, and search kinetics at primed versus naive enhancers, testing whether memory is stored in binding dynamics even when ChIP-level occupancy appears unchanged. Pair this with optogenetic or chemically dimerizable AP-1 to deliver defined pulse amplitudes, durations, and frequencies, identifying the minimal dynamic input that installs a lasting chromatin-accessibility change measured by time-resolved ATAC-seq.

question: ap1
title: "Avulsion": timed degron depletion to separate establishment from maintenance
description: Drawing on avulsion (a sudden tearing-away) and fallway/unsloped (decay path vs. plateau), tag FOS and JUN with dTAG or auxin degrons, deliver a defined stimulus pulse, then acutely strip AP-1 at staggered delays while tracking accessibility (ATAC) and occupancy (CUT&RUN). Memory predicts a handoff whereby early depletion collapses the primed state but late depletion leaves an unsloped plateau; run with and without cell-cycle arrest to distinguish replication-coupled dilution from active erasure, and repeat with FOS/FOSB/JUNB swaps to test which family member (allonymous) carries the memory.

question: ap1
title: "Verveled" lineages: heritable barcoding to measure how long memory survives mitosis
description: A vervel is the owner's identifying ring on a hawk's leg; analogously, heritably barcode single cells (Watermelon/CellTag plus single-cell multiome), stimulate, allow several divisions, then restimulate and ask whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction propagate down clonal trees. The key measurement is the decay constant of sister- and cousin-cell correlation in AP-1 site accessibility as a function of generation number, distinguishing true inheritance from stochastic resampling.

question: ap1
title: Lexicon vs. usage: causal test that retained AP-1 sites drive the second response
description: The material is a list of words that exist in the dictionary but are almost never used, highlighting that an element being present is not evidence it is functional; likewise an open chromatin site is not necessarily a working memory element. Challenge primed cells with a second stimulus and measure nascent transcription (TT-seq, Pol II CUT&RUN, or live MS2 imaging of burst frequency and latency), then CRISPRi-silence or delete the retained AP-1 elements to test whether the potentiation disappears.

question: ap1
title: "Insulator": testing whether AP-1 memory is a bounded 3D neighborhood property
description: Taking the word insulator literally, map Micro-C and CTCF alongside ATAC before, during, and after stimulation, then degrade cohesin/RAD21 and insert synthetic CTCF boundaries adjacent to a memory locus. If primed accessibility spreads in cis and is halted by an engineered boundary, AP-1 memory is a property of an insulated neighborhood rather than an independent per-site mark.

question: ap1
title: "Quadratics": hysteresis and bistability in synthetic AP-1 site arrays
description: Build synthetic reporter arrays that vary AP-1 site number, spacing (spithame, a hand-span measure), and affinity, then measure the complete up-going and down-going dose-response to a tunable stimulus. A genuine memory mechanism should display hysteresis, with non-overlapping ascending and descending curves and a sharp switch-like threshold in site number, whereas a passively relaxing system retraces the same curve in both directions.

question: ap1
title: Glyphic test: separating AP-1 the writer from AP-1 the reader with acute degron depletion
description: Inspired by "glyphic" (a mark that outlasts the hand that cut it), tag FOS/JUN family members with auxin or dTAG degrons and deplete them either during a transient stimulus or only after washout, then assay ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN accessibility at AP-1 enhancers and the amplitude/latency of a second response. If memory requires AP-1 only during encoding but survives its post-stimulus removal, AP-1 writes the mark; if the potentiated second response collapses whenever AP-1 is absent, AP-1 is continuously read out rather than stored.

question: ap1
title: Semicolon experiment: AP-1 bookmarking across the mitotic break
description: A semicolon interrupts a sentence without severing it, which is the structural question for memory through cell division: image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN/ATF in live mitotic cells (plus mitotic CUT&RUN and H3S10ph-matched controls) to quantify retention on condensed chromatin at specific enhancers. Pair this with stimulating mother cells, tracking single daughters by lineage imaging, and testing whether potentiated re-induction is inherited and whether it is lost when bookmarking is disrupted by an AP-1 DNA-binding-deficient or mitosis-evicted mutant.

question: ap1
title: Hornbook grammar: an MPRA of AP-1 motif syntax under two-hit stimulation
description: Like a hornbook, where a few letters in defined arrangements generate the whole lexicon, build a synthetic reporter library systematically varying TRE/CRE motif number, spacing, affinity, and flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, CEBP, nucleosome-positioning sequences), and measure each variant's output after a single stimulus versus a stimulus-washout-restimulus protocol. This directly reads out which cis-grammars confer the hallmark of memory—faster, larger, or lower-threshold second responses—rather than mere responsiveness.

question: ap1
title: Weighing the engram: single-cell dose-response-to-memory transfer functions
description: Treating AP-1 as a "graduator" that meters an analog quantity, use live-cell endogenous FOS/JUN translational reporters with a dynamic transcriptional readout to measure, in the same cell, the integrated AP-1 activity during a first graded stimulus and the magnitude of the subsequent response weeks-to-hours later. Fitting the resulting transfer function distinguishes graded (analog, dose-proportional) memory from digital latching and reveals whether cell-to-cell variability in memory is predicted by AP-1 level or by a downstream bistable element.

question: ap1
title: Undo: targeted erasure and decay-rate measurement at individual AP-1 enhancers
description: Taking "undo" as the operative test of any memory claim, use dCas9-LSD1/HDAC/DNMT3A tethering, enhancer deletion, or CRISPRi tiling at specific stimulus-induced AP-1-bound enhancers after the stimulus is gone, and ask whether the potentiated second response is selectively erased while the naive response is preserved. In parallel, measure memory half-life across a washout time course with and without proliferation arrest to determine whether decay is set by chromatin turnover, dilution by cell division, or active removal.

question: ap1
title: Haploid test: allele-resolved AP-1 reporters
description: Use SNP-resolved allele-specific RNA FISH or dual-color knock-in reporters at the two alleles of an AP-1 target (e.g., AXL, SERPINE1) to test whether the same allele remains the high-expressing one across days and through cell division. Allele-autonomous, cis-restricted persistence implies chromatin-encoded memory rather than a diffusible trans-factor set point.

question: ap1
title: Leash-and-unkennel: pulse-release kinetics of Fos/Jun
description: Place FOS/JUN under optogenetic or dTAG/auxin degron control, deliver a defined pulse, then fully remove the factor and measure the decay half-life of the downstream state (ATAC accessibility, target RNA, drug-resistant colony formation) relative to division time. Persistence across many divisions after the input is gone is the operational signature of memory; rapid relaxation marks it as a maintained steady state.

question: ap1
title: Instructor versus terminator: lineage-barcoded causality
description: Combine barcode lineage tracing (Rewind/FateMap-style retrospective clone recovery) with sorting on an AP-1 activity reporter to test whether AP-1-high cells are the same clones that later survive drug selection. Pair with timed gain- and loss-of-function to distinguish AP-1 as an instructive writer of the state, a permissive reader, or merely the terminator of an already-established transition.

question: ap1
title: Relocable marks: identifying the physical memory substrate
description: Run a CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag time course for AP-1 occupancy, H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and nucleosome positioning at primed enhancers after factor withdrawal, plus DNA-FISH/Hi-C for enhancer repositioning and mitotic-chromosome staining for AP-1 bookmarking in synchronized cells. This separates heritable chromatin marks that outlive the factor from simple re-recruitment of AP-1 each cycle.

question: ap1
title: Tachylalia and esperance: burst kinetics and anticipatory re-stimulation
description: Use MS2 live-cell imaging of an AP-1 target to quantify whether the remembered state is encoded in burst frequency versus amplitude, and measure sister-cell correlation of burst frequency after mitosis. Then compare a second stimulus pulse to a naive first pulse: faster and larger reinduction, plus inherited burst frequency, is a quantitative memory signature distinguishable from residual mRNA or protein carryover.

question: ap1
title: Patination time course: decay kinetics of the AP-1 chromatin layer
description: Inspired by 'patination' (a surface layer that accrues with repeated exposure and persists), stimulate cells for varying doses/durations, withdraw the stimulus, and profile FOS/JUN CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, and H3K4me1/H3K27ac over hours to weeks at the same loci. Memory is supported if accessibility and H3K4me1 outlive AP-1 occupancy and accumulate with the number of prior exposures rather than resetting to baseline.

question: ap1
title: Bimodal single-cell re-response test
description: Taking the word 'bimodal' as the signature of a discrete latent state, use single-cell RNA/ATAC plus a live AP-1 target reporter to compare naive versus previously stimulated populations upon restimulation, testing statistically for bimodality rather than a uniform graded shift. Confirm that the high mode corresponds to cells retaining accessibility at AP-1 sites.

question: ap1
title: 'Unshifted' clonal barcode lineage tracing of the primed state
description: Memory must survive mitosis, so barcode cells, stimulate, sort responders, expand, and restimulate to ask whether responsiveness re-concentrates in the same barcodes. Sister-cell split experiments then quantify how many divisions the correlation persists, giving a heritability half-life for the AP-1 primed state.

question: ap1
title: Evacuative degron: separating establishment from maintenance
description: Tag endogenous FOS, JUN, and JUNB with dTAG/AID degrons and acutely deplete them either during the initial stimulus or only during the post-stimulus memory window. Persistence of memory after post-hoc depletion implies AP-1 writes a chromatin mark it no longer needs to hold, whereas collapse implies continuous AP-1 occupancy is itself the memory.

question: ap1
title: Vocabulary-without-grammar MPRA of AP-1 enhancer syntax
description: Echoing a word list that has lexicon but no syntax, build an integrated massively parallel reporter library varying AP-1 motif number, spacing, affinity, and flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, lineage factors). Measure which configurations sustain elevated output after stimulus withdrawal to determine whether memory resides in AP-1 sites alone or in their grammatical context.

question: ap1
title: Tasimetry: a quantitative memory transfer function
description: Stimulate cells across a matrix of AP-1-inducing doses and durations, wash out, wait defined intervals, then apply a deliberately sub-threshold second pulse and read out target induction by scRNA-seq or a live transcriptional reporter. Fitting response amplitude and latency against first-pulse strength and rest interval yields a memory gain curve and decay half-life, the minimal quantitative signature a true memory mechanism must show.

question: ap1
title: Epenthesis: motif insertion/deletion syntax library
description: Build an MPRA plus CRISPR knock-in library that inserts TRE/CRE motifs at varied copy number, spacing, and flanking context into naive and endogenous loci, and deletes them from memory-competent enhancers. Measuring which configurations retain accessibility and poised transcription after stimulus withdrawal separates motif presence from motif syntax as the actual carrier of memory.

question: ap1
title: Nucleosome hysteresis after stimulus washout
description: Run a washout time course combining ATAC-seq, Fos/Jun CUT&RUN, and high-resolution MNase footprinting to test whether enhancers remain nucleosome-depleted and H3K4me1/K27ac-marked after AP-1 occupancy falls below detection. Decoupling of accessibility from occupancy indicates a stored chromatin trace; synchronous loss argues AP-1 merely reports ongoing signaling.

question: ap1
title: Degron timing to separate establishment from maintenance
description: Tag endogenous Fos/Jun family members with auxin- or dTAG-inducible degrons and deplete them before stimulus, immediately after enhancer opening, and days into the rested state. Memory that survives acute late depletion but is erased during a defined consolidation window implies AP-1 writes to a stable substrate, whereas collapse at any time implies AP-1 is itself the store.

question: ap1
title: Clonal heritability and mitotic bookmarking
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes with a split-clone design to test whether re-challenge responsiveness after several divisions is clone-correlated rather than randomly distributed across the population. Pair this with live imaging and single-molecule residence-time measurements of Halo-tagged Fos/Jun during mitosis to test whether AP-1 physically bookmarks target enhancers through cell division.

question: ap1
title: "Underlap": decoupling AP-1 occupancy from the accessibility it leaves behind
description: Pulse cells with a stimulus and run parallel washout time courses of AP-1 protein abundance (Halo-tag live imaging/quantitative immunoblot), AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN), and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq). Memory is supported if a class of sites retains accessibility and H3K4me1/H3K27ac for many AP-1 protein half-lives after occupancy is undetectable, with a bimodal rather than occupancy-tracking decay-time distribution.

question: ap1
title: "Exaugurate": timed degron removal to map the window of AP-1 dependence
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN/JUNB with dTAG or AID degrons and ablate AP-1 at a graded series of delays after a priming pulse, then assay survival of the primed enhancer landscape and the potentiated secondary response. The latency at which degradation no longer erases memory defines the handoff from AP-1 to a maintenance mechanism such as nucleosome positioning, a partner TF, or DNA methylation loss.

question: ap1
title: "Cathood": clonal inheritance of the primed state through division
description: Combine expressed lentiviral barcodes with a split-clone design: prime a population, allow 1-8 divisions without stimulus, then assay one half of each clone by scATAC/scRNA-seq and challenge the other half. Heritability is quantified as within- versus between-clone concordance of AP-1-site accessibility and secondary-response magnitude, with dilution versus faithful copying distinguished by the slope across division number.

question: ap1
title: "Prewelcome": dual-pulse recall kinetics at single-allele resolution
description: Knock MS2/PP7 cassettes into AP-1 target genes and live-image transcriptional bursting across a priming pulse, rest interval, and second pulse, testing whether memory appears as shortened latency, higher burst frequency, or reduced cell-to-cell variance. Critically, test whether the same alleles that fired first fire again, establishing allele-level rather than merely cell-level memory.

question: ap1
title: "Tetrasemic"/"hemiglyph": synthetic AP-1 enhancer ladders to find the dose-memory law
description: Integrate at a single safe-harbor locus a panel of reporters with 1, 2, 4, or 8 canonical TRE sites plus half-site and spacing variants, and measure both initial induction and retained memory after washout. Supralinear scaling of memory depth with site number alongside linear scaling of initial induction would implicate cooperative, self-reinforcing occupancy as the storage mechanism rather than proportional signal readout.

question: ap1
title: A "lexicon of latent entries": decay-constant atlas of AP-1 sites after transient stimulus
description: Run a dense time course (hours to weeks) after a transient stimulus measuring FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC), and AP-1 protein levels, fitting a per-site decay constant to classify elements as transient versus long-lived, like rare words retained in a dictionary long after use. Memory predicts a reproducible subpopulation whose accessibility half-life far exceeds that of AP-1 occupancy, with single-molecule tracking of Halo-JUN testing whether persistence reflects longer residence time rather than more protein.

question: ap1
title: Erasing entries: acute degron depletion after the memory is written
description: Tag FOS/JUNB and paralogs with dTAG/AID degrons and deplete them only after priming, asking whether AP-1 is the scribe or the inscription. Survival of primed accessibility and enhanced secondary response implies downstream storage (nucleosome state, histone marks, DNA methylation), whereas collapse implies AP-1 occupancy itself is the memory substrate; re-addition tests reversibility.

question: ap1
title: Heritability through division: clonal barcoding plus multiome
description: Combine heritable lentiviral barcodes (Rewind/FateMap-style) with scATAC+scRNA multiome to test whether primed AP-1 states are concordant within clones and transmitted across mitoses, since a dictionary is memory only if editions are copied faithfully. Quantifying within- versus between-clone variance in AP-1 motif accessibility over 5-20 divisions, in cycling versus arrested cells, separates heritable epigenetic memory from slow protein-level hysteresis.

question: ap1
title: Spelling rules for persistence: synthetic AP-1 element libraries
description: Genomically integrate a library of thousands of synthetic elements varying TRE/CRE motif identity, affinity, copy number, spacing and helical phasing, nucleosome-positioning sequence, and partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, ETS, NF-kB), reading out both acute and weeks-later retained activity. This identifies the minimal cis-grammar that converts a transient input into a stored one, analogous to how a word's morphology predicts its survival in a lexicon.

question: ap1
title: Does the lexicon record order? Combinatorial stimulus-sequencing experiments
description: Deliver two or three distinct AP-1-activating inputs (growth factor, cytokine, mechanical stretch) in all permutations and intervals, then test whether the final AP-1 landscape and response amplitude depend on order and spacing or only on the set of stimuli, since the material is an unordered list. Path-dependence would indicate a sequence-sensitive trace, set-dependence an unordered vocabulary of past exposures, and interval titration yields the memory capacity and timescale.

question: ap1
title: Sister-cell/clonal recurrence test of AP-1 memory heritability ("recur")
description: Barcode a population (e.g., Watermelon/ClonMapper-style lineage barcodes), stimulate transiently, then let clones expand and re-stimulate: if AP-1 is a memory mechanism, the magnitude of the secondary AP-1 response should be far more correlated among cells sharing a barcode than among unrelated cells, and that intraclonal correlation should decay with a measurable number of divisions. Combine with split-clone designs (one half naive, one half primed) and single-cell multiome to show the heritable unit is AP-1 motif accessibility rather than a generic proliferative state.

question: ap1
title: Mitotic bookmarking by FOS/JUN at memory enhancers ("dyaster")
description: Test whether AP-1 remains chromatin-bound through mitosis by performing CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for FOS/JUN and ATAC-seq on mitotically arrested and sorted primed vs. naive cells, paired with live-cell Halo-JUN imaging and FRAP on condensed chromosomes to measure residence time. Then test necessity with a cell-cycle-restricted auxin/dTAG degron that removes AP-1 only during the M-phase window, asking whether daughter cells lose the primed response while cells degraded in G1 retain it.

question: ap1
title: Degron epistasis separating writing, maintenance, and reading ("unmask")
description: Using dTAG- or auxin-tagged endogenous FOS/JUN (and a FOS-family-wide degron to handle redundancy), degrade AP-1 in three nonoverlapping windows — during the priming stimulus, during the quiescent memory interval, and only at re-stimulation — and score secondary response amplitude, latency, and enhancer accessibility. This distinguishes AP-1 as the writer that unmasks latent enhancers, as a continuously required maintenance factor, or merely as the reader that exploits a trace stored by other means (e.g., H3K4me1, CTCF loops, DNA methylation).

question: ap1
title: Dose- and pulse-layering to test accretive memory ("serpulidan")
description: Deliver controlled trains of stimulus pulses (varying number, amplitude, and spacing, ideally with optogenetic or small-molecule-gated AP-1 input) and ask whether primed AP-1 enhancer accessibility and secondary output accumulate in discrete, stimulus-countable increments rather than tracking only the most recent or the integrated dose. Fitting the resulting response surface discriminates a genuine accretive recorder from a slow-relaxation filter, and identifies the subset of "layer-forming" AP-1 sites for follow-up.

question: ap1
title: Single-molecule footprinting of the residual trace ("limacel")
description: Apply single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (SMF/Fiber-seq) at AP-1 memory enhancers days after the stimulus has decayed, to distinguish on individual DNA fibers between persistent low-level AP-1 occupancy, a bound-factor-free but nucleosome-depleted "empty shell," and fully reclosed chromatin. Quantifying the fraction of molecules in each state, and how that fraction predicts single-cell secondary response by paired scSMF/transcriptome readout, tests whether the stored trace is a structural remnant rather than ongoing signaling.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing across drug exposure
description: Introduce heritable random barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcode libraries) into a clonal population before treatment, then sequence barcodes in survivors and in pre-treatment cells. Matching barcodes between the two timepoints will show whether survivors come from a pre-existing subclone or arise de novo from drug-induced reprogramming.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiomics predicting survival
description: Perform paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) on untreated cells, then compare the profiles of cells that later survive versus die using a lineage-linked readout such as barcodes or live-cell photoconversion. Identifying transcriptional or chromatin-accessibility signatures that predict survival would reveal whether tolerance is primed before the drug is given.

question: persister
title: Live-cell reporter tracking of individual fates
description: Use fluorescent reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell-cycle phase, ERK-KTR for pathway activity, and a drug-efflux or stress reporter) in time-lapse microscopy during drug exposure. Linking each cell's reporter state before and during treatment to its eventual death or survival will show which dynamic signaling or cell-cycle states confer tolerance.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens with survival bottlenecks
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens at high library coverage under a strong drug dose that kills most cells, then compare guide representation in survivors against untreated controls. Hits that enrich in survivors point to genes whose loss or gain is needed for tolerance, and comparing them with resistance screens from chronic exposure separates transient from stable mechanisms.

question: persister
title: Chromatin and metabolic profiling of sorted survivors with reversibility tests
description: Sort or harvest surviving cells after a short drug pulse and profile their chromatin (CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me3, ATAC-seq), metabolism (mitochondrial respiration, lipid and iron/ferroptosis markers), and proteome against bulk controls. Then test whether the survivor state is reversible by drug holidays and by inhibiting the implicated epigenetic or metabolic pathways, which distinguishes an adaptive epigenetic state from a fixed genetic one.

question: persister
title: Single-cell lineage tracing with barcoded clones
description: Introduce heritable random DNA barcodes (e.g., CRISPR-based or lentiviral barcodes) into a clonal population, treat with the targeted drug, and follow barcode frequencies over time and in persister-enriched fractions. This reveals whether survival is pre-determined in a subset of clones (pre-existing tolerance) or arises stochastically/induced during treatment, and how many independent lineages contribute to the surviving population.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment single-cell profiling linked to fate
description: Perform single-cell RNA-seq and/or ATAC-seq on untreated cells, then use live-cell reporters or sorting to isolate cells that will survive versus die after drug exposure, and compare their baseline transcriptional and chromatin states. Identifying a predictive signature (e.g., stemness, drug-efflux, or cell-cycle markers) would show whether survival is encoded before treatment.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved live-cell imaging of drug response
description: Use fluorescent reporters for the drug target pathway (such as ERK activity or cell-cycle sensors) together with longitudinal microscopy to track individual cells from drug addition through death or survival. This captures the kinetics of signaling changes, whether survivors show delayed or incomplete pathway suppression, and whether they divide during treatment.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screens for persistence modifiers
description: Run genome-wide CRISPR knockout or CRISPRa/i screens under sustained drug exposure and compare guide representation in surviving cells versus controls at multiple timepoints. Hits that enrich in survivors point to genes whose loss or gain enables tolerance, and can be validated for causal roles in persistence.

question: persister
title: Epigenetic and chromatin perturbation to test memory of survival
description: Measure chromatin accessibility, histone marks, and DNA methylation in persister cells sorted after drug withdrawal versus drug-naive cells, then perturb candidate epigenetic regulators (e.g., KDM5 family, DNMTs, or BET proteins) to see if persistence is reversed. Comparing drug-naive, persister, and drug-removed-regrown populations separates transient adaptive states from stable, heritable changes.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing with drug pulses
description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes in survivors versus the pre-treatment pool. Shared barcodes across survivors reveal whether persisters are pre-existing, clonally selected, or arise from a non-genetic switch in many cells. Adding washout and re-challenge arms tests whether the surviving state is reversible.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multi-omics time course during treatment
description: Profile scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or multiome) on cells at baseline, early after drug exposure, and at several later timepoints, then compare the trajectories of cells that die with those that persist. Pre-treatment states that predict survival, such as chromatin accessibility at lineage or stress genes, can be identified and tested for causality.

question: persister
title: Live-cell reporter imaging linked to fate
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell cycle (e.g., FUCCI), stress signaling (e.g., NF-κB or p53 activity), or a drug-target pathway readout, and track individual cells with time-lapse microscopy through treatment. Retrospectively correlating each cell's reporter dynamics before and during drug exposure with its eventual death or survival reveals the dynamic signatures that distinguish persisters.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screen comparing survivors with the bulk population
description: Run genome-wide or epigenome-focused CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screens under drug treatment and sequence guides in survivors versus untreated controls. Genes whose loss either eliminates or enriches persisters point to the regulators of tolerance, and follow-up with arrayed validation can separate primary survival mechanisms from bystander effects.

question: persister
title: Metabolic and epigenetic state profiling of sorted persisters
description: Sort out drug-tolerant cells from a reporter or viability-based gate and profile them for mitochondrial function, metabolite levels, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility compared with sensitive cells. Testing whether pharmacologically perturbing the identified pathway (for example, OXPHOS inhibition or a histone demethylase inhibitor) changes survival fraction would establish whether the state is functionally necessary.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing across drug pulses
description: Introduce heritable cellular barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcode libraries) into a clonal population, then apply the targeted drug and track which barcoded lineages survive. Comparing barcode frequencies before and after treatment, and across washout and re-challenge, shows whether survivors were pre-existing rare clones or arose through drug-induced reprogramming.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment sorting and profiling of future survivors
description: Use live-cell reporters or surface markers to sort cells before drug exposure, then profile sorted subpopulations and the survivor fraction with single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. This tests whether a transcriptional or chromatin state that predicts survival already exists in the untreated population.

question: persister
title: Live-cell signaling and cell-cycle reporters linked to fate
description: Express biosensors such as ERK or AKT kinase translocation reporters and FUCCI cell-cycle markers, then image individual cells continuously through drug addition and record their fate. Correlating signaling amplitude, dynamics, and cell-cycle phase at the moment of treatment with eventual survival identifies the dynamic states that predict persistence.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide and single-cell CRISPR screens under drug pressure
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screens with the drug, comparing guide representation in surviving versus dying cells, and follow hits with Perturb-seq to see how each perturbation shifts the persister state. Hits from chromatin, signaling, and stress-response genes point to the mechanisms that enable survival, and validation of top candidates tests whether they are necessary and sufficient.

question: persister
title: Metabolic and epigenetic priming profiling with washout and re-challenge
description: Measure metabolic state (for example NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging, mitochondrial respiration, and metabolomics) and key histone marks or chromatin accessibility in pre-treatment, early-treatment, and surviving cells. Then remove the drug and re-challenge: if survivors retain their metabolic or epigenetic signature across several passages, the data point to a heritable adaptive memory, while loss of the signature implies a reversible tolerance state.

question: persister
title: Single-cell lineage barcoding with drug-response tracking
description: Label a clonal cancer population with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CRISPR-based lineage tracers), treat with the targeted drug, and track which lineages persist and how their transcriptomes and chromatin states differ before treatment. This separates pre-existing 'drug-tolerant' clones from cells that switch state after exposure.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment single-cell multi-omics to find predictive baseline states
description: Profile untreated cells with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) and use machine learning to identify baseline features, such as expression of stress, quiescence, or drug-efflux genes, that predict which cells will survive. Validate by sorting the predicted tolerant subpopulation and testing its drug response.

question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging with reporter-based fate tracking
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell cycle (e.g., FUCCI), signaling activity (e.g., ERK or AKT biosensors), and drug-target engagement, and follow individual cells over days of treatment. This reveals whether survivors were in a slow-cycling or signaling-low state before drug exposure, or whether they adapt over time.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved persister-state transitions with pulse-chase drug exposure
description: Expose cells to the drug for short pulses, then wash out and sort survivors at multiple timepoints for bulk or single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. This distinguishes stable genetic or epigenetic persistence from transient, reversible drug-tolerant states that re-enter the cycle after drug withdrawal.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens for survival and resistance mechanisms
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens under sublethal drug doses, comparing sequencing of survivors versus the starting population to identify genes that enable survival without acquired mutations. Follow up hits with combination-drug tests to determine whether the survival machinery is a druggable vulnerability.

question: persister
title: Single-cell lineage barcoding with drug-response tracking
description: Introduce heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CRISPR-based scar or lentiviral barcode libraries) into a clonal population, treat with the targeted drug, and track barcode frequencies and transcriptomes over time. This reveals whether survivors are pre-existing clones or arise from non-genetic state transitions, and whether they share a common precursor identity.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment single-cell profiling to find predictive states
description: Perform scRNA-seq and/or ATAC-seq on untreated cells, then sort or computationally back-trace the cells that later survive (e.g., via live-cell reporters or FACS-based pulse-labeling of persisters). Comparing survivors to non-survivors before drug exposure identifies baseline chromatin, metabolic, or cell-cycle features that predispose cells to persistence.

question: persister
title: Live-cell reporter tracking of persister emergence
description: Use fluorescent reporters for drug target pathway activity, cell-cycle phase (e.g., FUCCI), or stress signaling (e.g., NRF2, p53) combined with time-lapse microscopy under drug. Following individual cells from drug addition to survival or death reveals whether persistence is tied to a transient signaling or cycle state at the moment of treatment.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens for survival versus drug sensitivity
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens under sublethal and lethal drug doses, sequencing guides in surviving cells at multiple time points. Hits enriched among survivors identify genes whose loss or gain shifts the fraction of persisters, pointing to the pathways that confer tolerance rather than resistance.

title: Pre-treatment baseline correlated with post-treatment fate

question: persister
title: Four-point susceptibility of drug survival events

question: persister
title: Propensity analysis from pre-treatment single-cell state
description: Before drug exposure, record each cell's morphology, cell-cycle reporter (e.g., FUCCI), signaling activity (e.g., ERK or AKT biosensors), and mitochondrial state, then train a classifier to predict which cells survive and which die. question: persister
title: Null-model tests against spatial and lineage structure

question: persister
title: Barcode-based lineage tracing of tolerant state inheritance
description: Label founder cells with heritable DNA barcodes and track them through drug exposure and recovery to determine whether the survival state is passed to daughters and how long it persists across generations. question: persister
title: Washout and re-challenge to measure tolerance relaxation

question: persister
title: Live-cell single-cell fate tracking with fluorescent activity reporters
description: Borrowing the single-particle fluorescence probe approach, track thousands of individual cells under drug with a live reporter for a readout such as caspase-3/7 activity, ERK-KTR signaling, or mitochondrial membrane potential, recording each cell's trajectory over days. Sort the cells that stay active or survive and compare their pre-treatment reporter levels to those of cells that die.

question: persister
title: Same-cell multiplexed profiling before and during treatment
description: Mirroring operando spectroscopy in the same reactor, use imaging mass cytometry, multiplexed immunofluorescence, or cyclic imaging to measure phospho-proteins, drug-target occupancy, and efflux-pump levels in the same cells at several time points during treatment. This shows whether survival is linked to a specific signaling state that changes over time, rather than to a fixed trait.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment feature mapping linked to later survival
description: Analogous to TEM/STEM imaging before and after reaction, record baseline single-cell features (cell size, cell-cycle phase, organelle content, chromatin marks) by imaging, then follow the same cells through treatment and use correlative imaging to identify which pre-existing features predict survival. Survivors are then checked for the presence or absence of those features.

question: persister
title: Comparing survival with the distribution of a baseline variable
description: Following the particle-size comparison, measure a candidate intrinsic variable (drug-target expression, efflux transporter levels, DNA content, or cell size) across the whole population by flow cytometry or single-cell RNA-seq, then compare its distribution with the distribution among survivors. question: persister
title: Pulse-chase drug exposure with lineage barcoding
description: Use a probe-style approach by pulsing the drug for a short period and then withdrawing it, combined with heritable DNA barcodes, to see whether surviving cells are a pre-existing subpopulation or a transiently induced state. question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug-level mapping
description: Quantify effective intracellular drug concentration per cell, using fluorescent drug analogs or imaging mass spectrometry, and sort by drug level to test whether survivors simply accumulate less drug through reduced uptake, increased efflux, or lysosomal sequestration. question: persister
title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy sorting before treatment

question: persister
title: Per-cell protein turnover profiling

question: persister
title: Density-dependent and secreted-factor dependence of survival

question: persister
title: Asymmetric partitioning of tolerance factors at mitosis
description: Use live imaging with fluorescently tagged drug target or efflux proteins to track how these proteins partition between daughter cells at division, and correlate the inherited amount with each daughter's fate under drug. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming in each cell before drug exposure (BH3 profiling by flow cytometry, with cytochrome c release after BH3 peptides), then sort high- and low-priming subpopulations and compare their survival under the drug. question: persister
title: Per-cell drug accumulation linked to target occupancy
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable analog of the drug, or a target-engagement biosensor, to measure intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy in individual live cells by imaging. question: persister
title: Death-hazard kinetics from single-cell fate tracking
description: Track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with a caspase or apoptosis reporter and record each cell's time to death, arrest, or escape. question: persister
title: Chromosomal instability reporter sorting with clonal re-derivation

question: persister
title: Neighbor-density and local contact perturbation

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification and sorting
description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates, using a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging, then sort low- and high-accumulating cells and test whether low uptake or lysosomal sequestration alone predicts survival. question: persister
title: Lineage-tracked proteostasis inheritance
description: Use photoconvertible or tandem aggregation reporters with time-lapse mother-daughter tracking to test whether survivors inherit lower protein-aggregate or misfolded-protein burden through division. question: persister
title: Paracrine rescue by survivor-secreted factors
description: Fractionate conditioned medium from survivor cultures, identify candidate secreted proteins or metabolites by mass spectrometry, and test whether they rescue drug-sensitive cells in co-culture. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment ERK/AKT signaling dynamics with optogenetic causality test
description: Track ERK and AKT activity pulses in single living cells with FRET biosensors before drug addition, and check whether pulse frequency or amplitude predicts later survival. Then use optogenetic control of the pulses to test whether the dynamics cause the survival difference.

question: persister
title: Nascent translation rate as a pre-treatment predictor
description: Quantify per-cell nascent protein synthesis with puromycin or HPG labeling at the start of treatment, sort by translation rate, and test whether high-translation cells survive more and are more sensitive to translation inhibitors. This tests whether a protein-synthesis state, rather than transcription, sets tolerance.

question: persister
title: Single-cell ecDNA copy-number tracking
description: Quantify extrachromosomal DNA copy number per cell (FISH on metaphase spreads or interphase, plus single-cell DNA sequencing) before drug exposure and in survivors. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment target-engagement imaging linked to fate
description: Pre-load live cells with a clickable or fluorescent version of the inhibitor, or a target-occupancy reporter, and image per-cell effective drug occupancy before adding the drug. Sort cells by occupancy, re-plate them under treatment, and check whether low-engagement cells are the ones that survive.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned density and contact control
description: Grow cells on micropatterned islands that set local density, cell spreading, and cell-cell contact independently of clone size. Measure survival fraction under drug as a function of geometry, and test whether the effect runs through mechanotransduction (YAP/TAZ) by perturbing it.

question: persister
title: Proteostasis inheritance through division

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy at single-cell resolution

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment mitochondrial membrane potential sorting with mtDNA heteroplasmy readout
description: Sort live cells by baseline TMRM or MitoTracker signal before drug exposure, challenge each sorted pool with the drug, and sequence mtDNA and measure OXPHOS capacity in survivors. question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug accumulation as a pharmacokinetic filter
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in individual cells using a clickable or intrinsically detectable drug analog, or by single-cell mass spectrometry imaging, and correlate it with later survival in live-cell tracking. question: persister
title: Live ERK/AKT activity pulse dynamics before treatment, linked to fate
description: Express kinase translocation reporters (e.g., ERK-KTR) in a clonal population and record pulse frequency and amplitude for many hours before adding drug. question: persister
title: Nascent protein synthesis rate per cell as a survival predictor
description: Label newly made proteins with puromycin or OPP click chemistry in single cells before treatment, sort by translation rate, and challenge each sorted fraction with the drug. question: persister
title: Spatial mapping of survivors within micropatterned or density-controlled colonies

question: persister
title: Sort pre-treatment cells by mitochondrial membrane potential, then challenge

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug quantification by imaging mass cytometry
description: Use a mass-tagged or fluorescent analog of the drug, or mass spectrometry imaging, to measure intracellular drug concentration in each cell shortly after dosing. question: persister
title: Time-to-death distributions from a live caspase biosensor

question: persister
title: Nuclear mechanics and chromatin compaction measured by microfluidic constriction

question: persister
title: Smfish and live-cell MS2 imaging of transcriptional bursting in efflux and target genes

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment ERK/AKT pulse dynamics linked to fate
description: Use live fluorescent kinase translocation or FRET reporters to record signaling pulse frequency and amplitude in each cell before drug addition, then score each cell's fate after treatment. question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug and target-engagement quantification
description: Combine fluorescent or isotope-labeled drug analogs with imaging or flow-based readouts to measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates and how much target is occupied (e.g., with a NanoBRET or CETSA-style readout). question: persister
title: Spatial niche and neighbor-density effects on survival
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and in mixed co-cultures, then use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to map survivors relative to their neighbors and local secreted-factor gradients. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment mechanical phenotype sorting
description: Sort cells by nuclear and whole-cell deformability using microfluidic deformability cytometry or AFM before drug exposure, then test the sorted fractions for drug tolerance and compare their cytoskeletal and nuclear-lamina profiles. question: persister
title: Per-cell nascent translation rate as a predictor of tolerance
description: Measure nascent protein synthesis in individual cells using puromycin incorporation or a SunTag-based translation reporter before treatment, sort high- and low-translation fractions, and compare their drug responses. question: persister
title: Live-cell kinase reporter rebound kinetics
description: Expose cells to a titrated dose of a targeted inhibitor while imaging a live ERK or AKT translocation biosensor (KTR) in each cell. question: persister
title: Asymmetric drug partitioning at mitosis
description: Use the intrinsic autofluorescence of the drug, or a fluorescent analog, with time-lapse imaging and daughter-cell tracking across division. question: persister
title: Single-cell mtDNA heteroplasmy and membrane potential
description: Sort cells by mitochondrial membrane potential (e.g., TMRM) before drug exposure, then perform single-cell or clonal mtDNA sequencing to measure heteroplasmy in each sorted fraction. question: persister
title: Drug-induced mutagenesis fluctuation assay
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests with a reporter for mutation under sublethal drug, and compare the mutation rate and spectrum in survivor clones with those from drug-naive lineages. question: persister
title: Lysosomal sequestration of basic-amine inhibitors
description: For kinase inhibitors with basic amines, co-stain for lysosomal volume and acidity (LysoTracker, LAMP1) and measure per-cell drug fluorescence by imaging or flow cytometry. question: persister
title: Barcode lineage tracing to separate pre-existing from drug-induced survivors
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expand the population, treat with drug, and use scRNA-seq to see whether surviving barcoded clones were already transcriptionally distinct before treatment. question: persister
title: Live-cell signaling and cell-cycle reporters with retrospective fate tracking
description: Express a KTR-type ERK or AKT activity reporter together with a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter, image cells by time-lapse before and during drug exposure, and compute each cell's signaling pulse frequency and cycle phase history. Comparing these dynamics between cells that die and cells that survive tests whether temporal signaling behavior, not average activity, predicts survival.

question: persister
title: Sorting on pre-treatment mitochondrial state and testing survival and metabolism
description: Sort the untreated population by TMRM or mitochondrial membrane potential and by NADH autofluorescence, then challenge each fraction with drug and measure survival. Pair this with 13C tracing on sorted survivors to determine whether an OXPHOS-high or glycolysis-high metabolic state is a causal, pre-existing determinant of persistence.

question: persister
title: Single-cell measurement of drug uptake and efflux heterogeneity
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs or intracellular LC-MS on sorted subpopulations to quantify how much drug each cell accumulates and how quickly it is pumped out. question: persister
title: Drug-holiday and re-challenge assays to test reversibility and epigenetic memory
description: Expose cells to drug until a persister pool forms, withdraw drug for several passages, then re-challenge and track the survivor fraction and CUT&Tag or ATAC profiles over time. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
description: Track signaling and cell-cycle reporters (e.g., FUCCI, ERK-KTR, p53 pulses) in individual cells before drug exposure, then map each cell's pre-treatment state to its post-treatment fate. This tests directly whether survival is predictable from a cell's state at the time of treatment.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced tolerance
description: Introduce heritable barcodes into the population, treat, and use scRNA-seq to see whether survivors share barcodes with pre-marked clones or arise from many lineages that switch state after drug exposure. This distinguishes selection of rare pre-adapted cells from drug-induced reprogramming.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration in each cell using fluorescent drug analogs or imaging mass spectrometry, and correlate it with survival. Differences in uptake or efflux could explain survival even when target and genotype are identical.

question: persister
title: Chromatin accessibility priming with epigenetic perturbation
description: Use scATAC-seq on untreated cells to find regions that are already open near survival-associated genes in the rare cells that later persist. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they are causal for tolerance.

question: persister
title: Metabolic state sorting by NAD(P)H FLIM
description: Measure each cell's NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime as a label-free readout of its metabolic state, sort cells by that readout, and test whether the metabolically distinct subsets differ in drug survival. question: persister
title: Pre-treatment reporter tracking linked to retrospective single-cell profiling
description: Use live-cell fluorescent reporters (e.g., CDK2 activity, cell-cycle or stress-pathway sensors) to follow individual cells through drug exposure and record their fate. question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding to distinguish pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance
description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable DNA barcode before treatment and track barcode frequencies through drug exposure and recovery. If survivors come from a small set of pre-marked clones, tolerance was pre-existing; if barcodes are randomly represented, tolerance is induced by the drug.

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification
description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates, using fluorescent analogs of the drug or LC-MS on flow-sorted cells. Test whether survivors have lower intracellular drug levels due to uptake or efflux differences rather than altered target biology.

question: persister
title: Chromatin accessibility priming and causal perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility by scATAC-seq in drug-naive cells and identify regions that are open in cells that later survive. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they causally change survival fraction.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell transcriptomic readout
description: Run a genome-wide knockout screen under drug treatment with single-cell RNA readout so each perturbation's effect on both survival and cell state is measured together. This separates genes that drive survival from those that merely mark a tolerant state.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding plus scRNA-seq to trace survivor origin
description: Label each cell with a heritable barcode before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies and transcriptomes of survivors to pre-treatment clones. This shows whether survivors were pre-existing lineages with a stable state or arose from induced switching in cells that were not previously distinguished.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
description: Track individual cells with a cell-cycle or stress reporter before drug addition, then add the drug and follow each cell to death or survival. Matching pre-treatment reporter state to eventual fate tests whether slow cycling or a specific pre-drug state predicts survival.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
description: Quantify intracellular drug levels in individual cells with a fluorescent analog, or in sorted subpopulations by LC-MS, and relate them to survival. This tests whether differences in uptake, efflux, or sequestration, rather than target biology, explain why some cells escape.

question: persister
title: Sort-and-replate memory and heritability assay
description: Sort cells defined by a survival-linked reporter before treatment, re-expose them to drug, and measure how well the survival phenotype is inherited across divisions and after drug withdrawal.
