question: persister
title: Endogenous target-abundance and noise profiling
description: Tag the drug target at its endogenous locus and quantify per-cell target protein levels and their variability before treatment. Testing whether cells with low target abundance or high expression noise are preferentially spared identifies a dose-target stoichiometry mechanism that could be therapeutically exploited.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment lineage barcoding with fate mapping
description: Label individual progenitor cells with heritable DNA barcodes before drug exposure, then sequence barcodes in survivors after treatment. If surviving clones share barcodes with specific pre-treatment clones, survival reflects pre-existing cell identity rather than stochastic or induced changes.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment live-cell imaging linked to fate
description: Track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with cell-cycle and stress reporters (e.g., FUCCI, pathway-activity biosensors) before drug addition, then record each cell's fate. Machine-learning models on pre-treatment features can test whether survival is predictable from measurable single-cell states.

question: persister
title: Chromatin accessibility priming in early-treated cells
description: Profile ATAC-seq and histone marks in cells sorted by early drug response (e.g., reporter activation at 24 h) versus bulk. Differential accessibility at lineage or stress genes would indicate epigenetic priming that precedes survival.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR activation and interference screen for persister modifiers
description: Run pooled CRISPRa and CRISPRi screens under sublethal-to-lethal drug doses and sequence surviving cells to identify genes that raise or lower persister frequency. Hits that act only when the drug is present point to tolerance mechanisms distinct from baseline essentiality.

question: persister
title: Replay-and-reversibility test of heritable tolerance
description: Sort surviving cells, expand them drug-free, and re-challenge them alongside parental cells, measuring survival fraction and tracking reversion over multiple cycles. Persistent tolerance after drug withdrawal indicates a heritable epigenetic memory, whereas rapid reversion indicates a transient, reversible state.

question: persister
title: Baseline signaling and cell-cycle dynamics with fate tracking
description: Expose cells to live-cell reporters (e.g., ERK-KTR and FUCCI) before adding the drug, then track each cell's history and fate. This tests whether survivors already occupy distinct signaling pulse patterns or cell-cycle states that predict survival, before any treatment.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding coupled to single-cell transcriptomics
description: Label founder cells with heritable barcodes, challenge with drug, and sequence both barcode and transcriptome at single-cell resolution. This distinguishes survivors that descend from a few pre-existing clones from survivors that reach a shared state through induced switching.

question: persister
title: Sorting by drug accumulation and mitochondrial state
description: Sort live cells by efflux-pump activity, intracellular drug level, or mitochondrial membrane potential, then challenge each fraction with the drug. Pair this with mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing to test whether intracellular drug handling or OXPHOS state primes survival.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screen with time-resolved persister sampling
description: Run a genome-wide knockout or CRISPRi screen and sample at several times during drug exposure and during drug holidays. Comparing enrichment dynamics separates genes that set persister frequency from genes that maintain the tolerant state.

question: persister
title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility priming before treatment
description: Profile chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) and transcription jointly on untreated cells, then identify loci accessible in future survivors. Validate candidate regulators by sorting for accessibility and testing survival in the sorted cells.

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification linked to fate

question: persister
title: Live-cell cell-cycle reporter tracking at drug addition
description: Use FUCCI or a similar reporter with time-lapse imaging to record each cell's cycle phase when the drug is added and follow it to death or division. This tests whether quiescent or slow-cycling cells are the ones that persist, and whether they re-enter the cycle later.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding combined with pre-treatment scRNA-seq
description: Barcode cells before treatment, profile their transcriptomes, then see which barcoded lineages and states survive. This separates survivors that were already in a distinct state from survivors whose state was induced by the drug, and shows whether a few clones dominate.

question: persister
title: Reversibility and memory test of sorted survivors

question: persister
title: Causal pooled CRISPR with single-cell readout
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen read out by single-cell RNA-seq under drug, and check which knockouts shift cells out of the survivor state or change their survival. This tests whether candidate survival programs are causal rather than just correlated with survival.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with drug challenge and transcriptomic readout
description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable barcode, expose the population to the drug, and sequence barcodes plus transcriptomes of survivors. This tests whether survivors arise from a few pre-existing clones or from stochastic, independent cell-level switches, and whether survivor states are inherited.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Measure each subpopulation's mitochondrial apoptotic priming with BH3 profiling before drug exposure, then sort high- and low-priming cells and challenge each with the drug. question: persister
title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome of chromatin priming before and during treatment
description: Profile paired ATAC and RNA in drug-naive cells and at early drug timepoints to find accessible-chromatin states and transcription factor motifs that predict survival. Validate top factors by perturbing them and measuring survival.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and OXPHOS heterogeneity in survivors
description: Sequence mtDNA and image membrane potential and respiration in sorted survivor and dying populations. Test whether naturally varying mitochondrial genotype or function among genetically identical nuclear genomes sets drug tolerance.

question: persister

description: Label a population with a heritable DNA barcode library (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcodes), then compare barcode clone frequencies before and after drug exposure and after drug withdrawal and re-challenge. question: persister
title: Live-cell reporter tracking of pre-treatment predictors
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell-cycle phase (FUCCI), signaling activity (e.g., ERK-KTR), or stress state, and follow individual cells through drug exposure with time-lapse imaging. This tests whether survival is a stable, binary trait and whether a single endpoint captures it.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiomics on sorted pre-treatment subpopulations
description: Profile transcriptome and chromatin accessibility (scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq) of the untreated population, then train a classifier that predicts which cells survive and check it with sorted cells in a validation experiment. question: persister
title: Single-cell mtDNA heteroplasmy as a natural lineage barcode
description: Use mtDNA variants, which occur naturally and are inherited maternally, as endogenous lineage markers by applying single-cell mtDNA-calling methods (e.g., mgatk-style analysis of scATAC or scRNA reads) to pre-treatment and survivor populations. Shared heteroplasmic haplotypes across timepoints reveal the clonal origin of survivors without any engineered barcode, and may expose mitochondrial genotype as a survival determinant.

question: persister
title: Micronucleus rupture and cGAS-STING history as a survival predictor
description: Use live imaging of a nuclear-localization reporter and a cGAS sensor to score which cells form micronuclei, rupture them, or activate innate immune signaling during the first drug cycle. Then test whether cells with prior micronuclear damage are enriched among survivors, and whether blocking cGAS or STING before treatment changes persister frequency.

question: persister
title: Conditioned-neighbor rescue assays with dying-cell secretomes
description: Co-culture a labeled reporter population with drug-killed neighbors in transwell and direct-contact configurations, and separately collect conditioned medium from dying versus surviving cultures for mass spectrometry of secreted factors. Adding back candidate factors or depleting them from the medium will show whether survival depends on signals from neighboring cells rather than on intrinsic cell properties alone.

question: persister
title: Dynamic BH3 profiling of apoptotic priming at baseline
description: Before drug exposure, measure each population's mitochondrial apoptotic priming by dynamic BH3 profiling with peptides such as BIM and BAD, then sort on priming level and treat. If survivors sit at the low-priming end, survival reflects how far cells are from the mitochondrial death threshold rather than a specific drug-resistance pathway.

question: persister
title: Intracellular drug accumulation and target engagement in individual survivors
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable analog of the drug, or LC-MS on FACS-sorted cells, to measure intracellular drug levels, and use NanoBRET or CETSA to measure target occupancy in survivors versus dying cells. This tests whether persisters simply retain less effective drug (through efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or uptake differences) before any signaling rewiring occurs.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy as a natural lineage barcode
description: Use single-cell mtDNA sequencing (for example mtscATAC-seq or long-read mtDNA profiling) to read endogenous mtDNA variants as heritable clone markers in a population that is treated and allowed to regrow. Comparing heteroplasmy frequencies in survivors with baseline reveals whether specific mitochondrial genotypes, which change oxidative metabolism, are enriched without any engineered barcodes.

question: persister
title: Paracrine rescue via conditioned media and extracellular vesicles
description: Collect conditioned medium and extracellular vesicles from sorted persisters, fractionate them, and add each fraction to drug-naive cells under treatment to see whether survival can be transferred to neighbors. Transwell co-cultures with sorted survivors can then test whether the protection is secreted and dose-dependent.

question: persister
title: Collateral-sensitivity fingerprinting of survivors across a drug panel
description: Expose drug-tolerant survivors and naive controls to a panel of 100 or more mechanistically diverse compounds and build a drug-response fingerprint for each. Compounds that kill survivors but spare the parental population reveal exploitable collateral vulnerabilities, and the pattern itself shows whether tolerance is a broad state or a narrow, drug-specific adaptation.

question: persister
title: Sort by intracellular drug content, not by reporter state
description: Measure each cell's drug load with a clickable or fluorescent drug analog, or by LC-MS on FACS-sorted fractions, then compare survival of low- and high-accumulation cells at matched target engagement. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (efflux, uptake, sequestration) from genuine target-based tolerance.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial genome swap via cybrids
description: Fuse enucleated cytoplasts from survivor-enriched clones into a rho0 nuclear background carrying sensitive-clone nuclei, and reciprocally. If drug survival follows the mtDNA rather than the nuclear genotype, mitochondrial genome variation is causal, a test that is rarely run in persister studies.

question: persister
title: Spatial niche mapping in drug-treated spheroids
description: Use multiplexed imaging (e.g., CODEX or MERFISH) on spheroids at 24–72 h of treatment, registering each surviving cell to local hypoxia, nutrient, and necrotic-core gradients. Then test the spatially enriched niche by reproducing it in controlled hypoxia or nutrient gradient devices to see whether it causes survival.

question: persister
title: Pulse-duration by dose matrix with a mechanistic transition model
description: Expose cultures to a grid of drug concentrations and pulse durations, measure survivor fractions over time, and fit an ODE model with explicit rates for death, dormancy entry, and reawakening. Model-selected rates then predict the outcome of untested schedules, inferring the switching mechanism without lineage labels.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric inheritance of proteostasis damage at first mitosis
description: Label a drug-induced aggregate or chaperone reporter with HaloTag and pulse-chase it through the first post-treatment division, then track which daughter inherits the damaged load. If daughters receiving less damage are the ones that persist, segregation of proteotoxic burden at mitosis is a candidate determinant of survival.

question: persister
title: Natural mtDNA heteroplasmy as a lineage barcode
description: Use naturally occurring mitochondrial DNA variants, which need no transduction, as heritable clonal markers. Profile heteroplasmy by mtscATAC-seq or mtDNA long-read sequencing before and after drug, and test whether survivors come from clones with a particular mtDNA haplotype or from heteroplasmy shifts.

question: persister
title: Sorting by intracellular drug accumulation
description: Use a fluorescent or intrinsically fluorescent analog of the drug, or mass-spectrometry imaging, to measure each cell's drug uptake and efflux pump activity. Sort cells into low, mid, and high accumulation bins, treat each bin, and test whether survival tracks pharmacokinetic heterogeneity rather than a molecular state.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned adhesion area as a survival variable
description: Plate cells on fibronectin micropatterns of defined sizes so that spreading area and cytoskeletal tension are controlled, then apply the drug and quantify survival against area. Check whether YAP/TAZ nuclear localization and nuclear size explain the survivors, which would make mechanics a determinant of persistence.

question: persister
title: Paracrine protection from dying neighbors
description: Test whether dying cells release factors that protect neighbors. Use transwell co-cultures, conditioned medium from drug-killed cells with extracellular vesicles removed by ultracentrifugation, and proteomic or metabolite profiling of that medium. Then apply the protective factor to naive cells to see whether it rescues them from drug.

question: persister
title: Ferroptotic threshold and membrane lipid composition
description: Sort or image cells for lipid peroxidation with C11-BODIPY and profile membrane phospholipid acyl chains by lipidomics, comparing survivors and non-survivors. Then add a GPX4 or ferroptosis inhibitor and a polyunsaturated fatty acid challenge to test whether survivors are simply less susceptible to lipid peroxidation.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy as a natural lineage barcode
description: Sequence mtDNA variants and copy number in single cells (e.g., mtscATAC or single-cell mtDNA sequencing) before treatment and after drug selection, using naturally occurring heteroplasmy as a heritable lineage tag. If survivors are enriched for particular mtDNA haplotypes or respiratory-capacity states, that points to oxidative-phosphorylation fitness as a pre-existing determinant of tolerance, testable by swapping mitochondria with cybrids.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric partitioning of drug load at mitosis
description: Use a click-tagged or intrinsically fluorescent drug analog to track how intracellular drug is divided between daughter cells during division in live imaging. If one daughter inherits systematically less drug or more efflux-pump protein, the survival of that lineage would reflect stochastic segregation rather than a stable cell state.

question: persister
title: Per-cell target protein turnover measured by HaloTag pulse-chase
description: Endogenously tag the drug target with a HaloTag, pulse-label with a cell-permeant dye, and measure the per-cell synthesis and degradation rate of the existing protein pool by time-lapse imaging under treatment. Survivors may carry a slower target turnover or higher replacement rate that buffers drug occupancy, which can be tested by modulating proteasome or lysosomal degradation.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment optical redox imaging to sort by metabolic state
description: Image NAD(P)H and FAD autofluorescence in living cells to compute an optical redox ratio for each cell before drug exposure, then sort the extremes and test drug response in each fraction. This label-free readout captures mitochondrial and glycolytic balance without genetic perturbation, and it can reveal whether tolerance follows a continuous metabolic gradient rather than a discrete subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Spatial neighborhood mapping of survivors in dense versus sparse colonies
description: After treatment, map surviving cells in situ (multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics) and quantify survival as a function of local neighbor density and contact with dying cells. If survival depends on local neighborhood rather than intrinsic cell identity, the mechanism involves community or contact-dependent protection, which can be tested by co-culture and conditioned-medium experiments.

question: persister
title: Single-cell BH3 profiling for apoptotic priming
description: Before drug exposure, measure each cell's mitochondrial apoptotic priming by exposing permeabilized cells to BH3 peptides and quantifying cytochrome c release. Sort cells by priming level and test whether the least-primed fraction is enriched for survivors, which would show that persistence reflects a sub-lethal apoptotic threshold rather than a specific signaling state.

question: persister
title: Mitotic partitioning of drug target and efflux capacity
description: Tag the drug target and an efflux or drug-metabolizing protein with photoconvertible or split fluorescent reporters, then follow individual divisions by time-lapse. Test whether one daughter cell inherits a low target or high efflux load, and whether persisters preferentially descend from the asymmetrically endowed sister.

question: persister
title: Natural mtDNA heteroplasmy as a lineage marker
description: Deep-sequence the mitochondrial genome of the parental population and of survivors to find pre-existing mtDNA variants that serve as native, non-engineered lineage tags. Enrichment of specific mtDNA haplotypes among survivors would indicate heritable mitochondrial background underlies persistence, and an ethidium-bromide-depleted arm would test whether this depends on oxidative phosphorylation.

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification with lysosomal sequestration probes
description: Measure the free intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells, using intrinsic fluorescence or a clickable analog, together with LysoTracker-based acidic compartment volume. Survivors with low cytosolic drug despite equal extracellular dosing would point to pharmacokinetic sequestration as a cause of persistence, separate from target biology.

question: persister
title: Density-dependent autocrine rescue and conditioned-medium swap
description: Titrate seeding density and swap conditioned medium between high- and low-density cultures before drug addition to test whether the persister fraction depends on secreted factors accumulated by neighboring cells. Fractionating the conditioned medium (e.g., by size exclusion) would then isolate the protective factor if the effect is medium-borne.

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug-load mapping
description: Quantify how much drug each cell actually accumulates, using intrinsic fluorescence of the drug, an isotope-labeled analog, or imaging mass spectrometry, and link each cell's drug load to its survival over time. If survivors take up or retain less drug, the mechanism is pharmacokinetic rather than signaling-based, which would call for dosing or transporter interventions rather than pathway inhibitors.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy profiling of survivors
description: Call mtDNA variants and estimate heteroplasmy in single cells using reads from existing scATAC or scRNA-seq data (for example with mgatk), then compare survivors to non-survivors. This tests the premise that the population is genetically identical, since mtDNA is not controlled by nuclear clonality, and it can reveal inherited mitochondrial genotypes that shape drug tolerance.

question: persister
title: Membrane potential sorting with ion-channel perturbation
description: Stain live cells with voltage-sensitive dyes to measure resting membrane potential, sort the hyperpolarized and depolarized fractions, and re-challenge each with the drug. Then test whether pharmacological or genetic changes to specific K+ or Cl- channels shift the survival fraction, which would show a bioelectric state that predisposes cells to tolerance.

question: persister
title: Dead-neighbor conditioned signaling test
description: Encapsulate single cells or defined small numbers of cells in droplets with and without supernatant or lysate from drug-killed cells, then score survival by droplet. Fractionate the active material and identify it by mass spectrometry, which tests whether dying neighbors release factors that rescue survivors.

question: persister
title: Nuclear deformability and envelope-rupture phenotyping
description: Use real-time deformability cytometry to measure nuclear stiffness in untreated cells, sort by deformability, and track drug-induced nuclear envelope rupture with a fluorescent NLS reporter. Correlate lamin A/C levels with survival to test whether nuclear mechanics, rather than signaling, gates early drug-induced damage.

question: persister
title: Mother-daughter inheritance of protein aggregates
description: Express an aggregation-prone fluorescent reporter or an HSP70 chaperone sensor, then track mother-daughter pairs through mitosis during drug exposure. Test whether daughters that inherit a low aggregate or damaged-protein burden are the ones that survive, which would make persistence a matter of asymmetric proteostatic inheritance rather than a fixed transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned density and position mapping of survival
description: Plate cells on micropatterned islands of defined size and shape so that local density and edge position are controlled, then measure where survivors arise within each island. If survival clusters at specific positions regardless of genotype, the trait is a community or geometry effect rather than a cell-intrinsic one.

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug quantification linked to fate
description: Measure the intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells by imaging mass spectrometry or by a fluorescent or isotopically labeled analog, then sort or back-gate cells by drug content and test their survival. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (differences in uptake, efflux, or metabolism) from genuine target-state differences.

question: persister
title: Baseline nascent translation rate as a survival predictor
description: Quantify per-cell nascent protein synthesis before treatment using puromycin or OPP click labeling, sort the high and low translators, and compare their drug response and survival. This tests whether translational capacity, rather than transcription, sets how much the cell can mount a stress response.

question: persister
title: Secretome-mediated rescue of naive cells
description: Collect conditioned medium or extracellular vesicles from drug-treated cultures enriched for survivors and apply them to naive cells under drug, then identify the active factors by proteomics and a neutralizing-antibody or vesicle-depletion screen. A positive rescue would indicate that survival can be extrinsically conferred between cells, not only inherited.

question: persister
title: Barcode-based lineage tracing through a drug pulse
description: Label each progenitor cell with a heritable CRISPR or lentiviral barcode (e.g., CellTag or LARRY-style), treat the population, and sequence survivors to test whether they come from a pre-existing clone or arise de novo. The surprise would be that survival tracks a specific pre-marked lineage rather than stochastic induction.

question: persister
title: Live-cell ERK/AKT pulse tracking linked to fate
description: Use fluorescent kinase translocation reporters and time-lapse microscopy to record signaling dynamics in individual cells during the first hours of drug exposure, then score each cell's eventual fate. The surprise would be that the amplitude or timing of early signaling pulses predicts survival better than the baseline pathway activity measured before treatment.

question: persister
title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility to find epigenetic priming
description: Profile scATAC-seq plus RNA (multiome) on untreated cells and map which enhancers are already open in the cells that later survive, linking them to bypass or stress-response programs. The surprise would be that persisters are epigenetically primed before any drug exposure, so their vulnerability is set in advance.

question: persister
title: Dependency screens restricted to the drug-tolerant state
description: Sort or enrich drug-tolerant cells, then run a pooled CRISPR knockout screen (in vitro or in vivo) only in that state to find genes essential for survival under drug but dispensable in bulk cells. The surprise would be a small set of survival dependencies, unrelated to the drug target, that could be co-targeted to eliminate persisters.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric organelle inheritance during division
description: Label mitochondria, lysosomes, and drug efflux machinery with distinct fluorescent tags and track how they partition at mitosis, then test whether daughter cells that inherit a larger share of efflux or mitochondrial capacity are the ones that survive. The surprise would be that survival depends on how damaged or protective organelles are divided between daughters rather than on gene expression differences between parent cells.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment lineage barcoding to test whether survivors were marked before the drug
description: Label individual cells with heritable barcodes (e.g., CellTag-style lineage tags), expose the population to a targeted drug, and trace which clones persist. If survivors already carried a distinct barcode-linked state before treatment, the field's 'random switching' explanation is wrong and the pre-existing state becomes the target.

question: persister
title: Baseline multi-omic profiling with prospective sort-and-test validation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and transcription in drug-naive cells at single-cell resolution, train a classifier that predicts which cells will survive, then sort the predicted survivors and drop-treat them to check the prediction. Success or failure of the prospective test would show whether a survival signature exists before any drug exposure.

question: persister
title: Live reporters of drug engagement and cell-cycle state at the moment of dosing
description: Combine a kinase or target-occupancy biosensor with a cell-cycle reporter (e.g., FUCCI) and time-lapse imaging to record each cell's drug binding and cycling status at the instant of treatment. Retrospectively tracking which cells stay unbound, quiescent, or efflux-high would reveal whether survival is set by drug pharmacology rather than by intrinsic biology.

question: persister
title: Pulsed-dose CRISPR screens to find persister-specific dependencies
description: Run genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens at multiple timepoints during intermittent (pulsed) drug exposure rather than a single high dose, and compare guide dropout in persisters versus bulk cells. Genes that are essential only in the persister state would expose a therapeutic vulnerability that bulk-cell screens miss.

question: persister
title: Drug-holiday reversibility with epigenetic rewriting
description: Track chromatin marks (ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for histone modifications) across drug holidays and regrowth to see whether the survival state is inherited epigenetically. Then use targeted epigenetic editors to erase or install the marks and test whether survival is lost or gained without any genetic change.

question: persister
title: Barcode lineage tracing before and after drug exposure
description: Label thousands of genetically identical cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag or LARRY-style), treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes plus transcriptomes at intervals. Whether survivor clones were already present before treatment, or arose de novo from drug-exposed cells, would show if survival is pre-selected or induced.

question: persister
title: Live ERK/AKT reporter tracking of survivor cells
description: Use fluorescent kinase-activity biosensors (ERK-KTR, AKT-KTR) and time-lapse microscopy to follow individual cells through drug exposure, then recover and sort the survivors. Pre-treatment signaling dynamics, such as pulse frequency or basal activity, may predict which cells persist.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome on pre-treatment cells to find a chromatin priming signature
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression together (scATAC plus scRNA) in drug-naive cells, then sort and compare cells that later survive versus those that die, using a reporter or live-cell marker. A chromatin-state signature present before any drug exposure would indicate epigenetic priming.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen in persister-enriched populations
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens under sustained drug pressure with a sub-lethal dose, and compare guide representation in the rare surviving population against controls. Genes whose loss or gain changes survival, especially ones that act only in the tolerant state, would point to the mechanism.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and mitochondrial imaging of survivors
description: Combine live metabolic readouts (NAD(P)H autofluorescence, TMRM for membrane potential, or Seahorse-style measurements on sorted cells) with single-cell RNA-seq to test whether slow-cycling, oxidative-phosphorylation-high cells are the drug-tolerant fraction. Perturbing mitochondrial function in those cells would then test whether the metabolic state is causal.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with live-cell fate tracking (imagined 'Paper 1')
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag-style) and track each lineage by time-lapse imaging through drug exposure and washout. This reveals whether survivors come from a pre-existing clone or arise stochastically within lineages that were initially sensitive.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment multi-omic profiling linked to later fate (imagined 'Paper 2')
description: Profile individual cells before treatment with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, or index-sort them, then follow the same cells' fates with a live reporter of drug response. Searching for baseline chromatin or expression signatures that predict survival tests whether survival is encoded before the drug arrives.

question: persister
title: Reversibility kinetics after drug withdrawal (imagined 'Paper 3')
description: Use a fluorescent chromatin-state reporter (for example, an H3K27me3 or H3K4me3 sensor) and measure how survivors revert to sensitivity after drug removal, at single-cell resolution over days. Whether the survival state decays on a predictable timescale distinguishes a heritable epigenetic memory from a reversible, non-genetic switch.

question: persister
title: Pulsed-drug Perturb-seq screen (imagined 'Paper 4')
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen with single-cell RNA readout while cells receive short drug pulses rather than constant exposure. Genes whose knockdown changes the probability of survival, rather than just the average response, reveal the regulators that gate entry into the tolerant state.

question: persister
title: Spatial mapping of survivors within tumor niches (imagined 'Paper 5')
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on treated tumors or organoids to locate surviving cells relative to hypoxic zones, stromal contact, and vasculature. If survival clusters in specific niches, then niche-dependent signals, not intrinsic cell heterogeneity alone, drive persistence, and the niche becomes the therapeutic target.

question: persister
title: Heritable vs. induced survival via lineage barcoding
description: Label a founder population with a dense, heritable barcode library (e.g., CellTag-style), apply a targeted drug pulse, and track barcode frequencies over time. If survivors share barcodes with pre-treatment clones, survival is pre-existing and selected; if they don't, it is drug-induced state switching.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiome predicts survivors
description: Profile the untreated population with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, then sort or sequence the cells that persist after treatment and project them back onto the baseline map. Identifying a pre-existing chromatin and expression state that marks the eventual survivors would turn persistence into a predictable, measurable trait.

question: persister
title: Live reporters of epigenetic memory
description: Use fluorescent reporters for histone marks or chromatin-state readouts, combined with time-lapse imaging and drug washout, to follow individual cells through treatment and regrowth. Measuring whether the survival state is inherited across divisions or reset after drug removal distinguishes stable epigenetic memory from reversible, stochastic tolerance.

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug accumulation mapping
description: Quantify intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells, for example with a fluorescent analog or mass-spectrometry imaging, alongside efflux transporter expression. If rare cells keep sub-lethal drug levels because of low uptake or high efflux, survival is a pharmacokinetic problem at the single-cell level rather than a biological one.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved CRISPR screen under sub-lethal dosing
description: Run a pooled CRISPR knockout library at a sub-lethal drug dose and sort cells at multiple time points, rather than only at endpoint. Genes whose loss kills cells early but not late, or that enrich only in the persister fraction, reveal the sequence of adaptive steps that build tolerance and suggest which dependencies to target.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding plus single-cell transcriptomics before and during drug exposure
description: Tag each founder cell with a heritable barcode, treat the population, and profile surviving clones by scRNA-seq at baseline and early timepoints. This tests whether survivors were already transcriptionally distinct before treatment (pre-existing tolerance) or switched state after exposure (induced tolerance).

question: persister
title: Chromatin accessibility time course to find a primed epigenetic state
description: Run single-cell ATAC-seq across a drug time course and align the profiles with later survival, so the chromatin landscape of cells that will persist can be compared with that of cells that will die. Accessibility at lineage or stress-response enhancers that is already open before treatment would point to epigenetic priming.

question: persister
title: Live-cell fate tracking with reporters, then sort-and-rechallenge
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell-cycle phase, stress signalling (e.g., NRF2 or p53 activity), and mitochondrial state to follow individual cells under drug, then recover the cells that survive and re-challenge them. Reporter states that predict eventual survival would reveal the decisive variable.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved pooled CRISPR screen for genes that govern entry into and exit from persistence
description: Perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen with samples taken at multiple points during drug exposure and during drug withdrawal, not only at the endpoint. Genes whose loss changes the rate of entering the tolerant state, or the chance of regrowing from it, would separate the mechanisms that initiate persistence from those that sustain it.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment metabolic imaging to predict which cells will survive
description: Measure single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging and mitochondrial membrane potential in untreated cultures, then score each cell's metabolic state against its later survival under drug. A predictive metabolic signature before treatment would show whether survival is set by a baseline metabolic state.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded time-lapse of pre-treatment cells
description: Tag each cell with a heritable DNA barcode, image live cells under drug, and sequence barcodes at endpoints to test whether survivors descend from a pre-existing rare clone or arise de novo after exposure. Comparing barcode frequencies before and after treatment separates pre-existing from induced tolerance.

question: persister
title: Paired single-cell multiomics to find pre-treatment predictors
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and transcription together (e.g., paired scATAC plus scRNA) in untreated cells, then sort the rarest predicted-tolerant states and test whether they alone survive drug exposure. This checks whether a pre-existing epigenetic state is sufficient for survival, not just correlated with it.

question: persister
title: Dose-timed CRISPR screens on sorted survivors
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens with the drug added at defined times, then compare guide representation in sorted early survivors versus bulk population. Genes whose perturbation changes survival probability reveal the mechanisms that gate tolerance rather than just marking it.

question: persister
title: Label-retention and metabolic imaging of persisters
description: Use dye dilution (e.g., CFSE) to isolate slow-cycling cells and, in parallel, FLIM of NAD(P)H or mitochondrial reporters to measure each cell's metabolic state before and during drug exposure. Correlating these live readouts with later survival tests whether quiescence or oxidative metabolism predicts which cells persist.

question: persister
title: Drug-holiday reversion kinetics with fate-model fitting
description: Expose cells to drug, withdraw it at intervals, and track how quickly survivors revert to drug-sensitive behavior, then fit stochastic switching versus heritable memory models to the lineage-resolved fate data. Reversion timescales distinguish reversible non-genetic switching from stable epigenetic memory, which predicts different clinical dosing strategies.

question: persister
title: Heritable lineage barcoding with pre-treatment tracking
description: Introduce a CRISPR-based lineage recorder into a clonal cancer line, then follow single-cell lineages by time-lapse imaging through a drug pulse and sequence barcodes in survivors. If survivors cluster in lineages already distinguishable before treatment, persistence is pre-specified rather than drug-induced.

question: persister
title: Sorting on a pre-treatment reporter and re-challenging
description: Build a live reporter for a candidate persister-associated transcription factor or chromatin state, sort reporter-high and reporter-low cells before any drug exposure, and measure each sorted population's survival under drug. A large survival difference between sorted pools would show that a pre-existing state, not random chance, decides who survives.

question: persister
title: Temporally staged CRISPR screens with single-cell readout
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen with drug added at several time points and read out each perturbation by single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing. This reveals which regulators are required to enter, maintain, or exit the tolerant state, and when each one acts.

question: persister
title: Label-free metabolic imaging of single cells before treatment
description: Use fluorescence lifetime imaging of NAD(P)H or Raman spectroscopy to classify individual living cells by their metabolic state before drug exposure, then track which metabolic profiles survive. Sorting by that profile and testing metabolic inhibitors would show whether the survivors depend on a specific energy pathway.

question: persister
title: Spatial mapping of persisters within intact tumors
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to patient-derived xenograft tumors taken during and after treatment, and map where persister cells sit relative to vasculature, hypoxia, and stromal neighbors. If survivors are concentrated in particular niches, niche signals rather than intrinsic cell properties would be the main driver of survival.

question: persister
title: Barcoded scRNA-seq to test for pre-existing survivor states
description: Label an isogenic population with a lineage barcode library, profile single-cell transcriptomes before drug exposure, and then at several time points during treatment. Compare barcoded clones to see whether survivors already carried a distinct expression program (the 'tune without words') before treatment, or whether they acquired it only under drug, with no genetic change in either case.

question: persister
title: Live-cell lineage tracking with cell-cycle and stress reporters, plus washout
description: Use time-lapse imaging of FUCCI or p21/ERK biosensor reporter cells under drug to follow each cell's fate, cycling history and switching rate over days. Remove the drug at defined points to test whether the tolerant state reverses (non-genetic, reversible persistence) or stays heritable, which shows whether survival is a persistent trait that 'never stops'.

question: persister
title: Metabolic-state sorting under minimal fuel
description: Measure single-cell metabolic state with NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging or SCENITH, then sort cells by their pre-treatment metabolic profile and track which sorted fractions survive. Test whether survivors depend on oxidative phosphorylation or fatty-acid oxidation with targeted inhibitors, which would show they persist on a minimal resource budget.

question: persister
title: Paracrine protection assay from survivor secretomes
description: Co-culture sorted survivors with drug-sensitive cells under treatment, and profile the survivor secretome by mass spectrometry and cytokine arrays. Test candidate factors by conditioned-media experiments and by knocking them down in survivors, to see whether survivors keep their neighbours alive ('kept so many warm').

question: persister
title: Sublethal-dose CRISPR screen and chromatin profiling of the tolerant state
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen at a sublethal dose to find genes whose loss prevents the tolerant state, and pair it with scATAC-seq and CUT&Tag on sorted persisters to map the chromatin changes that accompany it. Dosing at a graded range of drug strengths maps the threshold at which survivors emerge, and checking whether the chromatin state persists after a drug holiday tests for epigenetic memory.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing with drug-pulse timing
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the drug, and track which clones persist. If survivors are already present before treatment, their barcodes will appear in the pre-treatment sample, and their lineage history will show whether they are stable pre-existing persisters or cells that switched state under drug. Like Ozymandias's shattered statue, the surviving clones are the remnants of a larger population that has mostly vanished.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved single-cell multiomics across the drug response
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the same cells at several times during the first days of treatment, and cluster the cells to find a transcriptional or chromatin state that is enriched before the drug takes effect or during the early tolerant window. Comparing the state of the cells that survive with the state of those that die shows whether the survivors were already different. This is analogous to reading the passions still carved into the statue's face: the residual cell state reveals what the cell was like before the drug arrived.

question: persister
title: Epigenetic memory test using drug holidays and sorted survivors
description: Sort drug-tolerant survivors and profile their chromatin (ATAC-seq, H3K27ac/H3K4me3 CUT&Tag, and DNA methylation) against drug-naive controls, then release the survivors from drug for several weeks and repeat the profiling. Chromatin marks that persist after release point to heritable epigenetic memory, while marks that reset point to reversible adaptation. The inscription on the pedestal outlasts the king, and similarly the epigenetic mark may outlast the drug.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen comparing survivors to controls
description: Perform a pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen under sustained drug exposure and compare guide abundance in surviving cells against an untreated reference at several time points. Genes whose loss consistently changes survival identify the pathways the survivors depend on, such as stress signalling, drug efflux, or mitochondrial or NAD metabolism. Follow-up with knockouts of the top hits in both survivor-enriched and non-enriched lines tests whether these pathways are necessary for persistence.

question: persister
title: Spatial and live metabolic mapping of survivor niches
