Compare each survivor with its nearest dying neighbors to find pre-existing or induced states (e.g., drug-efflux, anti-apoptotic, stress-response, chromatin features) that mark survival.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with replicate-population statistics
description: Barcode cells, split the population into many identical replicate dishes, and treat them all with the drug, then count which barcodes survive in each replicate. Barcodes recurring across replicates indicate pre-existing heritable survivors, whereas random barcodes indicate stochastic or induced survival, analogous to replicate fatigue tests that separate intrinsic from chance failure.

question: persister
title: Weibull-style survival-time distribution analysis
description: Run large numbers of single-cell or small-well drug-exposure time-to-death measurements and fit Weibull or mixture hazard models to the death-time distribution across doses. A distinct tail or separate subpopulation in the fitted shape and scale parameters would show whether survivors are a discrete tolerant class or the extreme end of a continuum, and it would let you quantify how treatments shift the tail.

question: persister
title: In situ live-cell tracking of damage initiation and recovery
description: Time-lapse microscopy with reporters for drug-target activity, DNA damage, apoptosis caspases, ROS and cell-cycle state follows each cell from before treatment through death or survival. Tracking where and when damage starts (e.g., signaling rebound, mitochondrial priming, slow cycling) shows what survivors do differently, much as in situ loading shows where cracks start and stop.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment state sorting and causal perturbation of candidate features
description: Before drug exposure, sort cells by candidate microstructure-like features such as reporter-defined transcriptional state, cell-cycle phase, mitochondrial content or epigenetic marks. Then challenge each sorted fraction with the drug to test whether the feature predicts survival, and use CRISPR or small-molecule perturbations to add or remove it, which would show whether it causes survival or only correlates with it.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded matched-pair comparison of survivors vs. non-survivors
description: Use heritable DNA barcodes to split a clonal population into replicate arms, then test whether the same lineages survive drug in independent replicates (pre-existing, heritable state) or survivors are random (stochastic). Sister-cell pairs or barcode-matched lineages sampled before treatment can be profiled by scRNA-seq to compare the pre-treatment states of future survivors against matched non-survivors, as in matched-pair designs.

question: persister
title: Hazard-model analysis of single-cell live imaging with pre-treatment covariates
description: Track thousands of individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with reporters (e.g., apoptosis, cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, mitochondrial state) before and after drug, and fit Cox/competing-risk survival models for death versus arrest versus division. Covariates measured before drug (cell cycle phase, signaling pulse history, size, lineage relatedness) quantify which hidden state variables predict survival, analogous to leverage and liquidity in firm hazard models.

question: persister
title: Difference-in-differences perturbation of candidate state regulators
description: Perturb candidate survival-state factors (e.g., drug efflux, anti-apoptotic BCL2-family proteins, stress-response or chromatin regulators) with CRISPRi or inhibitors, and compare the change in survivor fraction before and after drug versus matched untreated and non-targeting controls. This separates a causal effect on drug tolerance from general effects on proliferation or baseline fitness.

question: persister
title: Stress-test titration across dose, drug combination and environment
description: Systematically vary drug dose, exposure duration, pathway co-inhibition, nutrient and oxygen stress, and measure survivor fraction and survivor transcriptional states in each condition. Building the dose-response and shock-response curves for survivors shows whether tolerance is a single robust state or depends on conditions, and which stresses collapse the survivor fraction, as in stress-test simulations.

question: persister
title: Network-position and state-transition modeling from multi-omic single-cell data
description: Combine paired single-cell RNA, ATAC and protein or metabolic readouts of untreated cells and fit a dynamical model (e.g., Markov state-transition or RNA velocity-based) estimating switching rates between sensitive and tolerant states with and without drug. Include spatial or neighbor-cell covariates (contact, paracrine signaling) as a network-position effect, then validate by sorting predicted high-tolerance-state cells and testing their survival prospectively.

question: persister
title: Single-cell lineage tracking with fate mapping (mark-recapture analog)
description: Barcode individual cells (e.g., lineage barcodes or live-imaging tracking) and follow their fates before, during and after drug exposure, then retrospectively compare pre-treatment states of survivor lineages versus killed lineages. This tests whether survival is predicted by a heritable or transient pre-existing state, as ecologists do by tracking individual fates over time.

question: persister
title: Spatial microenvironment mapping of survivors (refuge analysis)
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging in 3D cultures or xenografts to measure local density, oxygen, drug penetration, nutrient gradients and neighbor identity around survivors versus dead cells. Fit spatial models (e.g., point-process or occupancy-style) to test whether survivors occupy drug refuges or microniches rather than being intrinsically different.

question: persister
title: Common-garden reciprocal transplant of survivors
description: Isolate survivors and non-survivors (or their pre-treatment sorted siblings), grow them in identical drug-free conditions for varying durations, then re-challenge them, and also swap them into different microenvironments (density, matrix, co-culture). Persistence of resistance across a common environment indicates intrinsic epigenetic/state differences, while loss of it indicates environmental or plastic causes.

question: persister
title: Manipulative perturbation of candidate refuge variables
description: Experimentally alter local density, oxygen, drug concentration gradients, or stromal contact in a controlled way (microfluidics or patterned co-culture) and measure survival fraction response. Dose-response of survivor frequency to each manipulated variable separates causal environmental refuges from stochastic or intrinsic causes.

question: persister
title: Long-term plot-style time series of state dynamics with stochastic modeling
description: Image or sequence the same cell populations repeatedly across drug exposure and recovery, measuring state markers (e.g., drug-tolerant persister signatures, cell-cycle state, drug efflux, mitochondrial activity). Fit state-transition models that estimate switching rates and compare them with the observed survivor fraction, which would show whether bet-hedging-like stochastic switching explains persistence.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment lineage-tracked survivor back-tracing
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate pools, and treat. Then profile sister cells from untreated replicates by scRNA-seq to find the pre-existing state of cells whose barcodes later survive. This is the analogue of comparing the pre-attack state of survivors with that of failed instances, and it separates pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptation.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with retrospective survivor tracking
description: Image single cells with fluorescent reporters (e.g. cell cycle, p53/ERK dynamics, mitochondrial potential, drug autofluorescence) for days before and during drug exposure. After treatment, trace the survivors back through their history and compare their trajectories with those of cells that died. This gives per-cell telemetry logs and shows which dynamic or state features predicted survival.

question: persister
title: Controlled perturbation screen of candidate state variables
description: Chaos-engineering style: systematically perturb suspected hidden variables such as cell-cycle phase, drug efflux, mitochondrial priming, chromatin state or stress-pathway activity, using CRISPRi/a, small-molecule modulators or synchronization. Measure how each shifts the survivor fraction, and use this to test which state differences cause survival rather than just correlate with it.

question: persister
title: Sort-and-compare multi-omics of survivors versus casualties
description: Use FACS or microfluidics to isolate cells on pre-treatment markers (e.g. drug uptake, apoptotic priming via BH3 profiling, or an efflux reporter). Then run matched ATAC-seq, proteomics, and single-cell RNA-seq on the sorted groups and treat the data like differential debugging to find the minimal set of state differences that separates the two.

question: persister
title: Rare-event statistics and heritability of survival
description: Run fluctuation-test and Luria–Delbrück-style experiments, plus sister-cell and clonal-relative comparisons, to estimate how often cells switch into and out of the survivor state and how long that state is inherited. Fit stochastic state-switching models to the survivor-fraction data across doses and times to tell apart random switching, epigenetic memory, and rare genetic or mutational causes. Complement this with deep sequencing to rule out hidden mutations.

question: persister
title: Matched survivor-vs-casualty forensic profiling
description: Before drug exposure, barcode and live-image cells, then treat and identify survivors. Retrospectively compare the pre-treatment state of each survivor lineage (transcriptome via lineage-barcoded scRNA-seq, signaling reporters, cell cycle, mitochondrial content) with its matched dying neighbors. This is the equivalent of comparing standing and collapsed buildings, and it tests which pre-existing state predicts survival instead of which state appears afterward.

question: persister
title: Microenvironment 'site-response' mapping
description: Record local conditions for every cell in culture or in tumor sections, including density, neighbor identity, oxygen, nutrient and pH gradients, drug penetration (using fluorescent drug analogs), and position within colonies. Then use spatial statistics to test whether survivors cluster in protective niches, as surviving buildings cluster on favorable soil. Compare against spatial transcriptomics from treated tumors.

question: persister
title: Randomized-parameter in silico models of drug response
description: Build mechanistic or stochastic models of the drug target pathway, apoptosis threshold, and efflux, and draw protein abundances and rate constants from measured single-cell distributions, like finite-element models with randomized material properties. Run sensitivity analysis to find which variable's variation (such as BCL-2 family ratios or target expression noise) best reproduces the observed survivor fraction. Then validate the top candidates experimentally.

question: persister
title: Controlled perturbation 'shake-table' on isogenic populations
description: Apply graded, standardized drug doses, pulses, and combinations to sorted subpopulations, for example high versus low expression of a candidate state marker. Quantify dose-response curves, time to death, and survivor fraction. Then perturb the candidate variability source directly, such as by tuning expression with CRISPRi/a or inhibiting a stress pathway, to test whether it causally shifts the survivor fraction.

question: persister
title: Heritability and state-transition kinetics of survival
description: Measure whether survival is transient or heritable by tracking sister cells and clonal lineages across drug-free and drug cycles. Use fluctuation-test (Luria-Delbrück) designs and Markov state-switching models to separate pre-existing epigenetic states from newly acquired mutations. Add whole-genome sequencing and chromatin accessibility of survivors to confirm that they are genetically identical and to find the epigenetic basis of their survival.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded longitudinal cohort tracking of persister fates
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate pools before drug, and sequence barcodes at several timepoints. This tests whether survival is pre-existing and heritable (the same barcodes surviving across replicates) or stochastic, as cohort studies do when following individuals over time.

question: persister
title: Positive-deviance single-cell profiling of pre-treatment survivors
description: Use barcode-matched sister cells, or live-cell reporters with sorting, to profile the pre-drug transcriptome, chromatin state and signaling of cells that later prove to be survivors. Comparing them with matched non-survivors from the same culture identifies the hidden factors, such as a drug-efflux or stress-response state, that predate treatment.

question: persister
title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with retrospective outcome linkage
description: Image fluorescent reporters of cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and mitochondrial or redox state continuously before and after drug, then link each cell's history to its fate. Mixed-methods logic applies here: dynamic traces generate hypotheses about routines such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling that distinguish survivors.

question: persister
title: Matched-control causal perturbation of candidate survival factors
description: Take candidate factors from the profiling, such as a state marker or regulator, and perturb them by CRISPRi/a or drug in a randomized, matched design. Compare survivor fractions with propensity-matched or randomized controls, adjusting for cell cycle, size and density, to test whether each factor causes survival rather than merely correlating with it.

question: persister
title: Microenvironment-matched neighbor and spatial analysis
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to compare survivors with non-survivors in matched local neighborhoods, controlling for density, nutrient gradients and paracrine signals. Controlling these 'identical school' conditions separates cell-intrinsic state from local context, and a co-culture or conditioned-medium experiment can then test the contextual factors.

question: persister
title: Single-cell live tracking with lineage-resolved drug response
description: Time-lapse microscopy tracks thousands of individual cells and their lineages through drug exposure, with reporters for signaling (e.g., ERK, p53) and cell-cycle state. This gives the full distribution of single-cell trajectories and shows whether survivors differ in dynamics before the drug is added, and when divergence begins.

question: persister
title: First-passage-time analysis of death and escape
description: Record each cell's time to apoptosis or to resumed division after drug addition, and fit the full distribution rather than the mean. A heavy tail or multimodal shape would indicate either a single stochastic rate process or a distinct slow-cycling subpopulation, and dose-dependence of the tail would constrain mechanistic models.

question: persister
title: Transition-path sampling by retrospective and prospective tracing of survivors
description: Follow cells continuously, then trace the survivors' ancestors backward to find what states they passed through before the drug. Compare these paths with those of cells that died, and where possible use barcoded or live-reporter sorting to isolate cells in candidate pre-resistant states and test whether they are enriched for survival.

question: persister
title: Autocorrelation and heritability of cell state to separate noise from hidden slow variables
description: Measure how long expression of candidate markers (e.g., drug-efflux or anti-apoptotic genes) stays correlated in a cell and between sister cells and cousins. Compare this timescale with the drug-exposure window. If the state persists for several generations, a slow epigenetic or metabolic variable is implied. If it decays quickly, fast noise is implied. Test the inference by sorting cells by marker level and measuring how survival changes with the delay between sorting and treatment.

question: persister
title: Barcoded clonal ensembles with sister-pair and replicate comparisons
description: Label cells with heritable lineage barcodes, split a population into parallel replicates, and treat them. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the survival state is pre-existing and heritable. If different barcodes survive, the cause is stochastic. Single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq on matched pre-treatment sister cells then identifies the molecular features that predict survival.

question: persister
title: High-replicate dose-response curves to resolve the survival tail
description: Run drug titrations across many replicate wells and extended dose ranges, using live-cell imaging or barcoded counting to fit the plateau of the survival curve. This gives the persister fraction and a dose-response shape that separates a stable tolerant subpopulation (a plateau) from continuous sensitivity. Also compare how the fraction changes with time and dose.

question: persister
title: Survivor vs. non-survivor matched profiling with lineage barcoding
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes and split the population before treatment. Sequence the barcodes in the survivors and in the untreated sister populations to test whether survivors come from pre-existing clones. Single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq on the matched pretreatment sisters then show which transcriptional or chromatin states predicted survival, as opposed to states induced by the drug.

question: persister
title: Live-cell tracking of pre-treatment state, size, and cell-cycle stage
description: Image reporter cells for cell-cycle phase, cell size, and signaling activity (e.g., ERK or p53 reporters) over time before the drug is added. Track each cell through treatment and record the fate. Then regress survival on the pre-exposure measurements to test whether the survivors were slower-cycling, larger, or in a particular phase. This is the analog of comparing survivors and non-survivors by age, size, and developmental stage.

question: persister
title: Re-challenge and drug-holiday experiments for inheritance of tolerance
description: Expand the survivors in drug-free medium for varying numbers of generations. Re-challenge them at different time points and compare the surviving fraction with that of naive cells. A fraction that reverts over time points to a reversible epigenetic or metabolic state. A fraction that stays high suggests a genetic change, which exome sequencing can then test for. Add single-cell-derived clones to measure how quickly the survival fraction relaxes back to baseline.

question: persister
title: Metabolic and epigenetic profiling with perturbation of candidate mechanisms
description: Compare sorted survivors and untreated cells using metabolomics (for example, NADH/NAD+ and ROS levels, mitochondrial activity), drug-efflux and detoxification activity, and histone-modification or DNA-methylation profiles. Then test causality by blocking the candidate pathways, such as with epigenetic inhibitors or metabolic modulators, and measuring whether the survival fraction changes.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell pair tracking with post-hoc molecular readout
description: Image dividing cells live to identify sister pairs, treat with drug, and record which sister survives, then compare pre-treatment features between pairs. Shared inheritance (sister concordance decay over generations) quantifies the memory timescale of the survival-permissive state, separating heritable from stochastic fluctuations.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment fate prediction via live reporter-to-survival mapping
description: Image cells carrying multiplexed live reporters (e.g., p53/ERK/NF-κB dynamics, mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-priming dye) before drug addition, track each cell's eventual fate, and train a model to predict survival from pre-drug dynamics. The predictive features reveal which pathway states causally precede survival.

question: persister
title: BH3 profiling / single-cell apoptotic priming and caspase kinetics
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming and drug-induced caspase activation timing in individual cells, sorted by survival outcome. This tests whether survivors simply sit lower on the apoptosis threshold (e.g., through BCL-2 family levels) rather than escape the drug's target inhibition.

question: persister
title: Intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy imaging
description: Use fluorescent or label-free (mass spec imaging, intrinsically fluorescent drugs, or a target-engagement biosensor) readouts to quantify drug accumulation, efflux, lysosomal sequestration, and target inhibition per cell. This tests whether survivors experience less effective drug exposure rather than possess altered downstream biology.

question: persister
title: Spatial/microenvironmental heterogeneity and cell-cell contact mapping
description: In 3D cultures or tissue sections, use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to relate survivor locations to local density, hypoxia, neighbor identity, and secreted-factor gradients, then perturb the implicated neighbor cues. This tests whether survival comes from transient local niche effects on genetically identical cells.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy and mitochondrial priming
description: Sequence mtDNA and perform BH3 profiling or live mitochondrial membrane potential/apoptotic-threshold measurements on sorted single cells before treatment, testing whether differences in mitochondrial state predict who survives.

question: persister
title: Inheritance of survival state across cell divisions via sister-cell pair analysis
description: Use time-lapse imaging of sister pairs and pedigrees, then apply the drug at different generations, to quantify how many divisions the persister-prone state is remembered and whether it is inherited as a fate-like memory or reset stochastically.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric partitioning of organelles and proteins at division
description: Label aggregated proteins, lysosomes, old mitochondria, or stress-granule components with photoconvertible or tandem timer tags and track whether cells that inherit larger or smaller loads at mitosis preferentially survive.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic flux and redox imaging
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, genetically encoded ATP/glutathione/ROS sensors, and lipid peroxidation probes in the same live cells later followed to survival, to test whether ferroptosis sensitivity and metabolic state determine persistence.

question: persister
title: Stochastic gene-expression noise manipulation
description: Engineer cells with promoter variants or feedback circuits that tune expression noise of a candidate survival gene at constant mean, then measure persister frequency to causally test whether noise itself, not the mean, drives survival.

question: persister
title: Cell-cycle-history and inheritance tracking via sister-cell pairs
description: Use time-lapse imaging of FUCCI or similar reporters plus sister-cell tracking to test whether survival correlates with pre-drug cell-cycle duration, and how strongly sisters share fate. Compare sister-pair concordance with unrelated cells and apply the drug at varied times after division to estimate the heritability and decay time of the survival state.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial content and mtDNA heteroplasmy sorting
description: Sort untreated cells by mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, or mtDNA heteroplasmy, then drug-challenge each bin to see whether mitochondrial state predicts survival. Single-cell mtDNA variants can also serve as natural lineage markers to test clonal inheritance.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment live-cell signaling dynamics as a predictor
description: Record dynamic reporters (ERK, AKT, p53, NF-κB kinase translocation) in single cells for days before drug addition. Then train a model on those dynamics to predict which cells survive, which would show whether signaling history rather than a static state determines the outcome.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D/tumor models
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to spheroids or xenografts after treatment to test whether survivors cluster by hypoxia, nutrient gradients, drug penetration, or neighbor contact. Pair this with local drug-concentration measurements, such as mass spectrometry imaging, to separate intrinsic from positional causes.

question: persister
title: Stochastic apoptosis-threshold measurement (BH3 profiling with live caspase reporters)
description: Measure each cell's mitochondrial apoptotic priming with single-cell BH3 profiling or live caspase and MOMP reporters. Then test how priming, rather than drug target inhibition, sets survival after drug exposure. Compare the variance in priming with that in target-inhibition readouts to see which drives the surviving fraction.

question: persister
title: Time-lapse lineage-linked pre-treatment history
description: Track single cells by live imaging with reporters (cell cycle, stress, apoptosis signaling) for several generations before drug addition, then retrospectively identify features of the cells that later survive. Sister-cell and cousin-cell survival concordance would quantify the heritability and timescale of the protective state.

question: persister
title: Spatial-transcriptomic neighborhood mapping of survivors
description: Apply multiplexed in situ imaging (MERFISH or similar) to 3D cultures or xenografts during treatment to test whether survivors cluster by local microenvironment such as oxygen, density, or contact with stromal cells. Compare with matched non-survivors to separate cell-intrinsic from position-dependent protection.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial priming and apoptotic threshold profiling
description: Use BH3 profiling and single-cell quantification of BCL-2 family proteins and caspase activation kinetics to measure how close each cell is to the apoptotic threshold. This tests whether survival comes from variable death-machinery wiring rather than from the drug target pathway.

question: persister
title: Drug uptake, efflux and intracellular concentration at single-cell resolution
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs or mass-spec imaging (e.g., CyTOF or nanoSIMS) to measure intracellular drug levels and target occupancy in individual cells, then link these to survival. Differences in transporter activity or lysosomal drug sequestration could explain survival without altering signaling.

question: persister
title: Stochastic gene expression noise manipulation
description: Use synthetic circuits or promoter and noise-modulating perturbations to raise or lower expression variability of candidate survival genes while keeping their mean level constant. Measuring the persister fraction as a function of noise tests causally whether cell-to-cell variation itself, rather than the average, sets the surviving fraction.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and mtDNA lineage tracing
description: Use naturally occurring mtDNA variants (e.g., via mtscATAC-seq) as endogenous clonal barcodes, and relate heteroplasmy levels and mitochondrial content/membrane potential in pre-treatment cells to later survival. This tests whether inherited mitochondrial state, not nuclear genome or transcriptome, predisposes cells to tolerance.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell pair tracking with fate prediction
description: Image dividing cells, then split or track sister pairs before drug exposure and test whether sister survival concordance exceeds that of random pairs, with decay of concordance over generations giving the memory time of the tolerant state. Combine with post hoc multiplexed profiling of the same cells to identify inherited features such as organelle load or cell size.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment live reporters of apoptotic priming
description: Measure single-cell BH3 profiling or live fluorescent reporters of caspase/MOMP threshold and BCL-2 family stoichiometry before drug exposure, then follow fate. This tests whether survivors are cells stochastically positioned further from the apoptosis threshold rather than having a distinct drug-resistance program.

question: persister
title: Stress-granule, translation, and ISR dynamics
description: Use ribosome profiling or puromycin/OPP incorporation at single-cell resolution plus ISR reporters (ATF4, eIF2α phosphorylation) during the first hours of drug exposure, with pharmacological ISR perturbation. This tests whether rapid translational reprogramming allows survival during the acute window before any transcriptional state change matters.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and redox flux imaging
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, genetically encoded ROS/ATP/lipid peroxidation sensors, and lipidomics on sorted cells to detect metabolic states such as altered ferroptosis susceptibility or lipid composition that predate or accompany tolerance. Follow with perturbations (GPX4 inhibition, lipid supplementation) to test causality.

question: persister
title: Pedigree-resolved sister-cell tracking with post-hoc transcriptomics
description: Time-lapse image cells for several generations before drug, then drug-treat and track survival, and finally lyse and sequence/FISH-profile identified survivors and their pre-drug sisters or cousins. This tests whether survival is heritable across divisions and which pre-existing state markers correlate with it, beyond static snapshots.

question: persister
title: Single-cell mitochondrial and metabolic state mapping (FLIM-NADH, mtDNA content, ROS) before drug
description: Measure NAD(P)H lifetime, mitochondrial membrane potential, mtDNA copy number and ROS in individual live cells, sort or track them, and then challenge with drug to see if metabolic/redox state predicts survival. Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and apoptotic priming can differ between genetically identical cells.

question: persister
title: BH3 profiling / dynamic apoptotic-priming and caspase-signal live reporters
description: Quantify per-cell mitochondrial apoptotic priming (BH3 profiling of sorted subpopulations, MCL1/BCL-xL/BIM levels) and use live caspase and cytochrome-c reporters to test whether survivors fail to commit to apoptosis after drug rather than escaping the drug's target inhibition.

question: persister
title: Extrachromosomal DNA and copy-number heterogeneity via single-cell long-read/ecDNA imaging
description: Use single-cell DNA sequencing and ecDNA FISH/CRISPR-imaging to test whether uneven ecDNA segregation and copy-number variation of target or bypass genes produces rare high-copy survivors in nominally identical cells. Longitudinal sampling shows if copy number changes reversibly under drug.

question: persister
title: Cell-cycle-and-stress-history reporters with optogenetic/perturbation of noise
description: Combine endogenous-tagged reporters (p53 pulses, ERK/AKT activity, FUCCI, heat-shock/UPR) in single cells and use these dynamics to predict survival, then causally test by optogenetically or chemically forcing the dynamics in cells. This distinguishes whether transient signaling fluctuations or cell-cycle position causally determines who survives.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment state tracking with lineage-linked sister-cell sampling
description: Split clonally related sister cells (via barcodes) so that one sibling is profiled by scRNA-seq before drug while the other is treated, then use barcode matching to identify which pre-drug transcriptional states predicted survival. This directly tests whether survivors are predetermined, rather than inferring it after the fact.

question: persister
title: Heritability decay of survival across generations
description: Isolate survivors and non-survivors, expand them without drug for varied numbers of divisions, then re-challenge to measure how fast the survival phenotype is lost. Fitting the decay kinetics gives the switching rates and memory timescale, which indicate whether the mechanism is stochastic, epigenetic, or genetic.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial and organelle inheritance asymmetry at division
description: Use live imaging of mitochondrial content, membrane potential, ROS and lysosomal drug sequestration in mother cells and daughters, then test whether unequal partitioning before treatment predicts survival. Photoactivatable or tagged organelles would let you test whether the inherited organelle state causes survival.

question: persister
title: Single-cell measurement of apoptotic threshold dynamics
description: Use live reporters for caspase activation and mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization, together with BH3 profiling of single cells. This quantifies cell-to-cell variation in how close each cell is to the death threshold and in the timing of commitment after drug exposure, separately from drug target inhibition.

question: persister
title: Intracellular drug and target-engagement heterogeneity
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a biosensor, or mass-spec imaging to measure per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy or pathway-reporter suppression (e.g., ERK kinase translocation reporter) over time. Linking these to survival tests whether survivors escape because the drug never fully engages the target or because they tolerate full inhibition.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment state memory via sister-cell pairing
description: Track lineages by time-lapse imaging, split sister cells so one is drugged and the other is profiled by scRNA-seq or proteomics. This links the pre-drug state of the sibling to the survival fate of its pair, which tests the causes directly and avoids correlating after the fact.

question: persister
title: Cell-cycle and mitotic timing history as a predictor
description: Use FUCCI or similar live reporters with long-term tracking to test whether the cell-cycle phase at drug exposure, G1 length, or a recent mitotic error predicts survival. Combine this with synchronization and perturbation of the cycle to test causality.

question: persister
title: Stress-response and apoptotic priming heterogeneity (single-cell mitochondrial priming)
description: Measure per-cell BH3 profiling or live mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization reporters, along with caspase kinetics and BCL-2 family protein levels. This tests whether survivors are cells with high apoptotic thresholds or slow death-signal accumulation.

question: persister
title: Stochastic gene-expression noise and fluctuation timescale modeling
description: Do time-resolved single-cell measurements of key drug-target pathway reporters in untreated cells. Fit stochastic state-switching models (Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests) to estimate how fast cells enter and leave the tolerant state and to predict how survival changes with drug-holiday schedules.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironmental niche mapping with perturbed density
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on 3D cultures or xenografts, and vary local density, cell-contact and secreted-factor conditions. This tests whether persister fate depends on microenvironmental position, such as hypoxia or paracrine rescue, rather than on intrinsic cell state.

question: persister
title: High-complexity lineage barcoding with fluctuation analysis
description: Barcode a clonal population, split into replicate arms, and treat; if the same barcodes survive across replicates, survival is a heritable pre-existing state, whereas random barcodes imply induced stochastic entry. Fitting state-switching rates to the barcode distributions quantifies how long the surviving state persists.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell pairing with pre-treatment profiling
description: Separate daughters of a division, destructively profile (scRNA-seq) one and treat the other, then link the profile to survival using clonal lineage similarity. This could identify the pre-treatment transcriptional state that predicts survival, rather than inferring it after the fact.

question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective lineage tracking
description: Image thousands of single cells for days before drug addition with reporters for cell cycle, ERK/p53 or stress signaling, and mitochondrial state, then follow fates after treatment. Mapping survivors back to their pre-drug dynamics (e.g., pulses, cycle length) reveals which dynamic features predict survival.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome of epigenetic priming
description: Perform joint ATAC and RNA profiling on untreated, early-treated, and persister populations to find chromatin accessibility present before drug that foreshadows the persister program. Validate by perturbing the identified regulators or chromatin modifiers (e.g., KDM5, HDAC inhibitors) to see if the surviving fraction shifts.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens plus BH3 profiling for survival mechanisms
description: Run CRISPR knockout/activation screens under drug to identify genes that set the persister fraction, and pair them with single-cell BH3 profiling to test whether survivors are in a lower apoptotic-priming state. This separates causal drivers from correlates and shows whether survival works through apoptosis evasion, metabolism, or stress response.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell splitting with lineage barcodes
description: Barcode a population, split it into replicate pools after a few divisions, and treat one pool while profiling the other by scRNA-seq. Matching barcodes between survivors and untreated sisters reveals the pre-treatment state of cells that would have survived, and shows how heritable it is.

question: persister
title: Retrospective live-cell tracking of future survivors

question: persister
title: BH3 profiling and apoptotic priming in untreated cells

question: persister
title: Persister-specific CRISPR dependency screens

question: persister
title: Barcode-and-rewind lineage tracing

question: persister
title: Live imaging of signaling dynamics linked to fate

question: persister
title: Fluctuation test with state-switching modeling

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome of persisters across drug time course

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPRi/a screen with persister-specific readout
description: Run genome-wide or targeted CRISPRi/a screens and score survival early under drug, before regrowth, and compare with late resistance outgrowth. question: persister
title: Barcoded sister-cell lineage tracing with transcriptome readout
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split each clone into two halves, and profile one by scRNA-seq before treatment while treating the other. question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters (pathway activity, cell cycle, mitochondrial state) for days before drug addition, then track each cell and its descendants through treatment. question: persister
title: Fluctuation test to separate switching from mutation
description: Perform Luria-Delbruck style assays with many parallel small clonal populations, plus drug-holiday re-challenge, and fit models to estimate phenotypic switching rates and memory duration.
