question: persister
title: Sorting on pre-treatment physiology, then drug challenge
description: Use FACS to isolate untreated cells by mitochondrial membrane potential, drug uptake or efflux (fluorescent analogs), size or slow-cycling dye retention, and measure survival of each fraction. This directly tests which physiological axes causally enrich persisters.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome with epigenetic perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and expression jointly (scATAC plus RNA) in pre-persister and persister cells, and identify candidate regulators. Validate by CRISPRi/a or chromatin inhibitors targeting those regulators to see whether persister frequency shifts.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with split-sample single-cell RNA-seq
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it before drug, profile one arm by scRNA-seq and treat the other, then identify which barcodes survive. This lets you read out the pre-treatment transcriptional state of cells destined to become persisters and test whether it is heritable.

question: persister
title: Luria-Delbrück fluctuation analysis of persister frequency
description: Expand many small independent clones, treat each, and compare the variance in persister counts to that expected under pre-existing versus drug-induced tolerance. Fitting a state-switching model to the data yields switching rates and distinguishes stochastic state fluctuations from stable epigenetic or genetic inheritance.

question: persister
title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective pedigree tracing
description: Image cells for days before and after drug with reporters for signaling (ERK, p53), cell cycle (FUCCI) and stress, then trace surviving cells back through their lineage. This shows whether dynamics, cycle history or sister-cell correlations predict survival, which fixed snapshots cannot show.

question: persister
title: Sort-then-challenge on pre-treatment physiological state
description: Use FACS to sort untreated cells by mitochondrial potential, ROS, drug efflux activity, or fluorescent drug uptake, then treat each sorted fraction and measure persister yield. This tests causality of candidate states and how long they last by delaying the drug challenge after sorting.

question: persister
title: Persister-fraction-focused CRISPR and epigenetic perturbation screens
description: Run pooled CRISPRi/a or epigenetic-inhibitor screens that read out the fraction of surviving cells at a fixed high dose, not bulk sensitivity. Hits that change only the persister fraction point to regulators of cell-state plasticity, and comparing them with scATAC/multiome data in persisters links them to chromatin mechanisms.

question: persister
title: Barcode-linked pre-treatment transcriptomes
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the population before drug, profile one half by scRNA-seq, and sequence barcodes in survivors from the other half. This directly reveals the pre-existing state of cells that go on to survive, and whether that state is shared among sister clones.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation tests with heritability timing
description: Run Luria-Delbrück style assays on many small parallel clonal expansions, varying time between subcloning and drug exposure. Variance in survivor numbers and its decay over generations quantify switching rates and memory duration, separating stable, transient and drug-induced tolerance.

question: persister
title: Live single-cell tracking with multi-reporter imaging, then retrospective fate mapping
description: Image cells for days before drug with reporters for cell cycle, p53/stress signaling, and ERK activity, then add drug and record who survives. Back-tracing survivors' pre-drug dynamics identifies predictive dynamic features such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling.

question: persister
title: Metabolic state sorting by FLIM/mitochondrial probes followed by drug challenge
description: Use NAD(P)H FLIM or mitochondrial membrane potential dyes to sort live cells by metabolic state pre-treatment, then expose each fraction to drug. This tests whether metabolic heterogeneity, such as oxidative phosphorylation reliance or redox buffering, causally predicts survival.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome of persisters with chromatin perturbation
description: Profile persisters and matched untreated cells by joint scRNA/ATAC to find chromatin accessibility states and transcription factors that define tolerance. Then test causality by perturbing the candidates with CRISPRi or epigenetic inhibitors and measuring changes in persister frequency.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split before drug
description: Barcode a population, split it into replicate arms, and treat one arm while profiling the other by scRNA-seq. Matching barcodes between survivors and untreated sister clones reveals the pre-existing transcriptional state that predicts survival and shows whether it is heritable, rather than inferred after the fact.

question: persister
title: Live reporter imaging with retrospective survivor tracing
description: Image cells with fluorescent reporters of target pathway activity, cell cycle, and stress for days before drug, then follow them through treatment. Tracing survivors back identifies which pre-drug dynamics, such as pathway pulses or long G1 dwell, predict survival.

question: persister
title: Adapted fluctuation test with state-switching modeling
description: Run Luria-Delbrück style experiments on many small independent clonal cultures and measure the variance in survivor counts. Fitting stochastic models then separates rare mutations from reversible non-genetic switching and estimates switching rates and persister-state memory.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome with FACS-based state enrichment
description: Use paired scRNA and ATAC profiling to define a persister-like signature and its regulatory elements. Sort cells by a surface marker or reporter for that state, challenge them with drug, and test causality by perturbing the identified chromatin regulators or transcription factors.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug exposure and apoptotic priming readout
description: Measure per-cell intracellular drug levels using fluorescent analogs or imaging mass spec, and measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming with BH3 profiling. This tests whether survival comes from lower effective drug exposure or from a higher death threshold, which expression data alone cannot separate.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sister-cell splitting
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split each population before drug, and compare survival and transcriptomes of sister clones to quantify heritability of persistence and recover pre-treatment states of future survivors via scRNA-seq of the untreated sibling arm.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation test plus switching-rate modeling
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style assays on many small clonal expansions, then fit stochastic models to separate pre-existing, rapidly switching states from drug-induced adaptation and estimate state switching rates and memory duration.

question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters (cell cycle, stress response, mitochondrial potential) for days before and during drug, then trace survivors back to identify which pre-drug features predicted survival.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome of persisters with epigenetic perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and RNA jointly in untreated cells and persisters to identify reversible regulatory states, then test causality with CRISPRi/CRISPRa or epigenetic inhibitors of the top candidate regulators.

question: persister
title: Pre-sorting by metabolic and mitochondrial state
description: Use FACS or FLIM to isolate cells by mitochondrial potential, NADH state, or lipid peroxidation susceptibility before drug exposure, then compare their survival to test whether metabolic heterogeneity causally drives tolerance.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sibling-split and pre-treatment profiling
description: Label clonal cells with expressed lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/FateMap-style), split sister cells before drug, profile one half by scRNA-seq and expose the other to drug, then test whether pre-treatment transcriptional state of a lineage predicts survival. This directly separates pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance and reveals the pre-treatment state of cells that would otherwise be destroyed.

question: persister
title: Epigenomic and extrachromosomal DNA profiling of isogenic single cells
description: Run single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA), histone-mark profiling (e.g., CUT&Tag), and ecDNA/copy-number sequencing on untreated and surviving cells to test whether chromatin states or ecDNA dosage heterogeneity, not sequence mutations, distinguish survivors. Perturb candidate regulators (e.g., KDM5, EZH2 inhibitors) to test causality.

question: persister
title: Long-term live-cell imaging with single-cell tracking and fate-mapping
description: Image thousands of individual cells for days before, during, and after drug using fluorescent reporters (cell cycle FUCCI, ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, apoptosis caspase reporters, mitochondrial potential), then retrospectively link dynamics to fate. This captures fluctuating, non-binary states and the temporal course of persister entry, exit, and regrowth, rather than endpoint averages.

question: persister
title: Rare-cell-enriched spatial and single-cell multi-omics from 3D/in vivo models
description: Treat organoids, co-cultures, or xenografts with the drug and perform spatial transcriptomics/proteomics (e.g., MERFISH, imaging mass cytometry) to map where survivors sit relative to drug gradients, hypoxia, stroma, and immune cells. Compare to 2D to show which survival states are microenvironment-dependent artifacts or contributors.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR perturbation screens with single-cell readout across drug schedules
description: Run CRISPRi/a and Perturb-seq screens under different doses and schedules (continuous, pulsed, combination) to find regulators of the persister state beyond the target pathway, covering metabolism, stress response, and chromatin. Compare hits across persistence, tolerance, and resistance phenotypes (time-kill curves) to determine which layer of regulation drives survival.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with split-population fate tracing
description: Label cells with heritable, expressed DNA barcodes, split the population into replicates before treatment, and compare which barcodes survive across replicates and with RNA profiles of sister cells taken before treatment. Shared survivors across replicates indicate a pre-existing heritable state, and random survivors indicate stochastic or induced entry, which tests the assumption that survivors are a fixed pre-existing state.

question: persister
title: Long-term live-cell imaging with lineage reconstruction before, during, and after drug
description: Track thousands of single cells and their families by time-lapse microscopy with reporters for cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and apoptosis. Then ask whether pre-drug history (cycle length, signaling pulses, sister-cell correlation) predicts survival. This replaces the endpoint-snapshot assumption with dynamic, cell-by-cell data.

question: persister
title: Whole-genome sequencing and ecDNA/mtDNA profiling of clonally derived survivors
description: Sequence single-cell-derived clones, or single-cell DNA from pre-treatment and survivor cells, for rare mutations, copy-number changes, ecDNA amplification, and mtDNA heterogeneity, and test whether those variants are enriched in survivors. This tests the assumption that cells are genetically identical, including variation below the resolution of standard exome or bulk sequencing.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multi-omics with protein, chromatin, and metabolic readouts
description: Combine scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, CITE-seq or mass cytometry for signaling proteins, and metabolic imaging such as NAD(P)H FLIM or mitochondrial membrane potential, then sort and profile cells that survive. This tests the assumption that transcript levels capture the relevant state. It can find epigenetic, proteomic, or metabolic determinants such as high mitochondrial priming or a drug-tolerant chromatin state.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironment perturbation of survival, in co-culture and 3D or in vivo
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging in 3D spheroids, co-cultures, or xenografts to map survivors relative to neighbors, oxygen and drug gradients, and stromal secretion. Then perturb the niche, for example with conditioned medium, a drug-penetration reporter, or fluorescent drug analogs, to test whether survival depends on local drug exposure or paracrine support instead of intrinsic state. This tests the assumptions that survival is cell-intrinsic, that drug exposure is uniform, and that monolayer culture suffices.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split-and-treat
description: Tag cells with expressed heritable barcodes, split clonal families before drug, and sequence the pre-treatment sibling to learn the baseline state of cells whose relatives survive. This tests whether survival is a pre-existing, heritable-like state versus post-drug stochastic adaptation, and recovers the pre-drug transcriptome of future survivors.

question: persister
title: Single-cell whole-genome and clonal deep sequencing for hidden genetics
description: Run single-cell DNA-seq (CNV, SNV) or deep clonal sequencing on pre-treatment populations and on survivors to test for rare subclonal variants, extrachromosomal DNA, or mtDNA heteroplasmy that were assumed absent. A matched comparison of survivors against the clonal parental population shows whether apparent non-genetic persistence has a cryptic genetic basis.

question: persister
title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment effects
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging with defined neighbor-density gradients, conditioned media, and sparse-versus-dense plating or microfluidic isolation of single cells to test whether survival depends on neighbors, paracrine signals, or local drug and oxygen gradients. Comparing isolated cells to colonies separates cell-intrinsic from community-driven survival.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with retrospective fate mapping
description: Image reporter lines (cell-cycle, ERK/AKT activity, apoptosis, stress response) in single cells for days before and during drug, then link dynamic histories (cycle length, signaling pulses) to fate by machine learning. This avoids post-hoc identification of survivors and shows whether survival is predicted by dynamics or history instead of a static snapshot state.

question: persister
title: Multi-omic profiling with dose-response and 3D/in vivo context
description: Apply paired single-cell ATAC/RNA plus proteomics or metabolic imaging (NADH FLIM, mitochondrial membrane potential) across a dose range, in 2D, organoid, and xenograft settings, to find whether survivors use multiple, dose- and context-dependent mechanisms. Perturbing candidate factors by CRISPRi in a pooled screen then tests which layers causally contribute, beyond mRNA-only single-cause models.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with sibling-pair and split-clone tracking
description: Barcode cells, split the expanded population into replicate arms before drug, and compare which barcodes survive across arms and between sister cells. This shows whether survival is heritable and pre-existing, or stochastic and drug-induced. It also gives the memory timescale of the state.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters, followed by retrospective fate mapping
description: Image cells for days before and after drug using reporters for ERK or p53 dynamics, cell cycle, and apoptosis, then trace survivors back to their pre-drug history. Dynamic features such as pulsing or cycle phase can then be tested as predictors of survival. Fixed-cell profiling of the same cells can be added afterward.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiomics of the same clone, including genetic and non-nuclear variation
description: Run joint scRNA/scATAC with single-cell DNA sequencing, which gives copy number, ecDNA and mtDNA variants, on cells before drug, during drug and after it. This tests whether small genetic or mitochondrial differences are hidden under apparent identity. It also tests whether survivors share any such difference or any state.

question: persister
title: Pre-drug state capture linked to fate, using Live-seq or photoactivatable isolation
description: Take a non-destructive RNA biopsy, or image-guided photo-marking and sorting, of individual cells before drug. Follow each cell to its fate, then train a model to predict survival from its prior state. This tests directly whether a pre-existing state exists, instead of inferring it from survivors only.

question: persister
title: Microenvironment and drug-exposure heterogeneity mapping in 3D and in vivo models
description: Use spheroids, organoids or xenografts with spatial transcriptomics, hypoxia and nutrient sensors, and mass-spectrometry imaging of drug levels. Compare survivors' positions and local drug concentration with their intrinsic state. This separates cells that are truly resistant from cells that were under-dosed or protected by neighbors or stroma.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with split-clone fate tracing
description: Label cells with expressed heritable barcodes, split the population before drug, treat one arm and profile the other by scRNA-seq, so each survivor's sister cells reveal its pre-treatment state. Clone-level concordance of survival across replicates distinguishes pre-existing heritable states from stochastic switching, which tests the assumption that survivors are a pre-existing, stable subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Time-lapse single-cell imaging with live reporters and retrospective tracking
description: Image cells for days before, during and after drug using reporters for cell-cycle state, ERK/AKT activity, p53 dynamics, and mitochondrial or ROS state, then trace survivors back to their pre-drug histories. Dynamic features such as pulsing, cell-cycle duration and recent mitosis may predict survival where static snapshots fail, which tests the fixed-property and single-time-point assumption.

question: persister
title: Deep genetic and epigenetic check of survivors versus matched sisters
description: Perform single-cell whole-genome or exome sequencing for copy-number changes and subclonal variants, along with scATAC or CUT&Tag for chromatin state, on sorted survivors and barcode-matched untreated sisters. This tests whether 'genetically identical' is actually true and whether heritable chromatin states, rather than transcript levels, carry the difference.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironment-resolved survival mapping in 3D or in vivo
description: Treat spheroids, organoids with stromal cells, or xenografts, then use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging with drug-penetration measurements to map survivors against position, oxygen, neighbor identity and local drug concentration. This tests whether survival comes from cell-intrinsic state or from niche and pharmacokinetic heterogeneity, as the 2D monoculture assumption implies.

question: persister
title: Multi-omic single-cell profiling of proteins, metabolism and signaling
description: Use CyTOF or CITE-seq for proteins and phospho-signaling, along with single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H FLIM or SCENITH, on cells sampled at several times after drug. Pair this with CRISPR perturbation of candidate non-target-pathway programs, such as oxidative phosphorylation, drug efflux or stress-response genes, to show causality. This tests the assumptions that transcripts are enough and that the drug's target pathway explains survival.

question: persister
title: Barcode lineage tracing with sibling-matched pre-treatment profiling
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the clonal sibling cells before drug, and profile one half by scRNA-seq while treating the other half, so that the barcodes identify which pre-treatment states gave rise to survivors. This tests whether survival is pre-existing and heritable, and avoids reading survivors only after the fact. Comparing barcode enrichment across replicate splits separates pre-existing from drug-induced states.

question: persister
title: Whole-genome and mtDNA deep sequencing of isolated survivors
description: Sort or isolate survivors and matched untreated clonal siblings, then run deep whole-genome, copy-number, ecDNA and mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing to look for rare subclonal variants. This tests whether 'genetically identical' actually holds, and finds low-frequency genetic contributors if it does not. Re-treating clones expanded from survivors indicates whether the resistance is stably inherited.

question: persister
title: Live-cell single-cell time-lapse with reporters, then retrospective fate assignment
description: Image cells for days before and after drug with reporters for cell cycle (FUCCI), ERK or AKT signaling, apoptosis, and drug-target activity, and track each cell's lineage to its eventual fate. Dynamic features such as pre-drug cell-cycle phase, pulsatile signaling, and time of arrest can then be tested as predictors of survival, replacing a single live/dead endpoint with trajectories. Fixing and staining the same cells afterward connects those dynamics to molecular state.

question: persister
title: Spatial and co-culture manipulation of neighbor effects
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and in micropatterns, use conditioned-medium swaps and mixed cultures with fluorescent labels, and run spatial transcriptomics, to test whether survival depends on local neighbors, paracrine signals, or position. Compare the survival of an isolated single cell to that of the same cell type in a cluster. A neighborhood-dependent effect would show survival is not purely cell-autonomous.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug uptake, efflux and metabolic imaging
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in individual cells, using fluorescent drug analogs or label-free mass spectrometry imaging, together with efflux activity, NAD(P)H/FLIM metabolic state, mitochondrial membrane potential and ROS, and then follow those cells' survival. This tests whether survivors differ in drug exposure or metabolism instead of in transcript levels. Pharmacological perturbation of the identified efflux or metabolic pathways can then provide a causal test.

question: persister
title: Single-cell whole-genome and mtDNA lineage sequencing of survivors vs. matched sister cells
description: Use barcoded lineage tracing plus single-cell DNA-seq (CNV, ecDNA, mtDNA heteroplasmy) on survivors and untreated sister lineages to test whether apparent 'identical' cells carry rare heritable genetic or mtDNA differences that predispose to survival.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded split-clone experiments with pre-treatment profiling
description: Barcode cells, split each expanding clone into a sister arm that is profiled by scRNA-seq/ATAC before drug and a sister arm treated with drug; the barcodes then link pre-existing states to survival and show whether tolerance is pre-existing and heritable or induced, using sister-clone concordance and fluctuation-test statistics.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and lineage tracking, followed by in situ endpoint omics
description: Image thousands of single cells and their ancestry for days before, during and after drug using biosensors (ERK/AKT activity, cell cycle, apoptosis, mitochondrial state), then fix and perform multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics on the same cells, to resolve dynamic trajectories and the timing of fate decisions that snapshots miss.

question: persister
title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment and neighbor effects
description: Compare survival in 3D spheroids, organoids or tumor sections using spatial transcriptomics, and in dense vs sparse and conditioned-medium or neighbor-ablation set-ups, to test whether survivors depend on position, drug penetration, or paracrine signaling from neighbors rather than intrinsic state.

question: persister
title: Multi-dose, multi-timepoint pharmacology with intracellular drug and target-engagement measurements plus CRISPR perturbation of candidate programs
description: Measure single-cell drug concentration (fluorescent or mass-spec imaging analogs), efflux activity and target occupancy and phospho-pathway rebound across doses and times, and run pooled CRISPR screens plus epigenetic (histone marks, chromatin accessibility) profiling of persisters to test which states causally govern survival and whether epigenetic or metabolic memory is required.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing with split-clone pre-drug sampling
description: Label cells with heritable expression barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/CellTag-style), split the population before treatment, and sequence one half while treating the other. This tests whether survivors are pre-determined by a heritable (non-genetic or hidden genetic) state by matching surviving lineages to their pre-drug transcriptomes, and measuring how much of survival is shared among sister clones versus random.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multi-omic and long-read genomic profiling of survivors for hidden genetic variation
description: Perform single-cell WGS or DNA+RNA co-profiling (plus ecDNA and copy-number analysis) on survivors and matched untreated cells, with ultra-deep duplex sequencing of the parental line. This directly tests the 'genetically identical' premise by detecting rare subclonal SNVs, CNVs, or ecDNA that are enriched in survivors.

question: persister
title: Long-term live-cell imaging with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image thousands of single cells for days before and during drug exposure using reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptosis, then identify survivors and trace their histories backward. This tests the assumption of static, binary, endpoint-measured survival by revealing whether pre-drug dynamics, such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or division-time history, predict survival, and whether cells enter and exit tolerance.

question: persister
title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment and drug exposure
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging in 3D spheroids or xenografts, together with microfluidic or conditioned-medium manipulations, to map where survivors sit relative to drug gradients, hypoxia, stroma, and neighboring dying cells. This tests the cell-intrinsic assumption by asking whether local niche, paracrine signals (e.g., from dying neighbors), or reduced effective drug dose, rather than intrinsic state, cause survival.

question: persister
title: Sorting live pre-drug cells by non-transcriptional state (metabolism, mitochondria, chromatin) and testing causality
description: Use live-cell reporters or dyes (mitochondrial membrane potential, NADH/FLIM, ROS, lysosomal content) and single-cell ATAC or histone-mark profiling to sort rare states, then challenge sorted fractions with drug. Pairing this with CRISPR perturbation or inhibitors of the candidate states (e.g., GPX4, histone demethylases) tests whether the tolerance state is encoded outside mRNA levels and whether it is causal rather than correlative.

question: persister
title: Pre-existing vs. induced state from lineage-barcoding datasets
description: Reanalyze public clonal barcoding scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Cellular Barcoding studies of BRAF-inhibitor-treated melanoma, EGFR-inhibitor-treated lung cancer, Shaffer/Hata/Oren/Goyal data in GEO). Test whether sister cells' pre-treatment transcriptomes predict survival, and quantify how much of survival is heritable versus stochastic, to separate pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment signature of persisters
description: Use public paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell expression data to build a classifier of the rare pre-treatment cell state, such as the NGFR-high, AXL-high or dedifferentiated melanoma states, and the EMT-like or drug-tolerant states. Validate it on held-out cell lines and on public drug-response data (GDSC, CTRP, DepMap PRISM) by testing whether the signature predicts tolerance across lines.

question: persister
title: Chromatin accessibility and epigenetic memory meta-analysis
description: Integrate public scATAC-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq and histone-mark data (H3K27me3, KDM5 targets, SWI/SNF) from persisters and parental cells. Find the transcription factor motifs and enhancers that open or close in persisters, and check whether those accessibility changes are already present in a subset of untreated cells, to identify the regulators that carry the memory.

question: persister
title: Transcriptional-noise and cell-cycle/metabolic state modeling
description: Using public time-course scRNA-seq and live-cell imaging datasets, calculate gene-expression variability, cell-cycle phase (slow-cycling or G0/G1 arrest) and metabolic signatures (oxidative phosphorylation, ferroptosis defense via GPX4). Fit stochastic state-switching models to estimate the switching rates and ask whether survival is better explained by noise, quiescence or metabolic state.

question: persister
title: Genetic-ruling-out and clinical concordance analysis
description: Reanalyze public whole-exome and whole-genome data and copy-number profiles from persister cells, resistant clones and matched patient biopsies (such as minimal residual disease samples). Rule out pre-existing mutations and copy-number changes as the cause, and check whether the persister transcriptional programs also appear in patient on-treatment samples and associate with relapse in TCGA and clinical trial cohorts.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing before and after drug (Watermelon/ClonTracer-style)
description: Label a clonal line with a high-complexity expression barcode library, split into replicate pools, treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes pre- and post-treatment. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the cause is a pre-existing heritable state. If different barcodes survive, the cause is stochastic or induced. Cost is roughly $5–10k, covering the library, cell culture and amplicon sequencing.

question: persister
title: Single-cell RNA-seq of matched lineages (pre-drug sister cells vs. survivors)
description: Split barcoded cells so that sister cells are profiled by scRNA-seq before drug and survivors are profiled after. This links the transcriptional state before treatment (for example drug-efflux, EMT-like, or stress-response programs) to later survival. Sequencing about 10–20k cells across timepoints fits within about $10–15k.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with fluorescent reporters and lineage tracking
description: Image cells for days before and during drug exposure. Use reporters for ERK or AKT signaling, cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptosis, and track single-cell lineages. This shows whether survival is predicted by pre-existing signaling dynamics, slow cycling, or inherited fluctuations, and whether it correlates between sister cells. Use an existing microscope and open-source tracking software, with reagents costing about $3–8k.

question: persister
title: Sort-and-profile of rare states (FACS on candidate markers, then bulk ATAC/RNA-seq and drug re-challenge)
description: Sort cells by candidate markers such as a surface marker, a fluorescent reporter of a resistance-associated gene, or a mitochondrial or ROS dye. Then test drug sensitivity and chromatin accessibility and expression in each fraction. Compare how fast sorted populations return to the original distribution to measure state-switching rates and epigenetic memory. Reagents and sequencing cost about $8–12k.

question: persister
title: Perturbation screen of candidate persistence mechanisms
description: Run a focused CRISPRi/CRISPRa screen, or a small-molecule screen, targeting chromatin regulators, stress-response genes, drug transporters, and metabolic enzymes. Treat with the drug and score enrichment or depletion of survivors. This tests which pathways are causally needed for survival, as opposed to merely correlated with it. Use a few hundred genes with 5–10 guides each, which costs about $10–15k.

question: persister
title: Lineage-tracked pre-treatment history of survivors
description: Long-term time-lapse of cells before drug addition, tracking lineages with nuclear and cell-cycle reporters (e.g., H2B-mCherry, FUCCI), then add drug and retrospectively trace survivors back to their ancestors. This tests whether survival is predicted by pre-existing states such as cell-cycle length, quiescence or division history, and whether sister and cousin cells share fates, which would indicate heritable rather than stochastic states.

question: persister
title: Live biosensors of signaling and stress dynamics
description: Image single cells carrying fluorescent reporters for the drug's target pathway (e.g., ERK KTR for MAPK inhibitors), p53, NF-κB, and the integrated stress response through drug exposure. Quantify whether survivors show faster pathway reactivation, pulsatile or adaptive dynamics, or lower stress amplitude than cells that die, linking dynamic signaling signatures to fate.

question: persister
title: Real-time apoptosis and caspase-threshold imaging
description: Use live caspase-3/7 or FRET-based caspase reporters, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes and BH3-sensitivity reporters to measure each cell's distance from the apoptotic threshold. Compare the timing, rate and reversibility (anastasis) of caspase activation in survivors and dying cells to show whether survivors resist initiation of death, show sublethal caspase activity, or recover after partial activation.

question: persister
title: Post-treatment fate mapping of persister state transitions
description: Continuously image survivors for weeks under drug with proliferation and cell-cycle reporters, plus size and morphology readouts. This classifies fates such as arrest, slow cycling, polyploidization, or drug-tolerant re-entry, and measures the kinetics of regrowth after drug withdrawal. It shows whether persisters are a stable subpopulation or a transient, reversible state, and how rare re-entry events arise.

question: persister
title: Live imaging of drug exposure and metabolic or organelle state
description: Image intrinsically fluorescent or fluorescently labeled drug to measure per-cell uptake and efflux, alongside live readouts of NAD(P)H/FAD autofluorescence (FLIM), mitochondrial content, ROS and lysosomal dye. This tests whether survival reflects lower intracellular drug dose, efflux activity, or distinct metabolic and organelle states, using single-cell correlations with eventual fate.

question: persister
title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split analysis
description: Label cells with heritable, non-perturbing expressed DNA barcodes (viral barcode library, no gene perturbation), split the population before treatment, and compare barcode abundance and pre-treatment transcriptomes of sister clones to test whether survival is pre-existing and heritable (clonal) versus stochastic. Pairing scRNA-seq of untreated sisters with the barcodes of survivors identifies the pre-treatment state that predicts persistence.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with fluorescent reporters and retrospective lineage analysis
description: Image thousands of single cells and their lineages for days before, during, and after drug using non-perturbing live reporters (e.g., FUCCI, ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes). Retrospectively link pre-drug cell-cycle length, signaling dynamics, and mother-daughter correlations to survival and then to regrowth, revealing which dynamic states and how heritable they are.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved single-cell multi-omics of drug response
description: Perform scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) at multiple time points (untreated, hours, days, weeks of drug) to map the trajectory from baseline cell states to persister states. Inferring state transitions with RNA velocity or trajectory methods distinguishes selection of rare pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptive reprogramming, and chromatin accessibility reveals candidate regulatory programs.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation (Luria–Delbrück-style) test and state-sorting experiments
description: Compare variance in surviving colony numbers across many parallel small cultures versus bulk replicates, and sort cells by candidate markers or reporters (e.g., high/low of a drug-tolerance-associated surface marker, ROS, or lipid content) before drug exposure. Measuring survival of each sorted fraction and how quickly sorted subpopulations re-equilibrate quantifies switching rates and tests whether tolerance is a reversible non-genetic state.

question: persister
title: Orthogonal genomic and metabolic profiling of persisters versus matched controls
description: Run single-cell or low-input whole-genome/exome sequencing on survivors to rule out or identify genetic or copy-number changes, alongside epigenomic profiling (histone marks, DNA methylation) and single-cell metabolic readouts (mass cytometry, NAD(P)H FLIM, mitochondrial/lipid dyes, drug efflux assays, and measurements of intracellular drug concentration). Pharmacologic perturbations (e.g., small-molecule epigenetic or metabolic inhibitors, not genetic) can then test which differences are functionally linked to persistence.

question: persister
title: Barcoded lineage tracing in a canine or zebrafish-derived cancer line
description: Use a clonal lentiviral/CRISPR barcode library in a genetically identical non-human, non-mouse cancer line (e.g., canine osteosarcoma or zebrafish melanoma ZMEL1 cells). Split the barcoded population into replicate arms, treat each with a targeted inhibitor (e.g., BRAF/MEK inhibitor in ZMEL1), and sequence barcodes in survivors. Barcodes that recur across independent replicates indicate a pre-existing, heritable survivor state. Barcodes that are random across replicates indicate stochastic, drug-induced adaptation.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome profiling of survivors in zebrafish melanoma, before and after drug
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on ZMEL1 cells (or on tumors in transparent casper zebrafish) at baseline, at early drug exposure, and at the drug-tolerant persister stage. Match surviving cells to their pre-treatment states using barcodes or transcriptional trajectories. This shows whether survivors come from a rare chromatin or transcriptional state (e.g., neural crest-like or slow-cycling) and which regulators lock that state in.

question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging of fate with in vivo zebrafish xenograft/transgenic reporters
description: Image fluorescent reporters of cell cycle (FUCCI), ERK/kinase activity (FRET biosensor), mitochondrial state and apoptosis in individual cells in transparent zebrafish tumors or cultured fish cancer cells. Record cells for days before and during drug exposure, and retrospectively classify the cells that survive. Because cells are tracked over time, this links pre-treatment dynamics (pulsatile signaling, quiescence, cell-cycle phase, mitochondrial priming) to survival at single-cell resolution, which snapshot omics cannot do.

question: persister
title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens in a Drosophila cell line or Drosophila tumor model
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens in Drosophila S2R+ cells, or RNAi screens in a Ras/Scrib fly tumor model, under a targeted inhibitor (e.g., a MEK or PI3K inhibitor). Look for genes that change the fraction of survivors without changing the average drug IC50. These genes, such as chromatin regulators, stress-response genes and drug-efflux genes, identify the machinery of tolerance as distinct from classical resistance, and the screens are cheaper and more tractable than in mammalian cells.

question: persister
title: Paired genetic, epigenetic and reversibility tests on survivor clones in yeast cancer-like models
description: Use drug-tolerant subpopulations in budding yeast (e.g., engineered with oncogenic RAS or TOR pathway activation under a targeted TOR/kinase inhibitor). Sort survivors by growth rate, expand clones, and whole-genome sequence them. Test heritability by regrowing without drug and re-challenging at timed intervals. Combine this with ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq and single-cell growth-rate measurements in microfluidics to separate mutation from reversible epigenetic or noise-driven states, and to measure state-switching rates directly.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment vs. post-treatment transcriptomics
description: Tag a clonal cell line with a heritable expression barcode library, split the population before drug exposure, profile one half by scRNA-seq, and treat the other half. Then match surviving barcodes back to the pre-treatment sister cells to find the transcriptional states that predicted survival and test whether those states are heritable or transient; this takes about 2–3 months with an established barcoding system.

question: persister
title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters, followed by fate-linked fixed profiling
description: Image cells carrying reporters (such as cell-cycle FUCCI, ERK/AKT activity, and apoptosis markers) for several days before and during drug treatment, and track single-cell fates. After imaging, fix the cells in place and run multiplexed immunofluorescence or in situ RNA staining on the same cells, which links dynamic signaling history and cell-cycle state to survival or death.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) of drug-tolerant persisters over a time course
description: Collect untreated cells and cells at days 3, 7, and 14 of treatment, and profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression jointly in the same cells. This tests whether persisters carry a distinct epigenetic state, such as an altered enhancer landscape or a stress/dedifferentiation program, and identifies the transcription factors that drive it.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR perturbation screen focused on candidate persister regulators
description: Run a targeted CRISPRi/CRISPRa library covering chromatin regulators, stress-response genes, anti-apoptotic factors, and metabolic genes, with drug versus vehicle arms and sgRNA counts read out at several time points. Genes whose loss reduces the persister fraction, or whose activation raises it, show which pathways are causally required, as opposed to only correlated with survival.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and apoptotic-priming measurements
description: Before treatment, sort cells by readouts such as mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, lipid content, or BH3 profiling for apoptotic priming. Then treat the sorted subpopulations and measure survival to test whether pre-existing differences in metabolism or mitochondrial apoptotic threshold set the likelihood of surviving. Follow with drug combinations that target the identified vulnerability, such as BCL-2 family inhibitors or ferroptosis inducers.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) of drug-naive populations with lineage barcodes
description: Profile untreated cells at one time point with scRNA-seq plus chromatin accessibility, and use clonal barcodes in parallel sister samples (Rosetta/Watermelon-style) to link pre-existing transcriptional and epigenetic states to later survival. This identifies the cell-state signatures and regulatory programs that predispose to persistence, and tests whether states are heritable.

question: persister
title: Single-cell profiling of survivors at one late post-treatment time point, with matched untreated control
description: Harvest cells after a fixed drug exposure and run scRNA-seq or CITE-seq, comparing against untreated cells to define the persister state (e.g., drug-tolerant, EMT-like, stress response, dormancy). Cell-surface markers from CITE-seq can then be used to isolate and test persisters.

question: persister
title: Spatial transcriptomics/multiplexed imaging of treated tumors or 3D cultures
description: Take a single fixed snapshot of treated spheroids or xenograft sections and map surviving cells with spatial transcriptomics or CODEX/IMC. This reveals whether survival depends on microenvironment, such as hypoxia, proximity to stroma, or drug-penetration gradients, rather than on cell-intrinsic state alone.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screen read out at a single endpoint
description: Transduce a genome-wide or focused (epigenetic, stress-response, apoptosis, drug-efflux) CRISPR library, treat, and sequence guide abundance once at endpoint relative to the untreated control. Enriched or depleted guides identify genes that causally enable or prevent persistence, which goes beyond correlative profiling.

question: persister
title: Single-cell quantification of drug, signaling and apoptotic-priming state in fixed cells
description: At one time point after treatment, use mass cytometry or high-content multiplexed immunofluorescence to measure target inhibition (phospho-signaling), intracellular drug levels (for fluorescent drugs), efflux pump expression, cell-cycle status, and BH3 profiling or cleaved caspase levels in each cell. This distinguishes persisters that avoid drug exposure, bypass target inhibition, or resist apoptosis, and it captures multiple mechanisms simultaneously per cell.

question: persister
title: Paired single-cell multi-omics of patient tumor biopsies before and during targeted therapy
description: Perform scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq (or multiome) on serial biopsies from the same patients at baseline, on-treatment (residual disease), and at progression to identify transcriptional and chromatin states enriched in surviving cells. Then test whether those states were already present at low frequency pre-treatment, which would indicate pre-existing rather than drug-induced tolerance.

question: persister
title: Lineage tracing in patient-derived organoids/primary cultures with barcoding and post-hoc transcriptomics
description: Introduce expressed DNA barcodes into patient-derived tumor cells, split the population into replicates, treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes and transcriptomes of survivors versus untreated sister cells. Barcodes shared across independent replicates reveal heritable, pre-existing persister states, while barcodes appearing in only one replicate point to stochastic or induced survival.

question: persister
title: Live-cell single-cell imaging and tracking of patient-derived cells with reporter-based fate readouts
description: Time-lapse image patient tumor cells expressing signaling reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, cell-cycle and apoptosis sensors) before and through drug exposure, tracking each cell's lineage to the end. Retrospective analysis shows whether pre-treatment signaling dynamics, cell-cycle position, or lineage history predict survival, and fixed-cell multiplex profiling of the same cells can then link the phenotypes to molecular states.

question: persister
title: Single-cell genomic and epigenomic profiling to exclude or confirm hidden genetic and epigenetic differences
description: Run single-cell DNA sequencing (copy number and mutations) and single-cell DNA methylation or histone-mark profiling (e.g., CUT&Tag) on patient tumor samples before treatment and on persisters. This separates rare pre-existing subclones or copy-number changes from purely non-genetic, epigenetically maintained states, and reveals which regulators, such as KDM5 or other chromatin modifiers, sustain the tolerant state.

question: persister
title: Spatial profiling of patient tumor sections to map the microenvironment around residual cells
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed protein imaging to matched pre-treatment and residual-disease patient specimens to see whether surviving cells cluster near specific stromal, immune, hypoxic, or nutrient-limited niches. Ligand–receptor analysis and co-culture of patient-derived cells with autologous stromal or immune cells can then test whether these niche signals cause tolerance.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation-test (Luria-Delbrück) analysis of survivor-rate variance
description: Seed many small replicate cultures from single cells or a few cells at varied expansion times, treat with drug, and compare the variance and mean of survivor counts across replicates and expansion times. Fit stochastic state-switching models to estimate switching rates in and out of the tolerant state, and thereby distinguish pre-existing heritable states, rapid reversible switching, and drug-induced adaptation, and to estimate state memory duration.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell pair survival concordance with time-resolved decay
description: Plate cells at clonal density, track the divisions of individual cells, and treat sister pairs, cousins and more distant relatives at defined times after division. Measure how survival concordance decays with lineage distance to quantify how long the tolerant state is inherited and whether the determinant is cytoplasmic (e.g. mitochondria, protein levels) or epigenetic.

question: persister
title: Mitotic-history and cell-cycle-timing dependence of survival
description: Combine live imaging with fluorescent cell-cycle reporters and a short drug pulse to test whether survival depends on cell-cycle phase at exposure, time since last division, or mitotic duration, including slow-cycling or G0-like states. Use pulsed or synchronized drug application and asymmetric partitioning markers (e.g. label-retention dyes) to separate the effects of cycle state from stable cell identity.

question: persister
title: Single-cell DNA copy number and extrachromosomal DNA heterogeneity profiling
description: Use single-cell DNA sequencing, or ecDNA FISH combined with drug-target gene imaging, on untreated and surviving cells to test whether apparently identical cells differ in target or bypass-gene copy number, ecDNA content, or low-frequency mutations. Compare the rate at which copy number diverges in sub-clones with survivor frequency to see whether copy number variation or ecDNA drives survival.

question: persister
title: Intracellular drug and target-engagement quantification per cell
description: Measure per-cell intracellular drug concentration (using intrinsically fluorescent drugs, a fluorescent drug analog, or mass-spec imaging/CyTOF for metal-labeled compounds) together with target occupancy or downstream phosphorylation shortly after exposure. Test whether survivors simply experience lower effective target inhibition (via efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or target abundance) versus tolerating equal inhibition, by sorting on drug content and re-challenging.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell concordance after forced division in microfluidic traps
description: Track pairs of daughters (or micro-colonies) and compare their drug fate versus random unrelated pairs, using decay of concordance over generations to estimate the memory timescale of tolerance. Fitting this to stochastic-switching models distinguishes fast fluctuation, epigenetic memory, and mutation without requiring molecular markers.

question: persister
title: Single-cell DNA replication stress and mitotic history readout (scEdU/53BP1 + fixed-cell Cell-Cycle profiling)
description: Quantify inherited DNA damage, under-replicated DNA, and 53BP1 nuclear bodies in mother-daughter pairs before drug, then relate them to survival. This tests whether persisters arise from a prior stress or mitotic-error history rather than from a stable transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Single-cell proteoform and signaling-network rewiring by mass cytometry or phospho-flow of drug-adjacent cells
description: Measure dozens of phospho-proteins and cleaved-caspase markers at several time points after drug in the same cells to infer the rewiring of the target's pathway and the feedback loops. Information-theoretic analysis (e.g., mutual information between input and output, or bypass-pathway reactivation) would show whether survivors reactivate signaling early, an event that transcriptomics often misses.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy and copy-number lineage tracing
description: Use natural mtDNA variants (via mitochondrial scATAC or MAESTER) as endogenous lineage barcodes in clonal lines, and test whether heteroplasmy level or mtDNA copy number in sister cells predicts survival. This provides non-genetic, non-nuclear heritable variation that can explain drug tolerance in a genetically identical population.

question: persister
title: Intracellular drug quantification at single-cell resolution
description: Use intrinsically fluorescent drugs, a fluorescent drug analog, or a target-engagement biosensor (such as a cellular thermal shift or a probe competition assay by imaging) to measure how much drug reaches and binds the target in each cell. Comparing this with fate shows whether survivors are simply under-dosed through uptake, efflux, or lysosomal sequestration, rather than intrinsically resistant.

question: persister
title: Sibling-pair death-timing correlation under drug
description: Film isolated daughter pairs (and later cousins) from a recent division through drug exposure and record each cell's time of death or arrest. High sister-sister concordance versus random pairing, with decay over generations, quantifies the heritability and half-life of the tolerance state without any molecular assumptions.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and redox state sorting by FLIM/biosensors, then drug challenge
description: Measure NAD(P)H lifetime, ATP/NADH biosensors, mitochondrial membrane potential, and ROS in individual drug-naive cells, then gently sort or track them and challenge with drug. This tests whether pre-existing metabolic or redox heterogeneity, not transcript level, predicts survival.

question: persister
title: Drug-target engagement and intracellular drug concentration heterogeneity
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a target-engagement reporter (such as a CETSA-like or phospho-substrate readout), or single-cell mass-spec/mass-cytometry to measure how much drug reaches the target in each cell. Compare survivors versus dying cells to determine whether efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or incomplete pathway inhibition explains survival rather than downstream adaptation.

question: persister
title: Nascent transcription and translation dynamics in early drug response (time-resolved metabolic labeling)
description: Apply scSLAM-seq or scNT-seq with 4sU labeling, plus puromycin-based translation readouts, during the first hours of drug exposure to separate newly induced stress programs from pre-existing mRNA. Comparing the labeled and unlabeled fractions shows whether survivors actively rewire, for example through ISR-driven selective translation, or just start from a different baseline.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D culture or xenograft sections
description: Run spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging (such as CODEX) on drug-treated spheroids or tumors, and test whether survivors cluster by local oxygen, density, stromal contact, or neighbor secreted signals. Complement this with conditioned-medium and density-titration experiments to determine whether tolerance is cell-intrinsic or induced by neighbors.

question: persister
title: Cell-cycle/division-history memory via dye dilution and H2B-FUCCI
description: Label cells with a retained dye or photoconvertible histone to record the number of divisions and time since last mitosis, then sort by division history before drug exposure. This tests whether survival is encoded by proliferative history (e.g., slow-cycling lineages, inherited from mother-cell age) rather than by a specific expression program.

question: persister
title: Single-cell DNA replication stress and copy-number/mutation mapping of survivors
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing (and scRNA-seq on the same cells via paired methods) on survivors versus matched pre-treatment clones to detect rare subclonal aneuploidy, extrachromosomal DNA amplification, or ongoing mutagenesis. This tests whether 'genetically identical' is actually false at the sub-chromosomal level, and whether persisters transiently up-regulate error-prone repair.

question: persister
title: Quantitative drug-target engagement per cell
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a CETSA/NanoBRET target-engagement reporter, or a phospho-substrate biosensor to measure how much drug actually binds its target in each cell in the first hours after treatment. Then sort by engagement and follow fates, to separate pharmacokinetic escape (low intracellular occupancy) from true downstream signaling rewiring.

question: persister
title: Noise-manipulation experiments of gene expression
description: Use synthetic circuits or promoter/CRISPR edits that change expression variability of a candidate gene while holding its mean constant, then measure persister fraction. This tests causally whether non-genetic heterogeneity (noise itself) generates survivors, and whether bet-hedging is selectable.

question: persister
title: Microenvironment and cell-neighbor contribution via spatial co-culture and conditioned-medium swaps
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and micropatterns, or use mixed fluorescent-labeled populations. Quantify survival as a function of neighbor identity, distance to dying cells, and secreted factors, using spatial transcriptomics or cell-cell proximity labeling (e.g., TurboID). This tests whether persistence is a cell-intrinsic state or a collective property that arises from paracrine rescue or local contact signaling.

question: persister
title: Mitotic-memory inheritance test via sister-cell asymmetry
description: Time-lapse image newly divided sister pairs and daughters across several generations, then apply drug and score survival concordance versus cousin pairs. Decay of sister/cousin correlation with generation distance gives the memory time of the tolerant state, and asymmetric partitioning of mitochondria, p53, or protein aggregates can be tested as causal inheritance.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and biophysical profiling of pre-drug cells
description: Before treatment, measure each cell's NAD(P)H/FAD lifetime (FLIM), mitochondrial membrane potential, cell mass (suspended microchannel resonator) and density, then track survival of those same cells. This tests whether physiological state, not just transcripts, predicts survival, and it avoids destructive profiling.

question: persister
title: Replication-stress and DNA damage history mapping
description: Combine EdU/BrdU pulse-chase, 53BP1 nuclear body imaging, and γH2AX tracking in the generation before drug exposure, then follow outcomes. This tests whether inherited damage or replication-timing differences from the previous cell cycle set up drug tolerance, which is a mechanism expression profiling would miss.

question: persister
title: Cell-cell interaction and microenvironment perturbation by micropatterning
description: Culture identical cells at controlled densities, in micropatterned islands, or in co-culture with conditioned-medium swaps, and quantify persister frequency against local neighbor density, position, and secreted factors, using spatial tracking. This separates intrinsic noise from local paracrine or contact-mediated protection that makes some cells survive.

question: persister
title: Optogenetic or inducible forcing of candidate states
description: Use CRISPRa, degron, or optogenetic control to impose a candidate state, such as a pulse of a stress-response transcription factor or temporary slowing of the cycle, in cells before drug exposure, with a dose-response of the induced level. If persister fraction rises or falls as predicted, the state is causal rather than merely correlated, and the dose-response gives the threshold for tolerance.

question: persister
title: Single-cell mitochondrial mutation lineage tracing of persister ancestry
description: Use naturally occurring mtDNA variants (scATAC/mito-enriched or MAESTER-style) as endogenous barcodes to reconstruct clonal relationships among surviving cells without engineered labels. Test whether survivors are clonally clustered beyond chance and how deep in the lineage tree shared tolerance extends, giving a memory length in divisions.

question: persister
title: Single-cell cytometry/proteomic profiling of apoptotic priming (BH3 profiling)
description: Perform dynamic BH3 profiling or single-cell mitochondrial priming measurements on untreated cells, then correlate priming with survival after sorting by priming level. This tests whether persistence is set by a pre-existing apoptotic threshold rather than by pathway reactivation.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironment-resolved persister mapping
description: Culture cells in 3D or spatially patterned conditions (micropatterns, spheroids) and use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging after drug exposure to test whether survivors localize to defined local density, hypoxia, or cell-contact niches. Perturbing density/contact (e.g., by cell-contact or secreted-factor manipulation) shows whether persistence is partly a neighborhood property rather than purely cell-intrinsic.

question: persister
title: Drug-target engagement and intracellular drug concentration at single-cell resolution
description: Measure intracellular drug levels (using fluorescent drug analogs, label-free imaging, or mass cytometry of target occupancy/phospho-readouts) and downstream pathway inhibition in individual cells shortly after dosing. This reveals whether survivors escape by receiving less effective inhibition, through efflux, sequestration (e.g., lysosomal trapping), or target-level differences, versus tolerating full inhibition.

question: persister
title: Cell-division asymmetry and partitioning of organelles/proteins
description: Track mother-daughter pairs by time-lapse imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, or aggregated proteins, and sort daughters by unequal inheritance to test whether asymmetric partitioning predicts survival. Pair with sibling-pair concordance analysis to separate inherited cytoplasmic state from chromatin-based memory.

question: persister
title: Inheritance-timescale analysis from sister-cell and cousin-cell survival correlations
description: Use time-lapse tracking of lineage trees before drug and quantify survival concordance between sisters, cousins and more distant relatives as a function of relatedness. Fitting a decay curve gives the memory half-life of the tolerant state in generations, which discriminates fast stochastic switching, epigenetic memory and genetic mutation, and tells you what timescale to look for mechanisms on.

question: persister
title: Mutation-rate and mtDNA/CNV profiling of survivors vs. matched sisters
description: Isolate surviving clones and their pre-drug sibling clones (split-clone design) and do deep whole-genome sequencing for low-frequency SNVs, extrachromosomal DNA amplifications, copy-number changes and mtDNA heteroplasmy. This tests the unglamorous hypothesis that 'identical' cells carry rare, hidden genetic or ecDNA differences, and quantifies how much of survival is explained by them.

question: persister
title: Transient mutator and DNA-damage-response state measurement in persisters
description: Combine live reporters of DNA repair factors (53BP1 foci, mismatch-repair and error-prone polymerase expression) with single-cell mutation-accumulation readouts during drug exposure. Test whether persisters transiently down-regulate high-fidelity repair, which would link tolerance to later genetic resistance and reveal a window for intervention.

question: persister
title: Single-cell proteome and translation-rate profiling of persisters
description: Measure global and specific translation (puromycin/OPP incorporation, ribosome profiling or polysome-seq on sorted cells, plus single-cell proteomics) to find survivors that differ in protein synthesis, ISR/eIF2α state or proteostasis capacity despite similar mRNA. This exposes post-transcriptional tolerance mechanisms invisible to scRNA-seq and ATAC.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironmental neighbor-effect analysis with density titration and conditioned-media swaps
description: Vary seeding density, local neighbor composition and secreted-factor exposure, and use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to ask whether survivors cluster or depend on paracrine or contact signals, such as cell-extruded metabolites, growth factors or cell-cell junction signaling. Comparing survivor frequency against local cell density tests whether 'cell-intrinsic' heterogeneity is actually positional or social.

question: persister
title: Mother-daughter inheritance of organelle and protein content via asymmetric division
description: Use time-lapse imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, or drug-efflux pumps (or a fluorescent drug analog) to quantify how unequal partitioning at division creates drug-handling differences between sister cells. Then test whether sisters with more of the inherited cargo preferentially survive, and perturb partitioning (for example, with spindle or mitochondrial-dynamics inhibitors) to see if survival changes.

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy measurement
description: Measure drug accumulation per cell using intrinsically fluorescent inhibitors, mass cytometry or imaging mass spectrometry, or a target-engagement biosensor such as a NanoBRET or CETSA-style readout. This tests whether survivors simply experience lower effective target inhibition (through efflux, lysosomal sequestration or altered metabolism) rather than having rewired downstream signaling.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment cell-state manipulation by transient perturbation followed by survival readout
description: Before adding drug, transiently shift cells with a short pulse of a candidate stressor or state modulator (such as a metabolic stress, a differentiation cue, or a chromatin inhibitor) and then wash it out. Compare survival fraction and how long the effect persists to show whether the tolerant state is causally inducible and heritable, and to estimate its memory length.

question: persister
title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D or in vivo
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on spheroids or xenografts, together with a lineage or reporter label, to test whether survivors cluster by local oxygen, nutrient, density or contact-signaling niches. Randomize the cell positions or density in matched cultures to separate cell-intrinsic from position-dependent tolerance.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic and proteostasis profiling of survivors
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, a ROS or lipid-peroxidation sensor, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes, or a proteasome or autophagy flux reporter. Image the same cells before and after drug exposure to see whether a metabolic or stress-handling state predicts survival, and use FACS sorting by that readout to validate it by orthogonal drug-response assays.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded fate mapping before drug exposure
description: Tag each cell with an expressed DNA barcode, split the population into sister cultures, and profile one by scRNA-seq before treatment while the other receives drug. Matching barcodes between pre-treatment states and survivors shows whether survival is predetermined by a heritable pre-existing state or arises stochastically after drug exposure, and it identifies the predictive signature.

question: persister
title: Live-cell tracking of dynamic reporters linked to retrospective survivor identification
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells with reporters for signaling (ERK, p53, NF-kB), cell cycle, and mitochondrial or stress state for days before drug addition. After drug treatment, trace survivors back through their histories to find dynamic features such as pulse frequency, cycle timing, or state-switching rates that predict survival better than any static snapshot.

question: persister
title: Multi-generational inheritance and decay-time measurement of the resistant state
description: Sort or isolate rare survivor-prone cells, then follow their lineages through divisions with imaging and single-cell multiomics to measure how long the state persists and how it fades. Fitting the data to stochastic state-switching models distinguishes epigenetic memory, transient noise, and slow-cycling states, and quantifies the transition rates between them.

question: persister
title: Joint single-cell chromatin, transcriptome, and mutation profiling of survivors versus matched sensitive cells
description: Apply single-cell multiome assays with targeted DNA sequencing and copy-number calling to the same cells at baseline and at several times on drug. This rules in or out rare genetic variants, extrachromosomal DNA, and mitochondrial heteroplasmy, and shows which chromatin accessibility states and regulators precede survival.

question: persister
title: Perturbation screens in the survivor state with in situ readouts of drug-target engagement
description: Run pooled CRISPR (knockout, interference, and base-editing) screens whose readout is survival fraction and single-cell state, combined with biosensors of drug-target occupancy and downstream pathway inhibition within individual cells. This tests causality, separating cells that never reach effective drug inhibition (uptake, efflux, metabolism) from those that inhibit the target yet rewire downstream, and it reveals which mechanisms can be targeted to eliminate survivors.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell tracing
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into sister aliquots before drug, then profile one aliquot by scRNA-seq/ATAC and treat the other to identify which barcodes survive. This lets you read out the pre-existing state of future survivors and test whether the state is heritable, how long it lasts, and whether it predicts survival better than genotype.

Follow up with single-cell ATAC-seq/multiome to identify the chromatin features that keep the state heritable.

question: persister
title: Seismic precursor monitoring: live-cell reporter time series before drug addition
description: Seismologists look for small signals that come before an earthquake. In the same spirit, image thousands of cells for 48–72 h before treatment using fluorescent reporters for key pathways (e.g., ERK/AKT KTR sensors, a NF-κB or AP-1 reporter), then add the drug and track which cells survive. Train a classifier on the pre-drug traces to test whether survivors show dynamic signatures beforehand, such as pulsing frequency or variance, rather than just steady-state levels.

question: persister
title: Ecological bet-hedging assay: fluctuation analysis of the primed state
description: Plants spread germination across seasons as a hedge against bad years. Borrowing that idea, run a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test: expand many single-cell-derived clones for different numbers of generations, treat them in parallel, and fit survivor-count distributions. This estimates how often cells switch into and out of the drug-tolerant state and how long that state is inherited, which separates stochastic hedging from fixed heterogeneity.

question: persister
title: Materials fatigue testing: graded drug-pulse stress protocols
description: Engineers learn how materials fail by applying cyclic, graded loads instead of a single break test. Expose cells to systematically varied drug pulse lengths, doses and recovery intervals, then measure survivor fractions alongside single-cell RNA-seq at each step. Mapping the dose-history response surface shows whether survival comes from a pre-existing state, adaptation the drug induces, or both, and where the transition happens.

question: persister
title: Epidemiological contact tracing: spatial neighbor analysis of survivors
description: Contact tracing in epidemiology finds out whether cases cluster because of shared exposures. Use high-plex spatial imaging (e.g., multiplexed smFISH or CODEX) on treated cultures and organoids to check whether survivors are enriched near particular neighbors, local densities, or secreted-factor gradients. Then test the candidate niche signals with conditioned-media and co-culture perturbations.

question: persister
title: Network percolation: CRISPR perturbation of the transition between states
description: Percolation theory looks at how removing individual nodes changes whether a whole network stays connected. Run pooled CRISPRi/a screens with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) to find regulators whose knockdown or activation shifts how often cells reach the tolerant state. Fitting a gene-regulatory network model to these results then identifies the hub factors whose shared fluctuations push a cell over the survival threshold.

question: persister
title: Black-box flight recorder: molecular history of the survivors
description: Borrowing from aviation crash investigation, where the flight recorder lets you read out the state of the plane before the event, engineer cells with a continuously writing CRISPR base-editing/prime-editing recorder coupled to promoters of candidate resistance pathways (e.g., AXL, NGFR, stress/ER programs) plus a static lineage barcode. After drug selection, sequence only the survivors and decode whether their recorders show pathway activity minutes-to-days before treatment, distinguishing pre-existing priming from post-treatment induction.

question: persister
title: Co-twin control design: split-sister transcriptomics
description: Adapt the epidemiological co-twin study, in which one twin is exposed and the genetically identical other serves as the unexposed control, by splitting each cell's immediate progeny (micromanipulation or an early-passage barcoded clone split) so that one half is drug-treated while the matched half is profiled untreated by scRNA/ATAC-seq. Correlating each twin-pair's pre-treatment molecular state with its partner's survival directly measures how much of survival is predictable from the heritable state, and for how many divisions that memory persists.

question: persister
title: Critical-slowing-down early-warning signals from live imaging
description: Use the climate/ecology tipping-point framework, where rising variance and autocorrelation in fluctuations precede a state transition, by long-term live-cell imaging of endogenous reporters (MAPK/ERK, stress, cell-cycle, mitochondrial potential) in thousands of cells before and during drug exposure. Compute per-cell fluctuation statistics (variance, autocorrelation time, dwell-time distributions) and test whether survivors are distinguished not by mean expression but by slow, large-amplitude excursions indicating proximity to an alternative stable state.

question: persister
title: Weakest-link fracture statistics to separate rare defects from stochastic nucleation
description: Apply materials-fatigue reasoning, where Weibull weakest-link statistics distinguish failure from pre-existing flaws versus random nucleation, by measuring survivor frequency as a function of population size, clone size, drug dose, and exposure duration, and fitting the resulting hazard functions. Pair this with a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test across many parallel expansions of the same clone: large between-culture variance implies heritable, early-arising 'flaws,' while Poisson-like variance implies transient, independently nucleated escape events.

question: persister
title: Microclimate refugia mapping of the physical and chemical neighborhood
description: Treat survival like species persistence in ecological refugia, where survivors mark sheltered microhabitats rather than intrinsically superior individuals, by mapping each survivor's local context at the time of treatment: local cell density and neighbor identity from imaging, intracellular drug concentration via a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging, and local oxygen/nutrient/matrix stiffness readouts. Mixed-effects modeling of survival against niche covariates versus cell-intrinsic expression quantifies how much of the 'rare survivor' phenotype is actually a rare microenvironment, testable by transplanting survivors into uniform conditions and re-challenging.

question: persister
title: Black-Box Flight Recorder: DNA-Based Molecular Logging of Pre-Treatment History
description: Borrowing from aviation accident forensics, engineer cells with CRISPR molecular recorders (DNA Typewriter, base-editing tapes) driven by stress, cell-cycle, and bypass-pathway promoters so each cell permanently writes its transcriptional history into DNA. Sequencing survivors then reads back the 'flight data' of states they occupied before and during treatment, instead of inferring cause only from the surviving wreckage.

question: persister
title: Critical Slowing Down: Early-Warning Signals from Climate Tipping-Point Theory
description: Apply the dynamical-systems signatures used to forecast ecosystem and climate regime shifts — rising variance, rising lag-1 autocorrelation, and slowed recovery from perturbation — to long-term live-cell imaging of drug-target pathway reporters before treatment. Test whether cells that later survive show these precursor signatures, using optogenetic or drug-pulse kicks to measure recovery rates directly.

question: persister
title: Weibull Reliability Analysis: Treating Cell Death as Material Fracture
description: Use extreme-value and Weibull statistics from materials fatigue engineering to fit single-cell time-to-death distributions across doses and clonal backgrounds, inferring how many independent 'flaws' (protective lesions or pathway activations) a cell needs to withstand treatment. The inferred flaw count becomes a quantitative prediction testable against measured numbers of upregulated bypass pathways in survivors.

question: persister
title: Seed-Bank Sorting: Dormancy Ecology Applied with Metabolic Labeling
