description: Following the seed-bank concept in plant and microbial ecology, non-destructively label cells by biosynthetic activity before drug exposure (BONCAT or OP-Puro for translation, heavy-water stimulated Raman for metabolic turnover) and sort dormant from active cells. Comparing survival between sorted fractions directly tests whether generic quiescence, rather than any specific resistance program, is the causal determinant.

question: persister
title: Discordant-Twin Case-Control Design from Epidemiology
description: Adapt the discordant-twin and matched case-control framework of human epidemiology by splitting sister cells at mitosis, profiling one twin by single-cell multiome while scoring the other twin's fate under drug. Extending the matching across generations of a barcoded lineage tree localizes how many divisions back the survival predisposition becomes heritable.

question: persister
title: Twin-study design for cells: barcoded sister-cell split profiling
description: Borrowing the discordant-monozygotic-twin design from epidemiology, label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, let each clone divide into sister subpopulations, then destructively profile one sister (scRNA-seq/ATAC) while drugging the other, and use the barcode to retroactively assign the pre-treatment molecular state of cells whose twins survived. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a pre-existing transcriptional/chromatin state rather than a post-hoc drug response.

question: persister
title: Foreshock detection: long-term live imaging for precursor dynamics and lead time
description: Treat rare survival like a rare earthquake and apply seismology's foreshock analysis: image cells for days before and during treatment with multiplexed live reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT kinase translocation sensors, NF-κB, stress and cell-cycle reporters), then align single-cell traces retrospectively to the survival outcome. Fitting the hazard of survival to the preceding signaling history yields both the identity of precursor signatures and the characteristic 'lead time' over which the predisposed state exists.

question: persister
title: Ensemble forecasting: measuring the memory timescale of the surviving state
description: Adapt the predictability/autocorrelation-decay analysis of weather and climate forecasting by isolating single cells, expanding them for variable numbers of generations, and re-challenging replicate subcultures with drug at each time point. The decay of correlation in survival fraction between sibling subcultures as a function of elapsed divisions quantifies how many generations the resistant state is inherited, cleanly separating transient fluctuation, epigenetic memory, and genetic mutation.

question: persister
title: Per-cell dosimetry: ruling out pharmacological escape before invoking cell state
description: Following occupational radiation safety, where every worker wears a personal dosimeter, measure the drug dose each individual cell actually receives and engages, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging of the unlabeled compound, efflux-pump reporters, and single-cell target-engagement readouts (phospho-target staining or in-cell thermal shift). This distinguishes survivors that are genuinely drug-tolerant from those that merely experienced a low effective dose because of uptake, efflux, or target abundance differences.

question: persister
title: Ice cores and tree rings: DNA-based molecular recorders that write signaling history
description: Use CRISPR base-editor or recombinase recording systems driven by pathway-responsive promoters so that each cell continuously inscribes a cumulative, timestamped proxy record of its signaling and stress history into its own genome, analogous to paleoclimate proxies in ice layers. Sequencing the recorder locus in the rare survivors after treatment recovers their multi-day history even though they were never destructively sampled, revealing whether survivors came from cells with distinctive prior pathway activity.

question: persister
title: Flight-recorder molecular memory (aviation black boxes)
description: Use a CRISPR base-editor 'recorder' that writes signaling and transcription-factor activity (AP-1, NF-kB, ERK, Wnt) into genomic barcodes during the days before drug exposure. Then sequence the recordings in survivors versus matched untreated cells to identify which pre-existing states predicted survival.

question: persister
title: Twin-study heritability of fate (human behavioral genetics)
description: Perform time-lapse imaging of full lineage trees with drug added at varied times post-division, measuring fate concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives. The decay of concordance with genealogical distance estimates how long a survival-priming state is heritable versus randomly reset.

question: persister
title: Actuarial hazard modeling of single-cell death (life-insurance statistics)
description: Image cells carrying multiple live reporters (ERK kinase translocation, caspase sensor, FUCCI cell cycle, mitochondrial potential) through treatment. Fit time-varying-covariate survival models to find which dynamic features, not snapshot levels, shift a cell's instantaneous risk of death.

question: persister
title: Early-warning signals of tipping points (ecology and climate science)
description: Test whether cells entering a drug-tolerant state show critical slowing down -- rising variance, autocorrelation, and flickering in reporter time series -- before committing. This would let you prospectively flag and sort pre-transition cells for molecular profiling.

question: persister
title: Microenvironmental neighborhood effects (urban epidemiology)
description: Treat each cell's local context as a neighborhood exposure: use spatial transcriptomics or imaging of dense cultures and organoids to test whether survival clusters spatially. Regress survival on local density, neighbor identity, and diffusible-factor gradients to separate cell-intrinsic priming from niche-conferred protection.

question: persister
title: Astronomical transient surveys → alert-triggered single-cell follow-up
description: Borrowing from sky-survey alert brokers that trigger rapid follow-up on rare transients, continuously image millions of drug-treated cells, automatically flag the rare cells still dividing or re-entering cycle, then photoconvert/photo-tag only those cells and isolate them immediately for scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteomics. This profiles the actual survivors at the moment of divergence instead of averaging them away in bulk or in post-hoc resistant lines.

question: persister
title: Control engineering Bode plots → drug delivered as a frequency sweep
description: As in system identification, drive the system with oscillating inputs across many frequencies: use microfluidics to deliver the targeted inhibitor as sinusoidal concentration waveforms with periods from minutes to days while recording pathway-activity reporters. Test whether pre-persister cells are defined by a distinct transfer function (slower, more damped signaling response) rather than by a static difference in baseline expression.

question: persister
title: Metallurgical fatigue testing → extreme-value statistics of survival
description: Materials scientists separate pre-existing-flaw failure from accumulated-damage failure using single-overload versus cyclic loading and Weibull/extreme-value fits. Deliver matched total drug exposure as one continuous dose versus many intermittent pulses across thousands of replicate wells, then fit the survivor-fraction distributions to ask whether survival follows a weakest-link model (rare pre-existing states) or a damage-accumulation model (tolerance built during treatment).

question: persister
title: Dendrochronology / isotope geochemistry → reading each survivor's recorded history
description: Like tree rings or ice cores storing a dated chemical record, apply sequential metabolic time-stamps before and during treatment (distinguishable 4sU/5-EU RNA pulses plus SILAC heavy-amino-acid pulses) so every cell carries layered, time-ordered evidence of its transcription and translation rates. Read these layers out in single surviving cells to reconstruct whether they were already slow-cycling or translationally quiet long before the drug was added.

question: persister
title: Dynamical systems "critical slowing down" → early-warning signals of fate commitment
description: Ecosystems and climate systems show rising variance, autocorrelation, and recovery time before a regime shift. Record long high-frequency single-cell reporter traces through treatment and compute rolling variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, and relaxation time after small optogenetic or washout perturbations, testing whether future persisters display these slowing-down signatures hours before they visibly diverge from dying neighbors.

question: persister
title: Flight-recorder lineage tracing (aviation black boxes)
description: Black boxes record a flight continuously so investigators can work out the cause after a crash. In the same way, give cells heritable barcodes and split each clone into twin populations before treatment: drug one half, and profile the untreated twin with single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq to read out the pre-drug state of the lineages that went on to survive. This shows whether survivors were already distinct before the drug was added, and which genes and chromatin features marked them.

question: persister
title: Precursor signals before survival (earthquake forecasting)
description: Seismologists look for patterns in small tremors that come before large earthquakes. Here, image live-cell reporters (for example ERK, AKT and p53 activity sensors, plus a cell-cycle reporter) for 48–72 hours before and during drug exposure. Then fit survival-analysis models to ask which features of each cell's signaling history best predict whether it lives or dies, such as how often it pulses, its baseline level, or its cycle phase.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell 'twin study' to split heritable from random effects (twin studies in epidemiology)
description: Epidemiologists compare identical and fraternal twins to separate inherited effects from chance. Similarly, track lineages by time-lapse microscopy and measure how often sister cells, cousins, and unrelated cells share the same outcome after drug treatment. Fitting these correlations to a branching model tells you how much of survival comes from a state passed down through divisions and how long that state lasts.

question: persister
title: Mark–recapture to measure state-switching rates (wildlife ecology)
description: Ecologists tag animals, release them and recapture them later to estimate population sizes and movement rates. Here, use FACS to sort cells that are high or low for a candidate persister marker (such as AXL, EGFR or NGFR), label each group with a different fluorescent dye or barcode, mix them back together, and then sample at several time points to measure how fast cells switch between states. Drug-challenging the samples at each time point then shows how survival potential decays as cells move between states.

question: persister
title: Stress-testing the survivor state (bank stress tests in finance)
description: Regulators test banks against simulated shocks to find weak points. Analogously, run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) at low drug doses, and score each gene by how much it raises or lowers the fraction of surviving cells, not just whether cells grow. This separates the genes that create the rare pre-resistant state from those that only help survival after the drug is added.

question: persister
title: Metal fatigue testing: hysteresis of the resistant state
description: Borrowing cyclic load-testing from materials science, expose cells to repeated pulses of drug with varying washout intervals and track single-clone phenotypes, measuring whether the surviving state relaxes back (elastic) or latches permanently (plastic deformation). Mapping the hysteresis loop — how long drug exposure must last and how long memory persists after removal — distinguishes transient transcriptional priming from heritable epigenetic or genetic fixation, and pinpoints the dosing interval that prevents the state from latching.

question: persister
title: Seed-bank ecology: quantifying dormancy depth as a bet-hedging trait
description: Treat survivors like a plant seed bank with staggered germination, and use long-term live imaging plus quiescence-depth reporters (CDK2 activity, p21, DNA-labeling dilution) to measure the full distribution of dormancy depths and re-entry times before and during treatment. Fitting classic bet-hedging models to the observed switching rates tests whether survival is an evolved stochastic dormancy strategy rather than a drug-induced response, and predicts the optimal drug-holiday timing to catch germinating cells.

question: persister
title: Transition-path theory: committor probabilities for candidate priming markers
description: Adapting rare-event analysis from statistical physics, build live reporters for candidate pre-resistance markers, FACS-sort untreated cells into narrow bins spanning the full expression range, and measure the fraction of each bin that survives drug — the empirical committor function. A marker whose committor rises sharply and monotonically is on the true reaction coordinate of survival; markers that merely correlate with survivors show flat or noisy committors, cleanly separating causal priming from bystander correlation.

question: persister
title: Water-utility leak auditing: per-cell drug accounting before blaming signaling
description: Before attributing survival to signaling states, audit the drug itself the way a utility meters flow to find leaks: use a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, intracellular mass-spectrometry imaging, and efflux-pump reporters to measure the actual single-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy (e.g., by a target-engagement FRET or thermal-shift reporter) in survivors versus dying neighbors. This tests whether the surviving fraction is a pharmacokinetic phenomenon — uptake, efflux, or sequestration heterogeneity — rather than a cell-state phenomenon.

question: persister
title: Actuarial survival modeling with time-varying covariates
description: Apply the insurance industry's hazard-modeling framework to single cells: from continuous imaging of thousands of cells during treatment, fit a Cox proportional-hazards model where each cell's time-to-death is regressed on time-varying covariates (reporter intensities, cell size, cell-cycle phase, local density, mitotic history) measured hours earlier. The resulting hazard ratios quantify how much each measurable feature actually changes the instantaneous risk of death, and deviations from proportional hazards reveal whether survivors are a distinct 'cured' subpopulation or just the tail of one continuous risk distribution.

question: persister
title: Retrospective state mapping of survivors via lineage barcoding (EBSD analog)
description: Tag every cell with a heritable barcode, split the population so one half is profiled by single-cell RNA-seq or multiplexed imaging before drug exposure while the sister half is treated, then match survivor barcodes back to their untreated siblings' profiles. This is the direct analog of mapping each specimen's grain structure before cycling and asking which microstructural signatures the survivors carried in advance.

question: persister
title: In situ live imaging of the drug-response trajectory with signaling reporters
description: Follow thousands of single cells by continuous time-lapse through treatment using reporters for pathway reactivation (ERK/AKT kinase translocation), cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptotic commitment, so the exact frame at which a future survivor diverges from its dying neighbors is recorded rather than inferred. This mirrors in situ synchrotron imaging and digital image correlation, which catch crack initiation as it happens instead of reconstructing it from the fracture surface.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation and mixture-model analysis of survival scatter across replicate clones
description: Expand many independent single-cell-derived clones, treat them identically, and analyze the variance in survivor counts and the shape of time-to-death distributions with Luria-Delbruck fluctuation statistics and Weibull or multi-component mixture fits. Just as Weibull analysis separates a built-in defect population from random variation in fatigue life, inflated between-clone variance or a distinct long-lived component indicates a heritable pre-existing subpopulation rather than moment-to-moment chance.

question: persister
title: Whole-cell structural scanning for rare 'inclusion-like' features
description: Apply high-content 3D imaging, imaging flow cytometry, and DNA FISH alongside single-cell DNA sequencing to score every cell for discrete structural features: extrachromosomal DNA copy number, micronuclei, ploidy, mitochondrial mass, and position within a colony, then test enrichment of each feature in survivors. This is the X-ray CT step, cataloguing pores and inclusions so one can ask whether survivors simply lacked or possessed a particular hot-spot feature.

question: persister
title: Staircase dose titration to measure a per-lineage tolerance threshold
description: Run a staircase design in which barcoded lineages are exposed to stepped drug concentrations and durations, estimating a survival threshold for each lineage, then re-derive clones from survivors and repeat to see whether the threshold is heritable and how fast it relaxes. This transfers staircase fatigue testing and endurance-limit estimation, converting a binary live/die readout into a distribution of per-unit tolerance limits whose stability over generations distinguishes stable resistance from transient tolerance.

question: persister
title: Split-sister concordance assay (linear mode connectivity analog)
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into replicate flasks at defined numbers of generations before treatment, then treat all replicates and measure the overlap of surviving barcodes across splits. Concordance as a function of split-to-treatment interval gives a quantitative 'memory half-life' for the primed state, separating heritable priming present at the split from fluctuations arising afterward — the biological counterpart of testing whether two runs from the same checkpoint land in the same basin.

question: persister
title: Rewinding survivors to their pre-treatment checkpoint
description: Use expressed, sequenceable lineage barcodes so that the barcodes of drug survivors can be read out and then traced back into a sibling aliquot of the same population that was profiled (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or barcode-targeted imaging) before any drug exposure. This retrospectively isolates the molecular state of the future survivors at the 'initialization checkpoint' rather than comparing survivors to the bulk population after selection has already distorted it.

question: persister
title: Iterative selection with lineage rewinding (IMP analog)
description: Run repeated cycles of drug kill, drug withdrawal, and re-expansion, tracking at each round whether the same barcodes survive (a fixed ticket) or a freshly drawn set does (a resampled ticket), and in parallel re-expand frozen early-passage aliquots of the same clone to test whether the winning potential was already fixed at that earlier point. Comparing 'same-ticket' recurrence against reset-by-rewinding mirrors iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding.

question: persister
title: Factorial dissection of the noise sources that generate survivors
description: Separately and combinatorially perturb each candidate source of cell-to-cell variability — chromatin-encoded memory (EZH2/DNMT/HDAC inhibition), cell-cycle phase at exposure (synchronization or live reporters), division history and local density, and drug-exposure variability (fluorescent drug analog uptake) — and score how each changes both the survivor fraction and the split-sister barcode concordance. This is the direct analog of ablating initialization versus data order versus dropout to find which randomness actually determines success.

question: persister
title: Prospective sorting test of the pre-treatment state
description: Train a classifier on the rewind data to predict survival from the untreated single-cell state, convert the top features into a live-cell readout (knock-in reporter, surface marker, or live RNA stain), then sort untreated cells on that readout and measure the fold-enrichment in survivor frequency after treatment. A large prospective enrichment establishes that the ticket is present at initialization, while a null result localizes fate determination to events during drug exposure.

question: persister
title: Clonal-twin split: reading the telemetry snapshot from just before the fault
description: Because profiling a cell destroys it, use lineage barcoding plus a sibling-split design (e.g., Rewind/FateMap-style): expand single-cell-derived clones, then split each clone so one half is profiled untreated by scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq while the matched half receives drug, letting you retrospectively assign the pre-treatment molecular state of lineages that survived versus those that died — the direct analog of comparing pre-fault telemetry in survivor and casualty replicas.

question: persister
title: Live-cell 'distributed tracing' with per-cell survival regression
description: Image cells for days before and during drug exposure while recording a multiplexed panel of fluorescent reporters (ERK/AKT activity, cell-cycle CDK2 sensor, mitochondrial membrane potential, ATF4/stress response, autophagy flux), then fit a time-varying Cox proportional-hazards model on the single-cell traces to identify which transient states, and in which time window relative to dosing, predict survival — the analog of tracing spans plus survival analysis over replica time series.

question: persister
title: Fault-injection matrix: is persistence state-specific or fault-specific?
description: Systematically vary the injected 'fault' — drug class (kinase inhibitor vs. chemotherapy vs. nutrient withdrawal), intensity, and schedule (step, ramp, pulse, repeated short bursts) — on barcoded replicate populations, and test by barcode overlap whether the same lineages survive every insult (a general robust state) or different lineages survive different insults (mechanism-matched states), mirroring chaos experiments that inject distinct fault types to localize the failure mode.

question: persister
title: Resource-reserve and local-load measurements (cache warmth, pool size, queue depth)
description: Quantify the cell-intrinsic 'resource state' at the moment of dosing — actual intracellular drug concentration via a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spec imaging, plus efflux-pump activity, lysosomal sequestration, NADPH/GSH redox buffer, ATP, and ribosome/translation capacity — alongside the cell's 'load context' (local cell density, neighbor identity, mechanical confinement) measured by spatial imaging, to separate survivors that never received the dose from survivors that absorbed it.

question: persister
title: Staging-environment replay: force the candidate state and re-run the incident
description: Take the top state inferred from the twin and tracing experiments and install it deliberately — CRISPRa/optogenetic or small-molecule induction of the marker gene program in a tunable fraction of cells, or FACS pre-sorting on a live reporter of that state — then test whether the surviving fraction rises proportionally and whether blocking the state collapses it, converting a correlational post-mortem into a reproducible, causal re-enactment of the failure.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell split design as a pre-shock administrative panel
description: Exploit the fact that a cell division produces two near-identical 'twins': profile one daughter destructively (scRNA-seq, proteomics, or a reporter snapshot) while its sister is exposed to the targeted drug and followed to a survival/death outcome, so the pre-shock covariate vector is measured on the same genetic and epigenetic unit whose fate is observed. This is the cancer-cell analogue of linking a firm's pre-shock census record to its post-shock exit status, and it cleanly separates predetermined advantage from post-treatment adaptation.

question: persister
title: Event study with pre-trend testing on continuous single-cell trajectories
description: Use long-term live imaging with multiplexed signaling and stress reporters to build per-cell time series spanning days before drug addition through weeks after, then align all cells on the treatment date and estimate the survivor-versus-dier difference at each lead and lag. Significant differences at negative leads identify genuinely preexisting heterogeneity, while a flat pre-period with divergence only after exposure would show that survivorship is generated by the shock itself, and the pre-trend test guards against the parallel-trends violation that naive survivor-versus-dier comparisons ignore.

question: persister
title: Matching survivors to dead peers on pre-treatment observables, then quantifying the unexplained residual
description: With barcoded clonal families profiled before treatment, construct nearest-neighbor or propensity-score matched pairs of future survivors and future dying cells balanced on cell-cycle phase, size, target-pathway activity, mitochondrial content, and local density, and test how much survival probability remains unexplained after balancing. The size and structure of that residual is itself the scientific result: it bounds how much of persistence is attributable to measured states versus unobserved or purely stochastic factors, exactly as economists bound selection on unobservables after matching on productivity and liquidity.

question: persister
title: Regression discontinuity around a tunable target-dosage cutoff
description: Use a degron- or inducible-promoter-titrated level of the drug target (or of a candidate resistance mediator) as a continuous running variable, with a sharp kill threshold, and compare cells falling just above versus just below the cutoff where assignment is effectively as-good-as-random. This isolates the causal contribution of that one variable to survival, separating it from the many correlated states that confound a simple association between high expression and persistence.

question: persister
title: Difference-in-differences across drug holiday and rechallenge to test whether the advantage is heritable or an adaptive pivot
description: Split each barcoded clone into treated and vehicle arms, then release survivors into drug-free medium, re-split, and rechallenge, estimating within-clone changes in survival relative to the never-treated arm of the same clone. A persistent within-clone shift indicates an inherited or epigenetically stabilized advantage, while reversion to baseline indicates a transient post-shock adaptive response — the direct analogue of distinguishing durable firm productivity from post-tariff product switching.

question: persister
title: Constant-dose kill-kinetics analysis (isothermal hold analog)
description: Hold cell populations at a fixed drug concentration and measure the death rate over time using live-cell imaging. A single-exponential decay points to a uniform stochastic hazard, while a biphasic curve with a plateau points to a pre-existing subpopulation with a lower hazard.

question: persister
title: Luria–Delbrück fluctuation test across many small subclones
description: Expand many independent subclones, each started from a few cells, for different numbers of generations, then treat them in parallel and compare how much the survivor counts vary from clone to clone. Variance near Poisson suggests drug-induced or random survival. Very high variance suggests pre-existing survivor states, and how it changes with expansion time gives the rate at which cells switch into and out of that state.

question: persister
title: Dose-ramp survival spectrum (freezing-spectrum analog)
description: Measure the fraction of cells surviving across a fine range of drug concentrations and convert it into a cumulative density of resistance-conferring states per cell, similar to how ice-nucleation work builds an active-site spectrum. Compare these spectra between cell lines and growth conditions to test whether a fixed, quantifiable cellular feature sets the tail.

question: persister
title: Retrospective lineage barcoding to identify the 'nucleating particle'
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the population, treat one half, and use single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing on the untreated twin half to profile the pre-treatment state of the lineages that later survived. This works like electron microscopy finding the particle responsible for freezing: it identifies the specific molecular feature linked to survival.

question: persister
title: Remove the putative site and re-test (site-deactivation control)
description: Use FACS to deplete, or CRISPR to knock down, the candidate marker found in idea 4 (for example, high expression of a drug-efflux or stress-response gene) before treatment, then check whether the low-survival tail disappears or comes back. This is like heat-treating samples to destroy nucleating sites, and it tests whether the feature actually causes survival.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment state profiling that predicts survival
description: Mirroring the battery practice of extracting early-life features that forecast lifetime, image barcoded clonal cancer cells with live reporters (signaling kinase translocation reporters, cell-cycle FUCCI, mitochondrial membrane potential, size) for 24-48 hours before drug addition, then track each cell's fate. Train an interpretable model to test which pre-treatment features, especially their variance and temporal dynamics rather than their means, predict which rare cells survive.

question: persister
title: Variance-of-difference analysis across re-challenge cycles
description: Adapting the delta-Q(V) variance feature, expose cells to repeated drug pulse and washout cycles and record single-cell response curves (viability, apoptotic reporter, growth rate) each cycle. Compute the cell-to-cell variance of the difference between early and later cycle curves, testing whether this spread predicts the surviving fraction far better than any population-average metric.

question: persister
title: Retrospective teardown by paired live imaging and in situ sequencing
description: Analogous to disassembling cells after cycling for CT and diffraction, perform live imaging through treatment to identify survivors, then fix the same plate and run single-molecule FISH or in situ transcriptomics on the imaged coordinates. This links each survivor's measured pre-drug behavior to its actual molecular state, closing the gap between predictive feature and mechanism.

question: persister
title: Clonal barcode replicate testing for reproducible versus stochastic survival
description: Like testing many cells from one production lot, split a highly barcoded population into parallel replicate cultures before treatment and ask whether the same barcodes survive in all replicates. Reproducible barcodes indicate heritable, stably primed states, while replicate-specific survivors indicate transient fluctuations, directly partitioning the variance that any predictive model must explain.

question: persister
title: Non-destructive impedance-like perturbation spectroscopy
description: In place of impedance spectra that probe a cell without damaging it, apply brief sub-lethal probes such as low-dose drug pulses, nutrient or oxidative stress, or optogenetic pathway stimulation at several frequencies, and read out the single-cell response amplitude and recovery kinetics. Test whether this response spectrum, measured before full treatment, is a non-destructive signature of the drug-tolerant state.

question: persister
title: Barcoded 'multiple worlds' replication of drug selection
description: Label an isogenic cell line with a high-complexity lentiviral barcode library, then split the identically barcoded population into many independent replicate flasks ('worlds') that each receive the same targeted drug, and deep-sequence the surviving barcodes in each. The cross-world reproducibility of which barcodes dominate — quantified as an intraclass correlation or rank overlap against a neutral-drift null — directly partitions survival into heritable intrinsic priming versus path-dependent chance.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell split design to measure fate predictability from pre-drug state
description: Use live imaging or microraft arrays to track single cells through a division, then send one daughter into drug and the other into single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq or a clonal expansion. Concordance between a sibling's molecular state and its twin's survival outcome gives a direct, lineage-matched estimate of how much of survival is written in the cell's prior state rather than generated during treatment.

question: persister
title: Retrospective capture of the rare founders before treatment ever happens
description: Apply a Rewind-style approach: use RNA FISH or barcode-guided sorting to pull out the specific cells that are destined to survive (identified by barcodes recovered from a replicate 'world' already treated), and profile those exact founders in the untreated state. This is the cancer-cell analogue of knowing which song wins and then going back to the pre-release recording to ask what, if anything, distinguished it.

question: persister
title: Cascade tracking by continuous time-lapse from before drug to outgrowth
description: Image the whole population continuously with signaling and stress-state reporters from several days before dosing through the emergence of resistant colonies, reconstructing full pedigrees with time stamps. This yields the diffusion-style record needed to identify which early fluctuations — a transient expression spike, an unusually long cell-cycle arrest, a particular neighborhood — actually preceded later dominance, versus which were common and inconsequential.

question: persister
title: Switching social feedback on and off across worlds
description: Run matched replicate worlds that differ only in whether cell–cell feedback can operate: dense monolayers versus single cells isolated in nanowells versus conditioned-media transfer, all at identical drug exposure. Comparing the inequality of clone success (Gini coefficient) and cross-world reproducibility across these conditions tests whether paracrine and spatial feedback acts as a rich-get-richer amplifier that converts small initial differences into large survival differences.

question: persister
title: Longitudinal single-cell time series of the pre-resistant state
description: Mirroring repeated T1/T2 monitoring of each qubit, use long-term live-cell imaging with lineage tracking and signaling or drug-target reporters (e.g., kinase activity, receptor tyrosine kinase, or stress-pathway reporters) for days before treatment, then add drug and ask whether survivors occupied a distinguishable reporter state and for how long. Autocorrelation and state-dwell-time analysis of each lineage reveals whether tolerance is a stable per-cell property or a transient fluctuation that cells drift in and out of.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell split-and-retreat assay for heritability and 'reset'
description: Analogous to thermal cycling to test whether a defect is built-in or transient, barcode cells and split each expanded clone into parallel arms: treat one arm now, culture the other drug-free for varying numbers of generations before treating. If survival frequency stays clone-specific, the trait is heritable/built-in; if it decays with a characteristic relaxation time, it is a fluctuating state, and the decay constant quantifies its memory.

question: persister
title: Tuning the 'resonance' with graded drug dose and pathway perturbation
description: Just as strain or electric fields tune a two-level system in and out of resonance with a qubit, sweep drug concentration, target-pathway modulators, and microenvironmental variables (growth factors, density, nutrient levels) while scoring survivor frequency. A survivor fraction that shifts smoothly with these knobs identifies which continuous cell-state variable sets the tolerance threshold, rather than merely cataloguing survivor markers.

question: persister
title: Retrospective molecular profiling of cells destined to survive
description: Equivalent to imaging a junction after the fact to find the flaw responsible, use methods that let you go back to the specific pre-treatment cells that later survived (e.g., Rewind-style barcode or FISH-based tagging of rare high-expressors, followed by isolation and RNA/ATAC/protein profiling of those exact cells). This separates the causal priming state from the downstream transcriptional program induced by the drug.

question: persister
title: Frequency-domain decomposition of fluctuation versus genetics
description: Borrowing the frequency-sweep logic that separates fixed material defects from drifting ones, apply high-depth clonal barcoding plus whole-genome/targeted sequencing of survivors to test whether survivors are a reproducible set of clones (genetic, fixed) or a different, non-overlapping set on each independent replicate of the same population (stochastic, fluctuating). Quantifying barcode overlap across replicates and the power spectrum of expression fluctuations in the implicated genes assigns each candidate mechanism to a stable or transient origin.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell concordance decay curve
description: Use microfluidic traps to catch mitotic sister pairs. Separate them and add drug at a range of delays after division (0 to more than 10 generations' worth), then measure how often both sisters survive or both die. How fast that concordance falls off gives the memory time of the survival-competent state. It also shows whether the state is inherited at birth or decided stochastically after division.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug uptake and target-occupancy imaging
description: Use isotope-labeled drug with NanoSIMS or MALDI imaging mass spec, or a FRET/fluorescent probe of target occupancy, to measure the intracellular drug concentration and how much of the target is inhibited in each cell. Then tie these readings to whether that cell survives. This tests a simple pharmacological explanation: survivors may just be under-dosed or have incomplete target engagement, rather than being in a different signaling or transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Change gene-expression noise without changing the mean, then measure survival
description: For candidate genes, build promoter or 5'UTR variants (e.g., changes to TATA-box or burst size) that keep average expression fixed but raise or lower cell-to-cell variability. Then test whether the surviving fraction changes. This gives a causal test that variability itself, not the average expression level, produces the rare surviving cells.

question: persister
title: Biophysical fate prediction with buoyant mass and growth rate
description: Measure single-cell buoyant mass, density and mass-accumulation rate with suspended microchannel resonators before adding drug. Then follow each cell through treatment in the same device. This tests whether physical traits that sequencing-based methods don't capture, such as cell size, density or biosynthetic rate, predict which cells survive.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric organelle partitioning at the last mitosis
description: Image photoactivatable or age-tagged (e.g., MitoTimer, SNAP-tag pulse-chase) mitochondria, lysosomes and protein aggregates through the last cell division before drug. Measure how unevenly each daughter inherits them and whether that predicts which daughter survives. This tests whether random, non-transcriptional inheritance of cellular contents seeds the rare surviving cells.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug exposure and target-engagement mapping
description: Measure how much drug each cell actually takes in and how strongly the target is hit, using fluorescent or isotope-labeled drug analogs (with NanoSIMS or stimulated Raman imaging) together with FRET target-activity biosensors, then link these values to which cells survive. This tests whether survivors are cells that are biologically primed or simply cells that get less effective drug because of uneven uptake, efflux or target occupancy.

question: persister
title: Unequal segregation of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) as hidden variability
description: Use ecDNA FISH or live-imaged ecDNA tagged with TetO/TetR to count, cell by cell, the copies of ecDNA carrying oncogenes or drug-target genes before treatment, and relate copy number to survival. Because ecDNA splits randomly at cell division, 'genetically identical' populations can still differ widely in gene dosage, and this is rarely measured in persister studies.

question: persister
title: Tuning noise while holding the mean fixed with synthetic circuits
description: Put a candidate resistance driver (e.g., a transcription factor or receptor) under a synthetic circuit that changes cell-to-cell variability without changing average expression, using negative-feedback or noise-tuner constructs. Then measure whether the surviving fraction tracks variance or mean. This directly tests whether expression fluctuations themselves, rather than a specific state, cause survival.

question: persister
title: Testing cell-autonomy by density and microwell titration
description: Plate cells over a wide range of densities and as isolated single cells in microwell arrays, with or without shared medium, and measure the surviving fraction and its Poisson statistics. Departures from density-independent, per-cell survival would show that survival depends on local community effects (paracrine rescue, nutrient sharing, contact) rather than intrinsic cell states.

question: persister
title: Tracking asymmetric inheritance of old or damaged cellular components
description: Use pulse-chase tags (SNAP/Halo-tag protein-age labeling, photoconvertible mito-Dendra2) to follow, over generations, how protein aggregates, aged proteome and mitochondria are split between daughter cells. Then test whether daughters that inherit 'younger' or 'older' material are more likely to persist, revealing a deterministic, division-linked source of survival differences.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug uptake and target engagement imaging
description: Use fluorescent or deuterium/alkyne-tagged drug analogs (imaged by stimulated Raman scattering or click chemistry), plus a FRET target-occupancy sensor, to measure how much drug and target inhibition each cell gets before its fate is known. This tests whether survivors simply got less drug or less target inhibition, as opposed to having a different downstream state.

question: persister
title: Synthetic noise-tuning of candidate genes at a fixed mean
description: Put a candidate survival gene under a synthetic circuit (for example, a negative-feedback or bursty promoter series) that changes cell-to-cell variance while keeping mean expression the same. Then measure how the survivor fraction changes. This shows whether variability itself, and not the average level, sets the rare surviving fraction.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric organelle inheritance tracking
description: Use photoconvertible or timer reporters (MitoTimer, old vs. new centrosome markers, protein-aggregate markers) to follow how mitochondria, aggregates and centrosomes split at division, and track daughter fates under drug. This tests whether survival depends on inheriting particular organelle ages or amounts, not on transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Label-free biophysical prestate profiling
description: Image cells for several generations before treatment with quantitative phase imaging and Brillouin microscopy to record dry mass, growth rate, volume and stiffness. Then add the drug and link fate back to each cell. This could reveal physical predictors of survival, such as density or growth-rate thresholds, that sequencing would miss.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned control of neighbor and geometry context
description: Plate single cells or small groups on micropatterned islands with set area, shape and neighbor number, and then treat them. This measures how much of the survivor fraction comes from local cell-intrinsic state and how much from contact, spreading or crowding. Spatial point-pattern analysis of survivor positions in normal dishes would be used to cross-check the results.

question: persister
title: Single-cell pharmacology: intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy as the hidden variable
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug levels using a fluorescent drug analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging of the compound, or a drug-displaceable target-binding biosensor, and correlate each cell's measured exposure with its subsequent fate by tracked imaging. This directly tests whether survival reflects pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (uptake, efflux, lysosomal sequestration, target abundance) rather than any transcriptional program, a confound that most state-centric studies never measure.

question: persister
title: Measuring the memory timescale of the primed state by delayed-treatment sister assays
description: Isolate pairs of sister and cousin cells (micropatterns, microfluidic traps, or single-cell cloning), then treat them after systematically varied delays of 0 to many generations, scoring concordance of survival as a function of relatedness and elapsed divisions. The decay curve of fate concordance yields a quantitative half-life for the heritable determinant, which distinguishes short-lived signaling fluctuations, multi-generation epigenetic memory, and permanent genetic differences without assuming what the determinant is.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming measured before treatment and linked to the same cell's fate
description: Apply BH3 peptides to individually tracked live cells with a mitochondrial outer-membrane potential or cytochrome-c reporter to score each cell's proximity to the apoptotic threshold, then release and challenge the sister cell with drug. This asks whether survival is set by the death machinery's set point (BCL-2 family stoichiometry) rather than by upstream oncogenic signaling, and identifies whether persisters are cells that simply cannot execute apoptosis quickly enough.

question: persister
title: Mitotic partitioning errors as the origin of fate asymmetry
description: Use live imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, aggresomes, and a dilutable protein marker to quantify how unequally cytoplasmic contents are divided at each mitosis, then follow both daughters through drug treatment. If survivors are systematically the daughters that inherited an excess of mitochondria, lysosomes (drug sinks), or damaged-protein aggregates, the root cause is stochastic cell-division mechanics rather than regulated state switching.

question: persister
title: mRNA-protein discordance mapping to locate the layer at which heterogeneity acts
description: Combine single-cell proteomics or high-plex antibody imaging with matched single-cell transcriptomes on the same cells (e.g., antibody-plus-RNA co-detection) for the drug target and its pathway, and test which layer predicts survival in a subsequent fate-tracked round. Finding that protein-level variability predicts fate while transcript level does not would redirect the field from transcriptional-state models toward translational and degradation control as the source of persistence.

question: persister
title: Tune noise in a candidate gene while keeping its mean fixed
description: Use synthetic gene circuits (for example, negative-feedback versus open-loop designs, or promoter variants with different burst kinetics) to change cell-to-cell variability in a candidate survival gene without changing its average level, then measure the survivor fraction. If survival scales with variance rather than mean expression, this is causal evidence that rare high-expressing tail cells, not the bulk level, explain survival.

question: persister
title: Measure drug uptake and target engagement in single cells
description: Pair fluorescent or clickable analogs of the inhibitor (or single-cell mass spectrometry) with a live readout of target pathway activity, such as an ERK kinase translocation reporter, in the same cells. This tells you whether survivors are cells where the drug never fully reached or inhibited its target (efflux, uptake, or target-level differences) or cells that were fully inhibited and survived anyway.

question: persister
title: Track unequal inheritance of organelles and proteins between sister cells
description: Use photoconvertible labels on mitochondria, lysosomes, or aggregated proteins to follow how these are split between sister cells at the divisions just before drug is added. Then test whether the sister that got more (or less) predicts which one survives. This separates a deterministic cell-division effect from heritable transcriptional priming.

question: persister
title: Control local neighborhood with micropatterning
description: Plate single cells or small groups on micropatterned islands with set neighbor number, spacing, and island geometry. Also mix barcoded cells with unlabeled carriers at different densities. This tests whether the chance of surviving depends on contact, local paracrine signaling, or mechanical context rather than on anything intrinsic to the cell.

question: persister
title: Optogenetically induce candidate states at set times to find when they matter
description: Optogenetically or chemically switch on candidate drivers (for example, AP-1 factors or receptor tyrosine kinases) in random subsets of cells for short pulses at different times before and after drug is added, then measure the survivor fraction. This maps the time window during which a transient state is enough to confer survival, and shows how long that state's protective effect lasts.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug uptake and target occupancy imaging
description: Use a fluorescent or click-chemistry-tagged analog of the targeted drug, together with a target-engagement readout such as a phospho-substrate biosensor, to measure how much drug each cell takes up and how fully its target is inhibited during live imaging. Then check whether survivors simply received less drug or had less target inhibition, for example because of efflux pumps or lysosomal trapping, rather than having a different transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned control of local geometry and density
description: Plate cells on micropatterned islands of defined size, shape, and neighbor number. Map survival against position (edge vs. center), local crowding, and YAP localization to test whether rare survival comes from microenvironment and mechanics within the dish rather than from an internal cell state.

question: persister
title: Buoyant mass and growth-rate profiling before treatment
description: Use suspended microchannel resonators, or quantitative phase imaging, to measure each cell's mass and mass-accumulation rate before adding drug, then track which cells survive. This tests whether biophysical traits such as cell size, protein dilution, or growth rate predict survival independently of gene expression.

question: persister
title: Tracking asymmetric partitioning at division
description: Pulse-label mitochondria, aggregated proteins, or the drug target using photoconvertible or SNAP-tag chemistry. Follow how these components are split between daughter cells in the divisions before treatment, and test whether daughters that inherit an unequal share are the ones that later survive the drug.

question: persister
title: Mitochondrial apoptotic priming in sister clones
description: Expand barcoded clones, split each into two halves, and run single-cell dynamic BH3 profiling on one half while giving the drug to the other. This links each clone's distance from the apoptotic threshold (how close it is to triggering cell death) to its survival, testing whether persisters are defined by how they handle death signals rather than by how they respond to the drug's signaling effect.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell split with divergent challenges: is the surviving state drug-specific or generic?
description: Image and micromanipulate individual mitotic pairs (or use barcoded clones split across many wells) so that one daughter/sibling receives the targeted drug and the other receives an unrelated stressor (different-target inhibitor, chemotherapy, nutrient starvation, heat, immune attack). Concordance of survival across arms quantifies how much of the rare-survivor phenotype is a generic stress-tolerant state versus a drug-pathway-specific one, and defines the dimensionality of the predisposing state space.

question: persister
title: Noise engineering: hold the mean, vary the variance of candidate determinants
description: Build isogenic lines in which a candidate resistance effector (e.g., an RTK, efflux pump, or anti-apoptotic protein) is expressed from synthetic promoter/UTR variants that are matched in mean abundance but differ several-fold in cell-to-cell CV and in state memory (autocorrelation time), using a knock-in of the endogenous locus plus degron tuning. Measuring survival fraction as a function of CV alone provides a causal test that expression variability per se, not average expression, sets the size of the surviving subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Allele-resolved nascent transcription to separate cis bursting from trans cell-state
description: Use allele-specific single-molecule RNA FISH or MS2/PP7 live imaging at both alleles of candidate resistance genes, combined with downstream fixation of the same cells after drug treatment. If the two alleles fluctuate independently in survivors, the rare state arises from stochastic transcriptional bursting at a single locus; if they covary, the cause is an upstream trans-acting cell state, and the measured burst/state autocorrelation time directly predicts how long a cell stays 'primed'.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric organelle and damaged-protein inheritance at the last division before treatment
description: Pulse-label mitochondria, lysosomes, and long-lived/oxidatively damaged proteins with photoconvertible or SNAP/Halo pulse-chase tags, then time-lapse image divisions immediately preceding drug addition and score which daughter survives. This quantifies whether survival is set by an inherently noisy partitioning event at cytokinesis (mitochondrial mass/membrane potential, lysosomal drug sequestration capacity, proteostasis load) rather than by a transcriptional program.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-controlled survival: micropatterned arrays plus optogenetic neighbor ablation
description: Seed cells on micropatterned islands or in microwells with defined, imaged local density, neighbor identity, and ECM contact, then treat and map survival against each spatial variable; follow up by optogenetically or laser-ablating specific neighbors, and by conditioned-medium and transwell swaps, to test causality. This distinguishes cell-intrinsic priming from non-cell-autonomous rescue via paracrine factors, local drug depletion, or contact-mediated signaling, which standard dissociated single-cell assays cannot separate.

question: persister
title: Measure how much drug actually hits its target in each cell
description: Before and during treatment, measure in each cell how much drug is bound to its target, using a NanoBRET or FRET target-engagement reporter or a fluorescent drug analog. Then check whether survivors started out with lower intracellular drug occupancy (from efflux, uptake or target abundance) or whether they were fully inhibited and survived through downstream rewiring.

question: persister
title: Test whether drug timing relative to the circadian clock matters
description: Synchronize cellular clocks with a dexamethasone or serum shock and add drug at different points across 48 hours. Then measure whether survivor frequency rises and falls with clock phase. Knocking out BMAL1 or CRY1/2 tests whether the clock's timing of gene expression controls who survives.

question: persister
title: Set the cell-to-cell spread of one gene's expression without changing its average
description: Use synthetic gene circuits (for example, noise-tuning promoter or feedback designs) to express a candidate survival gene at the same average level but with different amounts of cell-to-cell variation. Then measure survivor fraction. This tests directly whether the variation itself, rather than the average level, produces the rare surviving cells.

question: persister
title: Vary the drug pulse schedule to estimate how fast cells switch states
description: Treat parallel cultures with drug pulses across a wide range of on/off periods. Fit the survival curve against pulse frequency to a two-state switching model. This gives the rates at which cells enter and leave the drug-tolerant state, and how long they stay in it, without needing a marker for that state.

question: persister
title: Sort cells by physical traits, then treat each group
description: Before drug exposure, use FACS to sort live cells into bins by cell size, mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM), lysosome content or ribosome/translation rate (OPP labeling). Treat each bin separately to see which physical or organelle traits predict survival. These traits come from unequal splitting of cell contents at division and would not show up in transcript or chromatin data.

question: persister
title: Retrospective lineage tracing of the pre-treatment state
description: Barcode cells with an expressed, single-cell-readable lineage tag, let them divide a few times, then split the population so one half is profiled untreated and the other half is drug-treated; barcode matching lets you read out the pre-treatment transcriptome of the exact lineages that go on to survive. This converts an otherwise impossible retrospective question into a direct measurement and avoids relying on guessed marker genes.

question: persister
title: Twin-split assay to measure how heritable and how long-lived priming is
description: Split an expanded barcoded population into two or more replicate flasks and treat each independently, then ask how strongly survivor barcode identity is shared across replicates; the concordance quantifies heritability, and repeating the split after increasing numbers of pre-treatment generations gives the memory half-life of the primed state. This single design distinguishes stable genetic causes, semi-heritable epigenetic priming, and purely stochastic last-minute decisions.

question: persister
title: Prospective sorting plus controlled re-priming as a causality test
description: Use a live-cell reporter or surface marker for the candidate primed state to sort rare high cells before treatment and compare their survival frequency to sorted low cells, then test sufficiency by driving the same gene transiently at the amplitude and duration seen in natural fluctuations. Correlative profiling cannot tell you whether a state causes survival; this pairing of sorting and amplitude-matched induction can.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement imaging
description: Measure fluorescent drug analog accumulation and a phospho-specific target readout in the same cells during the first hours of treatment, so that each survivor can be labeled as under-dosed, poorly target-engaged, or fully engaged but death-resistant. This rules in or out the mundane pharmacological explanations that are rarely measured and that would otherwise confound any transcriptional story.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as the death-threshold axis
description: Apply BH3 profiling or a comparable mitochondrial depolarization assay at single-cell resolution to untreated cells, then relate measured priming to survival after drug challenge in matched lineages. This tests a distinct hypothesis from the usual signaling-state framing, namely that survivors differ not in how the drug is sensed but in how close they already sit to the apoptotic threshold.

question: persister
title: Split-sibling fluctuation assay to partition heritable vs. instantaneous causes
description: Grow many small clonal populations from single cells, split each into a profiled half and a drug-challenged half, and compare variance in survivor fraction across clones to the variance expected from pure chance. The shape of that variance distribution directly estimates how long before treatment the survival-determining state was set, and separates heritable priming from coin-flips happening at the moment of drug exposure.

question: persister
title: Lineage trees under drug: how many divisions does survival memory last
description: Image barcoded or sparsely labeled cells continuously from several divisions before drug addition through the persister phase, reconstructing full lineage trees. Correlating fates between sisters, cousins, and second cousins yields a quantitative half-life for the tolerant state, which distinguishes transient signaling fluctuations from epigenetically heritable programs.

question: persister
title: Rule out the boring explanation: per-cell drug exposure and cell-cycle position
description: Before invoking transcriptional states, measure what each cell actually experiences using a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging for intracellular drug concentration, plus a FUCCI reporter for cell-cycle phase at the moment of treatment. If survivors are simply cells that were quiescent or had low drug accumulation, that reframes the whole question, and a negative result makes downstream state-based claims far stronger.

question: persister
title: Colony-splitting state-to-fate map
description: Index-sort single cells, let each grow into a small colony, then split every colony between transcriptional or chromatin profiling and drug challenge. Because sibling cells share the heritable state, this gives a direct, prospective map from measured molecular state to measured survival probability, rather than the usual retrospective comparison of survivors to a bulk pre-treatment population.

question: persister
title: Cross-drug and cross-host reproducibility of the surviving lineages
description: Barcode one population, split it across several different targeted agents and across multiple xenograft hosts, and ask whether the same barcodes recur among survivors. Convergence implies a single general primed state, while drug-specific and host-specific survivor sets imply a repertoire of distinct, context-matched states, and the two possibilities call for completely different therapeutic strategies.

question: persister
title: Sibling-split profiling to read out the survivor's pre-drug state
description: Barcode a population, let each cell divide a few times, then physically split each clone so that one half is drug-challenged and the matched half is profiled untreated by single-cell RNA-seq. Because barcodes link the two halves, you can read the transcriptome of the cells that would have survived without ever exposing them to drug, cleanly separating pre-existing priming from drug-induced adaptation.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation analysis to estimate the rate of entry into and exit from the primed state
description: Expand many independent parallel cultures from small inocula, treat each identically, and analyze the variance in survivor counts across cultures using a Luria-Delbruck style framework extended to reversible states. The shape of the distribution distinguishes a rare heritable mutation from a transient, interconverting state, and fitting it yields quantitative switching rates rather than just a qualitative claim of plasticity.

question: persister
title: Prospective reporter sorting as a falsifiable test of priming
description: Knock fluorescent reporters into the endogenous loci of candidate priming genes, sort live untreated cells from the top and bottom of the expression distribution, and challenge each fraction with drug. The fold-enrichment of survival in the reporter-high fraction converts a correlational signature into a predictive, quantitative measurement, and re-sorting after varying culture times measures how long the state is remembered.

question: persister
title: Continuous imaging through the moment of drug addition, with in situ molecular endpoints
description: Time-lapse image a sparse population from before drug exposure through survivor outgrowth, recording cell-cycle phase, size, division history, and neighbor context for every cell, then perform in situ sequencing or multiplexed RNA FISH on the same field at the end. This retrospectively assigns a complete behavioral and molecular history to each survivor and to its non-surviving neighbors, which bulk or dissociated methods cannot do.

question: persister
title: Screening on survivor frequency rather than on survival itself
description: Run a CRISPR or small-molecule screen whose readout is the fraction of cells that enter the primed state, measured by a priming reporter or by the number of independent surviving colonies per starting cell, rather than overall viability. Perturbations that change the frequency without changing the identity of the resistant state point to the upstream machinery that generates rare-cell variability, a target class that conventional viability screens systematically miss.

question: persister
title: Twin-plate barcoding to read out the pre-treatment state of future survivors
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into twin plates so that each barcode is represented in both, treat one plate and deeply profile the untreated twin by scRNA-seq. Because survivors are identified retrospectively by barcode, this directly reveals the transcriptional state the surviving cells were in before they ever saw drug, rather than the post-hoc state of cells already reshaped by treatment.

question: persister
title: Measure the memory half-life of the primed state
description: Sort cells that are in the putative primed state (by a FISH-based or reporter-based readout), re-plate them, and assay drug survival and marker expression at a series of time points as the sorted population relaxes back toward baseline. The decay curve gives a quantitative switching rate that distinguishes a transient transcriptional fluctuation from a stably heritable epigenetic state.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation analysis of survivor counts to infer switching rates
description: Grow many small parallel cultures from few cells, treat each identically, and count survivor colonies per culture. The shape of the variance across cultures (Luria-Delbrück style) discriminates rare irreversible events arising early in the lineage from fast reversible state-switching, and yields switching and reversion rates without any molecular profiling.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome to test whether chromatin is primed before transcription
description: Perform joint ATAC and RNA profiling on untreated cells to ask whether the regulatory regions of resistance-associated genes are already accessible in cells that have not yet upregulated those transcripts. A population with open-but-silent chromatin would identify an intermediate, pre-primed compartment much larger than the eventual survivor fraction.

question: persister
title: Spatial and conditioned-media tests for non-cell-autonomous survival
description: Image whether survivor colonies are spatially clustered more than expected by chance, and complement this with conditioned-media transfer and mixed co-culture of labeled sensitive cells. Together these separate genuinely cell-intrinsic priming from local paracrine protection or density effects, a confound rarely excluded in single-cell priming studies.

question: persister
title: Sibling-split heritability clock
description: Separate pairs of related cells at defined numbers of generations apart (via dilution cloning or imaging-tracked micro-colonies), then treat one relative and score the other's descendants, measuring how the correlation in survival between relatives decays with generational distance. This converts the vague notion of a 'non-genetic state' into a quantitative heritability half-life, and distinguishes a state that is reset every cell cycle from one that persists for many divisions.

question: persister
title: Cross-drug identity test with shared lineage barcodes
description: Barcode one population, split it into arms challenged with mechanistically distinct targeted agents, and ask whether the surviving barcode sets overlap more than chance. Strong overlap implies a general drug-tolerant state (slow cycling, apoptotic unpriming), while disjoint sets imply drug-specific priming such as pathway-specific expression, and the two imply completely different therapeutic strategies.

question: persister
title: Decomposing survival into death, division, and arrest
description: Use week-long live imaging with an apoptosis/caspase reporter and automated tracking to measure, per surviving lineage, the death rate, the division rate, and the duration of arrest under drug. This distinguishes cells that never engage apoptosis from cells that die more slowly and from cells that keep proliferating outright, which are often conflated in endpoint colony counts.

question: persister
title: Separating state frequency from state fitness in a modifier screen
description: Run a CRISPR or small-molecule modifier screen with two independent readouts: the fraction of cells entering the primed state (scored by a reporter or marker before treatment) and the survival probability conditional on being primed. Hits that change entry rate point to the regulators that generate the rare state, while hits that change conditional survival point to the effectors that execute it; a conventional resistance screen cannot tell these apart.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure as a rule-out measurement
description: Measure actual intracellular drug levels cell by cell using a fluorescent drug analog, a target-engagement reporter, or mass-spec imaging, and correlate exposure with fate. This tests the mundane but rarely excluded possibility that survivors differ in uptake, efflux, or local drug access rather than in signaling state, and any residual fate variation after conditioning on exposure is a cleaner estimate of true state-driven survival.

question: persister
title: Retrospective profiling of future survivors via sibling-cell splitting
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into twin dishes, treat one with drug, and use the barcodes of the survivors to go back and sequence or image their untreated siblings. This directly measures the pre-treatment state of cells destined to survive, rather than inferring it from survivors after the drug has already reshaped them.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation analysis to measure the memory timescale of the primed state
description: Expand single cells into many sibling subclones, treat each, and compare the variance in survivor number against a Poisson expectation, Luria-Delbruck style. Repeating this with different expansion times converts the variance into an estimate of how many generations the survival-conferring state is inherited, separating a heritable epigenetic state from a purely instantaneous stochastic one.

question: persister
title: Prospective sorting to test sufficiency, not just correlation
description: Use a live marker of the candidate primed state (surface protein stain or a knock-in reporter) to sort the rare high cells before any drug exposure, then measure their survival frequency against sorted-low and unsorted cells. Enrichment that falls far short of the marker's purity would reveal the state is necessary but not sufficient, pointing to a second required factor.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as an alternative explanation to signaling state
description: Apply BH3 profiling or a single-cell cytochrome c release assay before treatment to measure how close each cell sits to the apoptotic threshold. This tests the distinct hypothesis that survivors are not signaling outliers but simply cells with more buffered mitochondria, an explanation that transcriptomics alone would miss.

question: persister
title: Cross-drug barcode overlap to ask whether priming is drug-specific
description: Split one barcoded population across several mechanistically distinct drugs and compare which barcodes appear among the survivors of each. Strong overlap would imply a general tolerant state such as slow cycling, while near-disjoint survivor sets would argue for many independent, pathway-specific primed states, a result that changes which combination therapies make sense.

question: persister
title: Retrospective lineage barcoding with sister-cell profiling (Rewind/FateMap)
description: Label cells with expressed barcodes, let them divide, then split the population. Treat one half with drug and profile the untreated sister cells by scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq to find the molecular state that existed before treatment in cells whose lineages went on to survive.

question: persister
title: Measuring how long the primed state lasts
description: Use FACS to isolate cells that are high or low for a priming marker such as EGFR or NGFR. Track their marker levels with smFISH and their drug survival over successive divisions to estimate how long the state persists and how often cells switch in and out of it. This tells you whether survival depends on a short-lived fluctuation or on a stable memory across many generations.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell concordance via live imaging
description: Track sister and cousin cells by time-lapse imaging during treatment, using signaling (ERK KTR) and cell-cycle (CDK2/p21) reporters. Measure how often related cells share the same fate and which reporter dynamics before treatment predict survival.

question: persister
title: Fate-coupled CRISPR screens for regulators of priming frequency
description: Run pooled CRISPR screens that read out how often cells enter the primed state or how many resistant colonies form, rather than overall viability. This identifies genes that control how often rare surviving states arise, separate from genes that affect general fitness.

question: persister
title: Multi-dose and multi-drug clone tracking
description: Expand barcoded populations and split them across several doses and several targeted drugs. Then measure whether the same barcoded clones survive under each condition. This shows whether surviving cells share one general tolerant state or several distinct states, each specific to a drug or dose.

question: persister
title: Split-sibling barcode design to test heritable memory
description: Tag a population with heritable DNA barcodes, let it expand so each barcode is represented by many sibling cells, then split the population into several arms treated independently. If the same barcodes dominate survivors across arms, the surviving state was present and heritable before treatment; if survivor barcodes differ across arms, survival is largely a chance event occurring during treatment.

question: persister
title: Retrospective imaging of the same cells before and after treatment
description: Image a sparse, position-registered untreated population with live reporters for candidate pathway activity, then add drug and return to the identical fields over days to link each cell's pre-treatment state to its fate. This avoids the usual problem that profiling methods destroy the cell whose outcome you want to know.

question: persister
title: Reversibility and re-treatment kinetics after drug holiday
description: Expand survivors in drug-free medium for varying lengths of time, then re-treat and measure how the fraction of survivors changes. A return toward the original low frequency indicates a transient, reversible state with a measurable relaxation time, while persistent high resistance indicates genetic or stably epigenetic change.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic threshold versus signaling output
description: In the same untreated cells, measure both proximity to the apoptotic threshold (for example by peptide-induced mitochondrial permeabilization) and drug-target pathway output. This distinguishes survivors that are genuinely drug-insensitive from those that receive full target inhibition but are simply harder to kill.

question: persister
title: Tuning the switching rate to test causality of state fluctuations
description: Use chromatin-modifying perturbations or controlled expression noise to raise or lower the rate at which cells enter the rare primed state, then ask whether survivor frequency moves correspondingly. This converts a correlative observation about rare states into a causal test and suggests interventions that reduce the reservoir of survivors.

question: persister
title: Timing the decision: sister-cell splitting across a delay series
description: Split each cell's progeny into a treated arm and an untreated arm after delays of 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 divisions (heritable barcodes plus imaging to track the splits), then ask how well one sister's fate predicts the other's as a function of delay. This directly measures whether fate is pre-encoded and for how long that information persists, instead of assuming a stable primed state exists; a predictability curve that decays to chance within a division argues the decision is made during treatment, not before.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood as a cause, not a nuisance: ablate the neighbors
description: Image survival in situ without replating, record each cell's local density and neighbor identity, then test causality by selectively killing or silencing defined neighbor subsets (inducible caspase or optogenetic ablation in a mixed co-culture) and by transplanting conditioned medium from candidate 'protective' neighborhoods. This converts the usual correlational spatial description into a test of whether survival is conferred by the local niche rather than owned by the cell.

question: persister
title: Audit the 'isogenic' assumption with single-cell DNA and mtDNA sequencing of survivors
description: Run matched single-cell whole-genome (CNV/aneuploidy) and mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing on the parental population and on drug survivors from the same barcoded lineages, so that lineage identity distinguishes pre-existing variants from treatment-induced ones. If survivors are enriched for particular karyotypes or mtDNA variants already present at low frequency, 'non-genetic heterogeneity' in that system is partly mis-assigned genetics.

question: persister
title: Per-cell pharmacology: measure the dose each cell actually got
