description: Use a fluorescent or clickable drug analog (validated against the parent compound) plus live efflux-activity reporters and a fixed-cell target-engagement/phospho-signaling readout to quantify intracellular drug level and target inhibition in every cell, then relate those to fate. This tests whether 'identical treatment' holds at the single-cell level and whether apparent state heterogeneity is downstream of exposure heterogeneity.

question: persister
title: Decompose survival into sequential bottlenecks by continuous long-term imaging
description: Follow every founder cell by continuous imaging from drug addition through weeks of persistence and regrowth, scoring death, arrest, cycling-through, and re-awakening as separate events, and fit predictors to each transition independently. This replaces the single binary endpoint with a staged model and can show that early tolerance and late outgrowth are governed by different, even anticorrelated, cell properties — and that averaging survivors conflates distinct routes.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell splitting across a delay ladder
description: Split pairs of sister cells at defined intervals before treatment (0, 1, 3, 7, 14 days of regrowth) and measure how concordance of survival between sisters decays with separation time, yielding the autocorrelation timescale of the resistant state and the residual fraction of fate that is an irreducible post-drug coin flip. This directly tests whether survival is predetermined and heritable, rather than assuming it; clone-level (MemorySeq-style) profiling then identifies transcripts that actually fluctuate on the measured timescale.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-resolved survivor mapping with mixing and conditioned-medium controls
description: Live-image a labeled monolayer through treatment and test whether each survivor's local density, contact number, and spatial position at the moment of dosing predict survival better than its own pre-drug reporter intensity. Follow with low- versus high-density plating, transwell/conditioned-medium transfer, and mixing of color-coded populations to separate paracrine or neighborhood rescue from intrinsic state.

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target engagement
description: Quantify how much drug each cell actually receives and what it does there, using a fluorescent drug analog or single-cell mass spectrometry/MALDI imaging for intracellular concentration, efflux-pump activity dyes, and a live pathway reporter such as an ERK kinase-translocation reporter. This asks whether survivors are simply cells with lower drug load or incomplete pathway shutoff rather than carriers of a distinct resistance program.

question: persister
title: Single-cell genome, CNV, and mtDNA profiling of sorted survivors versus matched dying cells
description: Perform single-cell WGS/low-pass CNV analysis plus mtDNA heteroplasmy calling on survivors and on a size-matched sample of the pre-treatment population, combined with high-complexity DNA barcoding to distinguish rare pre-existing genetic subclones from epigenetically fluctuating states. The decisive test is whether survivors are enriched for a variant already present, at the predicted frequency, before treatment.

question: persister
title: Forcing the candidate state on and off, with retrospective lineage validation
description: Use inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi or a degron to drive the candidate state in a tunable fraction of cells before dosing and measure whether survival probability tracks induced expression level quantitatively, establishing causality rather than correlation. Validate in the reverse direction with a Rewind-style barcode scheme that recovers the actual pre-treatment ancestors of eventual survivors and profiles them directly, instead of inferring their state from bulk survivor averages.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell fate correlation as a clock for how long priming lasts
description: Attacks the determinism assumption: split sister cells (by imaging or by barcoding followed by replicate splitting) and add drug at staggered intervals after division, then measure how the correlation in sister fates decays with elapsed time. Rapid decay implies a short-lived fluctuating state and bounds how much of the outcome is set before treatment versus rolled during it.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target occupancy as the primary variable
description: Attacks the uniform-pharmacology assumption: use a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spec imaging plus a live target-occupancy reporter (e.g., pathway phospho-reporter or NanoBRET-style binding readout) to quantify intracellular drug concentration and inhibition depth in every cell before fate is known. Test whether survivors are simply the cells that received or retained the least drug, which would reframe 'resistant state' as an efflux, uptake, or volume phenomenon.

question: persister
title: Controlled-neighborhood survival mapping
description: Attacks cell autonomy: use micropatterning or defined seeding densities, plus mixing of labeled cells at varying ratios, to measure survival probability as a function of local neighbor number and identity, with conditioned-media and transwell swaps to separate contact from secreted signals. This directly quantifies how much of the surviving fraction is explained by microenvironmental position rather than internal state.

question: persister
title: Testing whether rare survival is genetically heritable using replicate-split barcode lineages
description: Attacks the genetic-identity assumption: barcode a population, split it into many independent replicate cultures, treat each, and ask whether the same barcodes survive reproducibly across splits; pair this with single-cell DNA/CNV and mitochondrial heteroplasmy profiling of survivors. Perfect cross-replicate reproducibility implicates fixed genetic or stably heritable differences, partial reproducibility quantifies a heritable-but-reversible component.

question: persister
title: Sufficiency testing by forcing candidate states before treatment
description: Attacks the correlation-equals-cause assumption: take the states enriched in survivors and impose them prospectively using CRISPRa/CRISPRi or inducible expression of their candidate drivers, or sort live cells on a reporter of the state and re-plate them, then measure whether the surviving fraction shifts as predicted. A dose-response between imposed state level and survival probability converts a descriptive signature into a causal, quantitative claim.

question: persister
title: Twin-split clone assay with a tunable prediction horizon
description: Expand single cells into clones, split each clone into a profiled half and a drug-treated half, and ask how well the profiled half's state predicts the treated half's survival as a function of the delay between splitting and treatment. This directly tests the assumption of pre-existing determinism and measures the memory timescale of the fate-determining state, distinguishing heritable priming from a coin flip taken at the moment of treatment.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded genome and mitochondrial genotyping of survivors
description: Barcode the population, then deep-sequence whole genomes, single-cell CNV/ecDNA copy number, and mtDNA heteroplasmy in survivor colonies versus matched pre-treatment sisters of the same barcode lineage. This abandons the premise of genetic identity and tests whether a 'non-genetic' persister phenotype actually co-segregates with cryptic structural, ecDNA, or mitochondrial variation.

question: persister
title: Density- and neighbor-controlled survival mapping
description: Seed cells on micropatterns or in microwells at defined local densities and defined neighbor genotypes, image survival as a function of each cell's measured local neighborhood, and swap conditioned media or laser-ablate neighbors to test causality. This breaks the cell-autonomy assumption and quantifies how much of the rare-survivor probability is set by local context and paracrine signaling rather than by the cell itself.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and apoptotic-threshold measurement
description: Combine a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging of intracellular drug with efflux-pump activity reporters, single-cell target-occupancy readouts (phospho-signaling by iterative immunofluorescence), and dynamic BH3 profiling of mitochondrial priming. This tests whether survivors differ in the dose they actually receive and the death threshold they must cross, rather than in cellular identity.

question: persister
title: Long-term fate taxonomy by continuous imaging before retrospective profiling
description: Image thousands of cells continuously for weeks through treatment and regrowth to classify every outcome (immediate death, divide-then-die, arrest-then-resume, senescence escape, polyploidization), then retrieve and profile cells from each class separately. This refuses the binary survivor label and deconvolves what are almost certainly several mechanistically distinct routes to survival being averaged together.

question: persister
title: Genetic-vs-nongenetic partition using barcoded twin populations plus single-cell DNA and ecDNA readout
description: Tags the assumption of true genetic identity: label a population with high-complexity heritable barcodes, split it into replicate 'twin' flasks, and test whether the same barcodes survive drug in independent replicates (heritable/genetic) or different ones each time (transient state). Pair this with deep whole-genome sequencing of pre-treatment single-cell-derived clones, single-cell DNA-seq, and ecDNA FISH on the untreated population to quantify directly how much of the rare-survivor fraction is explained by cryptic mutations or amplifications rather than by non-genetic state.

question: persister
title: Retrospective profiling of the pre-treatment cells that are destined to survive
description: Tags survivor bias: identify the barcodes enriched in survivors, then go back to an archived, never-treated aliquot of the same barcoded population and physically recover those specific cells using barcode-targeted probes or barcode-driven reporters, so their transcriptome, protein, and chromatin state can be measured before any drug exposure. This separates the causal priming state from the downstream reprogramming that drug treatment imposes on survivors.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and apoptotic priming, not just RNA, measured live and linked to fate
description: Tags the assumption that the transcriptome and the nominal dose are the right variables: measure in each cell the actual intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging), the degree of target inhibition (live kinase-activity or signaling biosensors such as ERK/AKT reporters), efflux-pump activity, and mitochondrial apoptotic priming by single-cell dynamic BH3 profiling, then time-lapse track the same cells to death or survival. This tests whether rare survival is simply heterogeneous pharmacology and death-threshold setting rather than a transcriptional 'resistant program'.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-controlled survival assay: isolate the cell-autonomous component
description: Tags cell-autonomy: compare survival frequency for cells seeded as isolated singletons in microwells or micropatterns versus matched cells in dense colonies, swap conditioned media, and use time-lapse plus spatial transcriptomics to score each survivor's local density, contact history, and position within a colony. Cross-mixing of differentially labeled populations then reveals whether a surviving cell confers or receives protection, distinguishing an intrinsic primed state from a locally created protective niche.

question: persister
title: Measuring the timescale, heritability, and causal sufficiency of the primed state
description: Tags the assumption of a stable discrete subpopulation and of single-cell independence: build a live reporter of the candidate priming marker, track lineages for weeks, and compute sister/cousin/aunt correlation decay and state-switching rates to obtain the memory half-life and determine whether the state is discrete or continuous. Then sort marker-high cells, let them re-equilibrate for varying times before dosing to see how quickly survival advantage decays, and force the state on or off with inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi to test whether it is causally sufficient rather than merely correlated.

question: persister
title: Exhaust the genetic explanation before invoking a non-genetic one
description: Perform matched single-cell whole-genome and mitochondrial sequencing on survivors versus naive cells, with specific attention to extrachromosomal DNA and focal copy-number gains at the drug target and its bypass pathways, using FISH or CUT&RUN on the same cells where possible. This directly tests the 'genetically identical' premise and quantifies what fraction of survival is attributable to rare pre-existing genetic or ecDNA heterogeneity rather than cell state.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell split design to separate pre-existing state from drug-induced change
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes or physical separation of daughter cells so that one sister is profiled molecularly while its twin is exposed to drug and its fate recorded, letting you ask whether the pre-drug state is predictive of the sister's outcome. Varying the delay between the split and treatment also measures how long the predisposing state persists, distinguishing a heritable primed state from transient fluctuation or genuinely drug-induced adaptation.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-resolved survival and causal density perturbation
description: Track survival by long-term live imaging with single-cell segmentation, then model each cell's outcome as a function of its local neighbor count, neighbor identity, and contact history, rather than only its own features. Follow with causal tests, such as micropatterned colonies of defined size, conditioned-media transfer, and co-culture with labeled sensitive cells, to see whether survival is conferred by neighbors instead of residing in the cell itself.

question: persister
title: Ask whether survivors are one population or several, then test each separately
description: Cluster survivors by multimodal single-cell profiling and treat the clusters as competing hypotheses, assigning each a candidate dependency and testing them in parallel with a pooled CRISPR screen performed under drug with a single-cell readout. If distinct survivor subsets have non-overlapping genetic dependencies, that falsifies the implicit single-mechanism model and reframes the question as several mechanisms sharing one phenotype.

question: persister
title: Measure the dose each cell actually received, not the dose in the dish
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target engagement directly, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, mass spectrometry imaging, efflux-pump reporters, and live biosensors of the targeted signaling node. This tests whether survivors differ in pathway state at all, or simply in pharmacology, and would explain apparent resistance as a difference in exposure rather than in cell identity.

question: persister
title: Rule genetics in or out before invoking plasticity
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing plus ecDNA-sensitive assays (FISH, Circle-seq) on matched pre-treatment, survivor, and dying populations from the same isogenic culture, specifically asking whether survivors are enriched for pre-existing CNVs, ecDNA copy number, or subclonal variants. This directly tests the 'genetically identical' premise that the entire non-genetic-resistance literature rests on, and establishes what fraction of survival needs a non-genetic explanation at all.

question: persister
title: Measure the drug, not just the cell
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration and target engagement per cell — using fluorescent or clickable drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or a CETSA/NanoBRET-style occupancy reporter — jointly with survival outcome in the same cells. The field's default readout (RNA) may be measuring a correlate while the actual determinant is pharmacokinetic: efflux-pump activity, lysosomal sequestration, or uptake variation producing a sub-lethal exposure in a few cells.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
description: Use micropatterned islands, defined co-culture ratios, and conditioned-medium swaps to systematically vary each cell's local density and neighbor identity while holding genotype constant, then score survival as a function of neighborhood with live imaging. If survival probability depends on measured local context more than on any cell-intrinsic marker, the standard cell-autonomous framing — and the search for a 'primed cell' signature — is misdirected.

question: persister
title: Retrospective live imaging that converts snapshots into trajectories
description: Continuously image cells carrying a reporter for the candidate primed state (e.g., a knock-in of a resistance-associated gene) from before drug addition through outcome, then retrieve individual cells for sequencing via in situ transcriptomics or Live-seq. This reveals whether the state pre-exists, how fast it fluctuates relative to the treatment window, and whether survivors were already in the state at t=0 or entered it stochastically afterward — none of which a destructive snapshot can distinguish.

question: persister
title: Sufficiency test by synthetic state induction
description: Use inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi or degron systems to impose the candidate survivor state in a tunable fraction of cells before treatment, and ask whether the surviving fraction shifts quantitatively as predicted. This converts a correlative signature into a causal claim, and a failure to shift survival would be as informative as a success, indicating the signature is a consequence or bystander rather than the driver.

question: persister
title: Clone-splitting twin assay to partition fate variance
description: Using heritable expressed barcodes or physical splitting of small clones, treat one half of each clone and profile or re-challenge the other half, then quantify how much of survival probability is shared within a lineage versus private to each cell, and how fast that shared component decays over passages. This directly measures whether 'priming' is a stable pre-existing property or a short-lived fluctuation, instead of assuming it.

question: persister
title: Single-cell genome and ecDNA accounting of survivors
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing plus DNA FISH for ecDNA and target-locus copy number on parental and surviving cells, with duplex sequencing of the drug target to detect mutations below 0.1% allele frequency. This tests whether the 'genetically identical' premise is false and whether rare copy-number or ecDNA jackpot cells, not transcriptional states, account for survival.

question: persister
title: Per-cell intracellular drug dosimetry
description: Measure the actual drug concentration each cell receives using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, mass-spectrometry imaging, or a live target-engagement reporter, combined with per-cell efflux-pump activity, and correlate it with fate by live imaging. If survival tracks drug exposure rather than transcriptional state, the usual expression-based explanations are confounded by pharmacology.

question: persister
title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
description: Micropattern or seed cells at defined local densities, image the full field during treatment, and model each cell's survival as a function of its own state versus the number, proximity, and death timing of its neighbors; complement with conditioned-medium and apoptotic-debris transfer experiments. This tests whether survival is cell-autonomous at all or a property of local microenvironment and dying-neighbor signals.

question: persister
title: Forced-state causal test with graded fate readout
description: Use CRISPRa/CRISPRi or an inducible/optogenetic construct to drive candidate primed-state genes in a titratable fraction of cells before treatment, and ask whether the surviving fraction shifts proportionally; score outcome not as live/dead but as a continuous live-imaging trajectory (death, arrest, dormancy, proliferation). This converts a correlative state into a causal dose-response and resolves whether 'survivors' are one population or several.

question: persister
title: Cross-dataset meta-analysis of pre-resistant transcriptional states
description: Harmonize dozens of public pre-treatment scRNA-seq datasets across melanoma/BRAFi, lung/EGFR-TKI, breast/CDK4-6i and leukemia, and test whether the rare primed high-expressing subpopulations (AXL, NGFR, EGFR-high) reflect one shared program or lineage- and drug-specific ones. This distinguishes a universal priming axis from idiosyncratic per-model heterogeneity.

question: persister
title: Reanalysis of lineage-barcoding data for heritability and memory half-life
description: Public Watermelon, ClonMapper, TraCe-seq, Rewind and CellTag datasets contain sister- and cousin-cell relationships that allow survival to be partitioned into heritable-clonal versus stochastic components. Fitting a state-switching model yields the number of generations a primed state persists, a quantity rarely extracted in the original papers.

question: persister
title: Luria-Delbruck fluctuation analysis of published clonal outgrowth data
description: Apply fluctuation-test statistics to replicate-well colony counts reported after targeted-drug treatment to estimate the rate at which cells enter the drug-tolerant state. The shape of the across-well count distribution separates heritable genetic mutation from reversible epigenetic switching.

question: persister
title: DepMap/PRISM modeling of residual viability rather than IC50
description: Extract the dose-response plateau, i.e. the fraction surviving at saturating drug, across roughly a thousand cell lines in PRISM and GDSC, then regress it on baseline CCLE expression, methylation, chromatin and copy-number features. This identifies determinants of a large persister fraction that are independent of average drug sensitivity.

question: persister
title: Benchmarking in vitro persister signatures against patient residual disease
description: Score published on-treatment and minimal-residual-disease patient biopsies (scRNA-seq cohorts in GEO, plus deconvolved TRACERx/TCGA bulk data) against cell-line-derived persister signatures. This reveals which laboratory persister programs actually survive therapy in humans and which are culture artifacts.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation analysis with split sister clones
description: Grow many small clonal populations from single cells, split each into sister wells, and treat them with drug. Compare the variance in resistant-colony counts within sister pairs and between clones to tell a heritable pre-existing state (Luria–Delbrück-like jackpots that sisters share) from stochastic or drug-induced survival, and estimate how long the state lasts by varying the time before splitting (about $3–5k in plates, drug and imaging).

question: persister
title: Barcode 'twins' lineage tracing to capture survivors' pre-drug state
description: Label cells with a lentiviral barcode library, let them divide a few times, then split them so sister cells end up in both halves. Treat one half, sequence the barcodes of the survivors, and profile the untreated sisters with the same barcodes using targeted barcode capture plus one small single-cell RNA-seq run, to see which expression programs mark future survivors before any drug exposure (about $12–18k).

question: persister
title: Multiplexed smFISH/HCR counts of rare 'primed' cells before and during treatment
description: In thousands of untreated cells and along a fixed time course of drug treatment, image transcript counts of 10–20 candidate resistance genes (e.g., AXL, EGFR, NGFR, WNT5A, SOX10). This shows whether a rare subpopulation that co-expresses several markers exists beforehand, how often it occurs, and whether its frequency matches the surviving fraction (about $4–8k in probes and reagents, using existing microscopes).

question: persister
title: Live-cell imaging of signaling and cell-cycle history before drug addition
description: Express cheap fluorescent reporters (an ERK/AKT kinase-activity reporter plus FUCCI cell-cycle markers) and film cells for 1–2 days before and 3–5 days after drug addition. Then track each cell's lineage to test whether survival is predicted by earlier signaling pulses, cell-cycle phase, quiescence or inheritance from the mother cell (about $3–6k).

question: persister
title: Sorting and perturbation tests of candidate survival states
description: Use FACS to sort the top and bottom ~1% of cells for candidate markers (from the ideas above), and separately knock down or overexpress the candidate regulators with siRNA, CRISPRi or a small pooled guide library. Then count resistant colonies to test whether the marked state actually causes survival rather than just correlating with it (about $5–10k).

question: persister
title: Track lineages before treatment, then trace survivors back
description: Film cells for several generations before adding the drug, keep imaging through treatment, then trace every surviving cell back through its lineage tree. Comparing how often sisters and cousins of survivors also survive shows whether survival is a heritable pre-existing state and how many generations that memory lasts, compared with a random or drug-induced event.

question: persister
title: Test whether pre-drug signaling or rebound predicts survival
description: Express multiplexed kinase translocation reporters (for example ERK, AKT and JNK KTRs) and quantify each cell's baseline pathway activity and pulse dynamics before the drug, plus how quickly signaling recovers after it. Then test whether a high baseline or a fast rebound of bypass signaling predicts which cells survive.

question: persister
title: Use live reporters of a primed state to measure switching
description: Knock fluorescent tags or MS2/PP7 tags into endogenous genes linked to rare resistant states (for example AXL, EGFR, NGFR, or loss of SOX10) and image their fluctuations over days. This gives the rate at which cells enter and leave the high-expressing state, and shows whether cells that are in or entering that state when the drug arrives are the ones that survive.

question: persister
title: Check whether cell-cycle state at drug addition matters
description: Use FUCCI and a CDK2/CDK4/6 activity sensor to record each cell's cycle phase and proliferation commitment when the drug is added. This tests whether survivors come from cells that were already in spontaneous quiescence (CDK2-low) rather than from drug-induced arrest, and tracks how and when they re-enter the cell cycle to form resistant colonies.

question: persister
title: Predict survivors from label-free imaging and neighborhood context
description: Train a model on pre-drug, label-free features (morphology, motility, nuclear texture), live dyes for mitochondrial membrane potential and ROS, and spatial neighborhood data (local density, distance to other future survivors). This shows how early survivors can be identified and whether survival depends on the cell's own state, its metabolism, or its surroundings.

question: persister
title: Image-then-sequence fate mapping of individual cells
description: Continuously image a dish of cells for days before and during drug exposure, recording each cell's growth rate, morphology, division history and position, then fix the same dish and run in situ spatial transcriptomics so every imaged cell gets a molecular profile. Because imaging preserves cell identity, you can ask retrospectively which measurable features of a cell, hours or days earlier, predicted whether it died or persisted.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target-engagement mapping
description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates and how completely its target is inhibited, using a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging together with single-cell phospho-signaling readouts by mass cytometry or quantitative immunofluorescence across doses and times. This separates survivors that simply see less inhibited target (uptake, efflux, sequestration) from survivors whose target is fully inhibited yet whose downstream signaling and apoptotic machinery still keep them alive.

question: persister
title: Memory decay after a drug holiday
description: Isolate survivors, let them expand without drug for a graded series of recovery times, and re-challenge equal numbers at each time point while profiling chromatin accessibility and transcription in parallel. The rate at which the enriched survival fraction and its associated chromatin state revert to baseline quantifies how long the non-genetic resistant state is remembered and whether it is a stable alternative state or a transient excursion.

question: persister
title: Time-resolved multiome search for pre-existing versus induced survivor states
description: Profile joint RNA and chromatin accessibility in the same single cells at a dense series of time points spanning untreated, early killing, and established persistence, then search the untreated population for rare cells whose state already resembles the survivors. Finding such cells before treatment supports selection of a pre-existing state; their absence, with accessibility changes emerging only after drug, supports induction and adaptation.

question: persister
title: Mapping the non-genetic context that sets survival odds
description: Systematically vary context without touching the genome: local cell density and neighbor contact, conditioned-medium transfer, nutrient and oxygen levels, matrix stiffness, and position in the cell cycle scored by EdU incorporation and DNA content at the moment of drug addition. Quantifying how each factor shifts the fraction and the spatial clustering of survivors reveals how much rare survival is a property of a cell's environment and division state rather than of the cell alone.

question: persister
title: Split-population barcode "twin test" in zebrafish melanoma transplants
description: Label ZMEL1 zebrafish melanoma cells with a high-complexity heritable barcode library, split the expanded population into replicate arms, and treat each with BRAF/MEK inhibition: shared survivor barcodes across arms indicate a pre-existing heritable state, while non-overlapping survivors indicate stochastic or transient origins. Varying the delay between splitting and treatment turns the assay into a direct measurement of how many generations the survival-conferring state persists.

question: persister
title: Retrospective isolation of primed cells before drug in a canine tumor line
description: In a KIT-driven canine mast cell tumor line treated with toceranib, use an RNA-detectable expressed barcode so barcodes enriched among survivors can be found by hybridization in an untreated sister population, allowing the rare cells that would have survived to be sorted and profiled by scRNA-seq while still drug-naive. This measures the primed state itself rather than the post-treatment aftermath, the usual confound in persister profiling.

question: persister
title: Live signaling-dynamics tracking with optogenetic causality testing
description: Image ERK-KTR and AKT biosensors in rat or canine tumor cells for many hours before drug addition and follow each cell's fate, regressing pre-drug pulse frequency, amplitude, and duration against survival. Then use optogenetic ERK activation to impose the candidate dynamic pattern and test whether it is sufficient to generate survivors.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement to exclude trivial pharmacology
description: Quantify fluorescent drug-analog uptake, efflux-pump reporter activity, and a target-engagement readout in individual survivors versus dying neighbors in canine or rat lines. This distinguishes genuine cell-state heterogeneity from cells that simply received or retained less drug, a control rarely done at single-cell resolution.

question: persister
title: Intravital imaging of survivor niches in Drosophila and zebrafish tumors
description: Image labeled tumor cells through treatment in living Drosophila Ras/scrib tumors or zebrafish transplants, scoring survivor position relative to vasculature, hemocytes/macrophages, and surrounding stroma. Genetic ablation of the implicated host cell type then tests whether the local niche causes survival rather than merely correlating with it.

question: persister
title: Twin-split clonal barcoding to test heritability of survival
description: Lentivirally barcode a drug-sensitive cancer line at low MOI, expand briefly, then split the population into replicate arms that are treated identically with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. The degree to which the same barcodes survive across split replicates quantifies how much survival is driven by a heritable, pre-existing cell state versus a coin flip at the time of treatment, and the timescale over which splits stop agreeing gives the memory half-life of that state.

question: persister
title: Prospective sorting on candidate priming markers
description: Use scRNA-seq of the untreated population to nominate rare-cell markers with cell-surface or reporter-accessible products, FACS-sort the marker-high and marker-low fractions from drug-naive cells, and then treat both and count colonies. This converts a correlative single-cell signature into a prospective, causal test: if the marker defines the primed state, survival frequency should be strongly enriched in the sorted-high fraction.

question: persister
title: Continuous live imaging across the treatment boundary
description: Image a sparsely plated, nuclear-labeled population for 2-3 days before drug addition and for a week after, so each survivor can be traced back to its own pre-drug history of division rate, cell-cycle phase at dosing, size, motility, and signaling-reporter level. This directly answers whether survivors are distinguished by quiescence, cell-cycle timing, or a transcriptional reporter state before the drug ever arrives.

question: persister
title: Washout-and-rechallenge kinetics to time the memory
description: Isolate drug survivors, culture them without drug for a graded series of durations (days to weeks), and re-challenge at each timepoint to measure how fast the surviving fraction decays back to the naive baseline. A reversible, gradually decaying resistance implicates a non-genetic, epigenetically maintained state, whereas stable resistance points to a fixed genetic or permanently rewired cause.

question: persister
title: Paired multiome plus clonal genotyping of survivors versus naive cells
description: Run single-cell RNA plus ATAC on matched naive, early-persister, and late-resistant populations, and in parallel do low-coverage single-cell or bulk whole-genome copy-number and targeted driver sequencing on the same samples. This separates chromatin and expression reprogramming from selection of a pre-existing genetic subclone, and pinpoints which transcription-factor motifs gain accessibility before the expression changes appear.

question: persister
title: Split-sister barcoding: profile one twin, treat the other
description: Tag cells with heritable expressed barcodes, expand briefly, then divide the population into two matched halves; profile one half once by single-cell RNA+ATAC with no drug, and sequence barcodes once in the treated half at the endpoint. Barcodes shared between survivors and their untreated twins reveal which pre-existing expression and chromatin states confer survival, with each sample read out exactly once.

question: persister
title: Luria-Delbruck-style variance test for heritable priming
description: Seed many independent clonal cultures, grow them for varying numbers of doublings, treat each once, and count surviving colonies a single time per culture. The shape and variance of the survivor-count distribution across cultures distinguishes a heritable, inherited primed state from independent per-cell coin flips, and bounds how many generations that state is remembered.

question: persister
title: Sort on a rare-state reporter, then score survival once
description: Use multiplexed RNA imaging on fixed untreated cells to define the rare co-expression state (for example high AXL/NGFR/EGFR), build a live reporter or antibody panel for it, and sort high versus low cells. Treat each sorted fraction and count colonies at one endpoint to directly quantify the fold enrichment in survival probability attributable to that state.

question: persister
title: Genomic recorders that store each cell's past signaling
description: Express CRISPR base- or prime-editing recorders driven by pathway-responsive promoters (MAPK, NF-kB, AP-1) so each cell continuously writes its signaling history into its own DNA. A single-cell sequencing readout taken once after treatment recovers each survivor's cumulative upstream activity, converting a one-shot measurement into a retrospective time course.

question: persister
title: Endpoint Perturb-seq on survivors versus the starting pool
description: Introduce a genome-wide or focused CRISPR library, treat the population, and perform single-cell CRISPR sequencing once on the surviving cells, comparing guide abundance and transcriptomes against a one-time profile of the untreated library. This simultaneously names the genes whose loss or gain changes survival odds and the transcriptional programs those perturbations act through.

question: persister
title: Lineage-barcoded patient-derived organoids with twin splitting
description: Barcode a patient-derived organoid or PDX line at high complexity, split it into an untreated reference arm and a drug-treated arm, and test whether the surviving barcodes are reproducibly the same across replicate splits. Reproducible survivors indicate a heritable pre-existing state, while random survivors indicate stochastic induction, and the untreated twin allows direct profiling of survivor ancestors before drug exposure.

question: persister
title: Serial pre-treatment, on-treatment, and progression biopsies at single-cell resolution
description: Collect matched biopsies from the same patients at baseline, at the residual-disease nadir 2-4 weeks into targeted therapy, and at relapse, and profile all three by single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. The residual-disease timepoint is the only direct window onto persister cells in a human tumor and reveals whether the persister program pre-exists in a rare subpopulation or appears only under drug.

question: persister
title: Spatially resolved mapping of residual disease in on-treatment biopsies
description: Use imaging-based spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed protein imaging on on-treatment patient biopsies to determine whether surviving cells occupy non-random positions such as perivascular, hypoxic, invasive-front, or CAF- and immune-shielded niches. This separates cell-intrinsic tolerance programs from microenvironment-provided protection, which have very different therapeutic consequences.

question: persister
title: Whole-genome and clonal phylogeny analysis of survivor populations
description: Perform deep whole-genome sequencing and single-cell copy-number profiling on matched pre-treatment and residual or relapse patient samples to test whether survivors carry pre-existing resistance mutations, subclonal expansions, or no genetic distinction at all. Reconstructing the clonal phylogeny establishes whether relapse derives from a genetically privileged clone or from genetically identical cells in a permissive transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Live ex vivo drug exposure of fresh malignant effusions and circulating tumor cells
description: Expose freshly isolated pleural effusion, ascites, or CTC-derived tumor cells from patients to the targeted agent under live-cell imaging, then sort survivors for matched single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. Repeat sampling from the same patient across multiple taps tests whether the tolerant state is stable and heritable or transient and reversible.

question: persister
title: Allele-resolved readout of the rare high-expressing state
description: In a cell line with heterozygous SNPs (or an engineered dual-reporter knock-in at both alleles of a resistance driver such as AXL or NGFR), use allele-specific single-molecule FISH or nascent-transcript imaging to ask whether rare high-expressing cells activate one allele or both. Coordinated biallelic activation implicates an upstream trans/signaling fluctuation shared by the nucleus, whereas monoallelic activation implicates a cis-chromatin switch, which sharply narrows the mechanistic search space before any screening is done.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement as a competing explanation
description: Measure the actual intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy in single cells before scoring survival, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog plus a target-engagement readout (e.g., single-cell CETSA/thermal-shift or a proximity reporter for the inhibited kinase), combined with live efflux-pump activity dyes. This tests the frequently ignored possibility that survivors are pharmacologically under-dosed rather than transcriptionally privileged, and quantifies how much of the survivor fraction that alone explains.

question: persister
title: Sort-and-relax kinetics to fit a transition-rate model with a quantitative sufficiency test
description: Isolate the extreme tails of a live reporter for the candidate primed state by FACS, return them to drug-free culture, and track how the expression distribution relaxes back to steady state over days, fitting entry and exit rates of a two- or three-state Markov model. Then ask whether those independently measured rates numerically predict the observed survivor frequency and the frequency after a defined pre-treatment delay; a mismatch proves another determinant is in play.

question: persister
title: Manipulating the rate of state entry without touching the resistance genes
description: Vary only the cells' drug-free history (confluence, nutrient or hypoxic pulses, transient inhibition of specific chromatin writers/erasers, or enforced slow versus fast growth) and measure the resulting survivor frequency together with the abundance of primed cells. Finding conditions that shift survivor frequency severalfold while leaving bulk drug sensitivity unchanged identifies the upstream process that generates the rare state, which is the actionable target rather than the downstream marker.

question: persister
title: Spatial neighborhood mapping of survivors in fixed coordinates
description: Image the monolayer at the moment of drug addition to record each cell's local density, neighbor identities, and contact geometry, then re-image the identical field after the killing bottleneck to locate survivors. Testing whether survivors are spatially clustered, preferentially arise at colony edges, or sit beside specific secreting neighbors distinguishes a cell-intrinsic primed state from locally produced paracrine protection, which conditioned-medium and sparse-versus-dense plating controls can then confirm.

question: persister
title: Single-cell pharmacokinetics: image the drug itself
description: Synthesize an alkyne- or deuterium-tagged analog of the targeted inhibitor (or use its intrinsic fluorescence) and quantify intracellular drug concentration cell-by-cell with stimulated Raman scattering microscopy or MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging, at early timepoints and in the eventual survivors. This directly tests the rarely-excluded trivial hypothesis that persisters are simply cells with lower drug accumulation — from efflux, lipid-droplet sequestration, or lysosomal trapping — rather than cells in a special signaling state.

question: persister
title: Allele-resolved smFISH to separate a burst from a state
description: Use intron/exon and SNP-discriminating single-molecule FISH on candidate priming genes (e.g. AXL, NGFR, EGFR) in drug-naive cells to measure nascent transcription at each allele, then fit burst frequency, size, and duration. Monoallelic, short-lived bursts with uncorrelated alleles imply priming is transient transcriptional noise; coordinated biallelic activation that persists across the cell cycle implies an upstream heritable chromatin or signaling state — a distinction that bulk or standard scRNA-seq snapshots cannot make.

question: persister
title: CRISPR screen scored on survivor clone diversity, not survivor number
description: Barcode the library-infected population so every cell carries both a guide and a lineage barcode, then score each gene knockout by the barcode diversity (effective number of surviving clones) among survivors rather than by total survival. Genes that change how many independent clones survive while leaving bulk killing kinetics intact are regulators of state-switching rate, cleanly separable from genes that merely shift intrinsic drug sensitivity.

question: persister
title: Optogenetic entrainment to test sufficiency of the primed state
description: Use an optogenetic actuator of the candidate upstream node (e.g. opto-SOS/opto-Raf for frequency-encoded ERK, or a light-inducible dCas9 activator at a candidate priming locus) to drive the whole population into the putative primed state with defined pulse amplitude and frequency before adding drug. If priming is causal and rate-limiting, the persister fraction should rise toward 100% in a dose- and frequency-dependent way; failure to do so bounds how much of survival the state actually explains.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned neighborhoods and apoptotic-corpse swaps
description: Plate cells on micropatterns that fix colony size, spacing, and neighbor number, and separately add purified apoptotic bodies or conditioned medium from drug-killed cells to sparse cultures. This converts neighbor density from a correlate into a controlled variable and tests whether dying cells actively license their neighbors to survive — via released factors, apoptosis-induced proliferation signals, or metabolite handoff — rather than survivors being intrinsically special.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug exposure and target engagement, not just signaling state
description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates and how much target it actually engages — using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, lysosomotropic and efflux-pump reporters, cell volume/dry mass from quantitative phase imaging, and a single-cell target-engagement readout (e.g. NanoBRET or a phospho-substrate immunofluorescence dose curve) — then ask whether survivors are simply the cells that received the lowest effective dose. This tests the mundane but rarely excluded possibility that 'tolerance' is pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (sequestration, efflux, surface-to-volume, cell cycle–linked volume changes) rather than a primed regulatory state, and it sets the baseline any molecular model must beat.

question: persister
title: Hidden copy-number heterogeneity from extrachromosomal DNA and mis-segregation in 'isogenic' cells
description: Perform single-cell DNA sequencing plus DNA-FISH for the target gene and known resistance loci on untreated cells, survivors, and regrown colonies, scoring extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) copies, focal amplifications, and whole-chromosome aneuploidy per cell. Because ecDNA segregates randomly at mitosis, it generates heritable, rapidly reversible dosage variation that mimics epigenetic priming — so quantifying its distribution before treatment, and whether survivors are drawn from the upper tail, decides whether the phenomenon is genomic at all before any chromatin explanation is invoked.

question: persister
title: Survival as a neighborhood property: spatial statistics plus engineered context
description: Map the spatial coordinates of every survivor relative to local pre-treatment cell density, colony edge, and the positions of neighbors that died, testing for clustering beyond what clonal relatedness predicts; then control the variable directly with micropatterned islands of defined size, transwell separation, and medium conditioned by drug-killed cells. This asks whether the surviving fraction is partly set by paracrine signals released during apoptosis and by local crowding — a determinant that single-cell dissociation-based assays systematically destroy, and one that predicts survivor frequency should be tunable by plating geometry alone.

question: persister
title: Apoptotic threshold and mitochondrial inheritance rather than upstream signaling
description: Profile the death machinery itself at single-cell resolution — BH3-peptide-induced cytochrome c release or MOMP timing imaged live, together with per-cell mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, and BCL-2-family protein levels — and track how unevenly mitochondria and these proteins are partitioned between daughters at each division. If survivors come disproportionately from the daughter that inherited the less-primed mitochondrial pool, survival is a downstream execution threshold with a short, division-generated memory, which predicts that lowering the threshold with a BH3 mimetic collapses the surviving fraction without touching any upstream pathway.

question: persister
title: Tune expression noise while holding the mean fixed, as a causal test
description: For a candidate determinant, build isogenic lines expressing it from synthetic promoters or degron/feedback circuits that give matched mean levels but deliberately different cell-to-cell variability, and titrate global noise modifiers as an orthogonal arm; then measure survivor frequency across the panel. Most causal follow-ups shift the average level of a factor, which cannot distinguish 'more of X helps' from 'variability in X creates the rare cells that survive' — this design separates the two, and a quantitative prediction follows: survivor frequency should scale with the variance, not the mean.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug exposure and target occupancy as the null model
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging), efflux activity, and actual target engagement (NanoBRET or in-cell occupancy reporter), then ask whether survivors occupy the low-occupancy tail. This tests the rarely measured possibility that fractional survival reflects pharmacological heterogeneity in uptake, efflux, and target abundance rather than any distinct regulatory cell state.

question: persister
title: Sister-pair concordance decay to measure the memory half-life of the survival state
description: Reconstruct lineage trees by imaging up to the moment of dosing and score survival concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives as a function of generations since their common ancestor, yielding a model-free estimate of how long the predisposing state is inherited. Combine with quantification of what is asymmetrically partitioned at those divisions (mitochondria, lysosomes, efflux pumps, protein aggregates) to nominate the physical carrier of that memory.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation-test design to extract state-switching rates instead of state identities
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style experiments with many parallel small cultures expanded for different numbers of generations before treatment, and fit the variance structure of survivor counts to estimate forward and backward switching rates between tolerant and sensitive states. Using only colony counts, this distinguishes rare stochastic switching, continuously fluctuating traits, and pre-existing stable subclones, and produces rate constants that any mechanistic model must reproduce.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as a prospective functional predictor
description: Apply BH3 profiling (single-cell or on sorted fractions) to the naive population to map how close each cell sits to the mitochondrial death threshold, and prospectively sort on mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial mass, or sensitizer-peptide response before any drug exposure to test enrichment for survivors. This asks whether survival is set by the death machinery's setpoint rather than by target-pathway signaling or transcriptional identity.

question: persister
title: Survival as a neighborhood property rather than a cell-intrinsic property
description: Image the local context of every cell at the moment of dosing (local density, contact number, neighbor identity, distance to colony edge) and regress survival on these variables, then manipulate context directly with micropatterned colonies of defined size, density-matched seeding, and conditioned-medium or transwell swaps. If local secreted factors or contact confer survival, cell-autonomous profiling approaches will only ever recover correlates of position rather than causes.

question: persister
title: Single-cell intracellular drug exposure measurement
description: Quantify per-cell drug concentration directly using mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI/nanoSIMS), a clickable or intrinsically fluorescent drug analog, and efflux-activity dyes in treated cultures, then correlate exposure with fate. This tests whether survivors are cells that simply accumulated less compound, ruling in or out a pharmacokinetic explanation that transcriptome-focused studies routinely skip.

question: persister
title: Luria-Delbruck fluctuation analysis to measure the memory timescale of priming
description: Seed many replicate microcultures from small inocula, expand each for a different number of generations before identical treatment, and fit the across-well variance in survivor counts to a fluctuation model. The dependence of variance on expansion time yields a quantitative heritability timescale for the primed state using only colony counts, no sequencing.

question: persister
title: Pulse labeling to separate active maintenance from passive carryover
description: Combine 4sU/SLAM-seq with pulsed SILAC on sorted persisters versus bulk cells to decompose their distinctive profile into newly synthesized versus inherited, slowly degraded mRNA and protein. This distinguishes an actively transcribed regulatory program from passive inheritance of long-lived molecules, which implies very different intervention points.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Adapt dynamic BH3 profiling to imaging or flow cytometry at single-cell resolution to measure mitochondrial depolarization responses to BH3 peptides before and shortly after dosing, linking priming state to subsequent survival. Apoptotic threshold is the proximate life-or-death determinant and is largely invisible at the RNA level.

question: persister
title: Asymmetric organelle partitioning at mitosis as the origin of fate divergence
description: In sister-pair live imaging, quantify unequal inheritance of mitochondria, lysosomes, and damaged-protein aggregates at each division, then follow both daughters through treatment. This tests whether survival originates in a physical partitioning lottery at cytokinesis rather than in a stable transcriptional program.

question: persister
title: Non-genetic Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis
description: Seed many parallel small cultures from few cells, expand them for a varying number of generations, then treat each independently and count survivors, analyzing the across-culture variance-to-mean ratio rather than the mean. The shape of that distribution and its dependence on pre-treatment expansion time yields the state-switching rate and distinguishes pre-existing heritable priming from drug-induced conversion using only colony counts, with no molecular profiling and no assumption about which genes matter.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement as the first explanatory variable
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in single cells (fluorescent drug analog, efflux-substrate dye, or mass-spectrometry imaging) together with a direct target-occupancy readout such as NanoBRET or a proximal phospho-reporter, in the same cells whose fate is later scored. This tests the mundane but rarely excluded possibility that survivors are simply cells that received or retained less drug, and quantifies how much fate variance remains after pharmacological heterogeneity is accounted for.

question: persister
title: Promoter allelic series that changes expression noise at constant mean
description: Build a panel of synthetic or edited promoters driving a candidate tolerance gene that differ in transcriptional burst size and frequency while matching population-mean expression, then measure survivor frequency across the panel. If survival scales with variance at fixed mean, fluctuation-generated rare states are causally responsible, which no amount of correlative profiling of survivors can establish.

question: persister
title: Dual-reporter decomposition of the priming variable into gene-specific versus global noise
description: Insert two spectrally distinct reporters under identical copies of the candidate priming promoter in the same cell and compare their correlated versus uncorrelated fluctuations, alongside global physiology markers like cell size, ribosome content, and mitochondrial mass. This separates whether the rare tolerant state reflects a gene-specific stochastic program or is a downstream readout of a broader cell-physiological axis, which changes what should be targeted.

question: persister
title: Randomizing the microenvironment to test neighborhood-determined survival
description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and co-culture with differentially labeled cells to systematically vary each cell's local neighborhood size and composition, plus conditioned-medium and transwell swaps to isolate secreted factors. Comparing survival statistics across these designs tests whether apparent cell-intrinsic rare states are actually stochastic local niches, a confound shared by essentially all dish-based survivor-profiling experiments.

question: persister
title: Non-genetic fluctuation analysis to measure state switching rates
description: Adapt the Luria–Delbrück fluctuation test to a reversible, non-genetic state: expand many parallel sub-cultures from small inocula for varying numbers of generations, treat each in full, and fit the mean-versus-variance structure of survivor counts across cultures to competing kinetic models. The jackpot statistics yield numerical entry and exit rates for the tolerant state — distinguishing a rare, stably inherited subpopulation from a fast-flickering one — without ever identifying the responsible molecules.

question: persister
title: Sister- and cousin-cell concordance decay to time the memory
description: Physically separate related cells at defined lineage distances (sisters split immediately after mitosis, cousins after two divisions, with imaging to control elapsed time), treat all of them identically, and measure how fate concordance decays as a function of generations and hours since the common ancestor. The decay constant is a direct readout of the priming state's memory half-life, which can then be compared against measured protein and chromatin-mark half-lives to nominate the class of carrier molecule.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug exposure and target engagement as the first explanation to exclude
description: Quantify, cell by cell, how much inhibitor each cell actually accumulates (fluorescent drug analog or efflux-activity dye) alongside live target-pathway reporters such as an ERK kinase-translocation reporter, then follow the same cells to their fate. This tests the deflating but rarely measured possibility that survivors are simply cells with incomplete target inhibition or rapid signaling rebound dynamics, rather than occupants of a distinct transcriptional program.

question: persister
title: Micropatterned neighborhoods and ratio-mixing tests of non-cell-autonomy
description: Seed cells on micropatterned islands that fix local density, neighbor number, and colony geometry, and separately mix differentially labeled isogenic cells at varying ratios and total densities before treatment. If per-cell survival probability depends on neighborhood configuration or on the abundance of dying bystanders rather than being constant, the rare survivor is specified by context, and conditioned-medium and transwell swaps can then separate secreted from contact-mediated signals.

question: persister
title: Decoupling mean expression from cell-to-cell variability of candidate regulators
description: Using CRISPRa/dCas9 titration or a degron, shift the mean level of a suspected priming factor without changing distribution shape, and separately install a negative-feedback or microRNA-based buffering circuit that compresses cell-to-cell variability while holding the mean fixed. Comparing survivor frequency across these two orthogonal manipulations causally distinguishes a threshold acting on the rare tail of a noisy distribution from a mechanism that depends only on average expression.

question: persister
title: Single-cell drug pharmacology: are survivors resistant or just under-dosed?
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug using a fluorescent drug analog (cross-validated by MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging of the parent compound) alongside efflux activity (calcein-AM/rhodamine-123 extrusion), lysosomal sequestration (LysoTracker colocalization +/- bafilomycin), and a single-cell target-engagement readout such as NanoBRET or in-cell CETSA imaging. This separates 'low drug inside' from 'target bound but pathway output unchanged,' and is tested causally by blocking efflux or lysosomal trapping and asking whether the surviving fraction collapses.

question: persister
title: Imaging-based single-cell BH3 profiling of apoptotic priming
description: Measure each untreated cell's distance from the mitochondrial death threshold by microscopy BH3 profiling (digitonin permeabilization, graded BIM/BAD/HRK peptides, per-cell cytochrome-c release or TMRE loss), and test whether the rare 'unprimed' tail quantitatively matches the surviving fraction across doses. Causally, a BH3 mimetic should shrink the survivor fraction without changing targeted-pathway signaling, while graded BCL-2/MCL-1 overexpression should expand it predictably.

question: persister
title: Mitotic partitioning asymmetry as the origin of the primed state
description: Time-lapse the unequal inheritance of mitochondria, lysosomes, efflux transporters, damaged/aggregated protein, and the drug target itself at each division, then follow both daughters into drug to test whether partitioning asymmetry at a specific division predicts which sister survives. Perturb mitosis duration or mitochondrial fission (DRP1) to shift the asymmetry distribution and see whether survivor frequency moves as predicted, placing the origin of priming in stochastic division rather than transcription.

question: persister
title: Replicative age and label retention of future survivors
description: Install a division counter (doxycycline-pulsed stable H2B-fluorophore or photoconverted Dendra2) whose signal halves with each division, and ask both retrospectively and by prospective sorting whether survivors are drawn from label-retaining rarely-dividing cells or recently divided ones. This turns the vague slow-cycler hypothesis into a quantitative statement about how many divisions ago the surviving state was set, and isolates proteome age from transcriptional signature.

question: persister
title: Niche-conferred survival: neighbor ablation, micropatterning, and medium transplant
description: Use micropatterns and defined local-density gradients to test whether survival probability depends on neighborhood geometry, combined with selective laser or optogenetic (KillerRed/miniSOG) ablation of a prospective survivor's immediate neighbors just before drug, and transplant of conditioned medium from microwells that produced survivors. This asks whether the rare survivor is a rare cell or a rare location, a cell-extrinsic possibility that intrinsic-state assays cannot detect.

question: persister
title: Retrospective profiling of future survivors (barcode rewind)
description: Heritably barcode a clonal population, split it, treat one arm, and use the barcodes of surviving colonies to retrospectively isolate and sequence their untreated siblings from a frozen aliquot of the other arm. This directly measures the molecular state of cells destined to survive, before any drug exposure, instead of inferring it from post-treatment comparisons.

question: persister
title: Live-cell biography linked to end-point molecular state
description: Image every cell in a well continuously from before dosing through colony outgrowth, then perform in-situ transcriptomics or protein imaging on the same fixed plate, registering each survivor to its full behavioral history. This separates survival driven by a pre-existing expression state from survival driven by transient events such as cell-cycle phase, division timing, or neighbor death at the moment of treatment.

question: persister
title: Single-cell pharmacology: measure the drug, not just the cell
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration using fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or efflux-transporter reporters, paired with a live readout of target-pathway inhibition in the same cells. This tests the overlooked possibility that survivors are cells that simply received or retained less drug, rather than cells in a special signaling or transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell splits across a relatedness ladder
description: Physically separate sister cells, cousins, and progressively more distant clonal relatives, treating some while profiling or freezing the others, and measure how strongly survival fate is shared as a function of generations since common ancestor. This converts vague claims of non-genetic heritability into a measured memory half-life for the resistant state, with explicit units of cell divisions.

question: persister
title: Screening on the tail of the distribution rather than the mean
description: Run CRISPR, CRISPRi, or epigenetic-editing screens scored on the fraction of cells surviving drug or on the shape and tail-weight of a single-cell reporter distribution, rather than on bulk growth or mean expression. Hits that alter variability without altering the average, followed by targeted epigenetic writing and erasing of the primed state, would establish causal control over how many cells enter the surviving minority.

question: persister
title: Catch the survivor before it survives
description: Use clonal DNA barcodes plus barcode-specific RNA FISH (or a recorder that converts barcode identity into a sortable surface marker) to physically isolate, from an untreated population, the exact cells whose twins are destined to survive drug in a parallel dish, then profile them by single-cell multiome and proteomics. The surprise is methodological: it measures the pre-existing state of the future survivor directly rather than inferring it backwards from resistant colonies that have already been reshaped by weeks of drug.

question: persister
title: A memory half-life curve for resistance potential
description: Separate sister and cousin cells at defined numbers of divisions after a common ancestor, treat one branch while culturing the other drug-free for varying intervals, and measure how the concordance of survival decays with elapsed time and divisions. This turns "is it heritable?" into a quantitative decay constant, and distinguishes a stably inherited epigenetic state from a fluctuating state with a specific memory clock that sets the size of the surviving fraction.

question: persister
title: Per-cell drug dose, not per-cell biology
description: Quantify intracellular free drug concentration and target occupancy in individual cells before and during treatment using fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, and live target-engagement reporters, then correlate these directly with each cell's fate by imaging. The potentially deflating but decisive finding is that much of the variance in survival is explained by cell-to-cell differences in uptake, efflux, and drug–target stoichiometry rather than by any resistance program.

question: persister
title: Make the rare state common
description: Instead of describing the primed state, construct it: use CRISPRa/CRISPRi, defined signaling pre-treatments, or forced cell-cycle and metabolic states to drive a large fraction of cells into the candidate pre-resistant configuration, then measure whether the surviving fraction shifts by orders of magnitude in the predicted direction. Pairing this with erasure experiments converts a decade of correlative single-cell profiling into a sufficiency-and-necessity test with an effect size readout.

question: persister
title: Fluctuation analysis for non-genetic states
description: Run hundreds of small replicate subpopulations expanded from single cells for varying numbers of generations before identical drug challenge, and fit the distribution of survivor counts across replicates (a Luria–Delbrück-style analysis adapted to reversible states) to infer switching rates into and out of the primed state and its persistence time. The surprise is that counts of colonies alone, with no sequencing or imaging of cell state, can bound the mechanism and rule out whole classes of models.

question: persister
title: Twin-cell retrospective profiling with multimodal readouts
description: Barcode cells, let them divide, and split sister lineages: treat one half, then sequence the untreated twins of the survivors for RNA, chromatin accessibility and protein. This shows the pre-existing state that predicts survival. The surprise would be that this 'primed' state is a coordinated but fleeting program spread across many genes, not one marker or a stable subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Live imaging of signaling history before drug exposure
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging of reporters for kinase activity (such as ERK and AKT) and for the cell cycle, then add drug and link each cell's survival back to its full pre-treatment history. This tests whether survival depends on how signals changed over time (pulse frequency, recent stress) rather than on any single snapshot of the cell's state.

question: persister
title: Measuring memory with sister-cell fluctuation analysis
description: Run Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation assays together with sister-cell and cousin-cell survival correlations at different times since the cells last divided. This measures how strongly and for how long the tendency to survive is inherited. Comparing that timescale with gene-expression memory would show whether survival comes from transcriptional states, from inherited cell parts (such as mitochondria or protein aggregates), or from chance.

question: persister
title: Pooled CRISPR screens that separate priming from conversion
description: Run barcoded single-cell CRISPR screens that separately score (a) how many cells enter the primed state and (b) how efficiently primed cells become stably resistant after the drug is added. This would reveal that the two steps are controlled by largely separate regulators, so they could be targeted at different times.

question: persister
title: Spatial lineage tracing of survivors in tumors
description: Combine in vivo lineage barcodes with spatial transcriptomics, imaging tumors before and during treatment, to map where survivors start and which neighboring cells or local niches they sit in. This tests whether a cell's location and signals from nearby cells, rather than its own internal state, decide survival, and whether the in vitro picture of rare primed cells holds up in tissue.

question: persister
title: Retrospective twin capture: sequence the cell that was going to survive
description: Give every cell a heritable barcode that is both transcribed and readable by hybridization capture, split the population into a treated arm and an untreated arm, then use the barcodes of the survivors to go back and physically pull out their untreated clonal twins for single-cell RNA, ATAC, and imaging. This measures the pre-treatment state that caused survival rather than the post-treatment state that merely accompanies it.

question: persister
title: Memory half-life by serial clone splitting
description: Isolate single survivors, expand them, and repeatedly split the progeny into drug-challenge and continued-growth arms at defined numbers of divisions, fitting the decay of enriched survival to extract a switching rate and memory half-life. The headline number is a timescale, which cleanly separates a stably inherited epigenetic state from a transient fluctuation that happens to be sampled at the moment of drug addition.

question: persister
title: Single-cell apoptotic priming instead of single-cell signaling
description: Combine single-cell BH3 profiling or live reporters of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization with time-lapse tracking of death timing across the whole treated population, asking whether survivors differ in their death execution threshold rather than in drug-pathway signaling. The surprise this tests is that persistence is a property of the apoptotic machinery's variability, not of target-pathway rewiring.

question: persister
title: Screening for the knob that sets the fraction, not the mean
description: Run pooled CRISPR screens scored on the size and switching rate of the primed subpopulation, read out by barcode diversity and clone-size distributions of survivors, rather than on bulk viability. This finds regulators that change how many cells are primed while leaving average drug sensitivity untouched, which bulk screens systematically miss.

question: persister
title: Context at the moment of exposure: cell cycle, neighbors, and actual intracellular drug dose
description: Image cell cycle phase, local cell density, and intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent analog or mass spectrometry imaging) for every cell at the instant of treatment, then track each cell to its fate. This directly tests whether survival is explained by extrinsic position and real delivered dose before invoking any intrinsic transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: Clone-splitting to time when survival is decided
description: Barcode a population, let each clone expand for a defined number of divisions, split sister cells across replicate plates, and treat all plates identically with the targeted drug. The degree to which the same barcodes survive across replicates separates heritable pre-existing priming from coin-flip stochasticity at the moment of exposure, and varying the expansion interval measures how long the primed state persists.

question: persister
title: Retrospective profiling of the untreated sisters of future survivors
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes plus sister-cell splitting to identify, after the fact, which barcodes survived, then deeply profile the matched untreated sisters by single-cell RNA, ATAC, and surface protein measurement. This reveals the rare transient pre-treatment state that predicts survival, rather than the post-drug state of cells that have already been reshaped by treatment.

question: persister
title: Multigenerational live imaging of signaling and cycle history before drug
description: Track lineages for many generations with ERK/AKT activity reporters, cell-cycle reporters, and drug-target pathway sensors, then regress survival on each cell's full history, including pulse frequency, quiescence episodes, division timing, and asymmetric partitioning at mitosis. This tests whether temporal history predicts survival better than any single-timepoint snapshot of expression.

question: persister
title: Screens scored on frequency of priming rather than on survival
description: Combine pooled CRISPR or small-molecule perturbations with a live reporter of the primed pre-resistant state and lineage barcodes, scoring each perturbation by how it changes the frequency of primed cells and the rates of switching into and out of that state. This isolates regulators of the variability itself, which are often distinct from genes that confer resistance once a cell is already primed.

question: persister
title: Same-barcode fate comparison across drugs, doses, and in vivo context
description: Split one barcoded population across different targeted agents, doses, and matched in vitro versus xenograft environments, then ask whether the identical set of barcodes survives in each condition. Shared survivors would indicate a general primed state, while condition-specific survivors would show that the microenvironment and drug mechanism select different subsets, directly constraining which measurements could ever predict survival.

question: persister
title: Memory decay curves from barcoded sister-clone splits
description: Barcode a population, let it grow, split it into replicate plates at different numbers of generations, and treat each plate with drug. Measuring how often the same barcodes survive across splits as a function of time since division gives a quantitative memory timescale for the pre-resistant state, like a modern Luria–Delbrück fluctuation test. This would show directly whether survival is pre-encoded, heritable but transient, or decided only after the drug arrives.

question: persister
title: Pre-treatment multiome 'rewind' to identify the priming state
description: Use lineage barcodes to go back to the exact cells, before treatment, whose descendants later survived. Profile those cells with joint scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and protein measurements. Test whether rare survival comes from one coherent primed program or from many different low-probability states that each lead to survival, and identify the chromatin features that keep that state stable across divisions.

question: persister
title: Continuous live imaging through the drug decision
description: Engineer cells with reporters for signaling dynamics (e.g., ERK/AKT pulses), cell-cycle phase and stress responses, then follow thousands of single-cell lineages from days before treatment through weeks on drug. Link each cell's fate to both its history and its earliest responses after the drug is added. This would separate pre-existing state from events after drug exposure, such as cell-cycle phase at drug entry or how signaling recovers.

question: persister
title: CRISPR screens for regulators of the variability itself, not resistance
description: Run pooled perturbation screens, paired with barcoded fate readouts, that score each knockout by how much it changes the fraction of surviving cells, the diversity of survivor fates and the stability of the primed state, not just average drug sensitivity.
