This could reveal 'variability controller' genes that set how often cells enter rare states, which would be new targets for preventing resistance before it starts.

question: persister
title: Same clones across many hosts or environments
description: Inject a single barcoded population into many mice, or into many in vitro microenvironments that differ in density, stroma or nutrients. Treat each one and compare which barcodes survive. If the same clones survive everywhere, survival is cell-intrinsic; if the overlap depends on context, then spatial and microenvironmental factors such as neighbors, mechanics or metabolism help decide which identical cells survive.

question: persister
title: Clone splitting to test whether survival is a heritable pre-existing state
description: Barcode cells, let each clone expand for a few divisions, then split it. Profile one half (scRNA-seq, ATAC, imaging) and treat the other half with the drug. Varying the time before the split measures how long the 'survivor' state lasts across generations, which shows whether fate is set by a heritable pre-treatment state or decided by chance after the drug arrives.

question: persister
title: Live-cell signaling dynamics linked to each cell's fate
description: Use multiplexed live reporters (for example ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, cell-cycle sensors, and stress reporters) to track thousands of cells before and during treatment, then match each cell's signaling path to whether it survived. This tests whether survivors differ in how they adapt dynamically after drug exposure rather than in any static state measured before treatment.

question: persister
title: Single-cell measurement of intracellular drug and target engagement
description: Measure how much drug each cell takes up and how much of the target it actually blocks, using fluorescent drug analogs, target-engagement biosensors, or single-cell mass spectrometry imaging. Then ask whether survivors simply received or kept a lower effective dose because of efflux, size, or membrane differences. That would be a simple physical explanation that skips gene expression altogether.

question: persister
title: Perturbation screens that score how often survivors arise
description: Run pooled CRISPR or chromatin-modifier screens with single-cell readout. Score each perturbation by how much it changes the fraction of cells that survive and how fast cells switch into and out of the primed state, not only by whether resistance appears. This would map the regulatory network that sets the rate of rare survival, so the rare state could be expanded or eliminated on purpose.

question: persister
title: Spatial and neighbor-context mapping of survivors
description: Follow drug-treated cultures and tumors with spatial transcriptomics and time-lapse imaging that records each cell's position, local density, and neighbors (including dying neighbors). Then test whether survival depends on the cell's surroundings, for example signals released by dying cells nearby or niche contacts, rather than on its own internal state.

question: persister
title: Retrospective profiling of the cells that will survive
description: Barcode a population, split it into twin halves, treat one half with drug and profile the untreated half to recover the pre-treatment transcriptomes of exactly the clones that went on to survive. This turns a post-hoc description of resistant cells into a direct measurement of the primed state that existed before any drug was applied.

question: persister
title: Measure switching rates rather than states
description: Adapt Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis to non-genetic variability: grow many small clonal expansions for varying durations before treatment, and use the variance in survivor number across replicates to infer rates of entry into and exit from the tolerant state. The output is a memory half-life and a switching rate, which constrains mechanism far more tightly than any marker gene list.

question: persister
title: Quantify the drug itself in single cells
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or target-engagement reporters to measure intracellular drug concentration and actual target occupancy cell-by-cell during treatment. The surprising possibility is that survivors differ mainly in how much drug reaches the target—efflux, uptake, lysosomal sequestration—rather than in any downstream signaling or stem-like program.

question: persister
title: Continuous imaging from pre-treatment dynamics to final fate
description: Track thousands of individual cells by live imaging with reporters for pathway activity, cell-cycle position, and division history for days before and through drug exposure, then fix and profile the same cells in situ. This links time-varying features—signaling pulse frequency, time since last division, inherited organelle content—to survival, capturing dynamic information invisible to any snapshot assay.

question: persister
title: Test whether survival travels with the cell or stays with the neighborhood
description: Map survivors against their local context (density, neighbor identity, position in a colony or spheroid), then physically isolate candidate survivors and re-plate them in fresh contexts to see whether the phenotype is transplantable. If survival is conferred by position and neighbors rather than carried by the cell, the entire single-cell-intrinsic framing of persistence needs revision.

question: persister
title: "Perches in the soul": retrospective lineage barcoding of primed cells
description: Barcode a clonal population with heritable lineage tags, split it, profile one half by scRNA-seq before drug exposure and sequence barcodes in survivors after, so the pre-treatment transcriptional state of surviving lineages can be reconstructed. This distinguishes a rare pre-existing primed subpopulation from a state induced by the drug itself.

question: persister
title: "The tune without the words": RNA-protein mismatch in survivors
description: Jointly measure single-cell transcript and protein levels for the drug target and bypass pathways using CITE-seq or smFISH combined with immunofluorescence. This tests whether survivors are defined by translational or post-translational buffering that is invisible to transcript-only resistance screens.

question: persister
title: "Never stops at all": continuous live-cell tracking of survival trajectories
description: Perform long-term time-lapse imaging with signaling and cell-cycle reporters spanning drug addition, tracking each cell's complete history. This reveals whether survival reflects a persistent fluctuating state, cell-cycle phase at the moment of exposure, or stochastic escape from apoptotic commitment.

question: persister
title: "Sweetest in the Gale": dense sampling of transient states during treatment
description: Profile cells at many time points during the first 72 hours of treatment rather than only before and after, since the decisive state may be transient. Pair this with drug-on/drug-off pulse schedules to test whether the surviving state is reversible and the cells re-sensitizable.

question: persister
title: "Never asked a crumb": single-cell metabolic frugality of persisters
description: Quantify per-cell biosynthetic and metabolic demand in survivors using SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation translation-rate assays alongside dormancy markers and nutrient-limitation challenges. This tests whether persistence is an actively maintained low-consumption quiescent program rather than specific signaling rewiring.

question: persister
title: The Pedestal Inscription: retrospective barcoding to read the pre-treatment state of survivors
description: Just as the pedestal carries a legible record of a king who is otherwise gone, give every cell a heritable, transcribed DNA barcode (ClonMapper/Rewind-style) so that after treatment you can return to a pre-treatment aliquot of the same clone and ask what its untreated twins looked like by scRNA-seq. This separates rare pre-existing primed states from drug-induced states, and tests whether survival maps onto lineage at all.

question: persister
title: Two Trunkless Legs of Stone: profiling the 99% that die, not just the survivors
description: The poem defines Ozymandias by what was destroyed around him; likewise, run a fixation-based single-cell time course (fixed scRNA-seq or in-situ methods that retain dying cells) across the first 1-72 h of drug so apoptotic and arrested cells are sampled rather than lost to dissociation bias. The contrast between the trajectory of doomed cells and that of persisters is far more informative than an endpoint survivor profile, which by construction looks like a selected monument with no context.

question: persister
title: The Sculptor Who Read Those Passions: live-imaging fate mapping followed by in situ molecular readout of the same cells
description: The sculptor inferred passions from a living face and stamped them onto stone that outlasted them; invert this by imaging signaling and cell-cycle reporters (ERK-KTR, CDK2 sensor, ATF4/stress reporters) in thousands of individual cells through treatment, then fixing the plate and performing MERFISH or multiplexed immunofluorescence on those exact tracked cells. This yields a direct mapping from a measured pre-drug dynamic state to an individual survival outcome rather than a correlation across separate populations.

question: persister
title: Look on My Works: testing whether the survivor state is a durable monument or a transient pose
description: "Nothing beside remains" is a claim about durability over time, so measure it: take single survivor colonies, withdraw drug, and serially passage them while re-challenging sister sub-populations at intervals from days to months to quantify the half-life of the resistant phenotype. Pair this with single-cell ATAC-seq or CUT&RUN for H3K27me3/H3K4me1 at each timepoint to distinguish maintained chromatin memory, a genetically fixed mutation, and a reversible physiological condition.

question: persister
title: The Lone and Level Sands: survival as a property of local neighborhood, not the cell alone
description: The Wreck is defined partly by the emptiness around it, and persisters may likewise be made by their surroundings, so systematically vary local context (seeding density, micropatterned colonies of defined size, conditioned-medium swaps, fibroblast co-culture) and record position-resolved survival by imaging. Combine with spatial reporters of secreted factors to test whether survivors sit preferentially at colony edges or in paracrine shadows, reframing the question from "which cell" to "which place."

question: persister
title: Rose-moles in stipple: mapping the pre-treatment expression tail
description: Use single-molecule RNA FISH (or amplified clampFISH) against candidate resistance drivers across millions of untreated cells, then treat and re-image the identical field to test whether survivors came from the rare high-expressing 'stippled' subpopulation. This quantifies how much of survival is explained by the tail of each gene's distribution rather than its mean.

question: persister
title: Who knows how?: resolving the kinetic origin of the rare state
description: Measure transcriptional bursting of the candidate driver gene using intronic FISH or live MS2/PP7 reporters to determine whether rare high-expressing cells arise from increased burst frequency, larger burst size, or slow mRNA/protein turnover. Then perturb each parameter via promoter swaps or degron tags and test whether survivor frequency shifts accordingly.

question: persister
title: Swift, slow: live-imaging linkage of division kinetics to survival fate
description: Track thousands of single cells through drug addition with FUCCI cell-cycle reporters plus death and division readouts, retrospectively linking each survivor's pre-treatment cycle length and signaling dynamics to its outcome. This distinguishes persistence through quiescence from persistence through active bypass signaling, which have opposite therapeutic implications.

question: persister
title: Landscape plotted and pieced: spatial neighborhood versus cell-intrinsic causes
description: Grow cells at controlled densities and in spatially resolved colonies, then use spatial transcriptomics or imaging mass cytometry to test whether survivors cluster in local patches (indicating paracrine or contact-mediated protection) rather than scattering at random. Follow up with targeted neighbor ablation and conditioned-media swaps to establish causality.

question: persister
title: All trades, their gear and tackle: cataloguing distinct survivor programs and their heritability
description: Profile survivors with single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) and phospho-CyCIF to test whether they occupy one state or several distinct bypass-pathway programs requiring different combination therapies. Pair this with heritable lineage barcoding and split-and-retreat experiments to measure how long each primed state persists and whether it is re-inducible, identifying the invariant epigenetic generator behind the variable states.

question: persister
title: Clone-splitting with heritable barcodes to catch the primed cell before the drug arrives
description: Transduce the population with expressed lineage barcodes, let each clone expand, then physically split it: treat one half with the targeted drug and immediately profile the untreated twin half by single-cell RNA-seq, so that barcodes shared with the eventual survivors identify what the pre-treatment state of those specific cells looked like. This directly distinguishes a rare pre-existing transcriptional state (the filament already flung) from a state induced only after drug exposure, and can be extended with barcode-guided sorting to prospectively enrich and functionally test the primed subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Continuous live-cell imaging of signaling dynamics through the drug transition
description: Image thousands of single cells for days to weeks using kinase-translocation reporters for the drug-targeted pathway (e.g., ERK or AKT activity), plus cell-cycle and stress reporters, tracking every lineage from before treatment through survival or death. Quantify whether survivors are distinguished by repeated transient signaling pulses, a longer quiescent pause, or a single sustained reactivation event, i.e., which dynamic feature of the many 'throws' is the one that holds.

question: persister
title: Testing the microenvironment as the anchor point for survivors
description: Map where survivors sit and what they touch: spatial transcriptomics or in situ imaging of treated 3D cultures and tumor sections to score survivor proximity to ECM-rich regions, fibroblasts, vasculature, or hypoxic cores, paired with micropatterned substrates of defined stiffness and ligand composition to test causality. If survival probability depends on anchorage and neighbor contact rather than intrinsic state, the cell-autonomous framing is the wrong one.

question: persister
title: Single-cell multiome time course to reconstruct and then break the regulatory bridge
description: Collect joint RNA + ATAC profiles at closely spaced timepoints spanning the drug transition to infer which transcription factors and enhancers connect the rare primed state to the stable resistant state. Then test necessity by CRISPRi knockdown or degron depletion of the top bridging regulators at defined times, asking whether the surviving fraction collapses when the bridge is removed.

question: persister
title: Serial challenge-and-withdrawal to measure how long the surviving state is remembered
description: Expand survivors, withdraw drug for varying intervals, re-barcode or re-sequence existing barcodes, and re-challenge, asking whether the same clones survive again (heritable, stably rewired resistance) or whether a fresh random subset survives (a transient, re-sampled state). The decay curve of clone re-use across withdrawal times gives a quantitative memory timescale that predicts whether drug holidays should resensitize the population.

question: persister
title: Time-lapse measurement of the lifetime of the primed state
description: Knock a fluorescent reporter into an endogenous resistance-associated locus (AXL, NGFR, EGFR, WNT5A) and image untreated cells for days to extract per-cell dwell-time distributions in the high state. Add drug at a defined moment and retrospectively link survival to whether each cell was in the high state at treatment onset, testing whether survival requires occupancy of a short-lived state rather than membership in a stable subpopulation.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell splitting with varying delay to measure memory decay
description: Barcode cells, split each clone into two arms, and treat the second arm after delays from hours to weeks; twin-to-twin concordance in survivor frequency as a function of delay yields the decay constant of the heritable component. This quantifies how long the primed state is held before it subsides back to the population mean.

question: persister
title: Retrospective capture of the pre-treatment state (barcode rewind)
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes to identify, in an untreated replicate aliquot, the clones that survived in the treated arm, then barcode-sort those cells and profile transcriptome, chromatin accessibility, and histone marks. This captures the primed state in its original form, before survivors have transitioned to a different phenotype.

question: persister
title: Reversion kinetics after drug withdrawal
description: Subject survivors to a drug holiday and track resensitization via single-cell profiling and clonal re-barcoding across timepoints, asking whether and how fast the resistant phenotype relaxes back to the naive distribution. Full reversion implicates a transient non-genetic mechanism, while a non-reverting subset separates genuinely mutated clones from epigenetically primed ones and quantifies the mixture.

question: persister
title: Perturbing the duration of the state, not its mean
description: Apply chromatin-regulator inhibitors (DOT1L, KDM5, EZH2, HDAC) or degron-controlled modifiers before drug, and use reporter time-lapse to measure whether each perturbation changes state amplitude, entry frequency, or dwell time; then test which parameter predicts survivor frequency. If interventions that shorten dwell time reduce survivors without changing how many cells ever enter the state, survival is causally set by how long the state persists.

question: persister
title: Fearful Symmetry: the sister-cell split assay
description: Separate sister cells immediately after each division by micromanipulation or microwell tracking, expose one to the targeted drug and profile the other by scRNA-seq, then quantify fate concordance as a function of generational distance (sisters, cousins, second cousins). The decay of concordance with lineage distance directly measures the heritability and memory half-life of the primed state, distinguishing a stably inherited epigenetic configuration from a transiently fluctuating one.

question: persister
title: Burning Bright in the Forests of the Night: live reporters of rare high-expressing states
description: Knock fluorescent reporters into endogenous candidate resistance loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR, SOX10) and image untreated populations for days to catch the rare, transiently bright cells against the dark majority, then add drug and ask which imaged cells survive. This converts the retrospective question "what were survivors like beforehand?" into a prospective one, and also yields the on/off switching rates and state lifetimes that set the size of the surviving fraction.

question: persister
title: What the Hand Dare Seize the Fire: image-guided retrieval of watched survivors
description: Track rare survivors by live imaging through treatment, then photoconvert or laser-mark exactly those cells and recover them for same-cell multiomic profiling (joint ATAC + RNA + surface protein), so that the measured molecular state belongs to a cell whose full behavioral history — division timing, motility, drug-response dynamics — is already known. Pairing phenotype trajectory with molecular state in the same cell avoids the ambiguity of profiling bulk survivor pools in which several distinct escape routes are averaged together.

question: persister
title: In What Distant Deeps or Skies: barcode twin studies of survival origin
description: Transduce a high-complexity expressed barcode library, split the population into replicate "twin" plates, and ask whether the same barcode lineages survive in independent plates and in independent rounds of drug exposure after a drug holiday. Reproducible barcode overlap implicates a pre-existing heritable priming, non-overlap implicates stochastic induction, and partial overlap with decay over the holiday quantifies how long the primed state persists before it is re-created.

question: persister
title: Framing the Symmetry: timing when the tolerant state is forged shut
description: Run drug-on/drug-off cycles while sampling chromatin (CUT&RUN for enhancer remodeling, DNA methylation) and signaling (phosphoproteomics) at dense time points, and at each time point test reversibility by adding chromatin-modifier inhibitors or withdrawing drug. This identifies the window in which a reversible, fluctuating tolerant state is hardened into a stable resistant one — the practically important question of when the forge closes and which enzymes are holding the hammer.

question: persister
title: "I hear it in the deep heart's core": retrospective capture of pre-primed survivors
description: Barcode a clonal cancer cell population, split it, treat one half and profile the untreated half by single-cell RNA-seq, then trace survivor barcodes back to their untreated twin cells. This reveals whether the surviving state is a pre-existing transcriptional memory present before drug exposure rather than a drug-induced change.

question: persister
title: "Peace comes dropping slow": timescale of transcriptional state fluctuation
description: Knock in live-cell fluorescent reporters at candidate priming loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR) and use long-term timelapse imaging to measure dwell times and autocorrelation of the high-expressing state. Sorting cells by how long they have occupied that state and then challenging them tests whether survival probability depends on the duration, not just the level, of priming.

question: persister
title: "In the bee-loud glade": spatial and paracrine determinants of survival
description: Treat cells at controlled densities and micropatterned spacings, then image survivors in situ with multiplexed single-molecule FISH or spatial transcriptomics to test whether they arise in non-random neighborhoods. Conditioned-medium and transwell co-culture experiments then determine whether tolerance is transferable between neighbors or strictly cell-intrinsic.

question: persister
title: "Nine bean-rows and a hive": quiescence and metabolic self-sufficiency of survivors
description: Combine FUCCI cell-cycle reporters or dye-dilution proliferation tracking with single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H FLIM or SCENITH during the first days of treatment. This distinguishes survivors that are simply slow-cycling and metabolically frugal from those running a distinct resistance gene program.

question: persister
title: "I will arise and go now" (said twice): reversibility across drug-on/drug-off cycles
description: Barcode cells and run repeated cycles of treatment and drug holiday, sequencing barcode abundance plus matched single-cell DNA and RNA at each round. Recurrence of the same barcodes indicates heritable genetic or stably epigenetic resistance, whereas a fresh survivor set each cycle indicates a transient, stochastically re-entered state.

question: persister
title: The cloud's-eye view: retrospective lineage tracing of survivors
description: Like the speaker drifting 'on high o'er vales and hills' who notices the golden few only once they stand out, continuously image a whole well from before drug addition through survivor outgrowth, then trace each resistant colony back to its founder. This measures what the destined survivor was doing hours to days before treatment — size, cycle phase, reporter intensity, division history — rather than only what survivors look like at the end.

question: persister
title: 'Fluttering and dancing in the breeze': fluctuation timescales as the predictor
description: Place live-cell reporters on candidate priming genes (AXL, NGFR, EGFR) and measure the autocorrelation time of their fluctuations in untreated cells. The prediction is that only cells whose high state persists longer than the drug's killing window survive, making fluctuation memory time — not peak expression level — the decisive measurable.

question: persister
title: 'A host, of golden daffodils': sibling-split assays separating heritable from stochastic survival
description: Split single cells into daughter or granddaughter pairs, treating one branch with drug while profiling the untreated twin by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Concordance between siblings quantifies how many generations back the surviving state was established, cleanly distinguishing heritable priming from a coin flip at the moment of treatment.

question: persister
title: 'Beside the lake, beneath the trees': spatial niche mapping of survivors
description: Map each surviving cell's spatial context — local density, neighbor identity, distance to colony edge, ECM stiffness and substrate contact — by combining live imaging with spatial transcriptomics on the fixed well. Comparing matched dying cells at equivalent positions tests whether microenvironment, drug access, or paracrine signaling explains survival independently of cell-intrinsic state.

question: persister
title: 'The inward eye': drug holiday and re-challenge to test epigenetic memory
description: Echoing the poem's recollection after the event, withdraw drug from survivors, expand them for defined numbers of generations, and re-challenge at intervals while profiling chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation. The decay rate of resistance distinguishes reversible transcriptional tolerance from stably encoded epigenetic or genetic resistance and pinpoints loci that remain primed.

question: persister
title: "Allonymous" cells: retrospective capture of the pre-drug primed state
description: Barcode an isogenic population and use a sister-cell split design (Rewind/ClonMapper-style) so that survivors' barcodes can be traced back to their untreated twins, which are then profiled by scRNA-seq. This measures the cell state that existed before drug exposure, distinguishing pre-existing priming from drug-induced reprogramming.

question: persister
title: "Indelibly": measuring the memory half-life of the resistant state
description: Isolate primed or persister cells, culture them drug-free for intervals from hours to weeks, and re-challenge at each time point to build a decay curve of resistance probability. The decay rate, compared to the division rate, reveals whether the state is a transient fluctuation or a heritable epigenetic memory.

question: persister
title: "Insulator": stochastic chromatin boundary loss at resistance driver loci
description: Combine single-cell ATAC/CUT&Tag with Micro-C or 4C at loci such as AXL, NGFR, or MET in primed versus naive cells, then CRISPRi the implicated CTCF/cohesin boundary elements. This tests whether rare survival arises from sporadic loss of insulation that permits ectopic enhancer-promoter contact.

question: persister
title: "Sync": signaling and cell-cycle phase at the moment of drug addition
description: Image cells carrying ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters plus a PIP-FUCCI cell-cycle sensor continuously through drug addition and for days afterward, linking each cell's pre-treatment dynamics to its fate. This asks whether survival is determined by the timing and phase of signaling pulses, a dynamic cause invisible in fixed-cell snapshots.

question: persister
title: "Mesh": survival as a property of the local cellular neighborhood
description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and tunable-stiffness substrates, together with spatial transcriptomics of residual disease, to quantify how neighbor contacts, local density, and matrix mechanics predict persistence. Non-random spatial clustering of survivors would show that the rare state is partly environmental rather than cell-intrinsic.

question: persister
title: Glyphic hornbook: heritable barcodes plus a pre-treatment transcriptional lookup table
description: Transduce cells with expressed DNA barcodes and split the population into one arm profiled by scRNA-seq before treatment and one arm treated, so each surviving clone's barcode can be looked up against the untreated 'hornbook' of states. This directly tests whether survivors arise from pre-existing, heritable transcriptional states rather than random chance, and identifies the specific priming programs.

question: persister
title: Nitid/photolith: optical tagging of rare primed cells before drug exposure
description: Live-image a fluorescent reporter for a candidate priming marker and use photoconversion or photo-crosslinking to permanently mark the rare brightest cells, then sort and sequence them while following matched wells through treatment. This provides a causal link between a pre-drug optical phenotype and eventual survival, rather than a post hoc correlation.

question: persister
title: Impute: sister-cell split assay to recover the survivor's pre-drug state
description: Physically separate sister cells right after mitosis, treat one sister with drug and molecularly profile the other, thereby imputing the pre-treatment state of the very cell that lived or died. Varying the interval between separation and treatment measures how long the predictive non-genetic memory persists.

question: persister
title: Graduator/undo: fluctuation analysis plus reversibility kinetics
description: Perform Luria-Delbruck-style replicate expansions from small founder populations across a drug dose gradient to quantitatively partition survival into genetic, heritable-epigenetic, and transient non-genetic contributions. Then regrow survivor colonies without drug and re-challenge at increasing intervals to measure the timescale over which resistance is undone.

question: persister
title: Innerve/embassy: spatial niche and paracrine messenger analysis
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics to 3D cultures or co-cultures to ask whether survivors occupy distinctive cellular neighborhoods, and pair this with conditioned-media transfer and ligand-trap or receptor-blockade perturbations. Together these distinguish cell-intrinsic survival states from protection delivered by secreted envoys from neighboring cells.

question: persister
title: Gyromele retrieval: mark-then-profile the future survivors
description: Like the gyromele (a swallowed sampler that retrieves stomach contents for later inspection), use live imaging of a barcoded or photoconvertible cell population during treatment, then retrospectively identify which pre-treatment cells gave rise to survivors — either by photoconverting/laser-marking their sisters in a split-population design or by lineage barcodes shared with an untreated replicate — and run scRNA-seq on those specific pre-treatment cells. This directly measures the priming state that preceded survival rather than the post-hoc state of cells already reshaped by the drug.

question: persister
title: Piedfort test: is the survivor a different coin or the same coin struck thick?
description: A piedfort looks like an ordinary coin but is a physically distinct variant; analogously, run matched single-cell DNA + RNA (e.g., G&T-seq or scDNA panel plus scRNA) and deep targeted sequencing on survivor colonies to test whether they carry pre-existing mutations, copy-number changes, or amplifications at the drug target versus being genetically identical but transcriptionally distinct. Combining this with a Luria–Delbrück fluctuation assay on survivor frequency across sibling cultures quantifies what fraction of survival is genetic versus non-genetic.

question: persister
title: Tachylalia of transcription: burst kinetics of resistance genes
description: Tachylalia is abnormally rapid speech — a difference in rate rather than vocabulary. Use single-molecule RNA FISH plus MS2/PP7 live nascent-transcription imaging on candidate resistance drivers (e.g., RTKs, AXL, NGFR, efflux pumps) to test whether rare survivors differ by burst frequency/size rather than by expressing a unique gene set, and correlate each cell's measured burst history with its subsequent fate under drug.

question: persister
title: Leash and unkennel: how long is the memory of the primed state?
description: A jess and leash hold a hawk only until it is unkennelled; the question is how long the restraint lasts. Sort or image-mark cells in the putative primed state, then re-assay their drug survival after defined numbers of divisions (1, 3, 5, 10) with and without a washout, to measure the heritability half-life of the resistant state and distinguish transient fluctuation from stable epigenetic memory — pairing this with ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN at each timepoint to see which chromatin features persist.

question: persister
title: Hiveward: spatial neighborhoods of survival
description: "Hiveward" implies movement toward a collective center, so test whether survival is a property of neighborhoods rather than lone cells: grow colonies at defined densities, track survivors by in situ spatial transcriptomics or sequential FISH on the fixed, intact monolayer, and ask whether survivors are spatially clustered and locally enriched for secreted-factor signaling. Conditioned-media transfer and microfluidic cell-separation controls then distinguish paracrine rescue from cell-intrinsic priming.

question: persister
title: "Prescience": find out whether survivors were already different before treatment
description: Label cells with heritable barcodes, let them divide, and split sister cells into two groups. Treat one group and profile the untreated sisters of the survivors with single-cell RNA-seq to see whether survival comes from a state that existed before the drug (and what that state is) or from a response the drug induces.

question: persister
title: "Bimodal": look for genes switched strongly on in a few cells, and time how long that lasts
description: Before treatment, use single-molecule RNA FISH to find genes that are high in a small fraction of cells and low in the rest, then sort out the marker-high cells and track when they return to the normal mix and how their survival chance changes over time. Run a Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis alongside this to separate short-lived fluctuations from stable, inherited variation.

question: persister
title: "Patination": test whether a cell's recent history predicts survival better than its current state
description: Before and during treatment, film cells carrying live reporters, such as kinase-translocation reporters for ERK/AKT signalling and FUCCI for cell-cycle stage. Then ask whether the survivors share a pattern over time, such as slow cycling, signalling pulses, or a deep quiescent state, that a single snapshot would miss.

question: persister
title: "Evacuative": check whether some cells simply see less drug
description: Measure intracellular drug levels in single cells (fluorescent drug analogs or mass cytometry) and how fully the target is inhibited (phospho-flow or immunofluorescence). Combine this with efflux-pump inhibitors to see whether cell-to-cell differences in drug uptake or target shutdown explain part of the survival, separately from transcriptional state.

question: persister
title: "Flagstone": map whether a cell's neighbours affect its chance of survival
description: Do spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on treated dishes or tumour sections, then change seeding density and swap conditioned media. This shows whether survival depends on local crowding, signals released by nearby cells, or contact with neighbours, rather than only on traits inside the cell.

question: persister
title: Tasimetric look-back: retrospective linkage of pre-drug expression fluctuations to survival
description: Inspired by 'tasimetry' (measurement of minute changes), knock fluorescent reporters into endogenous candidate resistance loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR, MITF-low program genes) and continuously image a clonal population for several days before adding drug, then track each imaged cell's fate so that rare, transient, low-amplitude expression excursions can be scored as predictive or not. Complement this with a transcriptome-wide version in which cells are split and one half is profiled by scRNA-seq while the sister half is treated, or with RNA-barcode 'rewind' capture, so the pre-treatment state of the eventual survivors is recovered rather than inferred.

question: persister
title: Epenthetic barcoding: inserting lineage recorders to partition heritable memory from instantaneous noise
description: Like an epenthesis that inserts a segment into a word without changing its root, integrate expressed, scRNA-seq-capturable lineage barcodes (CellTag/Watermelon-style) into cells, then expand, split the labeled population into multiple replicate flasks, and treat each independently with the same targeted drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicate flasks far more often than chance, survival is governed by a heritable (epigenetically memorized) state whose half-life can be measured by varying expansion time between splitting and treatment; if barcode overlap is at chance, survival is set by short-lived fluctuations or by the drug exposure itself.

question: persister
title: Consocies mapping: testing whether survival is a neighborhood property rather than a cell-intrinsic one
description: Borrowing 'consocies' (a community subunit dominated by one member), grow cells at defined local densities and in defined spatial patterns (micropatterned islands, mixed co-cultures with fluorescently marked drug-sensitive or fibroblast/stromal partners), then image which positions within a colony yield survivors and test conditioned medium and Transwell separation to ask whether paracrine signals (HGF, NRG1, AXL ligands, extracellular vesicles) confer tolerance. Follow with spatial transcriptomics on treated colonies to correlate each survivor's transcriptional state with quantified features of its immediate neighborhood, such as local density, distance to colony edge, and neighbor identity.

question: persister
title: Rearousal kinetics: distinguishing pre-existing quiescence from drug-induced dormancy and measuring the awakening step
description: Use live-cell CDK2-activity and p21 sensors plus CFSE/H2B-photoconversion dilution to determine whether the cells destined to survive were already slow-cycling or arrested at the moment of drug addition, and time-lapse the identical fields through weeks of treatment to capture the exact division at which each persister 'rearouses'. Pair this with drug-holiday experiments (remove drug, re-expand, re-treat) to quantify what fraction of tolerance is reversible dormancy versus fixed resistance, and with scRNA-seq at multiple timepoints to define the transcriptional trajectory from arrest to re-entry.

question: persister
title: Preimbibition assay: single-cell measurement of drug uptake, efflux, and target engagement
description: Testing the mundane but often-ignored possibility that survivors simply 'preimbibe' less drug, measure intracellular drug concentration per cell using an intrinsically fluorescent or click-labeled analog of the inhibitor, single-cell mass spectrometry, or MALDI imaging of the colony, alongside efflux-pump reporters and dye-efflux (Hoechst side-population) assays. Immediately pair each cell's drug level with a single-cell readout of target engagement (quantitative immunofluorescence for phospho-ERK/phospho-AKT or a FRET kinase biosensor), so that pharmacokinetic heterogeneity can be cleanly separated from downstream signaling-state heterogeneity as the cause of survival.

question: persister
title: Clone-splitting to time the origin of the surviving state ("prewelcome")
description: Expand single-cell-derived clones, then split each clone into a treated arm and an untreated arm that is profiled by scRNA-seq/protein staining, so that any pre-existing transcriptional program enriched in the untreated twin of a high-survival clone is identified as a primed state present before drug exposure. Varying the number of divisions between splitting and treatment (1, 5, 10, 20 generations) converts the correlation decay into a direct measurement of how many cell generations the survival-conferring state is inherited.

question: persister
title: Absolute, spike-in-normalized profiling of survivors ("eustatic" baseline shift)
description: Because standard scRNA-seq normalization hides changes in the global level, quantify survivors with ERCC/UMI spike-ins plus measurements of cell volume, total RNA, total protein, and ribosome content, to test whether persisters differ by a uniform shift in transcriptome and biosynthetic scale (a slow-growing, low-output state) rather than by induction of specific resistance genes. The distinction determines whether the right therapeutic target is a pathway or the global growth/translation setpoint.

question: persister
title: Barcoded re-challenge after drug holiday to test reversibility ("reimpose")
description: Transduce cells with a high-complexity lineage barcode library, treat, expand survivors off drug for varying holiday lengths, then re-treat and sequence barcodes, asking whether the same lineages survive again (heritable/genetic or stably epigenetic) or a fresh random subset survives (reversible, re-sampled state). Pairing barcode recovery with whole-genome sequencing and ATAC-seq of the same expanded clones separates mutational resistance from chromatin-encoded memory from pure stochastic re-sampling.

question: persister
title: Spatial and neighborhood determinants of survival ("entangled" / "underlap")
description: Image cells at controlled densities and in micropatterned colonies, record each cell's local density, contact number, and position (edge versus interior) before treatment, then follow survival by live imaging, and apply spatial transcriptomics or in situ sequencing to the fixed endpoint. This tests whether survivors are defined by a crowded or edge niche with local paracrine signaling and drug-gradient shielding rather than by a cell-intrinsic state, which can be confirmed by conditioned-media and co-culture swaps.

question: persister
title: Continuous single-cell trajectories through treatment with retrospective in situ readout ("glide")
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging with cell-cycle (FUCCI), signaling (ERK/AKT biosensors), and candidate-marker reporters to track every cell continuously from before drug addition through death or persistence, then fix the plate and perform single-molecule FISH or multiplexed immunofluorescence on the same imaged cells to link dynamic history to final molecular state. Comparing abrupt dosing with gradual dose escalation reveals whether survival depends on the cell's phase and signaling-pulse history at the moment of exposure or on an adaptive trajectory acquired during treatment.

question: persister
title: Tail-resolved state census (Zipf analysis of the pre-treatment population)
description: Deeply sample 10^5-10^6 untreated cells by single-cell RNA-seq/multiome and explicitly model the rank-frequency tail rather than cluster averages, asking whether drug-tolerant programs (receptor-tyrosine-kinase, neural-crest, quiescence modules) exist as discrete rare states at ~0.1-1% frequency. Validate by FACS-sorting the tail on marker combinations and comparing colony survival to the bulk population.

question: persister
title: Twin-split lineage barcoding: read the word before you need it
description: Label cells with heritable expressed barcodes, then split each clone into a treated arm and an untreated arm profiled immediately, so that survivors in the treated arm identify barcodes whose siblings' pre-treatment transcriptomes and chromatin can be retrieved retrospectively. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a prior molecular state or arises only after drug exposure.

question: persister
title: Morphemic dissection of priming by combinatorial perturbation
description: Treat each candidate priming program as composed of reusable regulatory 'morphemes' (individual transcription factors, chromatin regulators, signaling nodes) and run CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens before drug addition, scoring changes in the frequency of surviving colonies rather than bulk viability. Pairwise perturbations then reveal which combinations are necessary versus merely co-occurring in the rare state.

question: persister
title: Persistence and reversibility timescales of the rare state
description: Use long-term live imaging with endogenous fluorescent knock-ins of candidate priming genes plus sister-cell and drug-holiday experiments to measure how many generations a high-expressing state persists and whether resensitization occurs after withdrawal. Luria-Delbruck fluctuation tests on split subclones quantify whether the heritability is genetic, epigenetic with memory, or transient.

question: persister
title: Locale test: microenvironment and drug exposure as confounders
description: Combine spatial/imaging-based transcriptomics with per-cell measurement of actual intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging) alongside local neighbor density, cell-cycle phase, and cell size. This distinguishes genuine intrinsic priming from mundane positional explanations such as a cell simply receiving less drug, the key control before any rare-state model is accepted.

question: persister
title: Clonal recurrence test with split-population barcoding ("recur")
description: Transduce the cell line with a high-complexity heritable barcode library (e.g., ClonMapper/Watermelon), split the labeled population into replicate arms, treat each independently, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. The degree of barcode overlap between arms quantifies how much survival is driven by a heritable, pre-existing clonal state versus a stochastic, non-heritable coin flip, and a barcode-plus-scRNA readout links each recurring clone to its expression program.

question: persister
title: Retrospective unmasking of the pre-treatment survivor state ("unmask")
description: Use a Rewind-style approach: image and single-cell-profile the untreated population, then apply drug, identify the rare survivors, and trace them back to their fixed/imaged ancestors (via live-cell tracking or barcode-guided recovery of the initial-state scRNA-seq profiles). This directly measures what the surviving cells looked like before drug exposure, rather than inferring cause from the post-treatment state, which is confounded by drug-induced reprogramming.

question: persister
title: Sister-cell divergence to measure the memory timescale ("twinter")
description: Live-image a reporter for a candidate priming factor (e.g., AXL, NGFR, or an ERK/EGFR activity biosensor) across tracked lineages, then treat and score which cells survive, comparing concordance of survival between sister cells, cousins, and unrelated cells as a function of time since division. The decay of concordance with lineage distance gives a quantitative half-life for the fluctuating state that confers tolerance, distinguishing short-lived signaling noise from multi-generation epigenetic memory.

question: persister
title: Single-cell metabolic phenotyping of the quiescent/starved state ("semifamine")
description: Apply label-free NAD(P)H/FAD fluorescence lifetime imaging plus SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation assays to measure per-cell translation rate, glycolytic/oxidative balance, and cell-cycle position at the moment of drug addition, then follow the same cells to survival outcome. This tests whether survivors occupy a dormant, low-biosynthesis, lipid-peroxidation-sensitive niche, and nominates metabolic co-treatments (e.g., GPX4 or OXPHOS inhibition) whose efficacy should track the measured state.

question: persister
title: Spatial accounting of dying neighbors and local niche effects ("ghostcraft")
description: Perform longitudinal imaging of the whole treated monolayer or 3D culture so that each survivor's local history is recorded: distance to dying cells, local density, time-integrated exposure to apoptotic-corpse-derived and secreted factors, measured against conditioned-media and spatially randomized controls. Pairing this with spatial transcriptomics of survivor neighborhoods distinguishes cell-intrinsic priming from non-cell-autonomous rescue by dying or stressed neighbors, which is testable by blocking candidate ligands.
